question: Is first-response and resolution speed on support tickets getting better or worse over time?
sql:
WITH month_dim AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cd.month_start AS month_start, cd.month_label AS month_label
  FROM calendar_days cd
  WHERE cd.calendar_date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND cd.calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
),
t0 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS tickets_created
  FROM tickets tk
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS tickets_with_first_response,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.first_response_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_first_response_hours,
         PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.first_response_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS median_first_response_hours
  FROM tickets tk
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND tk.first_response_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS tickets_resolved,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_resolution_hours,
         PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS median_resolution_hours
  FROM tickets tk
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND tk.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(DISTINCT tk.id) AS tickets_with_breach
  FROM tickets tk
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = tk.id
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
)
SELECT
  md.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(t0.tickets_created, 0) AS tickets_created,
  COALESCE(t1.tickets_with_first_response, 0) AS tickets_with_first_response,
  ROUND(t1.avg_first_response_hours::numeric, 1) AS avg_first_response_hours,
  ROUND(t1.median_first_response_hours::numeric, 1) AS median_first_response_hours,
  COALESCE(t2.tickets_resolved, 0) AS tickets_resolved,
  ROUND(t2.avg_resolution_hours::numeric, 1) AS avg_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(t2.median_resolution_hours::numeric, 1) AS median_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t3.tickets_with_breach, 0) / NULLIF(t0.tickets_created, 0), 1) AS sla_breach_rate_pct
FROM month_dim md
LEFT JOIN t0 ON t0.month_start = md.month_start
LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.month_start = md.month_start
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.month_start = md.month_start
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.month_start = md.month_start
ORDER BY md.month_start ASC

tags.details: Source: tickets, joined to sla_breaches for breach rate. Grain the month on tickets.created_at (date_trunc to month / use calendar_days.month_label for the label). Window: 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (full history, 36 rows). First response hours = extract(epoch from first_response_at - created_at)/3600, only for tickets where first_response_at is not null (report both the count with a response and the avg/median so the denominator is clear). Resolution hours = extract(epoch from resolved_at - created_at)/3600 for tickets where resolved_at is not null. SLA breach rate = distinct tickets in that month's cohort with at least one row in sla_breaches, divided by tickets created that month, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal. Round all hour figures to 1 decimal. Note in the report how many of the 36 months are returned, and flag that the most recent 1-2 months will understate resolution/response times for tickets still open (right-censoring) so we read the tail with caution. Order by month ascending.
tags.grain: one calendar month, platform-wide across all tenants

SELECT
  COALESCE(om.month, rm.month) AS month,
  om.orders_placed,
  rm.returns_requested,
  CASE WHEN om.orders_placed > 0 THEN ROUND(rm.returns_requested * 100.0 / om.orders_placed, 1) ELSE NULL END AS return_rate_pct,
  rm.returns_refunded,
  rm.avg_days_requested_to_refunded,
  rm.median_days_requested_to_refunded,
  CASE WHEN rm.returns_requested > 0 THEN ROUND(rm.returns_rejected * 100.0 / rm.returns_requested, 1) ELSE NULL END AS returns_rejected_pct
FROM
  (SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', placed_at), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, count(*) AS orders_placed
   FROM orders
   WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
   GROUP BY 1) om
FULL OUTER JOIN
  (SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', requested_at), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
          count(*) AS returns_requested,
          count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded') AS returns_refunded,
          count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'rejected') AS returns_rejected,
          ROUND(AVG(extract(epoch from (refunded_at - requested_at))/86400) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded' AND refunded_at IS NOT NULL), 1) AS avg_days_requested_to_refunded,
          ROUND(CAST(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch from (refunded_at - requested_at))/86400) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded' AND refunded_at IS NOT NULL) AS numeric), 1) AS median_days_requested_to_refunded
   FROM order_returns
   WHERE requested_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND requested_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
   GROUP BY 1) rm
ON om.month = rm.month
ORDER BY COALESCE(om.month, rm.month)

question: Was the May-June 2025 jump in ticket volume and resolution time concentrated in a few merchants, or broad-based across the platform?
sql:
SELECT
  tn.name AS merchant_name,
  a.mayjun_count AS tickets_created_may_jun_2025,
  ROUND(a.other_count / 10.0, 2) AS avg_monthly_tickets_other_2025,
  CASE WHEN a.other_count = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND( (a.mayjun_count/2.0) / (a.other_count/10.0), 2)
  END AS spike_ratio,
  CASE WHEN a.mayjun_count = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(d.delivery_count,0) / a.mayjun_count, 1)
  END AS delivery_tag_share_pct
FROM (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') AS total_2025,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-05-01' AND created_at < DATE '2025-07-01') AS mayjun_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
                      AND NOT (created_at >= DATE '2025-05-01' AND created_at < DATE '2025-07-01')) AS other_count
  FROM tickets
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) a
JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = a.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS delivery_count
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN ticket_tags_map ttm ON ttm.ticket_id = t.id
  JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-05-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND LOWER(st.name) IN ('delivery', 'where-is-my-order')
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
) d ON d.tenant_id = a.tenant_id
WHERE a.total_2025 >= 5
ORDER BY a.mayjun_count DESC, tn.name ASC
LIMIT 50

question: How satisfied are shoppers with support interactions overall, and is satisfaction trending up or down?
sql:
select
  strftime(date_trunc('month', submitted_at), '%Y-%m') as month,
  count(*) as csat_responses,
  round(avg(score)::numeric, 2) as avg_score,
  round(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by score)::numeric, 1) as median_score,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when score >= 4 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_satisfied,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when score <= 2 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_dissatisfied
from csat_responses
where submitted_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01' and submitted_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
group by date_trunc('month', submitted_at)
order by month asc

question: Does the returns/refund experience vary a lot across merchants, and does any merchant stand out as a problem spot the way Studio Vrij did on support tickets?
sql:
SELECT t.name as merchant_name,
  ord.orders_placed,
  ret.returns_requested,
  round(100.0 * ret.returns_requested / ord.orders_placed, 1) as return_rate_pct,
  rf.avg_days,
  rf.median_days,
  round(100.0 * coalesce(rej.rejected_count,0) / ret.returns_requested, 1) as returns_rejected_pct
FROM tenants t
JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as orders_placed FROM orders WHERE placed_at >= '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id) ord ON ord.tenant_id = t.id
JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as returns_requested FROM order_returns WHERE requested_at >= '2025-01-01' AND requested_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id) ret ON ret.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, round(avg(days),1) as avg_days, round(cast(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by days) as numeric),1) as median_days
           FROM (SELECT tenant_id, extract(epoch from (refunded_at - requested_at))/86400 as days FROM order_returns WHERE status='refunded' AND refunded_at IS NOT NULL AND requested_at >= '2025-01-01' AND requested_at < '2026-01-01') x
           GROUP BY tenant_id) rf ON rf.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as rejected_count FROM order_returns WHERE status='rejected' AND requested_at >= '2025-01-01' AND requested_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id) rej ON rej.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE ret.returns_requested >= 20
ORDER BY ret.returns_requested DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 50

question: Does a slower ticket resolution actually translate into a lower satisfaction score?
sql:
with resolved_tickets_with_csat as (
    select
        t.id as ticket_id,
        c.score as csat_score,
        extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 as resolution_hours
    from tickets t
    join csat_responses c
        on c.ticket_id = t.id
    where t.resolved_at is not null
        and t.created_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01'
        and t.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
),
bucketed_tickets as (
    select
        ticket_id,
        csat_score,
        case
            when resolution_hours < 4 then '<4h'
            when resolution_hours < 24 then '4-24h'
            when resolution_hours < 72 then '1-3 days'
            when resolution_hours < 168 then '3-7 days'
            else '>7 days'
        end as resolution_bucket,
        case
            when resolution_hours < 4 then 0
            when resolution_hours < 24 then 4
            when resolution_hours < 72 then 24
            when resolution_hours < 168 then 72
            else 168
        end as bucket_sort_key
    from resolved_tickets_with_csat
),
bucket_summary as (
    select
        resolution_bucket,
        bucket_sort_key,
        count(*) as ticket_count,
        round(avg(csat_score)::numeric, 2) as avg_csat_score,
        round(100.0 * sum(case when csat_score >= 4 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_satisfied,
        round(100.0 * sum(case when csat_score <= 2 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_dissatisfied
    from bucketed_tickets
    group by resolution_bucket, bucket_sort_key
)
select
    resolution_bucket as resolution_time_bucket,
    ticket_count as tickets,
    avg_csat_score as avg_csat_score,
    pct_satisfied as pct_satisfied,
    pct_dissatisfied as pct_dissatisfied
from bucket_summary
order by bucket_sort_key

Support response & resolution time trend, monthly
tags.details: Source: tickets joined to csat_responses on tickets.id = csat_responses.ticket_id. Only include tickets with resolved_at not null and a matching csat_responses row. resolution_hours = extract(epoch from resolved_at - created_at)/3600. Bucket into: '<4h', '4-24h', '1-3 days' (24-72h), '3-7 days' (72-168h), '>7 days' (168h+). Window: tickets.created_at 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (full history, to get a reliable sample size per bucket). avg score over csat_responses.score for tickets in that bucket, rounded to 2 decimals. '% satisfied'/'% dissatisfied' as in the other CSAT reports, rounded to 1 decimal. Order by the bucket's natural time order (use a numeric sort key for the lower bound of each bucket, e.g. 0, 4, 24, 72, 168), not alphabetically. Expect exactly 5 rows.

WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', t.created_at) AS month_start,
    t.rating,
    t.is_verified_purchase
  FROM product_reviews t
  WHERE t.is_approved = true
    AND t.created_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(t0.month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
  t0.review_count AS reviews_submitted,
  t1.avg_rating,
  t2.median_rating,
  t3.pct_low_rating,
  t3.pct_high_rating,
  t3.pct_verified_purchase
FROM (
  SELECT month_start, COUNT(*) AS review_count
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_start
) t0
JOIN (
  SELECT month_start, ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_start
) t1 ON t1.month_start = t0.month_start
JOIN (
  SELECT month_start, ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY rating)::numeric, 1) AS median_rating
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_start
) t2 ON t2.month_start = t0.month_start
JOIN (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN rating IN (1,2) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_low_rating,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN rating IN (4,5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_high_rating,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_verified_purchase THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_verified_purchase

question: Among orders marketing can take credit for, which campaign channels generate the most attributed orders and revenue, and what's the resulting average order value?
sql:
WITH attr AS (
  SELECT
    c.channel AS channel,
    a.order_id AS order_id,
    a.attributed_revenue AS attributed_revenue,
    CASE WHEN a.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS fx_rate
  FROM attributions a
  JOIN campaigns c ON c.id = a.campaign_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = a.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(a.occurred_at AS date)
  WHERE a.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND a.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND a.order_id IS NOT NULL
),
per_channel AS (
  SELECT
    channel,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS attributed_orders,
    SUM(attributed_revenue / fx_rate) AS attributed_revenue_eur
  FROM attr
  GROUP BY channel
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(attributed_revenue_eur) AS total_revenue_eur FROM per_channel
)
SELECT
  pc.channel,
  pc.attributed_orders,
  ROUND(pc.attributed_revenue_eur, 0) AS attributed_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(pc.attributed_revenue_eur / t.total_revenue_eur * 100, 1) AS share_of_revenue_pct,
  ROUND(pc.attributed_revenue_eur / pc.attributed_orders, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur
FROM per_channel pc
CROSS JOIN totals t
ORDER BY attributed_revenue_eur DESC, channel ASC

columns_requested: attributed_orders - count of distinct attributions.order_id where order_id is not null
attributed_revenue_eur - sum of attributions.attributed_revenue converted to EUR, rounded to 0 decimals
share_of_revenue_pct - attributed_revenue_eur / total attributed_revenue_eur across all channels * 100, rounded to 1 decimal
avg_order_value_eur - attributed_revenue_eur / attributed_orders, rounded to 0 decimals
tags.details: Source: attributions joined to campaigns on campaign_id to get channel; filter attributions.occurred_at in 2025-01-01..2025-12-31 and order_id is not null (i.e. actual purchase-linked touches, not view-through-only rows). Convert attributed_revenue to EUR using exchange_rates: join on base_code='EUR', quote_code = attributions.currency_code, as_of = the calendar date of occurred_at; amount_eur = attributed_revenue / rate (treat currency_code='EUR' as rate 1). No tenant filter — aggregate across all merchants. Order by attributed_revenue_eur descending, tie-break by channel ascending. Expect well under 50 rows since campaigns.channel is a small code list.
tags.grain: one row per campaign channel (campaigns.channel)

question: Which acquisition channels bring the most site traffic across all merchants, and how has that mix shifted versus a year ago?
sql:
select
  channel,
  sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end) as sessions_2025,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)
    / nullif(sum(sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)) over (), 0), 1) as share_of_2025_sessions_pct,
  sum(case when started_at >= date '2024-01-01' and started_at < date '2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end) as sessions_2024,
  round(100.0 * (
    sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)
    - sum(case when started_at >= date '2024-01-01' and started_at < date '2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)
  ) / nullif(sum(case when started_at >= date '2024-01-01' and started_at < date '2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end), 0), 1) as yoy_change_pct,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' and is_bounce then 1 else 0 end)
    / nullif(sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end), 0), 1) as bounce_rate_2025_pct,
  round(avg(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then page_view_count end), 1) as avg_page_views_2025

order by sessions_2025 desc, channel asc
limit 12

question: How much discounting is happening platform-wide each month, and how often are coupon codes actually used?

WITH months AS (

  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE year_num = 2025
),
order_calc AS (
  SELECT
    to_char(o.placed_at, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    o.grand_total / CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS revenue_eur,
    o.discount_total / CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS discount_eur,
    CASE WHEN o.discount_total > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_discount
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = date(o.placed_at)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
order_agg AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
    SUM(has_discount) AS orders_with_discount_count,
    SUM(revenue_eur) AS total_order_revenue_eur,
    SUM(discount_eur) AS total_discount_amount_eur
  FROM order_calc
  GROUP BY month
),
coupon_agg AS (
  SELECT
    to_char(cr.redeemed_at, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cr.coupon_id) AS distinct_coupons_used
  FROM coupon_redemptions cr
  WHERE cr.redeemed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND cr.redeemed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
  m.month,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_with_discount_count, 0) AS orders_with_discount_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_with_discount_count, 0)::numeric * 100.0 / NULLIF(oa.orders_count,0), 1) AS discount_rate_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.total_order_revenue_eur,0)::numeric, 0) AS total_order_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.total_discount_amount_eur,0)::numeric, 0) AS total_discount_amount_eur,

  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.total_discount_amount_eur,0)::numeric / NULLIF(oa.orders_with_discount_count,0), 0) AS avg_discount_per_discounted_order_eur

question: Is the dominant 'direct/none' traffic channel spread evenly across merchants, or concentrated in a handful of them?
sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS tenant_name,
  COALESCE(t1.total_sessions_2025, 0) AS total_sessions_2025,
  COALESCE(t2.direct_sessions_2025, 0) AS direct_sessions_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.direct_sessions_2025, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COALESCE(t1.total_sessions_2025, 0), 0), 1) AS direct_share_of_tenant_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.direct_sessions_2025, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t3.platform_direct_sessions_2025, 0), 1) AS pct_of_platform_direct_sessions
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_sessions_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS direct_sessions_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND (utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(utm_source) = '')
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS platform_direct_sessions_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND (utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(utm_source) = '')
) t3
ORDER BY direct_sessions_2025 DESC, tenant_name ASC
LIMIT 15

builds_on: Website traffic channel mix, 2025 vs 2024
columns_requested: total_sessions_2025 - count of web_sessions for that tenant with started_at in 2025
direct_sessions_2025 - count of those sessions where utm_source is null/blank
direct_share_of_tenant_pct - direct_sessions_2025 / total_sessions_2025 * 100, rounded to 1 decimal
pct_of_platform_direct_sessions - direct_sessions_2025 / (sum of direct_sessions_2025 across all tenants) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal

question: The platform-wide discount rate jumped from a ~35% baseline to 53-59% in January and July 2025 with no increase in average discount size — was that driven by a handful of merchants running sitewide promotions in those two months?
sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS tenant_name,
  t0.industry AS industry,
  COALESCE(t1.orders_jan_jul, 0) AS orders_jan_jul_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t1.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t1.orders_jan_jul, 0), 1) AS discount_rate_jan_jul_pct,
  COALESCE(t2.orders_other, 0) AS orders_other_months_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t2.orders_other, 0), 1) AS discount_rate_other_months_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t1.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t1.orders_jan_jul, 0), 1)
    - ROUND(COALESCE(t2.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t2.orders_other, 0), 1) AS delta_pct_points
FROM tenants t0
JOIN (
  SELECT
    o1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_jan_jul,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o1.discount_total > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS discount_orders
  FROM orders o1
  WHERE o1.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o1.placed_at) = 2025
    AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o1.placed_at) IN (1, 7)
  GROUP BY o1.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o2.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_other,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o2.discount_total > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS discount_orders
  FROM orders o2
  WHERE o2.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o2.placed_at) = 2025
    AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o2.placed_at) NOT IN (1, 7)
  GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE t1.orders_jan_jul >= 20
ORDER BY delta_pct_points DESC, orders_jan_jul_2025 DESC
LIMIT 15

builds_on: Discounting baseline: monthly coupon usage and discount rate

discount_rate_jan_jul_pct - share of those orders with discount_total > 0, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
orders_other_months_2025 - count of that tenant's orders placed_at in the other 10 months of 2025
discount_rate_other_months_pct - share of those orders with discount_total > 0, *100, rounded to 1 decimal

question: Compared to full-price orders, do discounted orders in 2025 have a healthy order value, basket size, and return/cancellation rate, or do they look worse on the metrics that matter?
sql:
SELECT order_group, orders_count, avg_order_value_eur, avg_items_per_order, return_rate_pct, cancelled_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    case when o.discount_total > 0 then 'discounted' else 'full price' end as order_group,
    count(*) as orders_count,
    round(avg(o.grand_total / case when o.currency_code = 'EUR' then 1 else er.rate end)::numeric, 0) as avg_order_value_eur,
    round(avg(coalesce(oi.item_qty,0))::numeric, 1) as avg_items_per_order,
    round(100.0 * sum(case when ret.order_id is not null then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as return_rate_pct,
    round(100.0 * sum(case when o.status = 'cancelled' then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as cancelled_rate_pct
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er on er.base_code = 'EUR' and er.quote_code = o.currency_code and er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  LEFT JOIN (select order_id, sum(quantity) as item_qty from order_items group by order_id) oi on oi.order_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN (select distinct order_id from order_returns) ret on ret.order_id = o.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= date '2025-01-01' and o.placed_at < date '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY case when o.discount_total > 0 then 'discounted' else 'full price' end
) t
ORDER BY (case when order_group = 'discounted' then 0 else 1 end)

builds_on: Discounting baseline: monthly coupon usage and discount rate
columns_requested: orders_count - count of orders in that group, placed_at in 2025
avg_order_value_eur - average orders.grand_total converted to EUR, rounded to 0 decimals
avg_items_per_order - average of sum(order_items.quantity) per order for that group, rounded to 1 decimal
return_rate_pct - share of orders in that group with at least one linked order_returns row, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
cancelled_rate_pct - share of orders in that group with status = 'cancelled', *100, rounded to 1 decimal

Join order_items for item counts (sum quantity per order_id, then average across orders in the group). Join order_returns on order_id to flag any return. Convert grand_total to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=orders.currency_code, as_of=date of placed_at; EUR rate=1). Exactly 2 output rows, ordered 'discounted' then 'full price'.

question: How much campaign messaging goes out, and is anyone opening or clicking — is this a strength or a weak spot across the platform?
sql:
WITH messages AS (
  SELECT
    cm.sent_at,
    cm.delivered_at,
    cm.opened_at,
    cm.clicked_at,
    cm.bounced_at,
    cm.unsubscribed_at,
    c.channel
  FROM campaign_messages cm
  JOIN campaigns c ON c.id = cm.campaign_id
  WHERE cm.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND cm.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    channel,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL) AS messages_sent,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS delivered_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND opened_at IS NOT NULL) AS opened_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND clicked_at IS NOT NULL) AS clicked_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL AND bounced_at IS NOT NULL) AS bounced_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL AND unsubscribed_at IS NOT NULL) AS unsubscribed_count
  FROM messages
  GROUP BY channel
)
SELECT
  channel,
  messages_sent,
  ROUND(100.0 * delivered_count / NULLIF(messages_sent, 0), 1) AS delivered_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * opened_count / NULLIF(delivered_count, 0), 1) AS open_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * clicked_count / NULLIF(delivered_count, 0), 1) AS click_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * bounced_count / NULLIF(messages_sent, 0), 1) AS bounce_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * unsubscribed_count / NULLIF(messages_sent, 0), 1) AS unsubscribe_rate_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY messages_sent DESC, channel ASC

columns_requested: messages_sent - count of campaign_messages with sent_at not null, created_at in 2025
delivered_rate_pct - share of sent messages with delivered_at not null, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
open_rate_pct - share of delivered messages with opened_at not null, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
click_rate_pct - share of delivered messages with clicked_at not null, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
bounce_rate_pct - share of sent messages with bounced_at not null, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
unsubscribe_rate_pct - share of sent messages with unsubscribed_at not null, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
tags.details: Source: campaign_messages joined to campaigns on campaign_id for channel. Filter campaign_messages.created_at between 2025-01-01 and 2026-01-01 (platform-wide, no tenant filter). messages_sent = sent_at is not null; all rate denominators as specified (delivered/open/click relative to delivered count where noted, bounce/unsubscribe relative to sent count). question: Does the 'discounted orders have higher AOV, bigger baskets, and fewer returns' pattern hold in consumer verticals, or is it mainly an artifact of B2B wholesale contract pricing?
sql:
WITH order_items_agg AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS item_qty
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
),
order_returns_flag AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id FROM order_returns
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    t.industry AS industry,
    CASE WHEN o.discount_total > 0 THEN 'discounted' ELSE 'full price' END AS order_group,
    o.status AS status,
    o.grand_total AS grand_total,
    o.currency_code AS currency_code,
    o.placed_at AS placed_at,
    COALESCE(oi.item_qty, 0) AS item_qty,
    COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS eur_rate
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN order_items_agg oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  b.industry AS industry,
  b.order_group AS order_group,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(AVG(b.grand_total / b.eur_rate), 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(b.item_qty), 1) AS avg_items_per_order,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN rf.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS return_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS cancelled_rate_pct
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN order_returns_flag rf ON rf.order_id = b.order_id
GROUP BY b.industry, b.order_group
ORDER BY b.industry ASC, b.order_group ASC

return_rate_pct - share of orders in that cell with at least one linked order_returns row, *100, rounded to 1 decimal

question: Among shoppers who actually place orders, do loyalty-program members order more often or spend more per order than non-members?
sql:
SELECT segment, users_count, orders_count_2025, avg_orders_per_user, avg_order_value_eur, total_revenue_eur
FROM (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la
      WHERE la.user_id = o.user_id AND la.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    ) THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id) AS users_count,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count_2025,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id), 2) AS avg_orders_per_user,
    ROUND(AVG(o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END))::numeric, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
    ROUND(SUM(o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END))::numeric, 0) AS total_revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la
      WHERE la.user_id = o.user_id AND la.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    ) THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END
) seg
ORDER BY CASE WHEN segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

columns_requested: segment - 'loyalty member' (user_id appears in loyalty_accounts) or 'non-member'
users_count - count of distinct users in that segment who placed at least one order with placed_at in 2025
orders_count_2025 - count of those users' orders placed_at in 2025
avg_orders_per_user - orders_count_2025 / users_count, rounded to 2 decimals
avg_order_value_eur - average orders.grand_total converted to EUR across that segment's 2025 orders, rounded to 0 decimals
total_revenue_eur - sum of orders.grand_total converted to EUR for that segment's 2025 orders, rounded to 0 decimals
tags.details: Source: orders (placed_at in 2025, all tenants) left joined to loyalty_accounts on user_id (and tenant_id) to classify each ordering user as a member (has any loyalty_accounts row) or non-member. Restrict to users who placed at least one 2025 order so the comparison is among active shoppers, not all signups. Convert grand_total to EUR via exchange_rates as in prior money reports. Exactly 2 output rows, ordered 'loyalty member' then 'non-member'.
tags.grain: one row per shopper segment: 'loyalty member' vs 'non-member'

question: How many A/B tests has the platform run, in what state are they, and how often does a test actually end with a declared winner?
sql:
SELECT
  t.status,
  t.tests_count,
  ROUND(t.tests_count * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ab_tests), 1) AS share_of_tests_pct,
  t.tests_with_winner_declared_count,
  ROUND(t.avg_variants_per_test, 1) AS avg_variants_per_test,
  ROUND(t.avg_duration_days, 1) AS avg_duration_days
FROM (
  SELECT
    a.status,
    COUNT(*) AS tests_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.winner_variant_id IS NOT NULL) AS tests_with_winner_declared_count,
    AVG(vc.variant_count) AS avg_variants_per_test,
    AVG(CASE WHEN a.started_at IS NOT NULL AND a.ended_at IS NOT NULL
         THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (a.ended_at - a.started_at)) / 86400.0 END) AS avg_duration_days
  FROM ab_tests a
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT ab_test_id, COUNT(*) AS variant_count
    FROM ab_variants
    GROUP BY ab_test_id
  ) vc ON vc.ab_test_id = a.id
  GROUP BY a.status
) t
ORDER BY t.tests_count DESC, t.status ASC

columns_requested: status - ab_tests.status (draft, running, paused, completed, archived)
tests_count - count of ab_tests in that status, all tenants, all-time
share_of_tests_pct - tests_count / total tests across all statuses * 100, rounded to 1 decimal
tests_with_winner_declared_count - count of tests in that status where winner_variant_id is not null
avg_variants_per_test - average number of linked ab_variants rows per test in that status, rounded to 1 decimal
avg_duration_days - average of (ended_at - started_at) in days for tests in that status where both are not null, rounded to 1 decimal
tags.details: Source: ab_tests left joined to ab_variants (count per ab_test_id) for the variants average; no date filter, all-time, all tenants, since this is a first look at whether the capability is used at all. Order by tests_count descending, tie-break status ascending.
tags.grain: one row per ab_tests.status value

question: Among shoppers who place orders, do people who were referred in, or who refer others, show different order frequency or spend than everyone else?
sql:
WITH classified AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.grand_total, o.currency_code, o.placed_at,
    CASE WHEN rr.referred_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'referred'
         WHEN rf.referrer_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'referrer'
         ELSE 'neither' END AS segment
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, referred_user_id FROM referral_redemptions) rr
    ON rr.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND rr.referred_user_id = o.user_id
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, referrer_user_id FROM referrals) rf
    ON rf.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND rf.referrer_user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
converted AS (
  SELECT c.*,
    CASE WHEN c.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN c.grand_total
         ELSE c.grand_total / er.rate END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM classified c
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = c.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(c.placed_at AS date)
)
SELECT segment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id || ':' || user_id) AS users_count,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_count_2025,
  ROUND(COUNT(*)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id || ':' || user_id),0), 2) AS avg_orders_per_user,
  ROUND(AVG(grand_total_eur)::numeric, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(grand_total_eur)::numeric, 0) AS total_revenue_eur
FROM converted
GROUP BY segment
ORDER BY CASE segment WHEN 'referred' THEN 1 WHEN 'referrer' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

columns_requested: segment - 'referred' (user_id appears in referral_redemptions.referred_user_id), else 'referrer' (user_id appears in referrals.referrer_user_id), else 'neither'
users_count - count of distinct users in that segment who placed at least one order with placed_at in 2025
orders_count_2025 - count of those users' orders placed_at in 2025
avg_orders_per_user - orders_count_2025 / users_count, rounded to 2 decimals
avg_order_value_eur - average grand_total (EUR) across that segment's 2025 orders, rounded to 0 decimals
total_revenue_eur - sum of grand_total (EUR) for that segment's 2025 orders, rounded to 0 decimals
tags.details: Source: orders (placed_at in 2025, all tenants), classify each ordering user by checking membership in referral_redemptions.referred_user_id first, then referrals.referrer_user_id, else 'neither' (mutually exclusive, in that priority order, to handle users who are both). Convert grand_total to EUR the same way as prior money reports. Exactly 3 output rows, ordered 'referred', 'referrer', 'neither'.
tags.grain: one row per shopper segment: 'referred', 'referrer', or 'neither'

question: Within the same industry, do loyalty-program members actually order more or spend more than non-members, or does the platform-wide 'members look worse' result just reflect which verticals have more loyalty members enrolled?
sql:
SELECT t.industry AS industry,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN o.user_id END) AS members_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL THEN o.user_id END) AS nonmembers_count,
  ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN o.id END)::numeric
        / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN o.user_id END), 0), 2) AS avg_orders_per_member,
  ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL THEN o.id END)::numeric
        / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL THEN o.user_id END), 0), 2) AS avg_orders_per_nonmember,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL
                 THEN o.grand_total / (CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END)
            END), 0) AS avg_order_value_member_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL
                 THEN o.grand_total / (CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END)
            END), 0) AS avg_order_value_nonmember_eur
FROM orders o
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) dla
  ON dla.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND dla.user_id = o.user_id
LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  AND t.industry IN (
    SELECT DISTINCT t2.industry
    FROM tenants t2
    JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.tenant_id = t2.id
    WHERE lp.is_active = true
  )
GROUP BY t.industry
ORDER BY t.industry

builds_on: Do loyalty program members behave differently from other shoppers?

question: How big is each merchant's business on Tidewick, and is it growing, flat, or shrinking over the last quarter?
sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS merchant_name,
  t0.industry AS industry,
  t0.employee_count AS employee_count,
  COALESCE(t1.orders_last90, 0) AS orders_last_90_days,
  COALESCE(t1.revenue_last90_eur, 0) AS gross_revenue_eur_last_90_days,
  COALESCE(t2.orders_prior90, 0) AS orders_prior_90_days,
  COALESCE(t2.revenue_prior90_eur, 0) AS gross_revenue_eur_prior_90_days,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.revenue_prior90_eur,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t1.revenue_last90_eur,0) - t2.revenue_prior90_eur) / t2.revenue_prior90_eur) * 100, 1)
  END AS revenue_growth_pct,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.orders_prior90,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t1.orders_last90,0) - t2.orders_prior90) / CAST(t2.orders_prior90 AS decimal)) * 100, 1)
  END AS order_growth_pct
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS orders_last90,
         SUM(o1.grand_total / er1.rate) AS revenue_last90_eur
  FROM orders o1
  JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = o1.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = CAST(o1.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o1.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o1.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-03 00:00:00'
    AND o1.placed_at <  TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY o1.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o2.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS orders_prior90,
         SUM(o2.grand_total / er2.rate) AS revenue_prior90_eur
  FROM orders o2
  JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = o2.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = CAST(o2.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o2.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o2.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-07-05 00:00:00'
    AND o2.placed_at <  TIMESTAMP '2025-10-03 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
ORDER BY gross_revenue_eur_last_90_days DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50

tags.details: Tables: orders, tenants, exchange_rates. Last 90 days is placed_at from 2025-10-03 through 2025-12-31. Prior 90 days is placed_at from 2025-07-05 through 2025-10-02. Exclude cancelled orders. Order by last 90 day revenue descending, tie-break tenant_id ascending. Cap 50 rows.

question: For each merchant, how much of their customer base is repeat buyers versus one-and-done, over the last 12 months?
sql:
SELECT
  t0.id AS tenant_id,
  t0.name AS merchant_name,
  t0.industry AS industry,
  t1.distinct_customers AS distinct_customers,
  COALESCE(t2.repeat_customers, 0) AS repeat_customers,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.repeat_customers, 0) * 100.0 / t1.distinct_customers, 1) AS repeat_purchase_rate_pct,
  COALESCE(t3.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders_last_12_months,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t3.total_orders, 0) * 1.0 / t1.distinct_customers, 2) AS avg_orders_per_customer
FROM tenants t0
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id) AS distinct_customers
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT x.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS repeat_customers
  FROM (
    SELECT o.tenant_id, o.user_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    GROUP BY o.tenant_id, o.user_id
  ) x
  WHERE x.order_count >= 2
  GROUP BY x.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
ORDER BY distinct_customers DESC, repeat_purchase_rate_pct DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50

columns_requested: distinct customers with at least one order in last 12 months
repeat customers with at least two orders in last 12 months
average orders per customer last 12 months

Order by distinct customers descending, tie-break repeat purchase rate descending, then tenant_id. Cap 50 rows.

question: For the biggest merchants, is Oct-Dec revenue really growing year over year, or is the recent growth just holiday seasonality?
sql:
SELECT t0.id AS tenant_id, t0.name AS merchant_name, t0.industry,
  COALESCE(t1.revenue_eur_a, 0) AS revenue_eur_2025,
  COALESCE(t2.revenue_eur_b, 0) AS revenue_eur_2024,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.revenue_eur_b, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t1.revenue_eur_a, 0) - t2.revenue_eur_b) / t2.revenue_eur_b) * 100, 1)
  END AS revenue_yoy_growth_pct,
  COALESCE(t3.orders_a, 0) AS orders_2025,
  COALESCE(t4.orders_b, 0) AS orders_2024,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t4.orders_b, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t3.orders_a, 0) - t4.orders_b)::numeric / t4.orders_b) * 100, 1)
  END AS order_yoy_growth_pct
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur_a
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur_b
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2024-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_a
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_b
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2024-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t4 ON t4.tenant_id = t0.id
ORDER BY COALESCE(t1.revenue_eur_a, 0) DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50

question: Which merchants show warning signs right now: rising refunds or cancellations, unpaid invoices, or falling shopper activity?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  round(coalesce(rr.refund_rate_last, 0) * 100, 2) AS refund_rate_last_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(rr.refund_rate_prior, 0) * 100, 2) AS refund_rate_prior_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(cr.cancel_rate_last, 0) * 100, 2) AS cancellation_rate_last_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(cr.cancel_rate_prior, 0) * 100, 2) AS cancellation_rate_prior_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(ov.overdue_eur, 0), 2) AS overdue_invoice_amount_eur,
  coalesce(ws.sessions_last, 0) AS web_sessions_last_90d,
  coalesce(ws.sessions_prior, 0) AS web_sessions_prior_90d,
  round(
    CASE WHEN coalesce(ws.sessions_prior, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE (ws.sessions_last - ws.sessions_prior) * 100.0 / ws.sessions_prior
    END, 2
  ) AS session_growth_pct
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ra.tenant_id,
         ra.refund_last_eur / NULLIF(ca.captured_last_eur, 0) AS refund_rate_last,
         ra.refund_prior_eur / NULLIF(ca.captured_prior_eur, 0) AS refund_rate_prior
  FROM (
    SELECT tenant_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN processed_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS refund_last_eur,
           SUM(CASE WHEN processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND processed_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS refund_prior_eur
    FROM (
      SELECT pr.tenant_id, pr.processed_at,
             pr.amount / COALESCE(er.rate, 1) AS amount_eur
      FROM payment_refunds pr
      LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
      WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
        AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) ra_inner
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ) ra
  JOIN (
    SELECT tenant_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN captured_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS captured_last_eur,
           SUM(CASE WHEN captured_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND captured_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS captured_prior_eur
    FROM (
      SELECT p.tenant_id, p.captured_at,
             p.amount / COALESCE(er.rate, 1) AS amount_eur
      FROM payments p
      LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
      WHERE p.status = 'captured'
        AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) ca_inner
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ) ca ON ca.tenant_id = ra.tenant_id
) rr ON rr.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01' AND status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::decimal
           / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS cancel_rate_last,
         SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND placed_at < DATE '2025-10-03' AND status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::decimal
           / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND placed_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS cancel_rate_prior
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) cr ON cr.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT i.tenant_id,
         SUM(i.amount_due / COALESCE(er.rate, 1)) AS overdue_eur
  FROM invoices i
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = (
        SELECT MAX(er2.as_of) FROM exchange_rates er2
        WHERE er2.base_code = 'EUR' AND er2.quote_code = i.currency_code AND er2.as_of <= DATE '2026-01-05'
      )
  WHERE i.status = 'past_due' OR (i.status = 'open' AND i.due_at < DATE '2026-01-05')
  GROUP BY i.tenant_id
) ov ON ov.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN started_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sessions_last,
         SUM(CASE WHEN started_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND started_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sessions_prior
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) ws ON ws.tenant_id = t.id
ORDER BY overdue_invoice_amount_eur DESC, refund_rate_last_90d_pct DESC, t.id
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Merchant size and recent growth trend
tags.details: Tables payment_refunds joined to payments for refund rate, equal to refund EUR divided by captured payment EUR per period. Orders for cancellation rate, equal to cancelled orders divided by all orders placed per period. Invoices for overdue amount, equal to amount_due in EUR where status is past_due, or status is open with due date already passed as of 2026-01-05. Web_sessions for session counts per period. Convert money via exchange_rates. Periods: last 90 days is Oct 3 to Dec 31 2025; prior 90 days is Jul 5 to Oct 2 2025. Order by overdue invoice amount EUR descending, tie-break refund rate last 90 days descending, then tenant_id. Cap 50 rows.
tags.grain: one row per merchant (tenant)

question: Is our audit trail continuous over time with no unexplained gaps, and are logged actions reliably tied to an identifiable actor rather than null/system placeholders?
sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
),
live AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         count(*) AS live_events,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL) AS live_null_actor,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_type IN ('system','api_key','service_account')) AS live_system_api
  FROM audit_log
  GROUP BY 1
),
archive AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         count(*) AS archived_events,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL) AS archived_null_actor,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_type IN ('system','api_key','service_account')) AS archived_system_api
  FROM audit_log_archive
  GROUP BY 1
),
actor_types AS (
  SELECT month_start, actor_type
  FROM (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start, actor_type FROM audit_log
    UNION ALL
    SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start, actor_type FROM audit_log_archive
  ) t
  GROUP BY month_start, actor_type
),
distinct_actor_types AS (
  SELECT month_start, count(*) AS distinct_actor_type_values
  FROM actor_types
  GROUP BY month_start
),
access AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start, count(*) AS access_events
  FROM access_log
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  coalesce(l.live_events,0) AS audit_log_live_events,
  coalesce(a.archived_events,0) AS audit_log_archived_events,
  coalesce(l.live_events,0) + coalesce(a.archived_events,0) AS total_audit_events,
  round(
    CASE WHEN (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (coalesce(l.live_null_actor,0)+coalesce(a.archived_null_actor,0))::numeric / (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0))
    END, 4) AS pct_actor_user_id_null,
  coalesce(dat.distinct_actor_type_values,0) AS distinct_actor_type_values,
  round(
    CASE WHEN (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (coalesce(l.live_system_api,0)+coalesce(a.archived_system_api,0))::numeric / (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0))
    END, 4) AS pct_actor_type_system_or_api,
  coalesce(acc.access_events,0) AS access_log_events
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN live l ON l.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN archive a ON a.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN distinct_actor_types dat ON dat.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN access acc ON acc.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start

columns_requested: audit_log_live_events (count from audit_log with occurred_at in month)
audit_log_archived_events (count from audit_log_archive with occurred_at in month)
pct_actor_user_id_null (share of combined rows where actor_user_id is null)
distinct_actor_type_values (count distinct actor_type across combined rows in month)
pct_actor_type_system_or_api (share where actor_type in ('system','api_key','service_account') rather than 'user')
access_log_events (count from access_log with occurred_at in month, as a separate sensitive-data-read signal)
tags.details: Sources: audit_log, audit_log_archive (same shape, union on occurred_at month), access_log (separate, not unioned — just a parallel count). Purpose is purely diagnostic: look for months with suspiciously low total_audit_events (possible logging gaps) and for high/rising pct_actor_user_id_null or pct_actor_type_system_or_api (possible actor-identity weakness, relevant before we cite audit evidence in the questionnaire). Order by month ascending.
tags.grain: one row per calendar month (based on occurred_at), combining live audit_log and audit_log_archive, from 2023-01 through 2025-12

question: Among internal staff users, how much elevated/role-based access exists today, and do deactivated or suspended staff still retain active role grants rather than having access revoked promptly?
sql:
WITH staff AS (
  SELECT id, status, last_login_at
  FROM users
  WHERE is_staff = true AND deleted_at IS NULL
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    s.id AS user_id,
    s.status,
    s.last_login_at,
    ur.id AS user_role_id,
    ur.created_at AS role_granted_at,
    r.is_system
  FROM staff s
  LEFT JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.user_id = s.id
  LEFT JOIN roles r ON r.id = ur.role_id
)
SELECT
  status,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS staff_user_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE user_role_id IS NOT NULL) AS users_with_any_role,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE user_role_id IS NOT NULL)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id),0), 4) AS pct_with_any_role,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE is_system = true) AS users_with_system_role,
  ROUND(COUNT(user_role_id)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id),0), 2) AS avg_roles_per_user,
  ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(role_granted_at AS date))) FILTER (WHERE user_role_id IS NOT NULL), 1) AS median_days_since_role_granted,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE last_login_at IS NULL)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id),0), 4) AS pct_never_logged_in,
  ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(last_login_at AS date))) FILTER (WHERE last_login_at IS NOT NULL), 1) AS median_days_since_last_login
FROM joined
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'active' THEN 1 WHEN 'invited' THEN 2 WHEN 'suspended' THEN 3 WHEN 'deactivated' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END, status

columns_requested: staff_user_count (count of is_staff=true users with this status, excluding deleted_at not null)
users_with_any_role (distinct users with >=1 row in user_roles)
users_with_system_role (distinct users holding a role where roles.is_system = true)
median_days_since_role_granted (median of 2025-12-31 minus user_roles.created_at, in days, over all grants for these users)
median_days_since_last_login (median of 2025-12-31 minus last_login_at, over users with a non-null last_login_at)
tags.details: Source: users joined to user_roles and roles (for is_system). This is a snapshot of current assignments (user_roles has no revocation/end timestamp in the schema), so please note that limitation on the report — it tells us what access exists today, not how quickly past revocations happened. Flag clearly if 'suspended' or 'deactivated' rows show non-trivial users_with_any_role or users_with_system_role counts, since that's the key signal of stale access. Order rows: active, invited, suspended, deactivated.
tags.grain: one row per users.status value (active, invited, suspended, deactivated), restricted to users.is_staff = true, across all tenants, as a current-state snapshot as of 2025-12-31

question: How many data subject requests do we receive each month, how quickly are they resolved relative to their due date, and how many are currently open — on time or overdue?
sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t0.month_start, t0.month_label
  FROM calendar_days t0
  WHERE t0.month_start BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-01'
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(r.requests_received,0) AS requests_received,
  COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0) AS completed_on_time,
  COALESCE(lt.completed_late,0) AS completed_late,
  COALESCE(nd.still_open_not_due,0) AS still_open_not_due,
  COALESCE(od.still_open_overdue,0) AS still_open_overdue,
  ROUND(avgc.avg_days_to_complete,1) AS avg_days_to_complete,
  ROUND(medc.median_days_to_complete,1) AS median_days_to_complete,
  ROUND( CASE WHEN (COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0)+COALESCE(lt.completed_late,0))=0 THEN NULL
    ELSE 100.0*COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0)/(COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0)+COALESCE(lt.completed_late,0))
  END, 1) AS pct_on_time
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t1.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS requests_received
  FROM data_subject_requests t1
  GROUP BY 1
) r ON r.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t2.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS completed_on_time
  FROM data_subject_requests t2
  WHERE t2.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND t2.completed_at <= t2.due_at
  GROUP BY 1
) ot ON ot.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t3.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS completed_late
  FROM data_subject_requests t3
  WHERE t3.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND (t3.completed_at > t3.due_at OR t3.due_at IS NULL)
  GROUP BY 1
) lt ON lt.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t4.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS still_open_not_due
  FROM data_subject_requests t4
  WHERE t4.completed_at IS NULL AND (t4.due_at IS NULL OR t4.due_at >= DATE '2025-12-31')
  GROUP BY 1
) nd ON nd.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t5.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS still_open_overdue
  FROM data_subject_requests t5
  WHERE t5.completed_at IS NULL AND t5.due_at < DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY 1
) od ON od.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t6.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t6.completed_at - t6.received_at))/86400.0) AS avg_days_to_complete
  FROM data_subject_requests t6
  WHERE t6.completed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
) avgc ON avgc.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT month_start, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days) AS median_days_to_complete
  FROM (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t7.received_at)::date AS month_start,
      EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t7.completed_at - t7.received_at))/86400.0 AS days
    FROM data_subject_requests t7
    WHERE t7.completed_at IS NOT NULL
  ) sub
  GROUP BY month_start
) medc ON medc.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start

columns_requested: completed_on_time (count with completed_at not null and completed_at <= due_at)
completed_late (count with completed_at not null and completed_at > due_at, or due_at is null)
still_open_not_due (not yet completed, due_at is null or due_at >= 2025-12-31)
avg_days_to_complete (avg of completed_at - received_at in days, completed requests only)
tags.details: Source: data_subject_requests. Use 2025-12-31 as the fixed 'as of' reference date for open/overdue logic (do not use CURRENT_DATE). The catalog doesn't enumerate this table's status codes — please inspect distinct status values and treat whichever represent a finished/closed request (e.g. completed_at populated) as 'completed'; note in the report which status strings/logic you used. All tenants combined (this is a platform-wide compliance metric, not per-merchant). Order by month ascending. If total rows exceed 50 they won't here (36 months expected).
tags.grain: one row per calendar month, based on the month of data_subject_requests.received_at, across all tenants combined, from 2023-01 through 2025-12

question: Do the data subject requests that look 'open and overdue' by timestamp actually carry an open status, or is that an artifact of missing completed_at values on closed requests — and is the due_at SLA window itself consistent?
sql:
SELECT
  status,
  request_type,
  COUNT(*) AS count_requests,
  COUNT(completed_at) AS count_with_completed_at,
  COUNT(*) - COUNT(completed_at) AS count_without_completed_at,
  SUM(CASE WHEN completed_at IS NULL AND due_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_overdue_open,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN due_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_due_at_null,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN due_at IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (due_at - received_at)) / 86400.0 END), 1) AS avg_sla_window_days,
  MIN(CASE WHEN completed_at IS NULL THEN received_at END) AS oldest_open_received_at
FROM data_subject_requests
WHERE received_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND received_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY status, request_type
ORDER BY status, request_type

builds_on: DSAR volume and timeliness by month
columns_requested: pct_due_at_null (share of this group where due_at is null)
avg_sla_window_days (avg of due_at - received_at in days, where due_at not null)
oldest_open_received_at (earliest received_at among rows with completed_at null, else blank)
tags.details: Source: data_subject_requests. This directly tests last night's finding that several months showed requests still open/overdue years later — need to see whether those rows' status column says something like 'completed'/'closed'/'rejected' (i.e. a timestamp-population gap) versus a genuinely open status like 'in_progress'/'received'. Also check whether due_at - received_at is a consistent SLA window per request_type (e.g. always ~30 days) as a timestamp-trust check, or whether due_at is frequently null/inconsistent. All tenants combined. Order by status, then request_type.
tags.grain: one row per combination of data_subject_requests.status and request_type, across all tenants, all received_at dates from 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31

question: Which permission categories represent real elevated/admin-type access, how many staff users hold each, and do any non-active (invited/suspended/deactivated) staff still hold them?
sql:
WITH staff_totals AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS total_staff
  FROM users
  WHERE is_staff = true AND deleted_at IS NULL
),
cat_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.category, u.id AS user_id, u.status
  FROM permissions p
  JOIN role_permissions rp ON rp.permission_id = p.id
  JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.role_id = rp.role_id
  JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = true AND u.deleted_at IS NULL
),
cat_perm_counts AS (
  SELECT category, count(DISTINCT code) AS distinct_permission_codes
  FROM permissions
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT
  cu.category,
  count(*) AS staff_users_with_category,
  round(100.0 * count(*) / st.total_staff, 2) AS pct_of_all_staff,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE cu.status = 'active') AS active_count,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE cu.status IN ('invited','suspended','deactivated')) AS non_active_count,
  cpc.distinct_permission_codes
FROM cat_users cu
CROSS JOIN staff_totals st
JOIN cat_perm_counts cpc ON cpc.category = cu.category
GROUP BY cu.category, st.total_staff, cpc.distinct_permission_codes
ORDER BY staff_users_with_category DESC, cu.category

builds_on: Staff access currency by account status
columns_requested: staff_users_with_category (distinct is_staff=true users holding >=1 role granting a permission in this category, via user_roles -> role_permissions -> permissions)
pct_of_all_staff (that count divided by total is_staff=true, non-deleted user count)
distinct_permission_codes (count of distinct permissions.code in this category, for context)
tags.details: Sources: permissions (category, code), role_permissions, user_roles, users (is_staff=true, exclude deleted_at not null). This replaces last night's is_system proxy, which turned out not to distinguish privilege level (100% of staff held an is_system role). The goal is to find which categories look sensitive (e.g. billing, security, admin, user-management) and whether non_active_count is non-trivial for those — that would be the stale-access signal Aylin is asking about. Order by staff_users_with_category descending.
tags.grain: one row per permissions.category value, computed over users where is_staff = true across all tenants, as a current-state snapshot as of 2025-12-31

question: Is staff access actively granted and revoked over time (evidence of ongoing access management), and can we attribute those changes to an identifiable actor?
reasons: does not compile: Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name to_char does not exist!
sql:
WITH combined_log AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, action, actor_user_id, entity_table, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log
  UNION ALL
  SELECT tenant_id, action, actor_user_id, entity_table, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log_archive
),
role_changes AS (
  SELECT
    occurred_at,
    action,
    actor_user_id
  FROM combined_log
  WHERE entity_table = 'user_roles'
    AND action IN ('create', 'delete')
    AND occurred_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
monthly_changes AS (
  SELECT
    to_char(occurred_at, 'YYYY-MM') AS month_label,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'create') AS role_grants_created,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'delete') AS role_grants_removed,
    count(DISTINCT actor_user_id) AS distinct_actor_user_id,
    count(*) AS total_changes,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL) AS null_actor_changes
  FROM role_changes
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  months.month_label AS month,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_created, 0) AS role_grants_created,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_removed, 0) AS role_grants_removed,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_created, 0) - coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_removed, 0) AS net_change,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.distinct_actor_user_id, 0) AS distinct_actor_user_id,
  CASE WHEN coalesce(monthly_changes.total_changes,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE round(100.0 * monthly_changes.null_actor_changes / monthly_changes.total_changes, 1)
  END AS pct_actor_user_id_null
FROM months
LEFT JOIN monthly_changes ON months.month_label = monthly_changes.month_label
ORDER BY months.month_label

question: What share of staff and customer accounts are protected by a confirmed MFA device, and does that differ by account status?
sql:
WITH user_mfa AS (
  SELECT user_id, tenant_id,
         max(case when confirmed_at is not null then 1 else 0 end) as has_confirmed,
         1 as has_any
  FROM mfa_devices
  GROUP BY user_id, tenant_id
)
SELECT
  u.is_staff,
  u.status,
  count(*) as total_users,
  sum(case when um.has_confirmed = 1 then 1 else 0 end) as users_with_confirmed_mfa,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when um.has_confirmed = 1 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_with_confirmed_mfa,
  sum(case when um.has_any = 1 then 1 else 0 end) as users_with_any_mfa_device,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when um.has_any = 1 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_with_any_mfa_device
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN user_mfa um ON um.user_id = u.id AND um.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
WHERE u.deleted_at is null
GROUP BY u.is_staff, u.status
ORDER BY u.is_staff desc, u.status

question: Which identity/access-control tables and actions actually appear in the audit trail, and under what naming — specifically, are role/permission grant and revocation events logged at all?
sql:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT entity_table, action, entity_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log
  WHERE occurred_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT entity_table, action, entity_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log_archive
  WHERE occurred_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  entity_table,
  action,
  COUNT(*) AS row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT entity_id) AS distinct_entity_id_count,
  MIN(occurred_at) AS min_occurred_at,
  MAX(occurred_at) AS max_occurred_at
FROM combined
WHERE entity_table IN (
  'users','user',
  'roles','role',
  'user_roles','user_role',
  'role_permissions','role_permission',
  'permissions','permission',
  'teams','team',
  'team_members','team_member',
  'api_keys','api_key',
  'invitations','invitation',
  'mfa_devices','mfa_device',
  'sessions','session',
  'service_accounts','service_account',
  'personal_access_tokens','personal_access_token'
)
GROUP BY entity_table, action
ORDER BY entity_table, action

question: For the data subject requests that were rejected without a completed_at timestamp, can the audit/change-history trail tell us when the rejection decision was actually made, and was it within the due date?
sql:
WITH rejected_dsr AS (
  SELECT id, request_type, received_at, due_at
  FROM data_subject_requests
  WHERE status = 'rejected' AND completed_at IS NULL
),
ch AS (
  SELECT entity_id, MIN(occurred_at) AS occurred_at
  FROM change_history
  WHERE entity_table = 'data_subject_requests'
    AND entity_id IN (SELECT id FROM rejected_dsr)
    AND after_data->>'status' = 'rejected'
  GROUP BY entity_id
),
al AS (
  SELECT entity_id, MAX(occurred_at) AS occurred_at
  FROM audit_log
  WHERE entity_table = 'data_subject_requests'
    AND entity_id IN (SELECT id FROM rejected_dsr)
    AND action = 'update'
    AND (summary ILIKE '%reject%' OR metadata::text ILIKE '%reject%')
  GROUP BY entity_id
)
SELECT
  r.request_type,
  r.received_at,
  r.due_at,
  COALESCE(ch.occurred_at, al.occurred_at) AS rejection_event_timestamp,
  ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(ch.occurred_at, al.occurred_at) - r.received_at)) / 86400.0, 1) AS days_received_to_rejection_event,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(ch.occurred_at, al.occurred_at) IS NOT NULL AND r.due_at IS NOT NULL
       THEN COALESCE(ch.occurred_at, al.occurred_at) <= r.due_at
  END AS within_due_at,
  CASE WHEN ch.occurred_at IS NOT NULL THEN 'change_history'
       WHEN al.occurred_at IS NOT NULL THEN 'audit_log'
       ELSE 'neither found'
  END AS rejection_source
FROM rejected_dsr r
LEFT JOIN ch ON ch.entity_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN al ON al.entity_id = r.id
ORDER BY r.received_at ASC, r.id ASC

question: For the data subject requests that were rejected without a completed_at timestamp, can the audit/change-history trail tell us when the rejection decision was actually made, and was it within the due date?
sql:
WITH rejected AS (
  SELECT id, request_type, received_at, due_at
  FROM data_subject_requests
  WHERE status = 'rejected' AND completed_at IS NULL
),
ch AS (
  SELECT r.id AS request_id, MIN(c.occurred_at) AS ch_ts
  FROM rejected r
  JOIN change_history c
    ON c.entity_table = 'data_subject_requests'
    AND c.entity_id = r.id
    AND c.after_data ->> 'status' = 'rejected'
  GROUP BY r.id
),
al AS (
  SELECT r.id AS request_id, MAX(a.occurred_at) AS al_ts
  FROM rejected r
  JOIN audit_log a
    ON a.entity_table = 'data_subject_requests'
    AND a.entity_id = r.id
    AND a.action = 'update'
  GROUP BY r.id
)
SELECT
  r.request_type,
  r.received_at,
  r.due_at,
  COALESCE(ch.ch_ts, al.al_ts) AS rejection_event_timestamp,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(ch.ch_ts, al.al_ts) IS NOT NULL
       THEN DATE_PART('day', COALESCE(ch.ch_ts, al.al_ts) - r.received_at)
  END AS days_received_to_rejection_event,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(ch.ch_ts, al.al_ts) IS NOT NULL
       THEN COALESCE(ch.ch_ts, al.al_ts) <= r.due_at
  END AS within_due_at,
  CASE WHEN ch.ch_ts IS NOT NULL THEN 'change_history'
       WHEN al.al_ts IS NOT NULL THEN 'audit_log'
       ELSE 'neither_found' END AS source
FROM rejected r
LEFT JOIN ch ON ch.request_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN al ON al.request_id = r.id
ORDER BY r.received_at ASC, r.id ASC

question: How much login activity fails, is there visible evidence of brute-force-style patterns, and are access-denied events actually being captured as suspicious activity over time?
sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
),
login_month AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         email,
         succeeded
  FROM login_attempts
),
login_agg AS (
  SELECT month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS total_login_attempts,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE succeeded = false) AS failed_login_attempts
  FROM login_month
  GROUP BY month_start
),
brute_force AS (
  SELECT month_start, COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS emails_with_5plus_failed
  FROM (
    SELECT month_start, email, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM login_month
    WHERE succeeded = false AND email IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY month_start, email
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
  ) t
  GROUP BY month_start
),
audit_combined AS (
  SELECT occurred_at, action FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'access_denied'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT occurred_at, action FROM audit_log_archive WHERE action = 'access_denied'
),
audit_agg AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS audit_access_denied_events
  FROM audit_combined
  GROUP BY month_start
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(la.total_login_attempts, 0) AS total_login_attempts,
  COALESCE(la.failed_login_attempts, 0) AS failed_login_attempts,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN COALESCE(la.total_login_attempts,0) = 0 THEN 0
       ELSE 100.0 * la.failed_login_attempts / la.total_login_attempts END, 2) AS pct_failed,
  COALESCE(bf.emails_with_5plus_failed, 0) AS emails_with_5plus_failed_in_month,
  COALESCE(aa.audit_access_denied_events, 0) AS audit_access_denied_events
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN login_agg la ON la.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN brute_force bf ON bf.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN audit_agg aa ON aa.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start

question: Where do shoppers drop off between landing on the storefront and placing a paid order, and does the shape differ across our biggest merchants?
sql:
WITH paid_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS paid_order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND status NOT IN ('pending', 'cancelled')
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
top_tenants AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, paid_order_count
  FROM paid_orders
  ORDER BY paid_order_count DESC, tenant_id ASC
  LIMIT 10
),
visits AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS visit_count
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
carts_created AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS cart_count
  FROM carts
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
orders_placed AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
assembled AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS tenant_id,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    COALESCE(v.visit_count, 0) AS visits,
    COALESCE(c.cart_count, 0) AS carts_created,
    COALESCE(o.order_count, 0) AS orders_placed,
    tt.paid_order_count AS orders_paid
  FROM top_tenants tt
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tt.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN visits v ON v.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN carts_created c ON c.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN orders_placed o ON o.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  visits,
  carts_created,
  orders_placed,
  orders_paid,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN visits > 0 THEN 100.0 * carts_created / visits ELSE NULL END, 1) AS visit_to_cart_pct,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN carts_created > 0 THEN 100.0 * orders_placed / carts_created ELSE NULL END, 1) AS cart_to_order_pct,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN orders_placed > 0 THEN 100.0 * orders_paid / orders_placed ELSE NULL END, 1) AS order_to_paid_pct,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN visits > 0 THEN 100.0 * orders_paid / visits ELSE NULL END, 1) AS overall_visit_to_paid_pct
FROM assembled
ORDER BY overall_visit_to_paid_pct DESC NULLS LAST, tenant_name ASC

columns_requested: orders paid in period (status not in pending, cancelled)
