question: Of shoppers who place a first order, how many come back and how long does it take?
reasons: does not compile: Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name to_char does not exist!
sql:
WITH paid_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, id, placed_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id, user_id ORDER BY placed_at, id) AS rn
  FROM orders
  WHERE status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled')
    AND placed_at IS NOT NULL
),
first_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, placed_at AS first_placed_at
  FROM paid_orders WHERE rn = 1
),
second_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, placed_at AS second_placed_at
  FROM paid_orders WHERE rn = 2
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    f.tenant_id,
    f.user_id,
    f.first_placed_at,
    s.second_placed_at,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', f.first_placed_at)::date AS cohort_month,
    CASE WHEN s.second_placed_at IS NOT NULL
         THEN (s.second_placed_at::date - f.first_placed_at::date)
    END AS days_to_second
  FROM first_orders f
  LEFT JOIN second_orders s
    ON f.tenant_id = s.tenant_id AND f.user_id = s.user_id
)
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(cohort_month, 'YYYY-MM') AS cohort_month,
  COUNT(*) AS first_time_buyers,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_second <= 30) / COUNT(*), 1) AS repeat_within_30_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_second <= 60) / COUNT(*), 1) AS repeat_within_60_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_second <= 90) / COUNT(*), 1) AS repeat_within_90_pct,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE second_placed_at IS NOT NULL) AS repeat_buyers,
  CAST(ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_second)) AS integer) AS median_days_to_second_order
FROM joined
WHERE cohort_month >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND cohort_month <= DATE '2025-10-01'
GROUP BY cohort_month
ORDER BY cohort_month

columns_requested: median days to second order (repeat buyers only)
tags.details: Table: orders (user_id, tenant_id, placed_at, status). Define a 'paid order' as status not in ('pending','cancelled'). For each user, their first-order date is the min placed_at among their paid orders; the cohort month is that date's calendar month. A user's second order is their next paid order (by placed_at) after the first. Compute, per cohort month: count of first-time buyers; the % of those whose second order occurred within 30/60/90 days of their first; the count who ever placed a second order; and the median (days between first and second order) among those who did. Restrict to cohort months from 2023-01 through 2025-10 inclusive, so every cohort has at least a 90-day observation window against data complete through 2025-12-31. Round percentages to 1 decimal and the median to a whole number of days. Order by cohort month ascending.
tags.grain: one row per first-order cohort month (calendar month of each user's first paid order)

question: Once a cart is created, is the drop-off to a paid order a single cliff or a slow bleed across stages, and does it differ by device or by how the shopper arrived?
sql:
SELECT 
  device_type,
  channel,
  COUNT(*) AS carts_started,
  SUM(CASE WHEN subtotal > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS carts_with_items,
  SUM(CASE WHEN order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_placed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN order_status IS NOT NULL AND order_status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_paid,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN subtotal > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 1) AS cart_to_item_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN subtotal > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0), 1) AS item_to_order_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_status IS NOT NULL AND order_status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0), 1) AS order_to_paid_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_status IS NOT NULL AND order_status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 1) AS overall_cart_to_paid_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    cb.cart_id,
    cb.subtotal,
    cb.device_type,
    CASE
      WHEN cb.raw_channel = 'direct' THEN 'direct'
      WHEN cb.raw_channel = 'unknown' THEN 'unknown'
      WHEN cb.raw_channel IN (
        SELECT all_channels.raw_channel
        FROM (
          SELECT
            COALESCE(
              (SELECT CASE WHEN ws2.utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(ws2.utm_source) = '' THEN 'direct' ELSE ws2.utm_source END
               FROM web_sessions ws2
               WHERE ws2.tenant_id = c2.tenant_id AND ws2.user_id = c2.user_id
                 AND ws2.started_at <= c2.created_at
                 AND CAST(ws2.started_at AS date) = CAST(c2.created_at AS date)
               ORDER BY ws2.started_at DESC LIMIT 1),
              'unknown'
            ) AS raw_channel
          FROM carts c2
          WHERE c2.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND c2.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
        ) all_channels
        WHERE all_channels.raw_channel NOT IN ('direct','unknown')
        GROUP BY all_channels.raw_channel
        ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
        LIMIT 6
      ) THEN cb.raw_channel
      ELSE 'other'
    END AS channel,
    (SELECT o.id FROM orders o WHERE o.cart_id = cb.cart_id AND o.tenant_id = cb.tenant_id ORDER BY o.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS order_id,
    (SELECT o.status FROM orders o WHERE o.cart_id = cb.cart_id AND o.tenant_id = cb.tenant_id ORDER BY o.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS order_status
  FROM (
    SELECT
      c.id AS cart_id,
      c.tenant_id,
      c.user_id,
      c.created_at,
      c.subtotal,
      COALESCE(
        (SELECT CASE
                  WHEN ws.user_agent ILIKE '%tablet%' OR ws.user_agent ILIKE '%ipad%' THEN 'tablet'
                  WHEN ws.user_agent ILIKE '%mobile%' OR ws.user_agent ILIKE '%android%' OR ws.user_agent ILIKE '%iphone%' THEN 'mobile'
                  WHEN ws.user_agent IS NOT NULL THEN 'desktop'
                  ELSE 'unknown'
                END
         FROM web_sessions ws
         WHERE ws.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = c.user_id
           AND ws.started_at <= c.created_at
           AND CAST(ws.started_at AS date) = CAST(c.created_at AS date)
         ORDER BY ws.started_at DESC LIMIT 1),
        'unknown'
      ) AS device_type,
      COALESCE(
        (SELECT CASE WHEN ws.utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(ws.utm_source) = '' THEN 'direct' ELSE ws.utm_source END
         FROM web_sessions ws
         WHERE ws.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = c.user_id
           AND ws.started_at <= c.created_at
           AND CAST(ws.started_at AS date) = CAST(c.created_at AS date)
         ORDER BY ws.started_at DESC LIMIT 1),
        'unknown'
      ) AS raw_channel
    FROM carts c
    WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  ) cb
) final
GROUP BY device_type, channel
ORDER BY carts_started DESC, device_type, channel

orders paid (status not in pending, cancelled)

For device type and channel: since there is no direct FK from carts to web_sessions, approximate by matching each cart's user_id to that user's most recent web_sessions row with started_at <= carts.created_at on the same calendar day (fall back to 'unknown' device/channel if no matching session exists); derive device type from web_sessions.user_agent (bucket as mobile/tablet/desktop/unknown via simple pattern match), and channel from web_sessions.utm_source (null/blank -> 'direct', otherwise the utm_source value, grouped to top 6 values + 'other'). question: When a cart doesn't convert, does the shopper give up quickly within the same visit, or does the cart linger for days before being abandoned or expiring?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    c.id,
    c.status,
    c.created_at,
    c.converted_at,
    c.abandoned_at,
    c.expires_at,
    CASE
      WHEN c.converted_at IS NOT NULL OR c.abandoned_at IS NOT NULL OR c.expires_at IS NOT NULL
      THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0
      ELSE NULL
    END AS resolution_hours
  FROM carts c
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik')
    AND c.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    CASE
      WHEN resolution_hours IS NULL THEN 'unresolved/still active'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 1 THEN '<1 hour'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 24 THEN '1-24 hours'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 168 THEN '1-7 days'
      ELSE '>7 days'
    END AS duration_bucket
  FROM base
)
SELECT
  duration_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
  ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_carts,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS converted_pct
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY duration_bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE duration_bucket
    WHEN '<1 hour' THEN 1
    WHEN '1-24 hours' THEN 2
    WHEN '1-7 days' THEN 3
    WHEN '>7 days' THEN 4
    WHEN 'unresolved/still active' THEN 5
  END

For each cart compute resolution_time = coalesce(converted_at, abandoned_at, expires_at) minus created_at, in hours; carts where all three are null are 'unresolved/still active' (no time computed). Bucket resolution_time into: '<1 hour', '1-24 hours', '1-7 days', '>7 days', plus a separate 'unresolved/still active' bucket for carts with no resolution timestamp. cart_count = carts in the bucket; pct_of_carts = bucket count / total carts in the base population * 100 (1 decimal); converted_pct = % of carts in that bucket with status = 'converted' (1 decimal). question: Does the >100% visit-to-cart ratio in the Q4 funnel reflect real shopper behavior, or is web-session tracking sparse relative to order volume for certain merchants (e.g. subscription sellers), making 'visits' an unreliable denominator for them?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.industry,
  COALESCE(v.visits_2025, 0) AS visits_2025,
  COALESCE(o.orders_2025, 0) AS orders_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(v.visits_2025, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(COALESCE(o.orders_2025, 0), 0), 2) AS visits_per_order,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(s.sub_linked_orders, 0) / NULLIF(COALESCE(o.orders_2025, 0), 0), 1) AS subscription_linked_orders_pct,
  COALESCE(a.active_subscriptions, 0) AS active_subscriptions
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS visits_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) v ON v.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_2025
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) o ON o.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS sub_linked_orders
  FROM orders o2
  WHERE o2.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o2.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM invoices i
      WHERE i.order_id = o2.id AND i.subscription_id IS NOT NULL
    )
  GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
) s ON s.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS active_subscriptions
  FROM subscriptions
  WHERE status = 'active'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) a ON a.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.name IN (
  'Brennquell Kaffee', 'Spice Route Box', 'Grind Collective', 'Honeycomb Larder',
  'Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane',
  'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik'
)
ORDER BY visits_per_order ASC, tenant_name ASC

question: Within the post-checkout order lifecycle, is the drop-off to a paid order a single cliff at one status or a slow bleed spread across several, and which status is it?
sql:
WITH base_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.created_at AS order_created_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN (
    SELECT o2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM orders o2
    WHERE o2.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND o2.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
    ORDER BY order_count DESC
    LIMIT 10
  ) top_tenants ON top_tenants.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND o.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
total_orders AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders FROM base_orders
),
status_list AS (
  SELECT status_name FROM (VALUES ('pending'),('confirmed'),('paid'),('partially_fulfilled'),('fulfilled'),('cancelled'),('refunded')) AS s(status_name)
),
first_reach AS (
  SELECT bo.order_id, osh.to_status AS status_name, MIN(osh.created_at) AS first_reached_at
  FROM base_orders bo
  JOIN order_status_history osh ON osh.order_id = bo.order_id
  WHERE osh.to_status IN ('pending','confirmed','paid','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','refunded')
  GROUP BY bo.order_id, osh.to_status
),
status_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    sl.status_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fr.order_id) AS orders_reaching_status,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (fr.first_reached_at - bo.order_created_at)) / 3600.0)) AS median_hours
  FROM status_list sl
  LEFT JOIN first_reach fr ON fr.status_name = sl.status_name
  LEFT JOIN base_orders bo ON bo.order_id = fr.order_id
  GROUP BY sl.status_name
)
SELECT
  sm.status_name AS status,
  COALESCE(sm.orders_reaching_status, 0) AS orders_reaching_status,
  ROUND(COALESCE(sm.orders_reaching_status, 0) * 100.0 / t.total_orders, 1) AS pct_of_total_orders,
  ROUND(sm.median_hours, 1) AS median_hours_to_status
FROM status_metrics sm
CROSS JOIN total_orders t
ORDER BY pct_of_total_orders DESC, sm.status_name ASC

For each status in (pending, confirmed, paid, partially_fulfilled, fulfilled, cancelled, refunded), 'orders reaching this status' = count of distinct orders that have at least one row in order_status_history with to_status = that status (occurred within the same order's lifetime, no extra date filter beyond the order being in the base population). Median hours = median of (first order_status_history.created_at with that to_status for the order) minus orders.created_at, in hours, rounded to 1 decimal. pct of total orders = orders_reaching_status / total_orders * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Order rows by pct of total orders descending, tie-break by status name.

question: For the real one-off retail merchants (excluding subscription-box sellers), is the drop-off between order creation and payment a single cliff or a slow bleed, and at which status does it happen?
sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
base_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.created_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN target_tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01' AND o.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
total AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS total_orders FROM base_orders
),
statuses AS (
  SELECT unnest(ARRAY['pending','confirmed','paid','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','refunded']) AS status
),
first_reach AS (
  SELECT bo.id AS order_id, osh.to_status AS status, min(osh.created_at) AS first_at
  FROM base_orders bo
  JOIN order_status_history osh ON osh.order_id = bo.id
  WHERE osh.to_status IN ('pending','confirmed','paid','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','refunded')
  GROUP BY bo.id, osh.to_status
),
joined AS (
  SELECT fr.order_id, fr.status, fr.first_at, bo.created_at,
         EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (fr.first_at - bo.created_at)) / 3600.0 AS hours
  FROM first_reach fr
  JOIN base_orders bo ON bo.id = fr.order_id
)
SELECT
  s.status,
  count(j.order_id) AS orders_reaching_status,
  round(100.0 * count(j.order_id) / NULLIF(t.total_orders, 0), 1) AS pct_of_total_orders,
  round(CAST(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY j.hours) AS numeric), 1) AS median_hours_from_order_creation
FROM statuses s
CROSS JOIN total t
LEFT JOIN joined j ON j.status = s.status
GROUP BY s.status, t.total_orders
ORDER BY pct_of_total_orders DESC, s.status ASC

question: Is the 'slow bleed' pattern in cart abandonment (most unresolved carts linger 1 hour to 7 days rather than dying instantly) consistent across retail merchants, or is it driven by one or two tenants' cart-expiry settings?
sql:
SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    b.bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY t.name), 1) AS pct_of_tenant_carts,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS converted_pct
FROM (
    SELECT
        c.tenant_id,
        c.status,
        CASE
            WHEN c.converted_at IS NULL AND c.abandoned_at IS NULL AND c.expires_at IS NULL
                THEN 'unresolved/still active'
            WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 1
                THEN '<1 hour'
            WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 24
                THEN '1-24 hours'
            WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 168
                THEN '1-7 days'
            ELSE '>7 days'
        END AS bucket
    FROM carts c
    WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
) b
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = b.tenant_id
WHERE t.name IN ('Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik')
GROUP BY t.name, b.bucket
ORDER BY t.name,
    CASE b.bucket
        WHEN '<1 hour' THEN 1
        WHEN '1-24 hours' THEN 2
        WHEN '1-7 days' THEN 3
        WHEN '>7 days' THEN 4
        WHEN 'unresolved/still active' THEN 5
    END

question: Do merchants whose deliveries run slower/later also see higher return rates — an early read on whether delivery experience is eroding trust?
sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Brennquell Kaffee','Spice Route Box','Grind Collective','Honeycomb Larder','Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
shipment_stats AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_delivered,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at))/86400.0) AS median_delivery_days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at))/86400.0 > 7 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100 AS pct_over_7
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM target_tenants)
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
order_stats AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS q4_orders,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)) AS orders_with_return
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM target_tenants)
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
)
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
  COALESCE(ss.shipments_delivered,0) AS shipments_delivered,
  ROUND(ss.median_delivery_days::numeric,1) AS median_delivery_days,
  ROUND(ss.pct_over_7::numeric,1) AS pct_over_7_days,
  ROUND( (os.orders_with_return::numeric / NULLIF(os.q4_orders,0)) * 100, 1) AS pct_orders_with_return
FROM target_tenants t
LEFT JOIN shipment_stats ss ON ss.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN order_stats os ON os.tenant_id = t.id
ORDER BY pct_over_7_days DESC NULLS LAST, t.name ASC

Shipments: from shipments joined through fulfillments to orders for tenant_id, where shipments.shipped_at is in 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31 and delivered_at is not null. delivery_days = delivered_at - shipped_at, in days. median_delivery_days = median across those shipments, rounded 1 decimal. pct_over_7_days = share of those shipments with delivery_days > 7, rounded 1 decimal (this is a generic proxy for 'late' since there's no promised-delivery-date field in the schema — flag this assumption in the report notes). Returns: among orders with placed_at in 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31 for that tenant, the % that have at least one row in order_returns (order_returns.order_id = orders.id), rounded 1 decimal. question: Within a single high-return vertical (apparel), do late-delivered orders actually have a higher return rate than on-time ones — controlling for the vertical effect that swamped the merchant-level comparison?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  base.delivery_bucket,
  count(*) AS shipments_count,
  round(
    100.0 * count(distinct case when exists (
        select 1 from order_returns orr where orr.order_id = base.order_id
      ) then base.order_id end)
    / nullif(count(distinct base.order_id), 0)
  , 1) AS pct_orders_with_return
FROM (
  select o.tenant_id, o.id as order_id,
    case when (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at) <= interval '7 days' then 'on-time' else 'late' end as delivery_bucket
  from shipments s
  join fulfillments f on f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  join orders o on o.id = f.order_id
  where s.shipped_at >= timestamp '2025-10-01'
    and s.shipped_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    and s.delivered_at is not null
) base
join tenants t on t.id = base.tenant_id
where t.name in ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
group by t.name, base.delivery_bucket
order by t.name, (case when base.delivery_bucket = 'on-time' then 0 else 1 end)

WITH retail_tenants AS (

    JOIN retail_tenants rt ON rt.id = o.tenant_id
    WHERE o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
),
base_orders AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM all_orders
    WHERE placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
      AND placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01'
),
order_has_return AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id
    FROM order_returns
),
next_order_per_base_order AS (
    SELECT b.id AS order_id, MIN(a.placed_at) AS next_placed_at
    FROM base_orders b
    JOIN all_orders a
      ON a.tenant_id = b.tenant_id
     AND a.user_id = b.user_id
     AND a.placed_at > b.placed_at
    GROUP BY b.id
),
order_level AS (
    SELECT
        b.id AS order_id,
        b.tenant_id,
        b.user_id,
        CASE WHEN ohr.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'has_return' ELSE 'no_return' END AS grp,
        CASE WHEN nop.next_placed_at IS NOT NULL
             THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (nop.next_placed_at - b.placed_at)) / 86400.0
        END AS days_to_next
    FROM base_orders b
    LEFT JOIN order_has_return ohr ON ohr.order_id = b.id
    LEFT JOIN next_order_per_base_order nop ON nop.order_id = b.id
)

    grp AS "group",
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT (tenant_id, user_id)) AS distinct_customers,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN days_to_next IS NOT NULL AND days_to_next <= 90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*),
        1
    ) AS pct_with_subsequent_order_within_90_days,
    ROUND(
        CAST(
            PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_next)
            FILTER (WHERE days_to_next IS NOT NULL AND days_to_next <= 90)
        AS numeric),
        0
    ) AS median_days_to_subsequent_order
FROM order_level
GROUP BY grp
ORDER BY CASE WHEN grp = 'has_return' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

question: Does a late delivery visibly reduce the chance a customer buys again, compared to an on-time delivery?
sql:
SELECT
  delivery_bucket,
  MAX(bucket_shipment_count) AS shipments_count,
  COUNT(*) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN min_days_to_next IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_customers_with_next_order,
  ROUND(
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY min_days_to_next) FILTER (WHERE min_days_to_next IS NOT NULL)
  , 0) AS median_days_to_next_order
FROM (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    user_id,
    delivery_bucket,
    MIN(days_to_next) AS min_days_to_next,
    MAX(bucket_shipment_count) AS bucket_shipment_count
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tenant_id,
      user_id,
      delivery_bucket,
      EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (next_order_at - delivered_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_to_next,
      COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY delivery_bucket) AS bucket_shipment_count
    FROM (
      SELECT
        o.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
        o.user_id AS user_id,
        CASE WHEN (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at) <= INTERVAL '7 days' THEN 'on-time' ELSE 'late' END AS delivery_bucket,
        s.delivered_at AS delivered_at,
        (
          SELECT MIN(o2.placed_at)
          FROM orders o2
          WHERE o2.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
            AND o2.user_id = o.user_id
            AND o2.placed_at > s.delivered_at
            AND o2.placed_at <= s.delivered_at + INTERVAL '90 days'
        ) AS next_order_at
      FROM shipments s
      JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
      JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
      JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
      WHERE t.name IN (
          'Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty',
          'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik'
        )
        AND s.delivered_at >= DATE '2025-09-01'
        AND s.delivered_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
        AND s.shipped_at IS NOT NULL
    ) shipment_level
  ) days_level
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id, delivery_bucket
) customer_level
GROUP BY delivery_bucket
ORDER BY CASE WHEN delivery_bucket = 'on-time' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, delivery_bucket

question: Do payouts consistently reconcile as net = gross minus fee, and do refunds actually reduce what we pay out, or could refunds be double-counted or missing from the payout math?
reasons: does not compile: Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name to_char does not exist!
sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start AS month
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
),
payout_agg AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', COALESCE(p.paid_at, CAST(p.arrival_date AS timestamp)))::date AS month,
    SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS gross_eur,
    SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS fee_eur,
    SUM(p.net_amount / er.rate) AS net_eur
  FROM payouts p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = COALESCE(CAST(p.paid_at AS date), p.arrival_date)
  WHERE COALESCE(p.paid_at, CAST(p.arrival_date AS timestamp)) IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),
refund_agg AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', pr.processed_at)::date AS month,
    SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refunds_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  to_char(m.month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.gross_eur,0),2) AS payout_gross_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.fee_eur,0),2) AS payout_fee_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.net_eur,0),2) AS payout_net_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pa.gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pa.fee_eur,0)),2) AS net_check_diff_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ra.refunds_eur,0),2) AS refunds_processed_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pa.gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pa.fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(ra.refunds_eur,0)),2) AS net_minus_refunds_diff_eur
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN payout_agg pa ON pa.month = m.month
LEFT JOIN refund_agg ra ON ra.month = m.month
ORDER BY m.month

question: Is there a clean, traceable link from an order to the money actually collected for it, or do orders vanish (no captured payment) or multiply (captured payments exceeding order value) along the way?
reasons: does not compile: Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name to_char does not exist!
sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
),
orders_filtered AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.currency_code, o.grand_total, o.placed_at,
         to_char(o.placed_at, 'YYYY-MM') AS month_label
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
orders_eur AS (
  SELECT ofl.order_id, ofl.month_label,
         ofl.grand_total / er.rate AS grand_total_eur
  FROM orders_filtered ofl
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = ofl.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(ofl.placed_at AS date)
),
payments_captured AS (
  SELECT p.id AS payment_id, p.order_id, p.amount, p.currency_code, p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status = 'captured' AND p.order_id IS NOT NULL
),
payments_linked AS (
  SELECT pc.payment_id, pc.order_id, ofl.month_label,
         pc.amount / er.rate AS amount_eur
  FROM payments_captured pc
  JOIN orders_filtered ofl ON ofl.order_id = pc.order_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = pc.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(pc.captured_at, ofl.placed_at) AS date)
),
order_agg AS (
  SELECT month_label,
         COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
         SUM(grand_total_eur) AS orders_grand_total_eur
  FROM orders_eur
  GROUP BY month_label
),
order_with_payment AS (
  SELECT month_label, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count
  FROM payments_linked
  GROUP BY month_label
),
payment_agg AS (
  SELECT month_label, SUM(amount_eur) AS captured_payment_total_eur
  FROM payments_linked
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0), 2) AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  COALESCE(owp.orders_with_captured_payment_count, 0) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0), 2) AS captured_payment_total_eur,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) - COALESCE(owp.orders_with_captured_payment_count, 0) AS orders_without_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) - COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0), 2) AS gap_eur,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND((COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) - COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0)) / oa.orders_grand_total_eur * 100, 1)
  END AS gap_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.month_label = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN order_with_payment owp ON owp.month_label = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN payment_agg pa ON pa.month_label = m.month_label
ORDER BY m.month_label

Base population: orders with status not 'cancelled', grouped by the month of placed_at. orders_count = count of such orders. orders_grand_total_eur = sum of their grand_total, converted to EUR. Join to payments on payments.order_id = orders.id and payments.status='captured' to find linked captured payments (an order can have 0, 1, or multiple captured payments). orders_with_captured_payment_count = count of distinct orders with at least one linked captured payment. captured_payment_total_eur = sum of all captured payments.amount linked to orders in that month's cohort, converted to EUR. orders_without_captured_payment_count = orders_count minus orders_with_captured_payment_count. gap_eur = orders_grand_total_eur minus captured_payment_total_eur. gap_pct = gap_eur divided by orders_grand_total_eur times 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Convert orders.grand_total using orders.currency_code and payments.amount using payments.currency_code, both via exchange_rates (EUR amount = local / rate) using the relevant event date. Tables: orders, payments, exchange_rates. Order by month ascending.

question: If we ask what revenue was in a given month from four different places (orders booked, payments captured, payouts settled, invoices paid), do we get the same answer, and how far apart are they?
sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start, month_label
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-01'
),

orders_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.placed_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate), 2) AS orders_booked_revenue_eur,
         COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

payments_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', p.captured_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(p.amount / er.rate), 2) AS payments_captured_eur,
         COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payments p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS DATE)
  WHERE p.status = 'captured'
    AND p.captured_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

payouts_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', po.paid_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(po.gross_amount / er.rate), 2) AS payout_gross_eur
  FROM payouts po
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = po.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(po.paid_at AS DATE)
  WHERE po.paid_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

invoices_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', i.paid_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(i.total / er.rate), 2) AS invoice_paid_revenue_eur
  FROM invoices i
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(i.paid_at AS DATE)
  WHERE i.status = 'paid'
    AND i.paid_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

refunds_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.processed_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(pr.amount / er.rate), 2) AS refunds_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
)

SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(orr.orders_booked_revenue_eur, 0) AS orders_booked_revenue_eur,
  COALESCE(pay.payments_captured_eur, 0) AS payments_captured_eur,
  COALESCE(pou.payout_gross_eur, 0) AS payout_gross_eur,
  COALESCE(inv.invoice_paid_revenue_eur, 0) AS invoice_paid_revenue_eur,
  COALESCE(ref.refunds_eur, 0) AS refunds_eur,
  COALESCE(orr.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  COALESCE(pay.payment_count, 0) AS payment_count
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN orders_rev orr ON orr.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN payments_rev pay ON pay.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN payouts_rev pou ON pou.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN invoices_rev inv ON inv.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN refunds_rev ref ON ref.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start

         COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
         SUM(grand_total_eur) AS orders_grand_total_eur
  FROM orders_eur
  GROUP BY month_label
),
order_with_payment AS (
  SELECT month_label, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count
  FROM payments_linked
  GROUP BY month_label
),
payment_agg AS (
  SELECT month_label, SUM(amount_eur) AS captured_payment_total_eur
  FROM payments_linked
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0), 2) AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  COALESCE(owp.orders_with_captured_payment_count, 0) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0), 2) AS captured_payment_total_eur,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) - COALESCE(owp.orders_with_captured_payment_count, 0) AS orders_without_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) - COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0), 2) AS gap_eur,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND((COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) - COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0)) / oa.orders_grand_total_eur * 100, 1)
  END AS gap_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.month_label = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN order_with_payment owp ON owp.month_label = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN payment_agg pa ON pa.month_label = m.month_label
ORDER BY m.month_label

Convert orders.grand_total using orders.currency_code and payments.amount using payments.currency_code, both via exchange_rates (EUR amount = local / rate) using the relevant event date. question: Is the 20-40% gap between order value and captured payments explained by order status (i.e. structural - many orders simply never get paid), or does it look like something else, once we only look at orders old enough that timing lag can't be the excuse?
sql:
SELECT
  pop.status AS order_status,
  pop.order_count,
  ROUND(pop.order_count * 100.0 / SUM(pop.order_count) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_orders,
  ROUND(pop.grand_total_eur, 2) AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  pop.orders_with_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pay.captured_eur, 0), 2) AS matched_captured_payment_eur,
  ROUND(pop.grand_total_eur - COALESCE(pay.captured_eur, 0), 2) AS gap_eur,
  ROUND((pop.grand_total_eur - COALESCE(pay.captured_eur, 0)) / NULLIF(pop.grand_total_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS gap_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.status,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS grand_total_eur,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'captured'
    ) THEN 1 END) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY o.status
) pop
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o.status,
    SUM(p.amount / er2.rate) AS captured_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = p.order_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p.status = 'captured'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY o.status
) pay ON pay.status = pop.status
ORDER BY orders_grand_total_eur DESC, pop.status

question: Once refunds are matched to the actual payments inside each payout (not just by calendar month), does net = gross - fee - refunds hold cleanly, confirming refunds are reflected once and only once in what we pay merchants?
sql:
WITH payout_eur AS (
  SELECT
    po.id AS payout_id,
    cd.month_start,
    cd.month_label,
    CASE WHEN po.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN po.gross_amount ELSE po.gross_amount / er.rate END AS gross_eur,
    CASE WHEN po.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN po.fee_amount ELSE po.fee_amount / er.rate END AS fee_eur,
    CASE WHEN po.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN po.net_amount ELSE po.net_amount / er.rate END AS net_eur
  FROM payouts po
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(po.paid_at AS date)
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = po.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = cd.calendar_date
  WHERE po.paid_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND po.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
refund_eur AS (
  SELECT
    po.id AS payout_id,
    CASE WHEN pr.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pr.amount ELSE pr.amount / er.rate END AS refund_eur
  FROM payouts po
  JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payout_id = po.id
  JOIN payment_refunds pr ON pr.payment_id = pi.payment_id AND pr.status = 'succeeded'
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE po.paid_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND po.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
payout_month_agg AS (
  SELECT month_start, month_label,
    SUM(gross_eur) AS payout_gross_eur,
    SUM(fee_eur) AS payout_fee_eur,
    SUM(net_eur) AS payout_net_eur
  FROM payout_eur
  GROUP BY month_start, month_label
),
refund_month_agg AS (
  SELECT pe.month_start, pe.month_label, SUM(re.refund_eur) AS linked_refunds_eur
  FROM refund_eur re
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT payout_id, month_start, month_label FROM payout_eur) pe ON pe.payout_id = re.payout_id
  GROUP BY pe.month_start, pe.month_label
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start, month_label FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0),2) AS payout_gross_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0),2) AS payout_fee_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0),2) AS payout_net_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0),2) AS linked_refunds_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0),2) AS implied_net_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0)),2) AS diff_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0))) / pg.payout_net_eur * 100
    END, 1) AS diff_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN payout_month_agg pg ON pg.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN refund_month_agg rf ON rf.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start

builds_on: Payout reconciliation to gross, fees and refunds
tags.details: For each payout, identify its settled payments via payout_items (payout_items.payout_id = payouts.id, payout_items.payment_id = payments.id). linked_refunds_eur for a month = sum of payment_refunds.amount (status='succeeded') where payment_refunds.payment_id is one of the payments settled in a payout whose paid_at falls in that month, converted to EUR via exchange_rates using payment_refunds.currency_code and processed_at date (refunds counted regardless of when they were processed, i.e. a refund processed any time against a payment that ended up in this month's payout). payout_gross_eur/payout_fee_eur/payout_net_eur = sum of payouts.gross_amount/fee_amount/net_amount for payouts with paid_at in that month, converted to EUR via payouts.currency_code and paid_at date. implied_net_eur = payout_gross_eur - payout_fee_eur - linked_refunds_eur. diff_eur = payout_net_eur - implied_net_eur. diff_pct = diff_eur / payout_net_eur * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: payouts, payout_items, payments, payment_refunds, exchange_rates. Order by month ascending.

question: Do different reasonable definitions of 'how many customers we have' or 'how many are active' give meaningfully different headcounts?
sql:
SELECT
  t.definition,
  t.user_count,
  round(t.user_count * 100.0 / tot.total_count, 1) as pct_of_all_customers
FROM (
  SELECT 'All customers (ever created)' as definition,
    (SELECT count(distinct u1.id) FROM users u1
       WHERE u1.is_staff = false AND u1.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01') as user_count
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Status = active',
    (SELECT count(distinct u2.id) FROM users u2
       WHERE u2.is_staff = false AND u2.status = 'active')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Placed at least one order, ever',
    (SELECT count(distinct u3.id) FROM users u3
       WHERE u3.is_staff = false
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o3 WHERE o3.user_id = u3.id
                       AND o3.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Placed at least one order in trailing 12 months',
    (SELECT count(distinct u4.id) FROM users u4
       WHERE u4.is_staff = false
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o4 WHERE o4.user_id = u4.id
                       AND o4.placed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
                       AND o4.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Has an active or trialing subscription',
    (SELECT count(distinct u5.id) FROM users u5
       WHERE u5.is_staff = false
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions s5 WHERE s5.user_id = u5.id
                       AND s5.status IN ('active','trialing')))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Logged in within last 90 days of data',
    (SELECT count(distinct u6.id) FROM users u6
       WHERE u6.is_staff = false
         AND u6.last_login_at >= timestamp '2025-10-03'
         AND u6.last_login_at < timestamp '2026-01-01')
) t
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT count(distinct u0.id) as total_count
  FROM users u0
  WHERE u0.is_staff = false AND u0.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
) tot
ORDER BY t.user_count DESC, t.definition

tags.details: Scope: all tenants combined, non-staff users only (users.is_staff = false). As-of date for all 'current state' columns: the data cutoff 2025-12-31. Rows (definitions), each counting distinct users.id: (1) 'All customers (ever created)' - all non-staff users with created_at <= 2025-12-31; this is the denominator for pct_of_all_customers. (2) 'Status = active' - users.status = 'active'. (3) 'Placed at least one order, ever' - distinct users.id appearing in orders (any status) with placed_at <= 2025-12-31. (4) 'Placed at least one order in trailing 12 months' - distinct users.id with an order placed_at between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31. (5) 'Has an active or trialing subscription' - distinct users.id with a subscriptions row where status in ('active','trialing'). (6) 'Logged in within last 90 days of data' - users.last_login_at >= 2025-10-03. pct_of_all_customers = user_count / (count from definition 1) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: users, orders, subscriptions. Order by user_count descending.

question: When a payment is refunded, does the refund happen before its payout settles (so it can cleanly reduce that payout) or after (so the clawback has no clean home in the payout data), and how much money is affected?
sql:
SELECT
  timing_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS refund_count,
  ROUND(SUM(amount_eur), 2) AS refund_amount_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(amount_eur) / SUM(SUM(amount_eur)) OVER () * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_refund_amount,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN timing_bucket = 'refund after payout paid_at' THEN days_lag END), 1) AS avg_days_lag
FROM (
  SELECT
    pr.id,
    CASE
      WHEN po.id IS NULL THEN 'payment not yet settled in any payout'
      WHEN pr.processed_at <= po.paid_at THEN 'refund before payout paid_at'
      ELSE 'refund after payout paid_at'
    END AS timing_bucket,
    CASE WHEN pr.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pr.amount ELSE pr.amount / er.rate END AS amount_eur,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (pr.processed_at - po.paid_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_lag
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  LEFT JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payment_id = pr.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN payouts po ON po.id = pi.payout_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = pr.processed_at::date
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
) sub
GROUP BY timing_bucket
ORDER BY refund_amount_eur DESC

builds_on: Payout net formula check via payment-linked refunds
tags.details: Population: all payment_refunds with status='succeeded' across full history (2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31). For each refund, find the payout (if any) that settled its payment via payout_items (payout_items.payment_id = payment_refunds.payment_id) joined to payouts (payout_items.payout_id = payouts.id). Bucket each refund as: 'refund before payout paid_at' when payment_refunds.processed_at <= payouts.paid_at; 'refund after payout paid_at' when payment_refunds.processed_at > payouts.paid_at; 'payment not yet settled in any payout' when no matching payout_items row exists for that payment_id. refund_count = count of refunds in the bucket. refund_amount_eur = sum of payment_refunds.amount converted to EUR via payment_refunds.currency_code and processed_at date. pct_of_total_refund_amount = refund_amount_eur / total refund_amount_eur across all buckets * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. avg_days_lag = average of (payment_refunds.processed_at - payouts.paid_at) in days for the 'after' bucket only (NULL for the other two buckets), rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: payment_refunds, payout_items, payouts, exchange_rates. Order by refund_amount_eur descending.
tags.grain: timing bucket (before payout settled / after payout settled / payment not yet in any payout)

question: How much of the gap between order value and 'captured' payments is really just that refunded/partially-refunded payments were excluded by my status filter, versus a genuine hole where money was never collected?
sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT
    o0.id AS order_id,
    o0.status AS order_status,
    o0.grand_total / er0.rate AS grand_total_eur
  FROM orders o0
  JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er0.quote_code = o0.currency_code
   AND er0.as_of = CAST(o0.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o0.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND o0.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00'
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT
    p1.order_id AS order_id,
    p1.amount / er1.rate AS gross_eur,
    (p1.amount - p1.amount_refunded) / er1.rate AS net_eur
  FROM payments p1
  JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = p1.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = CAST(p1.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p1.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p1.order_id IN (SELECT t0.order_id FROM t0)
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    t1.order_id AS order_id,
    SUM(t1.gross_eur) AS gross_eur,
    SUM(t1.net_eur) AS net_eur
  FROM t1
  GROUP BY t1.order_id
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_status AS order_status,
    COUNT(t0.order_id) AS order_count,
    SUM(t0.grand_total_eur) AS orders_grand_total_eur
  FROM t0
  GROUP BY t0.order_status
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_status AS order_status,
    COUNT(t2.order_id) AS orders_with_money_collected_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(t2.gross_eur, 0)) AS gross_collected_eur,
    SUM(COALESCE(t2.net_eur, 0)) AS net_collected_eur
  FROM t0
  LEFT JOIN t2
    ON t2.order_id = t0.order_id
  GROUP BY t0.order_status
)
SELECT
  t3.order_status AS order_status,
  t3.order_count AS order_count,
  t3.orders_grand_total_eur AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  t4.orders_with_money_collected_count AS orders_with_money_collected_count,
  t4.gross_collected_eur AS gross_collected_eur,
  t4.net_collected_eur AS net_collected_eur,
  t3.orders_grand_total_eur - t4.gross_collected_eur AS gap_vs_gross_eur,
  ROUND(
    (t3.orders_grand_total_eur - t4.gross_collected_eur) / NULLIF(t3.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) * 100,
    1
  ) AS gap_vs_gross_pct
FROM t3
JOIN t4
  ON t4.order_status = t3.order_status
ORDER BY t3.orders_grand_total_eur DESC, t3.order_status ASC

builds_on: Order-to-payment gap by order status, aged cohort
tags.details: Same population as the prior order-status report: orders with placed_at between 2023-01-01 and 2025-06-30 inclusive. Group by orders.status. order_count and orders_grand_total_eur as before (grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates using orders.currency_code and placed_at date). orders_with_money_collected_count = count of those orders with at least one linked payments row (payments.order_id = orders.id) whose status is in ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded') - i.e. any payment that was successfully captured at some point, whether or not it was later refunded. gross_collected_eur = sum of payments.amount for those linked payments (the original captured amount, before any refund), converted to EUR via payments.currency_code and captured_at date. net_collected_eur = sum of (payments.amount - payments.amount_refunded) for those same linked payments, converted the same way - this is what the merchant actually kept after refunds. gap_vs_gross_eur = orders_grand_total_eur - gross_collected_eur. gap_vs_gross_pct = gap_vs_gross_eur / orders_grand_total_eur * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: orders, payments, exchange_rates. Order by orders_grand_total_eur descending.

question: Does net equal gross minus fee cleanly for payouts in every currency, or do certain currencies show persistent drift in that basic arithmetic, separate from the refund timing issue already found?
sql:
select
  currency_code,
  count(*) as payout_count,
  sum(gross_amount) as gross_native_total,
  sum(fee_amount) as fee_native_total,
  sum(net_amount) as net_native_total,
  sum(net_amount) - (sum(gross_amount) - sum(fee_amount)) as net_check_diff_native,
  round(
    (sum(net_amount) - (sum(gross_amount) - sum(fee_amount))) / nullif(sum(gross_amount), 0) * 100,
    2
  ) as net_check_diff_pct
from payouts
where created_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01'
  and created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
group by currency_code
order by payout_count desc, currency_code

builds_on: Payout reconciliation to gross, fees and refunds
tags.details: Scope: all payouts across the full history from 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31, grouped by payouts.currency_code, deliberately kept in native currency with no EUR conversion so this checks pure arithmetic consistency without introducing any FX rounding or rate matching as a confound. payout_count is the count of payouts in that currency. gross_native_total is the sum of payouts.gross_amount. fee_native_total is the sum of payouts.fee_amount. net_native_total is the sum of payouts.net_amount. net_check_diff_native is net_native_total minus the quantity gross_native_total minus fee_native_total, which should be close to 0 if net equals gross minus fee holds. net_check_diff_pct is net_check_diff_native divided by gross_native_total, times 100, rounded to 2 decimals. Table: payouts. Order by payout_count descending.
tags.grain: currency code, using the payout's native currency with no FX conversion applied

question: How much have the currencies our merchants transact in moved against EUR over the three years of history, and is that movement large enough to distort revenue trends when we roll up multi-currency figures over time?
sql:
WITH currencies_used AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT currency_code FROM orders
),
tenant_counts AS (
  SELECT default_currency_code AS currency_code, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS tenant_count
  FROM tenants
  GROUP BY default_currency_code
),
orders_2025 AS (
  SELECT o.currency_code,
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
           ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END
    ) AS orders_2025_total_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.currency_code
),
rate_2023 AS (
  SELECT cu.currency_code,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er WHERE er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code=cu.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE '2023-01-02'),
      (SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er WHERE er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code=cu.currency_code AND er.as_of >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND er.as_of < DATE '2023-02-01' ORDER BY er.as_of ASC LIMIT 1)
    ) AS rate_early
  FROM currencies_used cu
),
rate_2025 AS (
  SELECT cu.currency_code,
    (SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er WHERE er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code=cu.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31') AS rate_late
  FROM currencies_used cu
)
SELECT
  cu.currency_code,
  COALESCE(tc.tenant_count,0) AS tenant_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(o25.orders_2025_total_eur,0),2) AS orders_2025_total_eur,
  CASE WHEN cu.currency_code='EUR' THEN 1.0 ELSE r23.rate_early END AS rate_eur_to_currency_2023_01_02,
  CASE WHEN cu.currency_code='EUR' THEN 1.0 ELSE r25.rate_late END AS rate_eur_to_currency_2025_12_31,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN cu.currency_code='EUR' THEN 0
    ELSE ( (r25.rate_late - r23.rate_early) / NULLIF(r23.rate_early,0) ) * 100
    END, 1
  ) AS pct_rate_change
FROM currencies_used cu
LEFT JOIN tenant_counts tc ON tc.currency_code = cu.currency_code
LEFT JOIN orders_2025 o25 ON o25.currency_code = cu.currency_code
LEFT JOIN rate_2023 r23 ON r23.currency_code = cu.currency_code
LEFT JOIN rate_2025 r25 ON r25.currency_code = cu.currency_code
ORDER BY orders_2025_total_eur DESC NULLS LAST, cu.currency_code

tags.details: Scope: every currency_code that appears in orders.currency_code across the full history. tenant_count is the count of distinct tenants whose default_currency_code equals this currency. orders_2025_total_eur is the sum of orders.grand_total for non-cancelled orders placed in 2025, converted to EUR via exchange_rates using the order's currency_code and placed_at date. rate_eur_to_currency_2023_01_02 is exchange_rates.rate where base_code is EUR, quote_code is this currency, and as_of is 2023-01-02, falling back to the earliest available date in January 2023 if that exact date is missing. rate_eur_to_currency_2025_12_31 is the same lookup for as_of 2025-12-31. pct_rate_change is the late rate minus the early rate, divided by the early rate, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: orders, tenants, exchange_rates. Order by orders_2025_total_eur descending.
tags.grain: currency code

title: EUR exchange rate movement by currency, 2023 vs 2025

question: For our B2B wholesaler merchants, how much of their outstanding receivables is genuinely overdue versus just within normal net terms lag, so we can present that line accurately in the annual accounts?
sql:
WITH scoped_tenants AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%office%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%wholesale%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%b2b%'
),
tenant_match_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM scoped_tenants
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    i.id,
    i.amount_due,
    i.currency_code,
    i.due_at,
    bp.net_terms_days,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31' THEN 'Not yet due'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date) BETWEEN 1 AND 30 THEN '1-30 days overdue'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date) BETWEEN 31 AND 60 THEN '31-60 days overdue'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date) BETWEEN 61 AND 90 THEN '61-90 days overdue'
      ELSE '90+ days overdue'
    END AS aging_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31' THEN 0
      ELSE (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date)
    END AS days_past_due,
    er.rate AS eur_rate
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN scoped_tenants st ON st.id = i.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN billing_profiles bp ON bp.id = i.billing_profile_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
  WHERE i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
    AND i.amount_due > 0
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    aging_bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS invoice_count,
    SUM(amount_due / eur_rate) AS amount_due_eur,
    AVG(days_past_due) AS avg_days_past_due,
    AVG(net_terms_days) AS avg_net_terms_days
  FROM base
  GROUP BY aging_bucket
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(amount_due_eur) AS total_amount_due_eur FROM bucketed
)
SELECT
  b.aging_bucket,
  b.invoice_count,
  ROUND(b.amount_due_eur, 2) AS amount_due_eur,
  ROUND(b.amount_due_eur / NULLIF(t.total_amount_due_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_amount_due,
  ROUND(b.avg_days_past_due, 1) AS avg_days_past_due,
  ROUND(b.avg_net_terms_days, 1) AS avg_net_terms_days
FROM bucketed b
CROSS JOIN totals t
WHERE (SELECT cnt FROM tenant_match_count) > 0

UNION ALL

SELECT
  di.industry AS aging_bucket,
  NULL::bigint AS invoice_count,
  NULL::numeric AS amount_due_eur,
  NULL::numeric AS pct_of_total_amount_due,
  NULL::numeric AS avg_days_past_due,
  NULL::numeric AS avg_net_terms_days
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT industry FROM tenants) di
WHERE (SELECT cnt FROM tenant_match_count) = 0

ORDER BY amount_due_eur DESC NULLS LAST, aging_bucket

tags.details: Scope: tenants whose industry indicates a B2B wholesale vertical such as industrial supplies or office equipment, matched via tenants.industry ILIKE patterns for industrial, office, wholesale, or B2B; if none match, instead return the distinct tenants.industry values present so the right filter can be identified. Population: invoices for those tenants with status in open or past_due and amount_due greater than 0, as of the snapshot date 2025-12-31. Bucket each invoice by days overdue, computed as 2025-12-31 minus invoices.due_at: Not yet due when due_at is null or due_at is on or after 2025-12-31, then 1 to 30 days overdue, 31 to 60 days overdue, 61 to 90 days overdue, and 90 plus days overdue. invoice_count is the count of invoices in the bucket. amount_due_eur is the sum of invoices.amount_due converted to EUR via exchange_rates using base_code EUR, quote_code equal to the invoice currency_code, and as_of 2025-12-31. pct_of_total_amount_due is amount_due_eur divided by the total amount_due_eur across all buckets, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal. avg_days_past_due is the average of 2025-12-31 minus due_at in days for the bucket, rounded to 1 decimal, with 0 for Not yet due. avg_net_terms_days is the average of billing_profiles.net_terms_days for the billing profile tied to each invoice, rounded to 1 decimal, for context on what normal lag looks like. Tables: tenants, invoices, billing_profiles, exchange_rates. Order by amount_due_eur descending.
tags.grain: receivables aging bucket

title: B2B wholesaler receivables aging

question: Which roles across our merchants carry the most permissions, how many users currently hold each role, and how many of those users look dormant (no recent login) — a first read on access-governance hygiene?
sql:
WITH role_perm_counts AS (
  SELECT role_id, COUNT(*) AS permission_count
  FROM role_permissions
  GROUP BY role_id
),
role_users AS (
  SELECT ur.role_id,
         u.id AS user_id,
         u.status,
         u.last_login_at
  FROM user_roles ur
  JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id AND u.tenant_id = ur.tenant_id
  WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
),
role_user_agg AS (
  SELECT role_id,
         COUNT(*) AS users_assigned,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS users_active,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active' AND (last_login_at IS NULL OR last_login_at < DATE '2025-10-05')) AS users_dormant,
         MAX(last_login_at) AS most_recent_login
  FROM role_users
  GROUP BY role_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  r.name AS role_name,
  r.is_system,
  rpc.permission_count,
  rua.users_assigned,
  rua.users_active,
  rua.users_dormant,
  rua.most_recent_login,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_qualifying_roles
FROM roles r
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
JOIN role_perm_counts rpc ON rpc.role_id = r.id
JOIN role_user_agg rua ON rua.role_id = r.id
ORDER BY rpc.permission_count DESC, rua.users_assigned DESC, t.name, r.name
LIMIT 50

columns_requested: users currently assigned this role (via user_roles)
of those, users with status = active
of those, users dormant (status = active but last_login_at is null or before 2025-10-05, i.e. no login in the trailing ~90 days)
most recent last_login_at among assigned users
tags.details: Source: roles joined to tenants; role_permissions grouped by role_id for permission count; user_roles joined to users for assignment counts and last_login_at. Exclude soft-deleted users (users.deleted_at is null). 'Dormant' = users.status = 'active' and (last_login_at is null or last_login_at < 2025-10-05, i.e. no login in the 90 days before the data cutoff 2025-12-31). Only include roles that have at least 1 permission and at least 1 assigned user (skip empty/unused roles for this first pass). Order by permission count descending, then users assigned descending, then tenant name, then role name as the final tie-break, capped at 50 rows — note how many qualifying role rows exist in total.
tags.grain: one row per tenant and role

question: Over the last 26 weeks, how many login attempts are we seeing platform-wide, what share fail, and are there signs of credential-stuffing-style behavior (many attempts concentrated on few IPs)?
sql:
WITH target AS (
  SELECT week_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date = DATE '2025-12-31'
),
windowed AS (
  SELECT
    cd.week_start,
    la.email,
    la.ip_address,
    la.succeeded
  FROM login_attempts la
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(la.occurred_at AS date)
  CROSS JOIN target t
  WHERE cd.week_start BETWEEN t.week_start - INTERVAL '175 days' AND t.week_start
),
ip_counts AS (
  SELECT week_start, ip_address, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM windowed
  GROUP BY week_start, ip_address
),
ip_max AS (
  SELECT week_start, MAX(cnt) AS max_ip_attempts
  FROM ip_counts
  GROUP BY week_start
),
weekly AS (
  SELECT
    week_start,
    COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
    SUM(CASE WHEN succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_logins,
    SUM(CASE WHEN NOT succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_logins,
    COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS distinct_identities,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS distinct_ips
  FROM windowed
  GROUP BY week_start
)
SELECT
  w.week_start,
  w.total_attempts,
  w.successful_logins,
  w.failed_logins,
  ROUND(100.0 * w.failed_logins / NULLIF(w.total_attempts, 0), 1) AS failure_rate_pct,
  w.distinct_identities AS distinct_emails_attempted,
  w.distinct_ips,
  ROUND(w.total_attempts * 1.0 / NULLIF(w.distinct_ips, 0), 1) AS avg_attempts_per_ip,
  m.max_ip_attempts AS max_attempts_single_ip
FROM weekly w
JOIN ip_max m ON m.week_start = w.week_start
ORDER BY w.week_start

columns_requested: average attempts per distinct IP (total attempts / distinct IPs)
max attempts from a single IP in the week
tags.details: Source: login_attempts (occurred_at, succeeded, email, user_id, ip_address). Bucket occurred_at::date into ISO weeks via calendar_days.week_start. Window: the 26 ISO weeks ending with the week containing 2025-12-31 (i.e. roughly 2025-07 through 2025-12, last available data). Aggregate across all tenants (no currency conversion needed, no money involved). failure rate = failed_logins / total_attempts, rounded to 1 decimal. 'max attempts from a single IP in the week' = the highest per-IP attempt count within that week (compute per-IP counts, then take the max per week). Order by week_start ascending, which is already unique so no further tie-break needed.
tags.grain: one row per ISO week (week_start), platform-wide across all tenants

title: Weekly sign-in attempt volume and failure pattern

question: For each merchant, what share of staff users and what share of shopper (non-staff) users have a confirmed, active MFA device, versus relying on password only?
sql:
SELECT t.id AS tenant_id,
       t.name AS tenant_name,
       t.status AS tenant_status,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff THEN u.id END) AS staff_user_count,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END) AS staff_users_with_mfa,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff THEN u.id END), 0), 1) AS staff_mfa_rate_pct,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff THEN u.id END) AS shopper_user_count,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END) AS shopper_users_with_mfa,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff THEN u.id END), 0), 1) AS shopper_mfa_rate_pct,
       COUNT(u.id) AS total_users
FROM tenants t
JOIN users u
  ON u.tenant_id = t.id
 AND u.deleted_at IS NULL
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT tenant_id, user_id, true AS has_mfa
    FROM mfa_devices
    WHERE confirmed_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
) um
  ON um.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
 AND um.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.status
ORDER BY staff_mfa_rate_pct ASC NULLS LAST, tenant_name ASC
LIMIT 50

tags.details: Source: users (tenant_id, is_staff, deleted_at) joined to tenants for name/status, and to mfa_devices (tenant_id, user_id, confirmed_at) to determine MFA status. A user counts as having 'confirmed MFA' if they have at least one mfa_devices row with confirmed_at not null. Exclude soft-deleted users (deleted_at is null). Split counts by is_staff = true (staff) vs is_staff = false (shopper/end-user). Compute staff_mfa_rate = staff_with_mfa / staff_count (null-safe if staff_count = 0), same for shopper rate, rounded to 1 decimal percent. Include all 120 tenants that have at least one user; order by staff MFA rate ascending (worst coverage first) with tenant name as tie-break, so the report surfaces the weakest merchants first. Note total tenant count returned vs. the 50-row cap.
tags.grain: one row per tenant (merchant)

question: What is the actual company-wide MFA adoption rate today for staff and for shoppers, and has it been improving or flat over the past year?
sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT month_label, MAX(calendar_date) AS month_end
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE year_num = 2025
  GROUP BY month_label
),
eligible_users AS (
  SELECT m.month_label, m.month_end, u.id AS user_id, u.is_staff
  FROM months m
  JOIN users u
    ON u.created_at <= m.month_end
   AND (u.deleted_at IS NULL OR u.deleted_at > m.month_end)
),
user_mfa AS (
  SELECT eu.month_label, eu.month_end, eu.user_id, eu.is_staff,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM mfa_devices md
      WHERE md.user_id = eu.user_id AND md.confirmed_at <= eu.month_end
    ) AS has_mfa
  FROM eligible_users eu
),
monthly_summary AS (
  SELECT month_label,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_staff) AS staff_users,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_staff AND has_mfa) AS staff_mfa_users,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_staff) AS shopper_users,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_staff AND has_mfa) AS shopper_mfa_users
  FROM user_mfa
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  month_label,
  staff_users,
  staff_mfa_users AS staff_users_with_mfa,
  ROUND(100.0 * staff_mfa_users / NULLIF(staff_users,0), 1) AS staff_mfa_rate_pct,
  shopper_users,
  shopper_mfa_users AS shopper_users_with_mfa,
  ROUND(100.0 * shopper_mfa_users / NULLIF(shopper_users,0), 1) AS shopper_mfa_rate_pct
FROM monthly_summary
ORDER BY month_label

builds_on: MFA adoption rate by merchant, staff vs. shoppers
columns_requested: staff users as of month end
staff users with confirmed MFA as of month end
shopper users as of month end
shopper users with confirmed MFA as of month end
tags.details: Source: users (tenant_id, is_staff, created_at, deleted_at) and mfa_devices (user_id, confirmed_at). For each of the 12 months Jan 2025 through Dec 2025 (use calendar_days distinct month_start/month_label values), take month_end = last day of that month. 'Staff users as of month end' = count of users with is_staff = true, created_at <= month_end, and (deleted_at is null or deleted_at > month_end). 'Staff users with confirmed MFA as of month end' = of those, count with at least one mfa_devices row where confirmed_at <= month_end. Same logic for shoppers (is_staff = false). Rates rounded to 1 decimal percent. This is a cumulative snapshot each month, not new signups in that month. Order by month_label ascending (already unique).

sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.status AS tenant_status,
  COUNT(*) AS total_login_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN la.succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_logins,
  SUM(CASE WHEN NOT la.succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_logins,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT la.succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS failure_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT la.email) AS distinct_emails_attempted,
  COUNT(DISTINCT la.ip_address) AS distinct_ip_addresses,
  (SELECT MAX(ip_count) FROM (
      SELECT COUNT(*) AS ip_count
      FROM login_attempts la2
      WHERE la2.tenant_id = la.tenant_id
        AND la2.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-24 00:00:00'
        AND la2.occurred_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 23:59:59'
      GROUP BY la2.ip_address
  ) ip_counts) AS max_attempts_single_ip,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (
      SELECT COUNT(*)
      FROM login_attempts la3
      WHERE la3.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-24 00:00:00'
        AND la3.occurred_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 23:59:59'
  ), 1) AS pct_of_platform_total
FROM login_attempts la
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = la.tenant_id
WHERE la.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-24 00:00:00'
  AND la.occurred_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 23:59:59'
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.status, la.tenant_id
ORDER BY total_login_attempts DESC, tenant_name ASC

question: Beyond the default 'Owner' role (which filled the entire first page of the prior report), what other roles across merchants carry significant permissions, how widely are they assigned, and how dormant are the users holding them?
sql:
WITH role_instance AS (
  SELECT r.id AS role_id, r.tenant_id, r.name, r.is_system,
         COUNT(DISTINCT rp.permission_id) AS perm_count
  FROM roles r
  JOIN role_permissions rp ON rp.role_id = r.id
  GROUP BY r.id, r.tenant_id, r.name, r.is_system
),
assigned AS (
  SELECT ur.role_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS assigned_users,
         COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) FILTER (WHERE u.status = 'active' AND (u.last_login_at IS NULL OR u.last_login_at < DATE '2025-10-05')) AS dormant_users
  FROM user_roles ur
  JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id AND u.tenant_id = ur.tenant_id
  WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY ur.role_id
),
qualifying AS (
  SELECT ri.tenant_id, ri.name, ri.is_system, ri.perm_count,
         a.assigned_users, a.dormant_users
  FROM role_instance ri
  JOIN assigned a ON a.role_id = ri.role_id
  WHERE ri.perm_count >= 1 AND a.assigned_users >= 1
)
SELECT
  name AS role_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS tenant_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_system THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_is_system,
  ROUND(AVG(perm_count), 1) AS avg_permission_count,
  MAX(perm_count) AS max_permission_count,
  SUM(assigned_users) AS total_users_assigned,
  SUM(dormant_users) AS total_users_dormant,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(dormant_users) / NULLIF(SUM(assigned_users), 0), 1) AS dormant_rate_pct
FROM qualifying
WHERE name <> 'Owner'
GROUP BY name
ORDER BY total_users_assigned DESC, role_name
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Privileged roles per merchant: grant size and dormancy
columns_requested: tenant count (distinct tenants with a role of this name)
share of those instances flagged is_system (%)
average permission count granted (across tenant instances of this role)
max permission count seen for this role name
total users currently assigned (summed across tenants, via user_roles, excluding deleted users)
total users dormant (status = active and last_login_at is null or before 2025-10-05, summed across tenants)
tags.details: Source: roles joined to role_permissions (for permission counts per role instance), user_roles joined to users (excluding users.deleted_at is not null) for assignment and dormancy. Restrict to role instances with >=1 permission and >=1 assigned non-deleted user (same population as the prior 'Privileged roles per merchant' report, i.e. drawn from that same 434-row qualifying set, but now grouped by role_name instead of by tenant+role so the whole landscape fits on one page). 'Dormant' = users.status = 'active' and (last_login_at is null or last_login_at < 2025-10-05). Dormant rate = total dormant / total assigned, rounded to 1 decimal percent. Order by total users assigned descending, then role name as tie-break; cap at 50 rows and note how many distinct role names exist in total.
tags.grain: one row per distinct role name (roles.name), aggregated across all tenants that have a role with that name

question: Is the audit trail (audit_log) consistently capturing sensitive actions across all merchants and over time, or are some action types thin, recent-only, or concentrated in a handful of tenants — could we credibly reconstruct 'who did what, when' if asked?
sql:
SELECT
  a.action AS action_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-05' AND a.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01') AS events_last_90_days,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT a.tenant_id) / t.tenant_count, 1) AS pct_of_tenants,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.actor_user_id) AS distinct_actor_users,
  MIN(a.occurred_at) AS earliest_occurred_at,
  MAX(a.occurred_at) AS most_recent_occurred_at
FROM audit_log a
CROSS JOIN (SELECT COUNT(*) AS tenant_count FROM tenants) t
WHERE a.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND a.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY a.action, t.tenant_count
ORDER BY total_events DESC, action_type ASC

columns_requested: events in the last 90 days (2025-10-05 through 2025-12-31)
distinct tenants with at least one such event

'Share of all 120 tenants' = distinct tenants with that action / 120, rounded to 1 decimal percent (note if the tenant count assumption of 120 needs adjusting based on what's actually in the tenants table). Order by total events descending, action type as tie-break (only 7 rows expected, well under the cap).
tags.grain: one row per audit_log action type (the 7 enum values: create, update, delete, login, logout, export, access_denied)

question: How many API keys does each merchant have, how many are active, and how many of those active keys look abandoned (never used, or unused for a long time)?
sql:
SELECT
  t.id AS tenant_id,
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.status AS tenant_status,
  COUNT(ak.id) AS total_api_keys,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_api_keys,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status IN ('revoked','expired') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS revoked_or_expired_keys,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' AND ak.last_used_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_never_used,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' AND ak.last_used_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-05 00:00:00' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_unused_90d,
  MAX(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' THEN DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE) ELSE NULL END) AS oldest_active_key_age_days,
  COALESCE(sa.service_account_count, 0) AS service_accounts_count
FROM api_keys ak
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ak.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS service_account_count
  FROM service_accounts
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) sa ON sa.tenant_id = t.id
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.status, sa.service_account_count
ORDER BY active_never_used DESC, active_unused_90d DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 50

columns_requested: active keys never used (last_used_at is null)
oldest active key age in days (2026-01-05 minus created_at)
service accounts count (from service_accounts table, for context)
tags.details: Source: api_keys (tenant_id, status, created_at, last_used_at, expires_at) joined to tenants; service_accounts counted separately per tenant (that table has no usage timestamp, so it's included only as a headcount for context, not an activity measure). 'Active' = status = 'active'. Use 2026-01-05 as the fixed reference date for all day-based calculations (per house standards, no CURRENT_DATE). Include every tenant that has at least one api_keys row. Order by 'active keys never used' descending, then 'active keys unused 90+ days' descending, then tenant name as tie-break, so the most abandoned-looking merchants surface first. Cap at 50 rows, note total tenant rows with at least one key.
tags.grain: one row per tenant

title: API key hygiene by merchant
