question: Putting cost and revenue side by side: how does the points value we issue and redeem per loyalty member compare to the revenue those members actually generate, versus non-members?
sql:
WITH population AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS user_id, u.tenant_id
  FROM users u
  JOIN orders o
    ON o.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
   AND o.user_id = u.id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
),
segment_membership AS (
  SELECT
    p.user_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    CASE WHEN la.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM population p
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) la
    ON la.tenant_id = p.tenant_id AND la.user_id = p.user_id
),
revenue_detail AS (
  SELECT
    sm.segment,
    o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS revenue_eur
  FROM segment_membership sm
  JOIN orders o
    ON o.tenant_id = sm.tenant_id AND o.user_id = sm.user_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
loyalty_tx_detail AS (
  SELECT
    sm.segment,
    lt.direction,
    ABS(lt.points) / lp.points_per_currency
      / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN lp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS points_value_eur
  FROM segment_membership sm
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la
    ON la.tenant_id = sm.tenant_id AND la.user_id = sm.user_id
  JOIN loyalty_transactions lt
    ON lt.tenant_id = la.tenant_id AND lt.loyalty_account_id = la.id
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp
    ON lp.tenant_id = la.tenant_id AND lp.id = la.loyalty_program_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = lp.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(lt.occurred_at AS date)
),
customer_counts AS (
  SELECT segment, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
  FROM segment_membership
  GROUP BY segment
),
revenue_totals AS (
  SELECT segment, SUM(revenue_eur) AS total_revenue_eur
  FROM revenue_detail
  GROUP BY segment
),
redeemed_totals AS (
  SELECT segment, SUM(points_value_eur) AS total_redeemed_eur
  FROM loyalty_tx_detail
  WHERE direction <> 'earn'
  GROUP BY segment
),
earned_totals AS (
  SELECT segment, SUM(points_value_eur) AS total_earned_eur
  FROM loyalty_tx_detail
  WHERE direction = 'earn'
  GROUP BY segment
)
SELECT
  cc.segment,
  cc.customer_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS total_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0) / cc.customer_count, 2) AS revenue_per_customer_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(red.total_redeemed_eur, 0), 2) AS total_points_redeemed_cost_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(red.total_redeemed_eur, 0) / cc.customer_count, 2) AS redeemed_cost_per_customer_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(earn.total_earned_eur, 0), 2) AS total_points_earned_liability_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(earn.total_earned_eur, 0) / cc.customer_count, 2) AS earned_liability_per_customer_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(red.total_redeemed_eur, 0) / NULLIF(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0), 0), 2) AS redeemed_cost_pct_of_revenue
FROM customer_counts cc
LEFT JOIN revenue_totals rev ON rev.segment = cc.segment
LEFT JOIN redeemed_totals red ON red.segment = cc.segment
LEFT JOIN earned_totals earn ON earn.segment = cc.segment
ORDER BY CASE WHEN cc.segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, cc.segment

question: Is the elevated refund rate among loyalty members a broad pattern across verticals, or is it concentrated in one or two verticals that happen to have naturally high returns, such as apparel?
sql:
WITH eligible_users AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        o.user_id,
        o.tenant_id,
        t.industry
    FROM orders o
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
    JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id AND u.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
      AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND u.is_staff = false
),
loyalty_flags AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id
    FROM loyalty_accounts
),
user_segment AS (
    SELECT
        eu.tenant_id,
        eu.user_id,
        eu.industry,
        CASE WHEN lf.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
    FROM eligible_users eu
    LEFT JOIN loyalty_flags lf
        ON lf.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id AND lf.user_id = eu.user_id
),
all_orders_for_users AS (
    SELECT
        o.id AS order_id,
        o.tenant_id,
        o.user_id,
        o.status,
        o.placed_at,
        o.currency_code,
        o.grand_total
    FROM orders o
    JOIN user_segment us
        ON us.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND us.user_id = o.user_id
),
refund_flags AS (
    SELECT
        ao.order_id,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM payments p
                WHERE p.order_id = ao.order_id AND p.amount_refunded > 0
             )
             OR EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r
                WHERE r.order_id = ao.order_id
             )
        THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
    FROM all_orders_for_users ao
),
order_value_eur AS (
    SELECT
        ao.order_id,
        ao.tenant_id,
        ao.user_id,
        ao.grand_total / er.rate AS order_value_eur
    FROM all_orders_for_users ao
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = ao.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(ao.placed_at AS DATE)
    WHERE ao.status <> 'cancelled'
),
per_user_stats AS (
    SELECT
        us.tenant_id,
        us.user_id,
        us.industry,
        us.segment,
        COUNT(ao.order_id) AS lifetime_order_count
    FROM user_segment us
    LEFT JOIN all_orders_for_users ao
        ON ao.tenant_id = us.tenant_id AND ao.user_id = us.user_id
    GROUP BY us.tenant_id, us.user_id, us.industry, us.segment
),
industry_segment_counts AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        segment,
        COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customer_count,
        AVG(lifetime_order_count) AS avg_lifetime_orders
    FROM per_user_stats
    GROUP BY industry, segment
),
order_value_agg AS (
    SELECT
        us.industry,
        us.segment,
        AVG(ov.order_value_eur) AS avg_order_value_eur
    FROM order_value_eur ov
    JOIN user_segment us
        ON us.tenant_id = ov.tenant_id AND us.user_id = ov.user_id
    GROUP BY us.industry, us.segment
),
refund_agg AS (
    SELECT
        us.industry,
        us.segment,
        AVG(CAST(rf.is_refunded AS DECIMAL)) * 100 AS refund_rate_pct
    FROM refund_flags rf
    JOIN all_orders_for_users ao ON ao.order_id = rf.order_id
    JOIN user_segment us
        ON us.tenant_id = ao.tenant_id AND us.user_id = ao.user_id
    GROUP BY us.industry, us.segment
),
qualifying_industries AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM industry_segment_counts
    GROUP BY industry
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT segment) = 2 AND MIN(customer_count) >= 20
)
SELECT
    isc.industry,
    isc.segment,
    isc.customer_count,
    ROUND(isc.avg_lifetime_orders, 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
    ROUND(ova.avg_order_value_eur, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
    ROUND(ra.refund_rate_pct, 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM industry_segment_counts isc
JOIN qualifying_industries qi ON qi.industry = isc.industry
LEFT JOIN order_value_agg ova ON ova.industry = isc.industry AND ova.segment = isc.segment
LEFT JOIN refund_agg ra ON ra.industry = isc.industry AND ra.segment = isc.segment
ORDER BY isc.industry, (CASE WHEN isc.segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)

question: Among closed B2B wholesale opportunities, what reliably differs between the ones we won and the ones we lost — deal size, touches/activities before close, days open, or how concentrated they are among accounts and reps?
sql:
WITH b2b_tenants AS (
  SELECT id FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
closed_opps AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id, o.account_id, o.owner_user_id, o.is_won, o.closed_at, o.created_at,
    o.amount,
    o.currency_code,
    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
         ELSE o.amount / (
           SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er
           WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
             AND er.as_of <= o.closed_at::date
           ORDER BY er.as_of DESC LIMIT 1
         )
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN b2b_tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.closed_at IS NOT NULL
),
activity_counts AS (
  SELECT co.id AS opportunity_id, COUNT(a.id) AS activity_count
  FROM closed_opps co
  LEFT JOIN activities a ON a.opportunity_id = co.id AND a.occurred_at <= co.closed_at
  GROUP BY co.id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN co.is_won THEN 'won' ELSE 'lost' END AS outcome,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities,
  ROUND(AVG(co.amount_eur), 2) AS avg_amount_eur,
  ROUND(CAST(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY co.amount_eur) AS numeric), 2) AS median_amount_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(ac.activity_count), 2) AS avg_activities_before_close,
  ROUND(CAST(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (co.closed_at - co.created_at)) / 86400.0) AS numeric), 1) AS avg_days_open,
  COUNT(DISTINCT co.account_id) AS distinct_accounts,
  COUNT(DISTINCT co.owner_user_id) AS distinct_reps
FROM closed_opps co
JOIN activity_counts ac ON ac.opportunity_id = co.id
GROUP BY co.is_won
ORDER BY co.is_won DESC

columns_requested: average activities per opportunity before close
tags.details: Scope to the same B2B wholesale tenants as the other two reports (industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR '%office equipment%' OR '%wholesal%'). Use opportunities where is_closed = true, split into is_won = true (won) vs is_won = false (lost), across all history through 2025-12-31. Convert opportunity amount to EUR using exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code = opportunity currency_code, rate as_of the opportunity's closed_at date, or nearest prior business day if a weekend) before averaging across tenants/currencies, per house standards. 'Activities before close' = count of rows in activities where activities.opportunity_id = opportunities.id and activities.occurred_at <= opportunities.closed_at, averaged per opportunity within each outcome group. Distinct accounts/reps are counts of distinct account_id / owner_user_id among opportunities in that outcome group. Order rows with 'won' first, then 'lost'.
tags.grain: one row per closed outcome (won or lost)

question: Across our B2B wholesale merchants, at which pipeline stage do the most opportunities get stuck or lost — i.e. which stage is the graveyard?
sql:
WITH wholesale_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, name AS merchant
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
stages AS (
  SELECT
    os.tenant_id,
    os.id AS stage_id,
    os.name AS stage_name,
    os.sort_position,
    os.win_probability,
    p.name AS pipeline_name
  FROM opportunity_stages os
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = os.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = os.tenant_id
  JOIN wholesale_tenants wt ON wt.tenant_id = os.tenant_id
),
opp_agg AS (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    o.stage_id,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_closed = false) AS open_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.is_won = true) AS won_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.is_won = false) AS lost_count,
    AVG(o.amount) AS avg_amount,
    MIN(o.currency_code) AS currency_code
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN wholesale_tenants wt ON wt.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id, o.stage_id
)
SELECT
  wt.merchant,
  s.pipeline_name,
  s.stage_name,
  s.sort_position AS stage_order,
  ROUND(s.win_probability, 4) AS default_win_probability,
  COALESCE(oa.open_count, 0) AS opportunities_open,
  COALESCE(oa.won_count, 0) AS opportunities_closed_won,
  COALESCE(oa.lost_count, 0) AS opportunities_closed_lost,
  ROUND(oa.avg_amount, 2) AS avg_opportunity_amount,
  oa.currency_code
FROM stages s
JOIN wholesale_tenants wt ON wt.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN opp_agg oa ON oa.tenant_id = s.tenant_id AND oa.stage_id = s.stage_id
ORDER BY wt.merchant, s.sort_position, s.stage_name

columns_requested: opportunities currently open at this stage (is_closed = false)
opportunities closed won with this as final stage_id
opportunities closed lost with this as final stage_id
average opportunity amount at this stage (in the opportunity's own currency)
tags.details: Scope to B2B wholesale merchants only: tenants where industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%' (per the company briefing's 'industrial supplies, office equipment' wholesalers). Use opportunities joined to opportunity_stages (stage_id) and pipelines, and tenants for the merchant name. For each (tenant, stage) pair count: opportunities where is_closed = false (currently sitting there), opportunities where is_closed = true and is_won = true and stage_id = this stage, and opportunities where is_closed = true and is_won = false (lost) and stage_id = this stage. Include avg(amount) per currency_code — do not convert currencies here since the grain is per-tenant so no cross-currency summing occurs. This is an all-time snapshot (all opportunities ever created through 2025-12-31), not time-windowed. Order by merchant name, then stage order (sort_position) ascending. Flag in the report notes if any wholesale tenant has zero opportunities or zero stages, since that would indicate the industry filter missed a merchant or the merchant doesn't use the CRM module.

question: Restricted to genuine new-customer acquisition deals (excluding renewals), how long does it take to close an opportunity, and is that cycle time trending up or down over the last three years?
sql:
WITH tenant_scope AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
new_business_pipelines AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, id AS pipeline_id
  FROM pipelines
  WHERE name = 'New business'
),
scoped_opportunities AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.is_won,
    o.created_at,
    o.closed_at
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN tenant_scope ts ON ts.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN new_business_pipelines nbp
    ON nbp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
   AND nbp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
    AND o.closed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.closed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.closed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
opportunities_with_month AS (
  SELECT
    so.id,
    so.is_won,
    cd.month_label,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (so.closed_at - so.created_at)) / 86400.0 AS cycle_days
  FROM scoped_opportunities so
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(so.closed_at AS DATE)
),
monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_won) AS closed_won,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_won) AS closed_lost,
    AVG(cycle_days) AS avg_cycle_days_raw,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cycle_days) AS median_cycle_days_raw
  FROM opportunities_with_month
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  month_label AS month,
  opportunities_closed,
  closed_won,
  closed_lost,

question: Restricted to genuine new-customer acquisition deals (excluding renewals), what reliably differs between won and lost opportunities — deal size, activities before close, days open, or concentration among accounts and reps?
sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
new_business_pipelines AS (
  SELECT id, tenant_id
  FROM pipelines
  WHERE name = 'New business'
),
base_opportunities AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN new_business_pipelines p
    ON o.pipeline_id = p.id
   AND o.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE o.tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM target_tenants)
    AND o.is_closed = true
),
opp_with_rate AS (
  SELECT
    bo.*,
    (
      SELECT er.rate
      FROM exchange_rates er
      WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = bo.currency_code
        AND er.as_of <= date(bo.closed_at)
      ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS eur_rate
  FROM base_opportunities bo
),
activities_before_close AS (
  SELECT
    a.opportunity_id,
    count(*) AS activity_count
  FROM activities a
  JOIN base_opportunities bo
    ON a.opportunity_id = bo.id
   AND a.tenant_id = bo.tenant_id
  WHERE a.occurred_at <= bo.closed_at
  GROUP BY a.opportunity_id
),
opp_final AS (
  SELECT
    owr.id,
    owr.account_id,
    owr.owner_user_id,
    owr.is_won,
    owr.amount / owr.eur_rate AS amount_eur,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (owr.closed_at - owr.created_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_open,
    COALESCE(ac.activity_count, 0) AS activity_count
  FROM opp_with_rate owr
  LEFT JOIN activities_before_close ac
    ON ac.opportunity_id = owr.id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN is_won THEN 'won' ELSE 'lost' END AS outcome,
  count(*) AS opportunities,
  round(avg(amount_eur)::numeric, 2) AS avg_amount_eur,
  round(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount_eur)::numeric, 2) AS median_amount_eur,
  round(avg(activity_count)::numeric, 2) AS avg_activities_before_close,
  round(avg(days_open)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_open,
  count(DISTINCT account_id) AS distinct_accounts,
  count(DISTINCT owner_user_id) AS distinct_reps
FROM opp_final
GROUP BY is_won
ORDER BY CASE WHEN is_won THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

question: Among B2B wholesale opportunities that were actually lost in new-customer acquisition (not renewals), which stage were they sitting in just before they were marked Closed Lost — i.e. where is the real graveyard?
sql:
WITH lost_opps AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id
  WHERE p.name = 'New business'
    AND o.is_closed = true
    AND o.is_won = false
    AND (t.industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%wholesal%')
),
last_stage_change AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (ch.entity_id)
    ch.entity_id,
    ch.tenant_id,
    (ch.before_data->>'stage_id') AS before_stage_id
  FROM change_history ch
  JOIN lost_opps lo ON lo.id = ch.entity_id AND lo.tenant_id = ch.tenant_id
  WHERE ch.entity_table = 'opportunities'
    AND 'stage_id' = ANY(ch.changed_columns)
  ORDER BY ch.entity_id, ch.occurred_at DESC
),
opp_stage AS (
  SELECT
    lo.id AS opportunity_id,
    os.name AS stage_name,
    os.sort_position AS stage_order
  FROM lost_opps lo
  LEFT JOIN last_stage_change lsc ON lsc.entity_id = lo.id
  LEFT JOIN opportunity_stages os ON os.id = CAST(lsc.before_stage_id AS bigint)
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(stage_name, 'No stage transition recorded') AS stage_name,
  stage_order,
  COUNT(*) AS lost_opportunities_last_seen_here,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_total_lost_in_new_business,
  SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS total_lost_opportunities_new_business
FROM opp_stage
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY lost_opportunities_last_seen_here DESC, stage_name

This means opportunities.stage_id only reflects the FINAL state and does not preserve where a lost deal actually stalled before dying — the earlier 'graveyard stage' question cannot be answered from current stage_id alone. This report reconstructs it from history. Scope: opportunities where tenant_id is a wholesale merchant (tenants.industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR '%office equipment%' OR '%wholesal%'), pipeline_id = the tenant's 'New business' pipeline (join pipelines on name = 'New business'), is_closed = true, is_won = false. For each such opportunity, look at change_history where entity_table = 'opportunities', entity_id = opportunities.id, changed_columns includes 'stage_id', ordered by occurred_at. Take the most recent such change event and read before_data->>'stage_id' as the stage the opportunity was in immediately before that final change (presumed to be the move into Closed Lost); join that id to opportunity_stages for stage_name/stage_order. If an opportunity has no change_history row with a stage_id change at all, bucket it as 'No stage transition recorded' (it was apparently created or recorded as lost without a logged progression). Group by the resulting stage (or the no-record bucket), count opportunities, and compute each group's share of all lost New-business opportunities for this tenant set. Order by lost_opportunities_last_seen_here descending. Please flag in the report notes if change_history has little or no coverage for these opportunities (e.g., most rows fall into 'No transition recorded'), since that would mean the audit trail can't answer this and we should say so plainly rather than over-interpret a small sample.

question: How much of our current B2B wholesale new-business pipeline is already older than the typical window in which deals actually win, i.e. how much open pipeline is quietly turning stale and at risk?
sql:
WITH fx AS (
  SELECT quote_code, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR' AND as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
),
scoped AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.amount,
    o.currency_code,
    o.created_at,
    (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.created_at AS DATE)) AS age_days
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = false
    AND lower(p.name) = 'new business'
    AND (
      lower(t.industry) LIKE '%wholesale%'
      OR lower(t.industry) LIKE '%industrial%'
      OR lower(t.industry) LIKE '%office equipment%'
    )
),
converted AS (
  SELECT
    s.*,
    CASE WHEN s.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN s.amount
         ELSE s.amount / fx.rate END AS amount_eur
  FROM scoped s
  LEFT JOIN fx ON fx.quote_code = s.currency_code
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    CASE
      WHEN age_days < 10 THEN '0-9 days'
      WHEN age_days < 20 THEN '10-19 days'
      WHEN age_days < 30 THEN '20-29 days'
      WHEN age_days < 45 THEN '30-44 days'
      WHEN age_days < 90 THEN '45-89 days'
      ELSE '90+ days'
    END AS age_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN age_days < 10 THEN 0
      WHEN age_days < 20 THEN 10
      WHEN age_days < 30 THEN 20
      WHEN age_days < 45 THEN 30
      WHEN age_days < 90 THEN 45
      ELSE 90
    END AS bucket_order
  FROM converted c
)
SELECT
  age_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_open_pipeline,
  ROUND(AVG(amount_eur), 2) AS avg_amount_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(amount_eur), 2) AS total_amount_eur
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY age_bucket, bucket_order
ORDER BY bucket_order

question: Does a bigger deal size correlate with a better or worse chance of closing, and does it drag out the cycle time?
sql:
WITH pipelines_filtered AS (
  SELECT p.id AS pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
  FROM pipelines p
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
    AND p.name = 'New business'
),
opp AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.is_won,
    o.created_at,
    o.closed_at,
    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
         ELSE o.amount / (
           SELECT er.rate
           FROM exchange_rates er
           WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
             AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
             AND er.as_of <= o.closed_at::date
           ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
           LIMIT 1
         )
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN pipelines_filtered pf ON pf.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND pf.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
),
banded AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN amount_eur < 3000 THEN '<3000'
      WHEN amount_eur < 6000 THEN '3000-5999'
      WHEN amount_eur < 9000 THEN '6000-8999'
      WHEN amount_eur < 12000 THEN '9000-11999'
      ELSE '12000+'
    END AS amount_band_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN amount_eur < 3000 THEN 1
      WHEN amount_eur < 6000 THEN 2
      WHEN amount_eur < 9000 THEN 3
      WHEN amount_eur < 12000 THEN 4
      ELSE 5
    END AS band_sort,
    is_won,
    closed_at,
    created_at
  FROM opp
)
SELECT
  amount_band_eur,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_won) AS closed_won,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_won) AS closed_lost,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_won) / COUNT(*), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (closed_at - created_at)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_open
FROM banded
GROUP BY amount_band_eur, band_sort
ORDER BY band_sort

question: How often do physical cycle counts come back different from the stock quantity we had on record, and how large are those differences in units and estimated value, across 2025?

with cc as (

  join stock_locations sl on sl.id = sm.stock_location_id
  where sm.kind = 'cycle_count'

)

  to_char(occurred_at, 'YYYY-MM') as month,
  count(*) as cycle_count_events,
  count(distinct warehouse_id) as warehouses_affected,

  coalesce(sum(quantity) filter (where quantity > 0), 0) as units_over,
  sum(quantity) as net_units_variance,
  sum(abs(quantity)) as abs_units_variance,

question: Does the stock-count mismatch concentrate in particular warehouses, particular storage-location kinds (e.g. bulk shelving vs pick bins), or particular merchants, in a way that signals valuation/write-off exposure?
sql:
WITH variant_cost AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
  FROM (
    SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
             PARTITION BY variant_id
             ORDER BY CASE WHEN is_preferred THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, unit_cost ASC
           ) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products
    WHERE unit_cost IS NOT NULL
  ) ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS tenant_id,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    w.id AS warehouse_id,
    w.name AS warehouse_name,
    sl.kind AS location_kind,
    COUNT(*) AS cycle_count_events,
    SUM(sm.quantity) AS net_units_variance,
    SUM(ABS(sm.quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(ABS(sm.quantity) * vc.unit_cost / CASE WHEN vc.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END) AS estimated_value_eur
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sm.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  JOIN variant_cost vc ON vc.variant_id = sm.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = vc.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(sm.occurred_at AS date)
  WHERE sm.kind = 'cycle_count'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.id, t.name, w.id, w.name, sl.kind
)
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  warehouse_name,
  location_kind,
  cycle_count_events,
  net_units_variance,
  abs_units_variance,
  ROUND(estimated_value_eur, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(estimated_value_eur / SUM(estimated_value_eur) OVER () * 100, 1) AS share_of_total_value_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY estimated_value_eur DESC, abs_units_variance DESC, tenant_name, warehouse_name, location_kind
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
columns_requested: estimated_value_eur (abs variance costed and converted to EUR, same method as report 1)
share_of_total_value_pct (this row's estimated_value_eur / sum of estimated_value_eur across all rows, *100, rounded 1dp)

Order by estimated_value_eur descending, tie-break by abs_units_variance descending, then tenant_name, warehouse_name, location_kind for determinism. question: Are stock-count discrepancies spread evenly across product categories, or concentrated in certain categories, lot/serial-tracked items, or high-velocity items — pointing to a handling problem vs a tracking-method problem?
sql:
WITH cycle_counts AS (
  SELECT
    sm.quantity,
    sm.lot_id,
    sm.occurred_at,
    pv.id AS variant_id,
    COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized') AS category_name
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = sm.variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
  WHERE sm.kind = 'cycle_count'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
cost_per_variant AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
  FROM (
    SELECT sp.variant_id, sp.unit_cost, sp.currency_code,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.variant_id ORDER BY sp.is_preferred DESC, sp.id) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products sp
    WHERE sp.unit_cost IS NOT NULL
  ) x
  WHERE rn = 1
),
cc_valued AS (
  SELECT
    cc.category_name,
    cc.quantity,
    cc.lot_id,
    CASE WHEN cv.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN cv.unit_cost
         WHEN cv.unit_cost IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE cv.unit_cost / er.rate
    END AS unit_cost_eur
  FROM cycle_counts cc
  LEFT JOIN cost_per_variant cv ON cv.variant_id = cc.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = cv.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = DATE(cc.occurred_at)
),
category_cc AS (
  SELECT
    category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS cycle_count_events,
    SUM(ABS(quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(quantity) AS net_units_variance,
    SUM(ABS(quantity) * COALESCE(unit_cost_eur, 0)) AS estimated_value_eur,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN lot_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_lot_or_serial
  FROM cc_valued
  GROUP BY category_name
),
sales AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized') AS category_name,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = oi.product_variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized')
)
SELECT
  cc.category_name,
  cc.cycle_count_events,
  cc.abs_units_variance,
  cc.net_units_variance,
  ROUND(cc.estimated_value_eur, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(cc.pct_lot_or_serial, 1) AS pct_events_lot_or_serial_tracked,
  ROUND(COALESCE(s.total_units_sold, 0) / 12.0, 1) AS avg_monthly_units_sold,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(s.total_units_sold, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE cc.abs_units_variance / COALESCE(s.total_units_sold, 0) * 1000
    END, 1) AS variance_per_1000_units_sold
FROM category_cc cc
LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.category_name = cc.category_name
ORDER BY ROUND(cc.estimated_value_eur, 2) DESC, cc.category_name ASC

question: When stock is reserved for an order, does the reservation get released normally (order fulfilled/cancelled in time), or do we see reservations left stuck past their expiry — quietly overstating what's actually available to sell?
sql:
SELECT
  category AS outcome_category,
  count(*) AS reservation_count,
  round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_total,
  sum(quantity) AS total_quantity_units,
  round(avg(quantity * 1.0), 1) AS avg_quantity_per_reservation,
  round(avg(duration_days), 1) AS avg_hold_duration_days
FROM (
  SELECT
    quantity,
    CASE
      WHEN released_at IS NOT NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR released_at <= expires_at) THEN 'released_on_time'
      WHEN released_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at IS NOT NULL AND released_at > expires_at THEN 'released_late'
      WHEN released_at IS NULL AND expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' THEN 'stuck_past_expiry'
      ELSE 'still_open_active'
    END AS category,
    CASE
      WHEN released_at IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (released_at - created_at)) / 86400.0
      ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' - created_at)) / 86400.0
    END AS duration_days
  FROM stock_reservations
  WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
) t
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY
  CASE category
    WHEN 'released_on_time' THEN 1
    WHEN 'released_late' THEN 2
    WHEN 'stuck_past_expiry' THEN 3
    WHEN 'still_open_active' THEN 4
  END

columns_requested: total_quantity_units (sum of quantity across reservations in this category)
avg_hold_duration_days (for released rows: released_at minus created_at; for still-open rows: 2025-12-31 minus created_at; rounded 1dp)
tags.details: Source: stock_reservations where created_at is between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31. Define four mutually exclusive outcome categories, evaluated with 2025-12-31 as the fixed 'as of' reference date (the last date the warehouse has complete data for — do not use CURRENT_DATE): (1) 'released_on_time' = released_at is not null and (expires_at is null or released_at <= expires_at); (2) 'released_late' = released_at is not null and expires_at is not null and released_at > expires_at; (3) 'stuck_past_expiry' = released_at is null and expires_at is not null and expires_at < 2025-12-31 (an expired hold that was never released — the 'zombie' case that overstates unavailable stock); (4) 'still_open_active' = released_at is null and (expires_at is null or expires_at >= 2025-12-31). Order rows in that fixed category order (released_on_time, released_late, stuck_past_expiry, still_open_active) rather than alphabetically, so the report reads as a funnel.
tags.grain: reservation outcome category

  WHERE sm.kind = 'cycle_count'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
variant_cost AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
  FROM (
    SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY variant_id ORDER BY is_preferred DESC, unit_cost ASC) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products
    WHERE unit_cost IS NOT NULL
  ) ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
),
valued AS (
  SELECT cc.location_kind,
         cc.stock_location_id,
         cc.quantity,
         CASE
           WHEN vc.unit_cost IS NOT NULL AND er.rate IS NOT NULL
           THEN ABS(cc.quantity) * vc.unit_cost / er.rate
           ELSE 0
         END AS value_eur
  FROM cycle_counts cc
  LEFT JOIN variant_cost vc ON vc.variant_id = cc.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = vc.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(cc.occurred_at AS date)
),
agg AS (
  SELECT location_kind,
         COUNT(DISTINCT stock_location_id) AS distinct_locations_with_activity,
         COUNT(*) AS cycle_count_events,
         SUM(ABS(quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
         SUM(quantity) AS net_units_variance,
         SUM(value_eur) AS estimated_value_eur
  FROM valued
  GROUP BY location_kind
)
SELECT
  k.location_kind,
  COALESCE(a.distinct_locations_with_activity, 0) AS distinct_locations_with_activity,
  COALESCE(lc.total_locations_of_this_kind, 0) AS total_locations_of_this_kind,
  COALESCE(a.cycle_count_events, 0) AS cycle_count_events,
  COALESCE(a.abs_units_variance, 0) AS abs_units_variance,
  COALESCE(a.net_units_variance, 0) AS net_units_variance,
  ROUND(COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0), 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0)
    / NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0)) OVER (), 0),
    2
  ) AS share_of_total_value_pct
FROM kinds k
LEFT JOIN location_counts lc ON lc.location_kind = k.location_kind
LEFT JOIN agg a ON a.location_kind = k.location_kind
ORDER BY COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0) DESC, k.location_kind ASC

question: With only 407 adjustment-kind events in the year but some as large as 192 units, which specific events are driving the value — do they cluster by warehouse, merchant, location kind, category or product, or are they scattered?
sql:
WITH adjustments_2025 AS (
    SELECT
        sm.id,
        sm.tenant_id,
        sm.variant_id,
        sm.stock_location_id,
        sm.quantity AS quantity_signed,
        sm.reference_type,
        sm.occurred_at
    FROM stock_movements sm
    WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment'
      AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
preferred_cost AS (
    SELECT
        sp.variant_id,
        sp.unit_cost,
        sp.currency_code,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.variant_id ORDER BY sp.id) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products sp
    WHERE sp.is_preferred = true
),
variant_cost AS (
    SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
    FROM preferred_cost
    WHERE rn = 1
),
fx AS (
    SELECT base_code, quote_code, rate, as_of
    FROM exchange_rates
    WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
enriched AS (
    SELECT
        a.id,
        a.occurred_at,
        t.name AS tenant_name,
        w.name AS warehouse_name,
        sl.kind AS location_kind,
        COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized') AS category_name,
        pv.sku,
        a.quantity_signed,
        a.reference_type,
        CASE
            WHEN vc.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ABS(a.quantity_signed) * vc.unit_cost
            ELSE ABS(a.quantity_signed) * vc.unit_cost / NULLIF(fx.rate, 0)
        END AS estimated_value_eur
    FROM adjustments_2025 a
    JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = a.stock_location_id
    JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
    JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = a.variant_id
    JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
    LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
    LEFT JOIN variant_cost vc ON vc.variant_id = a.variant_id
    LEFT JOIN fx ON fx.quote_code = vc.currency_code AND fx.as_of = CAST(a.occurred_at AS date)
)
SELECT
    occurred_at,
    tenant_name,
    warehouse_name,
    location_kind,
    category_name,
    sku,
    quantity_signed,
    ROUND(estimated_value_eur, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
    reference_type
FROM enriched
ORDER BY estimated_value_eur DESC NULLS LAST, ABS(quantity_signed) DESC, occurred_at, id
LIMIT 30

question: Unlike cycle_count (always exactly 1 unit), kind='adjustment' movements vary widely (avg ~10 units, max 192) — what is the monthly scale, direction (shrinkage vs gain) and estimated value of this stream, and how does it trend across 2025?
reasons: does not compile: Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name to_char does not exist!
sql:
WITH variant_cost AS (
  SELECT sp.variant_id, sp.unit_cost, sp.currency_code,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.variant_id ORDER BY sp.is_preferred DESC, sp.unit_cost ASC) AS rn
  FROM supplier_products sp
  WHERE sp.unit_cost IS NOT NULL
),
best_cost AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code FROM variant_cost WHERE rn = 1
),
movements AS (
  SELECT sm.id, sm.variant_id, sm.quantity, sm.occurred_at,
         CAST(sm.occurred_at AS date) AS occ_date
  FROM stock_movements sm
  WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
valued AS (
  SELECT m.id, m.quantity,
    date_trunc('month', m.occurred_at) AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN bc.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN bc.unit_cost
         WHEN bc.currency_code IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE bc.unit_cost / er.rate
    END AS unit_cost_eur
  FROM movements m
  LEFT JOIN best_cost bc ON bc.variant_id = m.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = bc.currency_code AND er.as_of = m.occ_date
)
SELECT
  to_char(month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
  COUNT(*) AS adjustment_events,
  SUM(CASE WHEN quantity < 0 THEN -quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_short,
  SUM(CASE WHEN quantity > 0 THEN quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_over,
  SUM(quantity) AS net_units_variance,
  SUM(ABS(quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
  ROUND(SUM(ABS(quantity) * COALESCE(unit_cost_eur,0))::numeric, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(ABS(quantity))::numeric, 1) AS avg_abs_units_per_event
FROM valued
GROUP BY month_start
ORDER BY month_start

question: The 407 stock_movements kind='adjustment' events (nearly all on 2025-12-31) appeared, in the top-30 detail, to be entirely B2B wholesale merchants (office equipment / industrial supplies) — is that concentration total, or do other merchants/verticals also appear further down the list?
sql:
SELECT
  sub.tenant_name,
  sub.industry,
  sub.adjustment_events,
  sub.abs_units_variance,
  sub.net_units_variance,
  sub.estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(sub.estimated_value_eur * 100.0 / SUM(sub.estimated_value_eur) OVER (), 2) AS share_of_total_value_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    t.industry AS industry,
    COUNT(*) AS adjustment_events,
    SUM(ABS(sm.quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(sm.quantity) AS net_units_variance,
    ROUND(SUM(
      ABS(sm.quantity) * COALESCE(
        (SELECT sp.unit_cost / er.rate
         FROM supplier_products sp
         JOIN exchange_rates er
           ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = sp.currency_code
          AND er.as_of = CAST(sm.occurred_at AS date)
         WHERE sp.variant_id = sm.variant_id
           AND sp.is_preferred = true
           AND sp.unit_cost IS NOT NULL
         ORDER BY sp.id
         LIMIT 1
        ), 0)
    ), 2) AS estimated_value_eur
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sm.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment'

question: What is our overall SLA breach rate for 2025, and which priority levels drive the misses?
sql:
with base as (
  select t.id as ticket_id, t.priority,
         sp.first_response_target_minutes,
         sp.resolution_target_minutes
  from tickets t
  join sla_policies sp on sp.id = t.sla_policy_id
  where t.created_at >= date '2025-01-01'
    and t.created_at < date '2026-01-01'
    and t.sla_policy_id is not null
),
breach_fr as (
  select ticket_id, avg(minutes_over) as minutes_over
  from sla_breaches
  where breach_kind = 'first_response'
  group by ticket_id
),
breach_res as (
  select ticket_id, avg(minutes_over) as minutes_over
  from sla_breaches
  where breach_kind = 'resolution'
  group by ticket_id
),
per_priority as (
  select
    b.priority::text as priority,
    count(*) as ticket_count_with_sla,
    round(avg(b.first_response_target_minutes)) as typical_first_response_target_minutes,
    round(avg(b.resolution_target_minutes)) as typical_resolution_target_minutes,
    round(100.0 * count(fr.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as first_response_breach_rate,
    round(100.0 * count(res.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as resolution_breach_rate,
    round(avg(fr.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_first_response,
    round(avg(res.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_resolution
  from base b
  left join breach_fr fr on fr.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
  left join breach_res res on res.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
  group by b.priority
),
overall as (
  select
    'All priorities'::text as priority,
    count(*) as ticket_count_with_sla,
    null::numeric as typical_first_response_target_minutes,
    null::numeric as typical_resolution_target_minutes,
    round(100.0 * count(fr.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as first_response_breach_rate,
    round(100.0 * count(res.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as resolution_breach_rate,
    round(avg(fr.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_first_response,
    round(avg(res.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_resolution
  from base b
  left join breach_fr fr on fr.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
  left join breach_res res on res.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
),
combined as (
  select 0 as sort_rank, * from overall
  union all
  select 1 as sort_rank, * from per_priority
)
select
  priority,
  ticket_count_with_sla,
  typical_first_response_target_minutes,
  typical_resolution_target_minutes,
  first_response_breach_rate,
  resolution_breach_rate,
  avg_minutes_over_first_response,
  avg_minutes_over_resolution
from combined
order by sort_rank, resolution_breach_rate desc nulls last, priority

columns_requested: priority (or 'All priorities' for the total row)
typical_first_response_target_minutes (from sla_policies for that priority, blank on the All row)
typical_resolution_target_minutes (from sla_policies for that priority, blank on the All row)
tags.details: Window: tickets.created_at between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31 inclusive, restricted to tickets with sla_policy_id not null. Source tables: tickets, sla_breaches, sla_policies. Compute breach rates per priority as % of that priority's tickets with a matching sla_breaches row (split by breach_kind = first_response / resolution); the 'All priorities' row aggregates across every priority (this is the headline number for the leadership review). Order: 'All priorities' row first, then the four priorities sorted by resolution_breach_rate descending. Round rates to 1 decimal percent, minutes to whole numbers.
tags.grain: one row per ticket priority (low, normal, high, urgent) plus one summary row labeled 'All priorities' totaling across all of them

question: Which agent groups miss first-response and resolution SLA targets most often, and by how much when they do?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.agent_group_id, COALESCE(ag.name, 'Unassigned queue') AS agent_group_name,
         t.created_at, t.first_response_at, t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN agent_groups ag ON ag.id = t.agent_group_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
),
ticket_stats AS (
  SELECT agent_group_id, agent_group_name,
         COUNT(*) AS ticket_count_with_sla,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM base
  GROUP BY agent_group_id, agent_group_name
),
breach_join AS (
  SELECT base.agent_group_id, base.agent_group_name, sb.ticket_id, sb.breach_kind, sb.minutes_over
  FROM base
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = base.id
),
breach_stats AS (
  SELECT agent_group_id, agent_group_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'first_response') AS fr_breach_tickets,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'resolution') AS res_breach_tickets,
    AVG(minutes_over) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'first_response') AS avg_minutes_over_first_response,
    AVG(minutes_over) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'resolution') AS avg_minutes_over_resolution
  FROM breach_join
  GROUP BY agent_group_id, agent_group_name
)
SELECT
  ts.agent_group_name,
  ts.ticket_count_with_sla,
  ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COALESCE(bs.fr_breach_tickets, 0) / ts.ticket_count_with_sla AS numeric), 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COALESCE(bs.res_breach_tickets, 0) / ts.ticket_count_with_sla AS numeric), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  ROUND(CAST(bs.avg_minutes_over_first_response AS numeric), 0) AS avg_minutes_over_first_response,
  ROUND(CAST(bs.avg_minutes_over_resolution AS numeric), 0) AS avg_minutes_over_resolution,
  ROUND(CAST(ts.avg_first_response_minutes AS numeric), 0) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(CAST(ts.avg_resolution_minutes AS numeric), 0) AS avg_resolution_minutes
FROM ticket_stats ts
LEFT JOIN breach_stats bs ON bs.agent_group_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ts.agent_group_id
ORDER BY
  (ts.agent_group_name = 'Unassigned queue') ASC,
  resolution_breach_rate DESC NULLS LAST,
  ts.agent_group_name ASC

columns_requested: ticket_count_with_sla (tickets created in 2025 with a non-null sla_policy_id)
first_response_breach_rate (% of those tickets with a sla_breaches row of breach_kind = first_response)
resolution_breach_rate (% with a sla_breaches row of breach_kind = resolution)
tags.details: Window: tickets.created_at between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31 inclusive, restricted to tickets with sla_policy_id not null (tickets actually under an SLA). Source tables: tickets, sla_breaches, agent_groups. Join sla_breaches on ticket_id, split by breach_kind. Order by resolution_breach_rate descending, 'Unassigned queue' row last. Round rates to 1 decimal percent, minutes to whole numbers.

question: How is ticket volume distributed across our agent groups, and does staffing (agent count) look balanced against that load?
sql:
WITH group_names AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT name AS agent_group_name
  FROM agent_groups
),

ticket_window AS (
  SELECT
    t.id,
    t.agent_group_id,
    t.tenant_id,
    ag.name AS group_name,
    t.status,
    t.assignee_agent_id,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN agent_groups ag
    ON ag.id = t.agent_group_id AND ag.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),

ticket_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(group_name, 'Unassigned queue') AS agent_group_name,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status NOT IN ('solved','closed')) AS open_ticket_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE assignee_agent_id IS NULL) AS unassigned_ticket_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM ticket_window
  GROUP BY COALESCE(group_name, 'Unassigned queue')
),

agent_counts AS (
  SELECT
    ag.name AS agent_group_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT agm.tenant_id::text || ':' || agm.support_agent_id::text) AS agent_count
  FROM agent_group_members agm
  JOIN agent_groups ag
    ON ag.id = agm.agent_group_id AND ag.tenant_id = agm.tenant_id
  GROUP BY ag.name
),

all_rows AS (
  SELECT agent_group_name FROM group_names
  UNION
  SELECT 'Unassigned queue'
)

SELECT
  r.agent_group_name,
  COALESCE(tm.ticket_count, 0) AS ticket_count,
  COALESCE(tm.open_ticket_count, 0) AS open_ticket_count,
  ac.agent_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(tm.ticket_count,0)::numeric / NULLIF(ac.agent_count,0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(tm.unassigned_ticket_count,0) / NULLIF(tm.ticket_count,0), 1) AS pct_unassigned,
  ROUND(tm.avg_first_response_minutes::numeric) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(tm.avg_resolution_minutes::numeric) AS avg_resolution_minutes
FROM all_rows r
LEFT JOIN ticket_metrics tm ON tm.agent_group_name = r.agent_group_name
LEFT JOIN agent_counts ac ON ac.agent_group_name = r.agent_group_name
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN r.agent_group_name = 'Unassigned queue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
  COALESCE(tm.ticket_count,0) DESC,
  r.agent_group_name

columns_requested: open_ticket_count (status not in solved, closed, as of 2025-12-31)

question: Is there a time-of-day or day-of-week pattern to when we breach first-response and resolution SLA targets?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS ticket_id,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    cd.day_name,
    cd.iso_day_of_week,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.created_at)::int AS hr
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(t.created_at AS date)
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    ticket_id,
    created_at,
    first_response_at,
    day_name,
    iso_day_of_week,
    CASE
      WHEN hr >= 0 AND hr < 6 THEN 'Night (00-06)'
      WHEN hr >= 6 AND hr < 12 THEN 'Morning (06-12)'
      WHEN hr >= 12 AND hr < 18 THEN 'Afternoon (12-18)'
      ELSE 'Evening (18-24)'
    END AS time_of_day_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN hr >= 0 AND hr < 6 THEN 1
      WHEN hr >= 6 AND hr < 12 THEN 2
      WHEN hr >= 12 AND hr < 18 THEN 3
      ELSE 4
    END AS bucket_order
  FROM base
),
breaches AS (
  SELECT
    ticket_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN breach_kind = 'first_response' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fr_breach,
    MAX(CASE WHEN breach_kind = 'resolution' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS res_breach
  FROM sla_breaches
  GROUP BY ticket_id
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    b.*,
    COALESCE(br.fr_breach, 0) AS fr_breach,
    COALESCE(br.res_breach, 0) AS res_breach
  FROM bucketed b
  LEFT JOIN breaches br ON br.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
)
SELECT
  day_name AS day_of_week,
  time_of_day_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(fr_breach) / COUNT(*), 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(res_breach) / COUNT(*), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN first_response_at IS NOT NULL
                 THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at)) / 60.0
            END)) AS avg_first_response_minutes
FROM joined
GROUP BY day_name, iso_day_of_week, time_of_day_bucket, bucket_order
ORDER BY iso_day_of_week, bucket_order

question: At the real operational unit (one merchant's one agent group), where is ticket load heaviest, and does staffing (agent count) look right for that load?
sql:
WITH ticket_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, agent_group_id,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE assignee_agent_id IS NULL) AS unassigned_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM tickets
  WHERE agent_group_id IS NOT NULL
    AND created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id, agent_group_id
),
breach_agg AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, t.agent_group_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sb.ticket_id) AS resolution_breach_count
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = t.id AND sb.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.agent_group_id IS NOT NULL
    AND t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id, t.agent_group_id
),
agent_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, agent_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT support_agent_id) AS agent_count
  FROM agent_group_members
  GROUP BY tenant_id, agent_group_id
)
SELECT
  ten.name AS tenant_name,
  ag.name AS agent_group_name,
  ta.ticket_count,
  COALESCE(ac.agent_count,0) AS agent_count,
  ROUND(ta.ticket_count::numeric / NULLIF(ac.agent_count,0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.unassigned_count / NULLIF(ta.ticket_count,0), 1) AS pct_unassigned,
  ROUND(ta.avg_first_response_minutes::numeric, 1) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(ta.avg_resolution_minutes::numeric, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(ba.resolution_breach_count,0) / NULLIF(ta.ticket_count,0), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM ticket_agg ta
JOIN tenants ten ON ten.id = ta.tenant_id
JOIN agent_groups ag ON ag.id = ta.agent_group_id
LEFT JOIN agent_counts ac ON ac.tenant_id = ta.tenant_id AND ac.agent_group_id = ta.agent_group_id
LEFT JOIN breach_agg ba ON ba.tenant_id = ta.tenant_id AND ba.agent_group_id = ta.agent_group_id
ORDER BY ta.ticket_count DESC, ten.name, ag.name
LIMIT 20

question: Is ticket volume and SLA breach pain concentrated in a handful of merchants, and do any merchants stand out as outliers?
sql:
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  ticket_count,
  round(pct_of_total_tickets, 1) AS pct_of_total_tickets,
  round(sum(pct_of_total_tickets) OVER (ORDER BY ticket_count DESC, tenant_name), 1) AS cumulative_pct_of_total_tickets,
  round(first_response_breach_rate, 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  round(resolution_breach_rate, 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  round(avg_resolution_minutes, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  agent_count,
  total_tenants_with_tickets
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    tk.tenant_id,
    tk.ticket_count,
    100.0 * tk.ticket_count / tot.total_tickets AS pct_of_total_tickets,
    100.0 * coalesce(frb.breach_count, 0) / nullif(tk.sla_ticket_count, 0) AS first_response_breach_rate,
    100.0 * coalesce(rb.breach_count, 0) / nullif(tk.sla_ticket_count, 0) AS resolution_breach_rate,
    tk.avg_resolution_minutes,
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT sa.id) FROM support_agents sa WHERE sa.tenant_id = tk.tenant_id) AS agent_count,
    tot.total_tickets,
    tnt.total_tenants_with_tickets
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tenant_id,
      count(*) AS ticket_count,
      count(*) FILTER (WHERE sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL) AS sla_ticket_count,
      avg(extract(epoch FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 60.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ) tk
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tk.tenant_id
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT count(*) AS total_tickets
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  ) tot
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS total_tenants_with_tickets
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  ) tnt
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT sb.tenant_id, count(*) AS breach_count
    FROM sla_breaches sb
    JOIN tickets tk2 ON tk2.id = sb.ticket_id
    WHERE sb.breach_kind = 'first_response'
      AND tk2.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND tk2.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      AND tk2.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY sb.tenant_id
  ) frb ON frb.tenant_id = tk.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT sb.tenant_id, count(*) AS breach_count
    FROM sla_breaches sb
    JOIN tickets tk3 ON tk3.id = sb.ticket_id
    WHERE sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
      AND tk3.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND tk3.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      AND tk3.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY sb.tenant_id
  ) rb ON rb.tenant_id = tk.tenant_id
) x
ORDER BY ticket_count DESC, tenant_name
LIMIT 30

question: What values does sla_breaches.breach_kind actually take, and do our assumed codes ('first_response', 'resolution') account for all breach rows so last night's breach-rate numbers can be trusted?

with sla_breaches_2025 as (

)

    breach_kind,
    row_count,
    distinct_tickets_affected,
    round(avg_minutes_over, 1) as avg_minutes_over,
    min_minutes_over,
    max_minutes_over,
    earliest_breached_at,
    latest_breached_at
from breach_kind_summary
order by row_count desc, breach_kind asc

question: How much do agents actually lean on canned-reply macros, and is usage concentrated in a few macros or spread across the library?

WITH macro_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_macro_count, SUM(usage_count) AS total_macro_usage_sum

question: Does the channel a ticket comes in on, or whether it currently sits unassigned, separate fast-resolving tickets from slow ones?
sql:
WITH ticket_window AS (
  SELECT
    t.id,
    t.tenant_id,
    t.channel,
    CASE WHEN t.assignee_agent_id IS NULL THEN 'Unassigned' ELSE 'Assigned' END AS assignment_status,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ticket_breach_flags AS (
  SELECT
    tw.id AS ticket_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN sb.breach_kind = 'first_response' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first_response_breached,
    MAX(CASE WHEN sb.breach_kind = 'resolution' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS resolution_breached
  FROM ticket_window tw
  LEFT JOIN sla_breaches sb
    ON sb.ticket_id = tw.id AND sb.tenant_id = tw.tenant_id
  GROUP BY tw.id
),
ticket_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tw.id,
    tw.channel,
    tw.assignment_status,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tw.first_response_at - tw.created_at)) / 60.0 AS first_response_minutes,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tw.resolved_at - tw.created_at)) / 60.0 AS resolution_minutes,
    bf.first_response_breached,
    bf.resolution_breached
  FROM ticket_window tw
  JOIN ticket_breach_flags bf ON bf.ticket_id = tw.id
)
SELECT
  channel,
  assignment_status,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(AVG(first_response_minutes)::numeric, 0) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(AVG(resolution_minutes)::numeric, 0) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(first_response_breached)::numeric, 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(resolution_breached)::numeric, 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM ticket_metrics
GROUP BY channel, assignment_status
ORDER BY avg_resolution_minutes DESC, channel, assignment_status

question: Does customer satisfaction after a resolved ticket track with how fast it was resolved and whether it breached SLA, or does something else seem to drive it?
sql:
SELECT
  bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(AVG(score), 2) AS avg_csat_score,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN breached THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_resolution_sla_breached,
  ROUND(AVG(resolution_minutes)) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  MIN(bucket_order) AS bucket_order
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.id AS ticket_id,
    c.score AS score,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 60.0 AS resolution_minutes,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM sla_breaches sb
      WHERE sb.ticket_id = t.id AND sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
    ) AS breached,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 4 THEN 'Under 4h'
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 24 THEN '4-24h'
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 72 THEN '1-3 days'
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 168 THEN '3-7 days'
      ELSE 'Over 7 days'
    END AS bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 4 THEN 1
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 24 THEN 2
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 72 THEN 3
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 168 THEN 4
      ELSE 5
    END AS bucket_order
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN csat_responses c ON c.ticket_id = t.id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
) x
GROUP BY bucket
ORDER BY bucket_order

question: Which knowledge base articles get used, and are the ones we have actually rated as helpful by customers?
sql:
WITH published AS (
  SELECT ka.id, ka.title, kc.name AS category_name, ka.view_count, ka.helpful_count, ka.not_helpful_count
  FROM knowledge_articles ka
  LEFT JOIN knowledge_categories kc ON kc.id = ka.knowledge_category_id
  WHERE ka.is_published = true AND ka.deleted_at IS NULL
),
agg AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_published_articles,
         SUM(helpful_count) AS total_helpful,
         SUM(helpful_count + not_helpful_count) AS total_votes
  FROM published
)
SELECT
  p.title,
  p.category_name AS knowledge_category_name,
  p.view_count,
  p.helpful_count,
  p.not_helpful_count,
  CASE WHEN (p.helpful_count + p.not_helpful_count) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(p.helpful_count::numeric / (p.helpful_count + p.not_helpful_count), 4)
  END AS helpful_rate,
  a.total_published_articles,
  ROUND(a.total_helpful::numeric / NULLIF(a.total_votes,0), 4) AS platform_avg_helpful_rate
FROM published p
CROSS JOIN agg a
ORDER BY p.view_count DESC, p.id ASC
LIMIT 20

columns_requested: helpful_rate (helpful_count / (helpful_count + not_helpful_count), null if no feedback)
total_published_articles (constant: count of knowledge_articles with is_published = true and deleted_at is null)
platform_avg_helpful_rate (constant: sum(helpful_count) / sum(helpful_count + not_helpful_count) across all published articles)

question: Are certain ticket topics (support tags) driving a disproportionate share of volume or taking much longer to resolve than others?
sql:
WITH tickets_2025 AS (
  SELECT id, tenant_id, created_at, first_response_at, resolved_at
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tagged AS (
  SELECT
    ttm.ticket_id,
    st.name AS tag_name,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at
  FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
  JOIN support_tags st
    ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id AND st.tenant_id = ttm.tenant_id
  JOIN tickets_2025 t
    ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id
),
breaches_per_ticket AS (
  SELECT
    ticket_id,
    BOOL_OR(breach_kind = 'first_response') AS fr_breach,
    BOOL_OR(breach_kind = 'resolution') AS res_breach
  FROM sla_breaches
  WHERE breach_kind IN ('first_response', 'resolution')
  GROUP BY ticket_id
),
tag_stats AS (
  SELECT
    tagged.tag_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tagged.ticket_id) AS ticket_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tagged.first_response_at - tagged.created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE tagged.first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tagged.resolved_at - tagged.created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE tagged.resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tagged.ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE bpt.fr_breach) AS fr_breach_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tagged.ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE bpt.res_breach) AS res_breach_count
  FROM tagged
  LEFT JOIN breaches_per_ticket bpt ON bpt.ticket_id = tagged.ticket_id
  GROUP BY tagged.tag_name
),
totals AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets_2025) AS total_tickets_2025,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ttm.ticket_id)
       FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
       JOIN tickets_2025 t ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id) AS total_tagged_tickets_2025
)
SELECT
  tag_stats.tag_name,
  tag_stats.ticket_count,
  ROUND(tag_stats.avg_first_response_minutes, 1) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(tag_stats.avg_resolution_minutes, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(tag_stats.fr_breach_count::numeric / NULLIF(tag_stats.ticket_count, 0), 4) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(tag_stats.res_breach_count::numeric / NULLIF(tag_stats.ticket_count, 0), 4) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  totals.total_tagged_tickets_2025,
  totals.total_tickets_2025
FROM tag_stats
CROSS JOIN totals
ORDER BY tag_stats.ticket_count DESC, tag_stats.tag_name ASC
LIMIT 20

question: Does our 2025 fee-revenue total hold up when broken down by currency, and which currencies carry our FX exposure?
sql:
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT
    p.currency_code,
    COUNT(*) AS payout_count,
    SUM(p.gross_amount) AS total_gross_native,
    SUM(p.fee_amount) AS total_fee_native,
    SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS total_gross_eur,
    SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS total_fee_eur
  FROM payouts p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = date(p.paid_at)
  WHERE p.status = 'paid'
    AND p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.currency_code
)
SELECT
  currency_code,
  payout_count,
  ROUND(total_gross_native, 2) AS total_gross_native,
  ROUND(total_fee_native, 2) AS total_fee_native,
  ROUND(total_gross_eur, 2) AS total_gross_eur,
  ROUND(total_fee_eur, 2) AS total_fee_eur,
  ROUND(total_fee_native / NULLIF(total_fee_eur,0), 4) AS implied_avg_rate_native_per_eur,
  ROUND(100 * total_fee_eur / SUM(total_fee_eur) OVER (), 2) AS share_of_total_fee_eur_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY total_fee_eur DESC, currency_code ASC

question: Is the Q4 2025 refund-rate increase concentrated in a handful of merchants, or spread broadly across the merchant base?
sql:
WITH t1 AS (
  SELECT
    t10.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t10.amount / t11.rate) AS captured_eur_q4,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t10.order_id) AS order_count_q4
  FROM payments AS t10
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t11
    ON t11.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t11.quote_code = t10.currency_code
   AND t11.as_of = CAST(t10.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE t10.status IN ('captured', 'partially_refunded', 'refunded')
    AND t10.captured_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND t10.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t10.tenant_id
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    t20.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t20.amount / t21.rate) AS captured_eur_baseline
  FROM payments AS t20
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t21
    ON t21.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t21.quote_code = t20.currency_code
   AND t21.as_of = CAST(t20.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE t20.status IN ('captured', 'partially_refunded', 'refunded')
    AND t20.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t20.captured_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY t20.tenant_id
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t30.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t30.amount / t31.rate) AS refund_eur_q4
  FROM payment_refunds AS t30
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t31
    ON t31.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t31.quote_code = t30.currency_code
   AND t31.as_of = CAST(t30.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE t30.status = 'succeeded'
    AND t30.processed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND t30.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t30.tenant_id
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT
    t40.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t40.amount / t41.rate) AS refund_eur_baseline
  FROM payment_refunds AS t40
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t41
    ON t41.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t41.quote_code = t40.currency_code
   AND t41.as_of = CAST(t40.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE t40.status = 'succeeded'
    AND t40.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t40.processed_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY t40.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t0.name AS merchant_name,
  t0.industry AS vertical,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t3.refund_eur_q4, 0) / NULLIF(t1.captured_eur_q4, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_q4_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t4.refund_eur_baseline, 0) / NULLIF(t2.captured_eur_baseline, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_baseline_pct,
  ROUND(
    (100.0 * COALESCE(t3.refund_eur_q4, 0) / NULLIF(t1.captured_eur_q4, 0))
    - (100.0 * COALESCE(t4.refund_eur_baseline, 0) / NULLIF(t2.captured_eur_baseline, 0))
  , 2) AS change_vs_baseline_pp,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t3.refund_eur_q4, 0), 2) AS refund_amount_q4_eur,
  t1.order_count_q4 AS order_count_q4
FROM tenants AS t0
JOIN t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE t1.order_count_q4 >= 10
ORDER BY change_vs_baseline_pp DESC NULLS LAST, refund_amount_q4_eur DESC, t0.id ASC

tags.details: Source: payment_refunds (status='succeeded', processed_at in quarter, amount converted to EUR via exchange_rates as_of processed_at date) as the numerator, divided by payments (status in 'captured','partially_refunded','refunded', captured_at in quarter, amount converted to EUR via exchange_rates as_of captured_at date) as the denominator, both joined to orders->tenants (or directly via payments.order_id->orders.tenant_id) to attribute to a merchant. Compute refund rate = 100 * refund EUR / captured payment EUR, once for Q4 2025 (2025-10-01 to 2026-01-01) and once pooled across Q1-Q3 2025 (2025-01-01 to 2025-10-01) as each merchant's own baseline. 'Change vs own baseline' lets us separate merchants with a structurally high rate (e.g. apparel, reportedly ~20% normally) from merchants whose rate genuinely jumped in Q4. Include only merchants with at least 10 orders in Q4 2025 to avoid noise from tiny volumes. Order by change vs own baseline descending (biggest jumps first), tie-break by refund amount Q4 2025 descending. Note total merchant count returned.
tags.grain: one row per merchant (tenant)

question: Which merchants look at risk right now, based on unpaid invoices, traffic decline, and revenue trend — our 'accounts to watch' list?
sql:
with latest_rates as (
  select distinct on (quote_code) quote_code, rate
  from exchange_rates
  where base_code = 'EUR' and as_of <= DATE '2025-12-31'
  order by quote_code, as_of desc
),
unpaid as (
  select i.tenant_id,
    sum(i.amount_due / case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then 1 else lr.rate end) as unpaid_eur
  from invoices i
  left join latest_rates lr on lr.quote_code = i.currency_code
  where i.status in ('open','past_due')
  group by i.tenant_id
),
traffic as (
  select tenant_id,
    count(*) filter (where started_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01' and started_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01') as q3_sessions,
    count(*) filter (where started_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01' and started_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01') as q4_sessions
  from web_sessions
  group by tenant_id
),
payout_rates as (
  select p.id as payout_id, p.tenant_id, p.paid_at,
    p.fee_amount / case when p.currency_code = 'EUR' then 1 else er.rate end as fee_eur
  from payouts p
  left join exchange_rates er
    on er.base_code = 'EUR' and er.quote_code = p.currency_code and er.as_of = CAST(p.paid_at AS DATE)
  where p.status = 'paid'
),
revenue as (
  select tenant_id,
    sum(fee_eur) filter (where paid_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01' and paid_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01') as q3_fee,
    sum(fee_eur) filter (where paid_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01' and paid_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01') as q4_fee
  from payout_rates
  group by tenant_id
),
last_order as (
  select tenant_id, max(placed_at) as last_placed_at
  from orders
  group by tenant_id
)
select
  t.name as merchant_name,
  t.industry as vertical,
  round(coalesce(u.unpaid_eur, 0), 2) as unpaid_invoice_balance_eur,
  round(case when tr.q3_sessions is null or tr.q3_sessions = 0 then null
             else 100.0 * (tr.q4_sessions - tr.q3_sessions) / tr.q3_sessions end, 1) as traffic_change_pct_q4_vs_q3,
  round(case when r.q3_fee is null or r.q3_fee = 0 then null
             else 100.0 * (r.q4_fee - r.q3_fee) / r.q3_fee end, 1) as fee_revenue_change_pct_q4_vs_q3,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lo.last_placed_at AS DATE)) as days_since_last_order,
  t.status as tenant_status
from tenants t
left join unpaid u on u.tenant_id = t.id
left join traffic tr on tr.tenant_id = t.id
left join revenue r on r.tenant_id = t.id
left join last_order lo on lo.tenant_id = t.id
where t.deleted_at is null
order by unpaid_invoice_balance_eur desc nulls last, traffic_change_pct_q4_vs_q3 asc nulls last, merchant_name
limit 50

question: Does the refund spike Finance flagged for Q3 2025 (naming OfficeHub Nordic and Sports & Outdoor sellers) hold up at the merchant level, and is it the same story as Q4?
sql:
WITH q3_refunds AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = pr.processed_at::date
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY pr.tenant_id
),
q3_payments AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(p.amount / er.rate) AS captured_amount_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = p.captured_at::date
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','partially_refunded','refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
h1_refunds AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = pr.processed_at::date
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY pr.tenant_id
),
h1_payments AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(p.amount / er.rate) AS captured_amount_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = p.captured_at::date
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','partially_refunded','refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
q3_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND placed_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry AS vertical,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(qr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(qp.captured_amount_eur,0), 2) AS refund_rate_q3_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(hr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(hp.captured_amount_eur,0), 2) AS refund_rate_h1_baseline_pct,
  ROUND(
    (100.0 * COALESCE(qr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(qp.captured_amount_eur,0))
    - (100.0 * COALESCE(hr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(hp.captured_amount_eur,0))
  , 2) AS change_vs_baseline_pp,
  ROUND(COALESCE(qr.refund_amount_eur,0), 2) AS refund_amount_q3_eur,
  qo.order_count AS order_count_q3
FROM q3_orders qo
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN q3_refunds qr ON qr.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN q3_payments qp ON qp.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN h1_refunds hr ON hr.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN h1_payments hp ON hp.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
WHERE qo.order_count >= 10
ORDER BY change_vs_baseline_pp DESC NULLS LAST, refund_amount_q3_eur DESC, merchant_name ASC

question: What operational cost-driver volumes do we actually have per merchant today, to serve as the measurable building blocks for a cost-to-serve model?
sql:
WITH shipment_costs AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS shipment_count,
         SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
returns_counts AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS return_count
  FROM order_returns r
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = r.order_id
  WHERE r.requested_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND r.requested_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
refund_amounts AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY pr.tenant_id
),
ticket_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
failed_webhooks AS (
  SELECT w.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS failed_webhook_count
  FROM webhook_deliveries wd
  JOIN webhooks w ON w.id = wd.webhook_id
  WHERE wd.status = 'failed'
    AND wd.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND wd.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY w.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry AS vertical,
  COALESCE(sc.shipment_count, 0) AS shipment_count_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(sc.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS total_shipping_cost_eur_2025,
  COALESCE(rc.return_count, 0) AS return_count_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ra.refund_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS refund_amount_eur_2025,
  COALESCE(tc.ticket_count, 0) AS ticket_count_2025,
  COALESCE(fw.failed_webhook_count, 0) AS failed_webhook_count_2025
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN shipment_costs sc ON sc.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN returns_counts rc ON rc.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN refund_amounts ra ON ra.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN ticket_counts tc ON tc.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN failed_webhooks fw ON fw.tenant_id = t.id
ORDER BY total_shipping_cost_eur_2025 DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
