question: Which merchants are slowest to pay their invoices, how large and how overdue are the balances, and is this concentrated in B2B wholesale?
sql:
SELECT t0.name AS merchant_name,
       COALESCE(t0.industry, 'Unknown') AS vertical,
       ROUND(COALESCE(m1.total_unpaid_eur,0),2) AS total_unpaid_balance_eur,
       COALESCE(m2.open_invoice_count,0) AS open_invoice_count,
       COALESCE(m3.days_overdue_oldest,0) AS days_overdue_oldest,
       ROUND(COALESCE(m4.largest_unpaid_eur,0),2) AS largest_unpaid_invoice_eur,
       m5.net_terms_days AS net_terms_days
FROM tenants t0
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT i0.tenant_id,
           SUM(i0.amount_due / CASE WHEN i0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx0.rate END) AS total_unpaid_eur
    FROM invoices i0
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT er0.quote_code AS currency_code, er0.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er0
        WHERE er0.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er0.as_of = (
              SELECT MAX(er1.as_of)
              FROM exchange_rates er1
              WHERE er1.base_code = 'EUR'
                AND er1.quote_code = er0.quote_code
                AND er1.as_of <= DATE '2025-12-31'
          )
    ) fx0 ON fx0.currency_code = i0.currency_code
    WHERE i0.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i0.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i0.tenant_id
) m1 ON m1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT i2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS open_invoice_count
    FROM invoices i2
    WHERE i2.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i2.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i2.tenant_id
) m2 ON m2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT i3.tenant_id,
           GREATEST(0, CAST(DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(i3.due_at) AS DATE) AS INTEGER)) AS days_overdue_oldest
    FROM invoices i3
    WHERE i3.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i3.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i3.tenant_id
) m3 ON m3.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT i4.tenant_id,
           MAX(i4.amount_due / CASE WHEN i4.currency_code='EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx4.rate END) AS largest_unpaid_eur
    FROM invoices i4
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT er2.quote_code AS currency_code, er2.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er2
        WHERE er2.base_code='EUR'
          AND er2.as_of = (
              SELECT MAX(er3.as_of) FROM exchange_rates er3
              WHERE er3.base_code='EUR' AND er3.quote_code=er2.quote_code AND er3.as_of <= DATE '2025-12-31'
          )
    ) fx4 ON fx4.currency_code = i4.currency_code
    WHERE i4.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i4.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i4.tenant_id
) m4 ON m4.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT bp0.tenant_id, MAX(bp0.net_terms_days) AS net_terms_days
    FROM billing_profiles bp0
    WHERE bp0.is_default = true AND bp0.deleted_at IS NULL
    GROUP BY bp0.tenant_id
) m5 ON m5.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE COALESCE(m1.total_unpaid_eur,0) <> 0
ORDER BY total_unpaid_balance_eur DESC, days_overdue_oldest DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50

question: Is Deskline Supplies' unusually high average shipping cost (~€1,038/shipment vs. ~€4-30/shipment for comparable merchants) a real freight-cost pattern or a data outlier?
sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT t1.id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants t1
  WHERE t1.name = 'Deskline Supplies'
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    s.carrier AS carrier,
    s.service_level AS service_level,
    s.shipping_cost AS shipping_cost,
    COALESCE(s.currency_code, tn.default_currency_code) AS ship_currency_code,
    s.shipped_at AS shipped_at
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  JOIN t0 ON t0.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
  JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = s.tenant_id
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t2.carrier AS carrier,
    t2.service_level AS service_level,
    t2.shipping_cost AS shipping_cost,
    CASE
      WHEN t2.ship_currency_code = 'EUR' THEN t2.shipping_cost
      ELSE t2.shipping_cost / er.rate
    END AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM t2
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = t2.ship_currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(t2.shipped_at AS date)
)
SELECT
  t3.carrier AS carrier,
  t3.service_level AS service_level,
  COUNT(*) AS shipment_count_2025,
  ROUND(SUM(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS total_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS avg_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(MIN(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS min_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(MAX(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS max_shipping_cost_eur
FROM t3
GROUP BY t3.carrier, t3.service_level
ORDER BY total_shipping_cost_eur DESC, t3.carrier ASC, t3.service_level ASC

question: Which merchants are currently behind on paying us or already cut off, and how big/active are they — our clearest churn-risk signal?
sql:
WITH tenant_base AS (
  SELECT t.id AS tenant_id, t.name AS merchant_name, t.industry AS vertical, t.status AS tenant_status, t.created_at
  FROM tenants t
  WHERE t.status IN ('past_due','suspended','churned') AND t.deleted_at IS NULL
),
last_order AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, MAX(placed_at) AS last_order_at
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
last_paid_payout AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, MAX(paid_at) AS last_paid_payout_at
  FROM payouts
  WHERE status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
fee_revenue_ttm AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p.fee_amount ELSE p.fee_amount / er.rate END) AS fee_revenue_eur
  FROM payouts p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.paid_at AS date)
  WHERE p.status = 'paid'
    AND p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tb.merchant_name,
  tb.vertical,
  tb.tenant_status,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(tb.created_at AS date)) AS tenure_days,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lo.last_order_at AS date)) AS days_since_last_order,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lp.last_paid_payout_at AS date)) AS days_since_last_paid_payout,
  ROUND(COALESCE(fr.fee_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS fee_revenue_ttm_eur
FROM tenant_base tb
LEFT JOIN last_order lo ON lo.tenant_id = tb.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN last_paid_payout lp ON lp.tenant_id = tb.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN fee_revenue_ttm fr ON fr.tenant_id = tb.tenant_id
ORDER BY
  CASE tb.tenant_status WHEN 'churned' THEN 1 WHEN 'suspended' THEN 2 WHEN 'past_due' THEN 3 END,
  fee_revenue_ttm_eur DESC,
  tb.merchant_name ASC

question: Using only the revenue and cost signals we currently trust, which verticals look directionally profitable to grow versus costly to serve?
sql:
WITH t_industry AS (
  SELECT
    t0.id AS tenant_id,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(t0.industry), ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical
  FROM tenants t0
),
d_vertical AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ti0.vertical AS vertical
  FROM t_industry ti0
),
m_merchants AS (
  SELECT
    ti1.vertical AS vertical,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ti1.tenant_id) AS merchant_count
  FROM t_industry ti1
  GROUP BY ti1.vertical
),
m_fee AS (
  SELECT
    ti2.vertical AS vertical,
    SUM(p0.fee_amount / COALESCE(er0.rate, CASE WHEN p0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 END)) AS fee_revenue_eur
  FROM payouts p0
  JOIN t_industry ti2 ON ti2.tenant_id = p0.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er0.quote_code = p0.currency_code
    AND er0.as_of = CAST(p0.paid_at AS date)
  WHERE p0.status = 'paid'
    AND p0.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p0.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti2.vertical
),
m_shipping AS (
  SELECT
    ti3.vertical AS vertical,
    SUM(s0.shipping_cost / COALESCE(er1.rate, CASE WHEN s0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 END)) AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM shipments s0
  JOIN t_industry ti3 ON ti3.tenant_id = s0.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er1.quote_code = s0.currency_code
    AND er1.as_of = CAST(s0.shipped_at AS date)
  WHERE s0.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s0.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND s0.shipping_cost IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ti3.vertical
),
m_refund AS (
  SELECT
    ti4.vertical AS vertical,
    SUM(r0.refund_total / COALESCE(er2.rate, CASE WHEN r0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 END)) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM order_returns r0
  JOIN t_industry ti4 ON ti4.tenant_id = r0.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er2.quote_code = r0.currency_code
    AND er2.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(r0.refunded_at, r0.requested_at) AS date)
  WHERE r0.status = 'refunded'
    AND COALESCE(r0.refunded_at, r0.requested_at) >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND COALESCE(r0.refunded_at, r0.requested_at) < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti4.vertical
),
m_tickets AS (
  SELECT
    ti5.vertical AS vertical,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets tk0
  JOIN t_industry ti5 ON ti5.tenant_id = tk0.tenant_id
  WHERE tk0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND tk0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti5.vertical
)
SELECT
  d0.vertical AS vertical,
  COALESCE(mm0.merchant_count, 0) AS merchant_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS fee_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ms0.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mr0.refund_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS refund_amount_eur,
  COALESCE(mt0.ticket_count, 0) AS support_ticket_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(ms0.shipping_cost_eur, 0) - COALESCE(mr0.refund_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS rough_net_contribution_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE 100.0 * (COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(ms0.shipping_cost_eur, 0) - COALESCE(mr0.refund_amount_eur, 0)) / mf0.fee_revenue_eur
    END, 1
  ) AS net_contribution_pct_of_fee_revenue
FROM d_vertical d0
LEFT JOIN m_merchants mm0 ON mm0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_fee mf0 ON mf0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_shipping ms0 ON ms0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_refund mr0 ON mr0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_tickets mt0 ON mt0.vertical = d0.vertical
ORDER BY rough_net_contribution_eur DESC, d0.vertical ASC

question: Is shipping actually a net cost exposure, or does what we collect from customers for shipping roughly cover what we pay carriers?
sql:
WITH order_rev AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(NULLIF(t.industry, ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.shipping_total / er.rate) AS shipping_revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'partially_fulfilled', 'fulfilled', 'refunded')
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
),
ship_cost AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(NULLIF(t.industry, ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical,
    SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(r.vertical, c.vertical) AS vertical,
  COALESCE(r.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(c.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(c.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_margin_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0) <> 0
      THEN (COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(c.shipping_cost_eur, 0)) / r.shipping_revenue_eur * 100
      ELSE NULL
    END, 1
  ) AS shipping_margin_pct
FROM order_rev r
FULL OUTER JOIN ship_cost c ON r.vertical = c.vertical
ORDER BY shipping_margin_eur ASC, vertical ASC

question: Among our largest merchants, which look efficient versus costly to serve on a like-for-like rate basis?
sql:
WITH payout_eur AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS gross_eur,
         SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS fee_eur
  FROM payouts p
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code AND er.as_of = p.paid_at::date
  WHERE p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
returns_eur AS (
  SELECT r.tenant_id,
         SUM(r.refund_total / er.rate) AS refund_eur
  FROM order_returns r
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = r.currency_code AND er.as_of = r.requested_at::date
  WHERE r.requested_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND r.requested_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY r.tenant_id
),
shipping_eur AS (
  SELECT s.tenant_id,
         SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_eur
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code AND er.as_of = s.shipped_at::date
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01' AND s.shipping_cost IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY s.tenant_id
),
orders_cnt AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_2025
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
tickets_cnt AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS tickets_2025
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT t.name AS merchant_name,
       t.industry AS vertical,
       ROUND(pe.gross_eur, 2) AS gross_payment_volume_eur,
       ROUND(pe.fee_eur, 2) AS fee_revenue_eur,
       ROUND(100 * pe.fee_eur / NULLIF(pe.gross_eur, 0), 2) AS take_rate_pct,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(re.refund_eur, 0) / NULLIF(pe.gross_eur, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(se.shipping_eur, 0) / NULLIF(pe.gross_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_cost_rate_pct,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(tc.tickets_2025, 0) / NULLIF(oc.orders_2025, 0)::numeric, 2) AS tickets_per_100_orders
FROM payout_eur pe
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN returns_eur re ON re.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN shipping_eur se ON se.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN orders_cnt oc ON oc.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN tickets_cnt tc ON tc.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
ORDER BY pe.gross_eur DESC, t.name
LIMIT 20

question: Which verticals look efficient versus costly to serve, measured as comparable rates against gross payment volume rather than misleading absolute euros against our thin fee take?
sql:
WITH tenant_industry AS (
    SELECT
        id AS tenant_id,
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(industry), ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical
    FROM tenants
),

payout_totals AS (
    SELECT
        p.tenant_id,
        SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS gross_eur,
        SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS fee_eur
    FROM payouts p
    JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(p.paid_at AS date)
    WHERE p.status = 'paid'
        AND p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),

refund_totals AS (
    SELECT
        r.tenant_id,
        SUM(r.refund_total / er.rate) AS refund_eur
    FROM order_returns r
    JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = r.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(r.refunded_at, r.requested_at) AS date)
    WHERE r.status = 'refunded'
        AND COALESCE(r.refunded_at, r.requested_at) >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND COALESCE(r.refunded_at, r.requested_at) < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY r.tenant_id
),

shipping_totals AS (
    SELECT
        o.tenant_id,
        SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_eur
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
    JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
    JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)
    WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
        AND s.shipping_cost IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),

order_counts AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM orders
    WHERE status IN ('paid', 'partially_fulfilled', 'fulfilled', 'refunded')
        AND placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
),

ticket_counts AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
),

merchant_counts AS (
    SELECT
        vertical,
        COUNT(*) AS merchant_count
    FROM tenant_industry
    GROUP BY vertical
),

tenant_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        ti.tenant_id,
        ti.vertical,
        COALESCE(pt.gross_eur, 0) AS gross_eur,
        COALESCE(pt.fee_eur, 0) AS fee_eur,
        COALESCE(rt.refund_eur, 0) AS refund_eur,
        COALESCE(st.shipping_eur, 0) AS shipping_eur,
        COALESCE(oc.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
        COALESCE(tc.ticket_count, 0) AS ticket_count
    FROM tenant_industry ti
    LEFT JOIN payout_totals pt ON pt.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN refund_totals rt ON rt.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN shipping_totals st ON st.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN order_counts oc ON oc.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN ticket_counts tc ON tc.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
),

vertical_agg AS (
    SELECT
        vertical,
        SUM(gross_eur) AS gross_eur,
        SUM(fee_eur) AS fee_eur,
        SUM(refund_eur) AS refund_eur,
        SUM(shipping_eur) AS shipping_eur,
        SUM(order_count) AS order_count,
        SUM(ticket_count) AS ticket_count
    FROM tenant_metrics
    GROUP BY vertical
)

SELECT
    va.vertical AS vertical,
    mc.merchant_count AS merchant_count,
    ROUND(va.gross_eur, 2) AS gross_payment_volume_eur,
    ROUND(va.fee_eur, 2) AS fee_revenue_eur,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.gross_eur = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.fee_eur / va.gross_eur END, 2) AS take_rate_pct,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.gross_eur = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.refund_eur / va.gross_eur END, 2) AS refund_rate_pct,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.gross_eur = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.shipping_eur / va.gross_eur END, 2) AS shipping_cost_rate_pct,
    va.order_count AS order_count_2025,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.order_count = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.ticket_count / va.order_count END, 2) AS tickets_per_100_orders
FROM vertical_agg va
JOIN merchant_counts mc ON mc.vertical = va.vertical
ORDER BY va.gross_eur DESC, va.vertical ASC

question: Roughly how much discount euro value comes from the same customer reusing a coupon code multiple times, given no usage or per-customer limit is enforced?
sql:
with redemptions as (
  select
    cr.coupon_id,
    c.code as coupon_code,
    d.kind as discount_kind,
    cr.user_id,
    cr.redeemed_at,
    cr.discount_amount / er.rate as discount_amount_eur,
    row_number() over (partition by cr.coupon_id, cr.user_id order by cr.redeemed_at asc, cr.id asc) as rn
  from coupon_redemptions cr
  join coupons c on c.id = cr.coupon_id
  join discounts d on d.id = c.discount_id
  join exchange_rates er
    on er.base_code = 'EUR'
   and er.quote_code = cr.currency_code
   and er.as_of = cast(cr.redeemed_at as date)
  where cr.redeemed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
    and cr.redeemed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
)
select
  coupon_code,
  discount_kind,
  count(*) as total_redemptions_2025,
  count(distinct user_id) as distinct_customers_2025,
  count(*) - count(distinct user_id) as redemptions_beyond_first_use,
  round(sum(discount_amount_eur), 2) as total_discount_amount_eur,
  round(sum(discount_amount_eur) filter (where rn > 1), 2) as discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur,
  round(100.0 * sum(discount_amount_eur) filter (where rn > 1) / nullif(sum(discount_amount_eur), 0), 2) as pct_of_discount_from_repeat_use
from redemptions
group by coupon_id, coupon_code, discount_kind
order by discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur desc nulls last, coupon_code asc
limit 20

columns_requested: discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur (excess discount from a customer's 2nd+ redemption of the same code)
tags.details: Source: coupon_redemptions joined to coupons (for code, and discount_id -> discounts for discount_kind), filtered to redeemed_at in calendar year 2025. Convert discount_amount to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=coupon_redemptions.currency_code, as_of=date(redeemed_at)). Group by coupon_id/code. distinct_customers_2025 counts distinct user_id redeeming that code in 2025. redemptions_beyond_first_use = total_redemptions_2025 - distinct_customers_2025 (i.e., repeat uses by the same customer beyond their first). discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur: for each (coupon, user_id) pair, sum discount_amount_eur from all but the earliest redemption (by redeemed_at) for that user, then sum across users for the coupon. pct_of_discount_from_repeat_use = discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur / total_discount_amount_eur * 100. Order by discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur descending; print top 20 coupons and note total number of distinct coupons redeemed in 2025.
tags.grain: one coupon code, for redemptions in 2025

question: Does the 16-40% quarterly gap between payments-based and order_returns-based refund totals come from refunds simply landing in a later quarter than the original purchase, rather than from missing or double-counted data?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT t0.id AS return_id, t0.order_id, t0.refund_total, t0.currency_code, t0.refunded_at
  FROM order_returns t0
  WHERE t0.status = 'refunded'
    AND t0.refunded_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t0.refunded_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
first_payment AS (
  SELECT t1.order_id, MIN(t1.captured_at) AS first_captured_at
  FROM payments t1
  WHERE t1.captured_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t1.order_id
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    b.return_id,
    b.refund_total,
    b.currency_code,
    b.refunded_at,
    o.id AS order_id,
    fp.first_captured_at
  FROM base b
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = b.order_id
  LEFT JOIN first_payment fp ON fp.order_id = o.id
),
rated AS (
  SELECT
    j.*,
    CASE WHEN j.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0
         ELSE er.rate END AS fx_rate
  FROM joined j
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = j.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(j.refunded_at AS date)
),
categorized AS (
  SELECT
    r.*,
    CASE WHEN r.fx_rate IS NULL OR r.fx_rate = 0 THEN NULL ELSE r.refund_total / r.fx_rate END AS refund_amount_eur,
    CASE WHEN r.first_captured_at IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.refunded_at)*4 + EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM r.refunded_at))
            - (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.first_captured_at)*4 + EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM r.first_captured_at))
    END AS quarter_diff,
    CASE WHEN r.first_captured_at IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.refunded_at - r.first_captured_at)) / 86400.0
    END AS lag_days
  FROM rated r
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    CASE
      WHEN c.quarter_diff IS NULL THEN 'no matching payment found'
      WHEN c.quarter_diff <= 0 THEN 'same quarter as purchase'
      WHEN c.quarter_diff = 1 THEN 'purchase 1 quarter earlier'
      ELSE 'purchase 2+ quarters earlier'
    END AS lag_category
  FROM categorized c
)
SELECT
  b.lag_category,
  COUNT(*) AS return_count,
  ROUND(SUM(b.refund_amount_eur), 2) AS refund_amount_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(b.refund_amount_eur) / SUM(SUM(b.refund_amount_eur)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_total_2025_refund_amount,
  ROUND(AVG(b.lag_days), 1) AS avg_lag_days
FROM bucketed b
GROUP BY b.lag_category
ORDER BY return_count DESC, b.lag_category ASC

builds_on: Refund Figures Cross-Check: Payments vs Order Returns, 2025
columns_requested: lag_category ('same quarter as purchase', 'purchase 1 quarter earlier', 'purchase 2+ quarters earlier', 'no matching payment found')
avg_lag_days (refunded_at minus the originating payment's captured_at)
tags.details: Source: order_returns with status='refunded' and refunded_at in calendar year 2025, LEFT JOIN orders on order_returns.order_id, LEFT JOIN payments on payments.order_id = orders.id (if an order has multiple payments, use the earliest captured_at). Convert order_returns.refund_total to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=order_returns.currency_code, as_of=date(refunded_at)). Compute the calendar quarter of refunded_at and the calendar quarter of the matched payment's captured_at; bucket into the four lag_category values based on how many quarters apart they are (or 'no matching payment found' if the join fails). avg_lag_days is the average of (refunded_at - captured_at) in days within each bucket (null for the no-match bucket). Order by return_count descending.

question: For a representative sample of 2025 transactions, does the shopper payment amount, any refund, the resulting merchant payout (gross/fee/net), and the linked ledger entries all tie out consistently?
sql:
WITH base_payments AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS payment_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.order_id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount AS payment_amount,
    p.amount_refunded,
    p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND p.order_id IS NOT NULL
),
fx_rates AS (
  SELECT quote_code, as_of, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
payments_with_eur AS (
  SELECT
    bp.*,
    CASE WHEN bp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN bp.payment_amount
         ELSE bp.payment_amount / fx.rate END AS payment_amount_eur
  FROM base_payments bp
  LEFT JOIN fx_rates fx
    ON fx.quote_code = bp.currency_code
   AND fx.as_of = CAST(bp.captured_at AS date)
),
payout_agg AS (
  SELECT payment_id, amount AS payout_item_amount, fee_amount AS payout_item_fee_amount
  FROM payout_items
),
ledger_agg AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'debit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS ledger_debit_total,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'credit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS ledger_credit_total
  FROM ledger_entries
  WHERE payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY payment_id
),
enriched AS (
  SELECT
    pwe.payment_id,
    pwe.tenant_id,
    pwe.order_id,
    pwe.currency_code,
    pwe.payment_amount,
    pwe.amount_refunded,
    pwe.payment_amount_eur,
    pa.payout_item_amount,
    pa.payout_item_fee_amount,
    la.ledger_debit_total,
    la.ledger_credit_total
  FROM payments_with_eur pwe
  LEFT JOIN payout_agg pa ON pa.payment_id = pwe.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN ledger_agg la ON la.payment_id = pwe.payment_id
),
tenant_top_payment AS (
  SELECT e.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.tenant_id ORDER BY e.payment_amount_eur DESC) AS tenant_rn
  FROM enriched e
),
largest_sample AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
    payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
    ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'A_LARGEST' AS sample_category
  FROM tenant_top_payment
  WHERE tenant_rn = 1
  ORDER BY payment_amount_eur DESC
  LIMIT 8
),
refund_candidates AS (
  SELECT
    e.*,
    CASE WHEN e.amount_refunded = e.payment_amount THEN 'FULL' ELSE 'PARTIAL' END AS refund_kind
  FROM enriched e
  WHERE e.amount_refunded > 0
),
refund_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    rc.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rc.tenant_id, rc.refund_kind ORDER BY rc.amount_refunded DESC) AS tenant_refund_rn
  FROM refund_candidates rc
),
refund_sample AS (
  (SELECT payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
          payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
          ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'B_REFUND' AS sample_category
   FROM refund_ranked WHERE refund_kind = 'FULL' AND tenant_refund_rn = 1
   ORDER BY amount_refunded DESC LIMIT 4)
  UNION ALL
  (SELECT payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
          payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
          ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'B_REFUND' AS sample_category
   FROM refund_ranked WHERE refund_kind = 'PARTIAL' AND tenant_refund_rn = 1
   ORDER BY amount_refunded DESC LIMIT 4)
),
tiled AS (
  SELECT e.*, NTILE(9) OVER (ORDER BY e.payment_id) AS tile
  FROM enriched e
),
tiled_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    t.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.tile ORDER BY (t.payout_item_amount IS NULL) DESC, t.payment_id) AS tile_rn
  FROM tiled t
),
typical_sample AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
    payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
    ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'C_TYPICAL' AS sample_category
  FROM tiled_ranked
  WHERE tile_rn = 1
),
all_samples AS (
  SELECT * FROM largest_sample
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM refund_sample
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM typical_sample
),
final AS (
  SELECT
    s.payment_id,
    o.order_number,
    t.name AS merchant_name,
    s.currency_code,
    s.payment_amount,
    s.amount_refunded,
    (s.payment_amount - s.amount_refunded) AS net_amount,
    s.payout_item_amount,
    s.payout_item_fee_amount,
    (s.payout_item_amount - s.payout_item_fee_amount) AS payout_net_amount,
    (COALESCE(s.ledger_debit_total,0) - COALESCE(s.ledger_credit_total,0)) AS ledger_debit_credit_diff,
    s.ledger_credit_total,
    CASE
      WHEN s.payout_item_amount IS NULL THEN 'PENDING PAYOUT'
      WHEN (s.payment_amount - s.amount_refunded) = s.payout_item_amount
           AND (COALESCE(s.ledger_debit_total,0) - COALESCE(s.ledger_credit_total,0)) = 0
        THEN 'OK'
      ELSE 'CHECK'
    END AS reconciliation_flag,
    s.sample_category
  FROM all_samples s
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = s.order_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = s.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  order_number,
  merchant_name,
  currency_code,
  payment_amount,
  amount_refunded,
  net_amount,
  payout_item_amount,
  payout_item_fee_amount,
  payout_net_amount,
  ledger_debit_credit_diff,
  ledger_credit_total,
  reconciliation_flag
FROM final
ORDER BY
  CASE sample_category WHEN 'A_LARGEST' THEN 1 WHEN 'B_REFUND' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END,
  payment_amount DESC,
  payment_id

question: Across all of 2025's payments, does the 'ledger credit = payment + refund' pattern seen in the sample hold universally, and how large are the 'no ledger entries' and 'other mismatch' buckets?
sql:
WITH qualifying_payments AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount,
    p.amount_refunded,
    p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
payment_amounts_eur AS (
  SELECT
    qp.id,
    qp.amount / er.rate AS payment_amount_eur,
    qp.amount_refunded / er.rate AS amount_refunded_eur
  FROM qualifying_payments qp
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = qp.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = date(qp.captured_at)
),
ledger_entries_eur AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id,
    le.direction,
    le.amount / er.rate AS amount_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = le.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = date(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.payment_id IN (SELECT id FROM qualifying_payments)
),
ledger_agg AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'credit' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS total_credit_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'debit' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS total_debit_eur,
    COUNT(*) AS entry_count
  FROM ledger_entries_eur
  GROUP BY payment_id
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    pa.id,
    pa.payment_amount_eur,
    pa.amount_refunded_eur,
    COALESCE(la.total_credit_eur, 0) AS total_credit_eur,
    COALESCE(la.total_debit_eur, 0) AS total_debit_eur,
    COALESCE(la.entry_count, 0) AS entry_count,
    (pa.payment_amount_eur - pa.amount_refunded_eur) AS target_net,
    (pa.payment_amount_eur + pa.amount_refunded_eur) AS target_gross
  FROM payment_amounts_eur pa
  LEFT JOIN ledger_agg la ON la.payment_id = pa.id
),
categorized AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    payment_amount_eur,
    total_credit_eur,
    total_debit_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN entry_count = 0 THEN 'no ledger entries'
      WHEN ABS(total_credit_eur - target_net) <= GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(target_net), 1) THEN 'credit = net amount'
      WHEN ABS(total_credit_eur - target_gross) <= GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(target_gross), 1) THEN 'credit = payment + refund'
      ELSE 'other mismatch'
    END AS reconciliation_category
  FROM classified
)
SELECT
  reconciliation_category,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_payments,
  ROUND(SUM(payment_amount_eur), 2) AS total_payment_amount_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(total_credit_eur), 2) AS total_ledger_credit_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(total_debit_eur), 2) AS total_ledger_debit_eur
FROM categorized
GROUP BY reconciliation_category
ORDER BY payment_count DESC

question: Using the right ledger accounts (revenue credits net of refund contra-revenue debits), does the ledger's net revenue tie to the payments table's net captured amount each quarter?
sql:
WITH ledger_q AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM le.occurred_at)::int AS yr,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM le.occurred_at)::int AS qtr,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN la.account_type = 'revenue' AND le.direction = 'credit'
          THEN (CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN le.amount ELSE le.amount / er.rate END)
          ELSE 0
        END) AS ledger_revenue_credit_eur,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN la.account_type = 'contra_revenue' AND le.direction = 'debit'
          THEN (CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN le.amount ELSE le.amount / er.rate END)
          ELSE 0
        END) AS ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  JOIN ledger_accounts la ON la.id = le.ledger_account_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = le.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = date(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND le.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND la.account_type IN ('revenue', 'contra_revenue')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
payments_q AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM p.captured_at)::int AS yr,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM p.captured_at)::int AS qtr,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN (p.amount - p.amount_refunded)
          ELSE (p.amount - p.amount_refunded) / er2.rate
        END) AS payments_net_amount_eur
  FROM payments p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = date(p.captured_at)
  WHERE p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT
  l.yr || '-Q' || l.qtr AS quarter,
  ROUND(l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur, 2) AS ledger_revenue_credit_eur,
  ROUND(l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur, 2) AS ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur,
  ROUND(l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur - l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur, 2) AS ledger_net_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(p.payments_net_amount_eur, 2) AS payments_net_amount_eur,
  ROUND((l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur - l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur) - p.payments_net_amount_eur, 2) AS diff_eur,
  ROUND(
    ((l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur - l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur) - p.payments_net_amount_eur)
    / NULLIF(p.payments_net_amount_eur, 0) * 100,
    2
  ) AS diff_pct
FROM ledger_q l
JOIN payments_q p ON p.yr = l.yr AND p.qtr = l.qtr
ORDER BY l.yr, l.qtr

question: Is the 2.1%-of-payments 'other mismatch' ledger bucket explained by a specific payment method (e.g. bank transfer/wire rather than card/gateway), or is it unexplained?
sql:
WITH t0_payments_eur AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS payment_id,
    p.payment_method_id,
    p.amount / er0.rate AS payment_amount_eur,
    p.amount_refunded / er0.rate AS amount_refunded_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er0.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er0.as_of = DATE(p.captured_at)
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
),

t1_ledger_credit AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id AS payment_id,
    SUM(le.amount / er1.rate) AS ledger_credit_total_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = le.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = DATE(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.direction = 'credit'
    AND le.payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),

t2_ledger_rowcount AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id AS payment_id,
    COUNT(*) AS ledger_row_count
  FROM ledger_entries le
  WHERE le.payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),

t3_payment_classified AS (
  SELECT
    t0.payment_id,
    t0.payment_method_id,
    t0.payment_amount_eur,
    COALESCE(t1.ledger_credit_total_eur, 0) AS ledger_credit_total_eur,
    COALESCE(t2.ledger_row_count, 0) AS ledger_row_count,
    (t0.payment_amount_eur - t0.amount_refunded_eur) AS expected_net_eur,
    (t0.payment_amount_eur + t0.amount_refunded_eur) AS expected_gross_eur,
    ABS(COALESCE(t1.ledger_credit_total_eur,0) - (t0.payment_amount_eur - t0.amount_refunded_eur)) AS diff_net_eur,
    ABS(COALESCE(t1.ledger_credit_total_eur,0) - (t0.payment_amount_eur + t0.amount_refunded_eur)) AS diff_gross_eur
  FROM t0_payments_eur t0
  LEFT JOIN t1_ledger_credit t1 ON t1.payment_id = t0.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN t2_ledger_rowcount t2 ON t2.payment_id = t0.payment_id
),

t4_other_mismatch AS (
  SELECT
    t3.payment_id,
    t3.payment_method_id,
    t3.payment_amount_eur,
    CASE WHEN t3.diff_net_eur <= t3.diff_gross_eur THEN t3.diff_net_eur ELSE t3.diff_gross_eur END AS abs_diff_eur
  FROM t3_payment_classified t3
  WHERE t3.ledger_row_count >= 1
    AND t3.diff_net_eur   > GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(t3.expected_net_eur), 1)
    AND t3.diff_gross_eur > GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(t3.expected_gross_eur), 1)
),

t5_mismatch_with_kind AS (
  SELECT
    t4.payment_id,
    t4.payment_amount_eur,
    t4.abs_diff_eur,
    COALESCE(pm.kind, 'unknown') AS payment_method_kind
  FROM t4_other_mismatch t4
  LEFT JOIN payment_methods pm ON pm.id = t4.payment_method_id
),

t6_grand_totals AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS grand_total_count,
    SUM(t5.payment_amount_eur) AS grand_total_amount_eur
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
),

t7_count AS (
  SELECT t5.payment_method_kind, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
  GROUP BY t5.payment_method_kind
),

t8_amount AS (
  SELECT t5.payment_method_kind, SUM(t5.payment_amount_eur) AS total_payment_amount_eur
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
  GROUP BY t5.payment_method_kind
),

t9_avgdiff AS (
  SELECT t5.payment_method_kind, AVG(t5.abs_diff_eur) AS avg_abs_diff_eur
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
  GROUP BY t5.payment_method_kind
)

SELECT
  t7.payment_method_kind AS payment_method_kind,
  t7.payment_count AS payment_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * t7.payment_count / NULLIF(t6.grand_total_count, 0), 2) AS pct_of_mismatch_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t8.total_payment_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS total_payment_amount_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t8.total_payment_amount_eur, 0) / NULLIF(t6.grand_total_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS pct_of_mismatch_amount,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t9.avg_abs_diff_eur, 0), 2) AS avg_abs_diff_eur
FROM t7_count t7
LEFT JOIN t8_amount t8 ON t8.payment_method_kind = t7.payment_method_kind
LEFT JOIN t9_avgdiff t9 ON t9.payment_method_kind = t7.payment_method_kind
CROSS JOIN t6_grand_totals t6
ORDER BY t7.payment_count DESC, t7.payment_method_kind ASC

WITH quarters AS (

ledger_filtered AS (

question: Is bank_transfer systemically more prone to ledger mismatches as a payment channel, or are the 19 flagged payments a rare exception within a much larger, mostly-clean population?
sql:
WITH fx AS (
  SELECT quote_code, as_of, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
payments_2025 AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.payment_method_id, p.amount, p.amount_refunded, p.currency_code, p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ledger_agg AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id,
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN le.direction = 'credit'
        THEN le.amount * COALESCE(fx.rate, CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END)
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS credit_eur,
    COUNT(*) AS entry_count
  FROM ledger_entries le
  LEFT JOIN fx ON fx.quote_code = le.currency_code AND fx.as_of = DATE(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),
calc AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    COALESCE(pm.kind, 'unknown') AS payment_method_kind,
    p.amount * COALESCE(fx_p.rate, CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS payment_amount_eur,
    p.amount_refunded * COALESCE(fx_p.rate, CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS refunded_amount_eur,
    la.credit_eur,
    la.entry_count
  FROM payments_2025 p
  LEFT JOIN payment_methods pm ON pm.id = p.payment_method_id
  LEFT JOIN fx fx_p ON fx_p.quote_code = p.currency_code AND fx_p.as_of = DATE(p.captured_at)
  LEFT JOIN ledger_agg la ON la.payment_id = p.id
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    payment_method_kind,
    CASE
      WHEN entry_count IS NULL OR entry_count = 0 THEN 'no_ledger_entries'
      WHEN ABS(credit_eur - (payment_amount_eur - refunded_amount_eur))
           <= GREATEST(1.0, 0.01 * ABS(payment_amount_eur - refunded_amount_eur))
        THEN 'credit_equals_net'
      WHEN ABS(credit_eur - (payment_amount_eur + refunded_amount_eur))
           <= GREATEST(1.0, 0.01 * ABS(payment_amount_eur + refunded_amount_eur))
        THEN 'credit_equals_payment_plus_refund'
      ELSE 'other_mismatch'
    END AS classification
  FROM calc
)
SELECT
  payment_method_kind,
  COUNT(*) AS total_payment_count_2025,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'credit_equals_net' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_credit_equals_net,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'credit_equals_payment_plus_refund' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_credit_equals_payment_plus_refund,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'other_mismatch' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_other_mismatch,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'no_ledger_entries' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_no_ledger_entries,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN classification IN ('credit_equals_net', 'credit_equals_payment_plus_refund') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    / COUNT(*),
    1
  ) AS pct_clean
FROM classified
GROUP BY payment_method_kind
ORDER BY total_payment_count_2025 DESC, payment_method_kind ASC

WITH payment_base AS (
  SELECT 
    p.id AS payment_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.order_id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount,
    p.amount_refunded,
    p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  JOIN payment_methods pm ON pm.id = p.payment_method_id
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND pm.kind = 'bank_transfer'
),
payment_eur AS (
  SELECT
    pb.payment_id,
    pb.tenant_id,
    pb.order_id,
    pb.currency_code,
    pb.amount,
    pb.amount_refunded,
    pb.captured_at,
    CASE WHEN pb.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pb.amount
         ELSE pb.amount / er.rate END AS payment_amount_eur,
    CASE WHEN pb.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pb.amount_refunded
         ELSE pb.amount_refunded / er.rate END AS amount_refunded_eur
  FROM payment_base pb
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = pb.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(pb.captured_at AS date)
),
ledger_credit AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN le.amount
             ELSE le.amount / er.rate END) AS ledger_credit_total_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = le.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(le.occurred_at AS date)
  WHERE le.direction = 'credit'
    AND le.payment_id IN (SELECT payment_id FROM payment_base)
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),
calc AS (
  SELECT
    pe.payment_id,
    pe.tenant_id,
    pe.order_id,
    pe.currency_code,
    pe.amount AS payment_amount,
    pe.amount_refunded,
    pe.captured_at,
    lc.ledger_credit_total_eur,
    (pe.payment_amount_eur - pe.amount_refunded_eur) AS net_amount_eur,
    (pe.payment_amount_eur + pe.amount_refunded_eur) AS payment_plus_refund_eur,
    CASE WHEN ABS(lc.ledger_credit_total_eur - (pe.payment_amount_eur - pe.amount_refunded_eur))
              <= ABS(lc.ledger_credit_total_eur - (pe.payment_amount_eur + pe.amount_refunded_eur))
         THEN (pe.payment_amount_eur - pe.amount_refunded_eur)
         ELSE (pe.payment_amount_eur + pe.amount_refunded_eur)
    END AS nearest_expected_eur
  FROM payment_eur pe
  LEFT JOIN ledger_credit lc ON lc.payment_id = pe.payment_id
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    (c.ledger_credit_total_eur - c.nearest_expected_eur) AS diff_eur,
    GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(c.nearest_expected_eur), 1) AS tolerance_eur
  FROM calc c
)
SELECT
  o.order_number,
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  cl.captured_at AS payment_captured_at,
  cl.currency_code,
  cl.payment_amount,
  cl.amount_refunded,
  ROUND(cl.ledger_credit_total_eur, 2) AS ledger_credit_total_eur,
  ROUND(cl.nearest_expected_eur, 2) AS nearest_expected_eur,
  ROUND(cl.diff_eur, 2) AS diff_eur
FROM classified cl
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = cl.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = cl.order_id
WHERE cl.ledger_credit_total_eur IS NOT NULL
  AND ABS(cl.diff_eur) > cl.tolerance_eur
ORDER BY diff_eur DESC, o.order_number

question: Is Albion Parcel's November-December breakdown concentrated in specific destination countries, or did it hit all regions roughly equally?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.shipped_at,
    s.delivered_at,
    c.name AS destination_country,
    (s.delivered_at::date - s.shipped_at::date) AS transit_days,
    CASE
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2025-11-01' THEN 'baseline'
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 'collapse'
    END AS period
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  JOIN orders o ON f.order_id = o.id
  JOIN addresses a ON o.shipping_address_id = a.id
  JOIN countries c ON a.country_id = c.id
  WHERE s.carrier = 'Albion Parcel'
    AND s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    destination_country,
    period,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS delivered_count,
    AVG(transit_days) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_transit_days,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND transit_days <= 3) AS within3
  FROM base
  WHERE period IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY destination_country, period
),
totals AS (
  SELECT period, SUM(shipments_shipped) AS total_shipments
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY period
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT destination_country
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY destination_country
  HAVING MAX(shipments_shipped) >= 15
)
SELECT
  a.destination_country,
  a.period,
  a.shipments_shipped,
  ROUND(a.avg_transit_days::numeric, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.within3 / NULLIF(a.delivered_count, 0), 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.shipments_shipped / t.total_shipments, 1) AS share_of_period_shipments_pct
FROM agg a
JOIN totals t ON a.period = t.period
JOIN qualified q ON q.destination_country = a.destination_country
ORDER BY a.destination_country ASC, a.period ASC

question: Are our two chronically weak carriers bad everywhere, or concentrated on specific lanes/countries?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    s.carrier,
    co.name AS destination_country,
    s.id AS shipment_id,
    s.delivered_at,
    (CAST(s.delivered_at AS date) - CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)) AS transit_days
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  JOIN addresses a ON a.id = o.shipping_address_id
  JOIN countries co ON co.id = a.country_id
  WHERE s.carrier IN ('Landfall Freight','Lowlands Express')
    AND s.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
carrier_totals AS (
  SELECT carrier, COUNT(*) AS carrier_shipments
  FROM base
  GROUP BY carrier
),
country_stats AS (
  SELECT
    carrier,
    destination_country,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
    AVG(transit_days) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_transit_days,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND transit_days <= 3) AS within_3_count
  FROM base
  GROUP BY carrier, destination_country
)
SELECT
  cs.carrier,
  cs.destination_country,
  cs.shipments_shipped,
  ROUND(cs.avg_transit_days, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * cs.within_3_count / cs.shipments_shipped, 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * cs.shipments_shipped / ct.carrier_shipments, 1) AS share_of_carrier_shipments_pct
FROM country_stats cs
JOIN carrier_totals ct ON ct.carrier = cs.carrier
WHERE cs.shipments_shipped >= 15
ORDER BY cs.carrier ASC, cs.shipments_shipped DESC, cs.destination_country ASC

question: Is Albion Parcel's November-December breakdown concentrated in a specific warehouse/hub (or the merchants it serves), or did it hit all origins roughly equally?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    f.warehouse_id,
    w.name AS warehouse_name,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    CASE
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2025-11-01' THEN 'baseline'
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 'collapse'
    END AS period,
    s.delivered_at,
    s.shipped_at
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = f.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE s.carrier = 'Albion Parcel'
    AND s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    warehouse_id,
    warehouse_name,
    tenant_name,
    period,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (delivered_at - shipped_at)) / 86400.0) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_transit_days_raw,
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND delivered_at - shipped_at <= INTERVAL '3 days')
      / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL), 0) AS pct_within_3_days_raw
  FROM base
  WHERE period IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY warehouse_id, warehouse_name, tenant_name, period
),
period_totals AS (
  SELECT period, SUM(shipments_shipped) AS total_shipments
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY period
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT warehouse_id
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY warehouse_id
  HAVING MAX(shipments_shipped) >= 10
)
SELECT
  a.warehouse_name,
  a.tenant_name,
  a.period,
  a.shipments_shipped,
  ROUND(a.avg_transit_days_raw, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(a.pct_within_3_days_raw, 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.shipments_shipped / pt.total_shipments, 1) AS share_of_period_shipments_pct
FROM agg a
JOIN period_totals pt ON pt.period = a.period
JOIN qualified q ON q.warehouse_id = a.warehouse_id
ORDER BY a.warehouse_name ASC, CASE a.period WHEN 'baseline' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

question: What is each carrier's full-year transit reliability and volume share, so I can estimate how much overall unreliability would disappear if the weak carriers matched the good ones?
sql:
SELECT
  carrier,
  COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
  COUNT(delivered_at) AS shipments_delivered,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN delivered_at IS NOT NULL THEN (delivered_at::date - shipped_at::date) END)::numeric, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND((PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (delivered_at::date - shipped_at::date)) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL))::numeric, 2) AS median_transit_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND (delivered_at::date - shipped_at::date) <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(delivered_at), 0), 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS share_of_total_shipments_pct
FROM shipments
WHERE shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY carrier
ORDER BY shipments_shipped DESC, carrier ASC

question: Do apparel/footwear merchants, where picking discrepancies are concentrated, actually see more orders go unfulfilled or delivered slowly -- or is that purely an inventory/accounting issue with no customer-facing effect?
sql:
WITH terminal_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, t.industry, o.status, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status IN ('fulfilled','cancelled','refunded')
    AND t.industry IS NOT NULL
),
order_qty AS (
  SELECT oi.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS qty_ordered, SUM(oi.quantity_fulfilled) AS qty_fulfilled
  FROM order_items oi
  GROUP BY oi.order_id
),
order_shipment AS (
  SELECT f.order_id,
         COUNT(s.id) AS shipment_count,
         SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivered_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS undelivered_count,
         MAX(s.delivered_at) AS max_delivered_at
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  GROUP BY f.order_id
),
order_flags AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_id,
    t0.tenant_id,
    t0.industry,
    t0.status,
    t0.placed_at,
    COALESCE(q.qty_ordered, 0) AS qty_ordered,
    COALESCE(q.qty_fulfilled, 0) AS qty_fulfilled,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(q.qty_fulfilled,0) < COALESCE(q.qty_ordered,0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_shortfall,
    CASE WHEN t0.status = 'fulfilled'
              AND s.shipment_count IS NOT NULL
              AND s.shipment_count > 0
              AND COALESCE(s.undelivered_count,0) = 0
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_fully_delivered,
    s.max_delivered_at
  FROM terminal_orders t0
  LEFT JOIN order_qty q ON q.order_id = t0.order_id
  LEFT JOIN order_shipment s ON s.order_id = t0.order_id
)
SELECT
  industry,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_placed_2025,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(has_shortfall) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 1) AS pct_orders_with_fulfillment_shortfall,
  SUM(is_fully_delivered) AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN is_fully_delivered=1 THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (max_delivered_at - placed_at))/86400.0 END) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_fully_delivered=1 AND (max_delivered_at - placed_at) <= INTERVAL '5 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(is_fully_delivered),0), 1) AS pct_within_5_days
FROM order_flags
GROUP BY industry
ORDER BY pct_orders_with_fulfillment_shortfall DESC, industry ASC

question: Once we only look at purchase orders old enough to have fully played out, are we genuinely behind on restocking, or was the Q4 backlog just a year-end timing artifact?
sql:
SELECT
  '2025-Q' || CAST(EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM ordered_at) AS INTEGER) AS quarter,
  COUNT(*) AS pos_ordered_total,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01') AS pos_matured,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01' AND received_at IS NOT NULL) AS pos_matured_received,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND received_at IS NULL
        AND status IN ('submitted','partially_received')
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'), 0), 1) AS pct_matured_still_open,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE
      WHEN ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01' AND received_at IS NOT NULL
      THEN DATE_DIFF('day', ordered_at, received_at)
    END), 1) AS avg_actual_lead_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND expected_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at > expected_at
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND expected_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at IS NOT NULL
    ), 0), 1) AS pct_received_late,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE
      WHEN ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND expected_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at > expected_at
      THEN DATE_DIFF('day', expected_at, received_at)
    END), 1) AS avg_days_late
FROM purchase_orders
WHERE ordered_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM ordered_at)
ORDER BY quarter ASC

builds_on: Purchase order replenishment performance by quarter, 2025

pos_matured (subset of pos_ordered_total with ordered_at <= 2025-11-01, i.e. at least 60 days elapsed before the 2025-12-31 cutoff)
pos_matured_received (matured subset with received_at not null)
pct_matured_still_open (matured subset with received_at null and status in ('submitted','partially_received') -- a true backlog signal, not a recency artifact)
avg_actual_lead_days (DATEDIFF(day, ordered_at, received_at), matured+received subset only)
pct_received_late (matured subset with both expected_at and received_at set, where received_at > expected_at)

question: In the same order-level metric I've already reported to Priya (pct within 5 days), how much better would our overall delivery reliability be if the three weak carriers matched everyone else?
sql:
WITH order_fulfillment_counts AS (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM fulfillments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
fulfillment_shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT fulfillment_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM shipments
  GROUP BY fulfillment_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.placed_at,
    s.carrier,
    s.delivered_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  JOIN order_fulfillment_counts ofc ON ofc.order_id = o.id
  JOIN fulfillment_shipment_counts fsc ON fsc.fulfillment_id = f.id
  WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND ofc.cnt = 1
    AND fsc.cnt = 1
    AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
scored AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    CASE WHEN carrier IN ('Albion Parcel','Landfall Freight','Lowlands Express') THEN 'Weak three' ELSE 'All other carriers' END AS carrier_group,
    (delivered_at::date - placed_at::date) AS delivery_days
  FROM base
)
SELECT
  carrier_group,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(AVG(delivery_days)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
FROM scored
GROUP BY carrier_group
ORDER BY carrier_group ASC

question: How much better would Lowlands Express's orders perform, and how much would that help overall, if we only used it on its strong home lanes (Netherlands, Belgium, France) and moved everything else off it?
sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.placed_at,
    o.shipping_address_id,
    s.carrier,
    s.delivered_at,
    (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - o.placed_at)) / 86400.0) AS delivery_days
  FROM orders o
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
    AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
    AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_id,
    t0.delivery_days,
    CASE
      WHEN t0.carrier = 'Lowlands Express' AND c.name IN ('Netherlands', 'Belgium', 'France') THEN 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)'
      WHEN t0.carrier = 'Lowlands Express' THEN 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)'
      ELSE 'All other carriers'
    END AS lane_group
  FROM t0
  LEFT JOIN addresses a ON a.id = t0.shipping_address_id
  LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.id = a.country_id
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    t1.lane_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    ROUND(AVG(t1.delivery_days)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t1.delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM t1
  GROUP BY t1.lane_group
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM t1
)
SELECT
  t2.lane_group,
  t2.orders_fully_delivered,
  t2.avg_delivery_days,
  t2.pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * t2.orders_fully_delivered / t3.total_orders, 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
FROM t2
CROSS JOIN t3
ORDER BY
  CASE t2.lane_group
    WHEN 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)' THEN 2
    ELSE 3
  END,
  t2.lane_group

question: How much of the November-December delivery slowdown is specifically attributable to Albion Parcel, versus everything else?
sql:
WITH elig_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
fulfillment_counts AS (
  SELECT f.order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_fulfillments
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN elig_orders eo ON eo.order_id = f.order_id
  GROUP BY f.order_id
),
single_fulfillment AS (
  SELECT f.id AS fulfillment_id, f.order_id
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN fulfillment_counts fc ON fc.order_id = f.order_id AND fc.n_fulfillments = 1
),
shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT s.fulfillment_id, COUNT(*) AS n_shipments
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN single_fulfillment sf ON sf.fulfillment_id = s.fulfillment_id
  GROUP BY s.fulfillment_id
),
single_shipment AS (
  SELECT s.fulfillment_id, s.carrier, s.delivered_at
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN shipment_counts sc ON sc.fulfillment_id = s.fulfillment_id AND sc.n_shipments = 1
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT eo.order_id, eo.placed_at, ss.carrier, ss.delivered_at
  FROM elig_orders eo
  JOIN single_fulfillment sf ON sf.order_id = eo.order_id
  JOIN single_shipment ss ON ss.fulfillment_id = sf.fulfillment_id
  WHERE ss.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
labeled AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    CASE WHEN placed_at < DATE '2025-11-01' THEN 'baseline' ELSE 'collapse' END AS period,
    CASE WHEN carrier = 'Albion Parcel' THEN 'Albion Parcel' ELSE 'All other carriers' END AS carrier_group,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (delivered_at - placed_at)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days
  FROM qualified
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    period,
    carrier_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM labeled
  GROUP BY period, carrier_group
)
SELECT
  carrier_group,
  period,
  orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(avg_delivery_days, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(pct_within_5_days, 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * orders_fully_delivered / SUM(orders_fully_delivered) OVER (PARTITION BY period), 1) AS share_of_period_orders_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY period ASC, carrier_group ASC

question: Confirmed and reconciled: how much does Lowlands Express's order-level reliability differ between its home lanes (Netherlands/Belgium/France) and everywhere else, versus the rest of our carriers combined?
sql:
WITH order_fulfillment_counts AS (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS fulfillment_count
  FROM fulfillments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
fulfillment_shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT fulfillment_id, COUNT(*) AS shipment_count
  FROM shipments
  GROUP BY fulfillment_id
),
eligible_orders AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.placed_at,
    o.shipping_address_id,
    f.id AS fulfillment_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_fulfillment_counts ofc
    ON ofc.order_id = o.id AND ofc.fulfillment_count = 1
  JOIN fulfillments f
    ON f.order_id = o.id
  WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
eligible_with_shipment AS (
  SELECT
    eo.order_id,
    eo.placed_at,
    eo.shipping_address_id,
    s.carrier,
    s.delivered_at
  FROM eligible_orders eo
  JOIN fulfillment_shipment_counts fsc
    ON fsc.fulfillment_id = eo.fulfillment_id AND fsc.shipment_count = 1
  JOIN shipments s
    ON s.fulfillment_id = eo.fulfillment_id
  WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
order_lane AS (
  SELECT
    ews.order_id,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ews.delivered_at - ews.placed_at)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days,
    CASE
      WHEN ews.carrier = 'Lowlands Express' AND c.name IN ('Netherlands', 'Belgium', 'France')
        THEN 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)'
      WHEN ews.carrier = 'Lowlands Express'
        THEN 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)'
      ELSE 'All other carriers combined'
    END AS lane_group
  FROM eligible_with_shipment ews
  LEFT JOIN addresses a ON a.id = ews.shipping_address_id
  LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.id = a.country_id
),
lane_groups AS (
  SELECT 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)' AS lane_group, 1 AS sort_order
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)', 2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'All other carriers combined', 3
),
lane_stats AS (
  SELECT
    lane_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100 AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM order_lane
  GROUP BY lane_group
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(orders_fully_delivered) AS total_orders FROM lane_stats
)
SELECT
  lg.lane_group,
  COALESCE(ls.orders_fully_delivered, 0) AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(CAST(ls.avg_delivery_days AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(CAST(ls.pct_within_5_days AS numeric), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ls.orders_fully_delivered, 0) AS numeric) / NULLIF(t.total_orders, 0) * 100, 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
FROM lane_groups lg
LEFT JOIN lane_stats ls ON ls.lane_group = lg.lane_group
CROSS JOIN totals t
ORDER BY lg.sort_order

question: What is each carrier's order-level delivery reliability (orders placed to orders delivered, within 5 days), in one single consistent query I can use as the ground truth for a reliability ceiling calculation?
sql:
SELECT
  carrier,
  orders_fully_delivered,
  avg_delivery_days,
  pct_within_5_days,
  share_of_orders_pct,
  0 AS sort_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    d.carrier AS carrier,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    ROUND(CAST(AVG(d.delivery_days) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN d.delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (
      SELECT COUNT(*)
      FROM (
        SELECT o2.id AS order_id
        FROM orders o2
        JOIN fulfillments f2a ON f2a.order_id = o2.id
        JOIN shipments s2a ON s2a.fulfillment_id = f2a.id
        WHERE o2.status = 'fulfilled'
          AND o2.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
          AND o2.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
          AND s2a.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
          AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments ff WHERE ff.order_id = o2.id) = 1
          AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments ss WHERE ss.fulfillment_id = f2a.id) = 1
      ) all_d
    ), 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
  FROM (
    SELECT
      o.id AS order_id,
      s.carrier AS carrier,
      (CAST(s.delivered_at AS DATE) - CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)) AS delivery_days
    FROM orders o
    JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
    JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
    WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
      AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
  ) d
  GROUP BY d.carrier
) per_carrier

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'ALL CARRIERS' AS carrier,
  orders_fully_delivered,
  avg_delivery_days,
  pct_within_5_days,
  100.0 AS share_of_orders_pct,
  1 AS sort_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    ROUND(CAST(AVG(delivery_days) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM (
    SELECT
      (CAST(s.delivered_at AS DATE) - CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)) AS delivery_days
    FROM orders o
    JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
    JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
    WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
      AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
  ) all_orders
) totals

ORDER BY sort_rank, orders_fully_delivered DESC

  SELECT f.id AS fulfillment_id, f.order_id, f.tenant_id, COUNT(s.id) AS shipment_count
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN single_fulfillment sf ON sf.order_id = f.order_id AND sf.tenant_id = f.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id AND s.tenant_id = f.tenant_id
  GROUP BY f.id, f.order_id, f.tenant_id
),
qualifying_fulfillments AS (
  SELECT fsc.fulfillment_id, fsc.order_id, fsc.tenant_id
  FROM fulfillment_shipment_counts fsc
  WHERE fsc.shipment_count = 1
),
order_shipment AS (
  SELECT qf.order_id, qf.tenant_id, s.carrier, s.delivered_at
  FROM qualifying_fulfillments qf
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = qf.fulfillment_id AND s.tenant_id = qf.tenant_id
  WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
order_detail AS (
  SELECT
    qo.order_id,
    qo.tenant_id,
    qo.placed_at,
    os.carrier,
    os.delivered_at,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (os.delivered_at - qo.placed_at)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days
  FROM q_orders qo
  JOIN order_shipment os ON os.order_id = qo.order_id AND os.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
),
order_detail_grouped AS (
  SELECT
    od.order_id,
    od.tenant_id,
    od.placed_at,
    od.delivery_days,
    CASE
      WHEN od.carrier IN ('Albion Parcel', 'Landfall Freight', 'Lowlands Express') THEN od.carrier
      ELSE 'All other carriers'
    END AS carrier_group
  FROM order_detail od
),
with_quarter AS (
  SELECT
    odg.order_id,
    odg.delivery_days,
    odg.carrier_group,
    cd.year_num,
    cd.quarter_num
  FROM order_detail_grouped odg
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(odg.placed_at AS DATE)
),
quarter_totals AS (
  SELECT year_num, quarter_num, COUNT(*) AS total_orders
  FROM with_quarter
  GROUP BY year_num, quarter_num
),
group_agg AS (
  SELECT
    year_num,
    quarter_num,
    carrier_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100 AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM with_quarter
  GROUP BY year_num, quarter_num, carrier_group
)
SELECT
  ga.carrier_group AS carrier_group,
  CONCAT(CAST(ga.year_num AS VARCHAR), '-Q', CAST(ga.quarter_num AS VARCHAR)) AS quarter,
  ga.orders_fully_delivered AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(CAST(ga.avg_delivery_days AS NUMERIC), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(CAST(ga.pct_within_5_days AS NUMERIC), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(CAST(ga.orders_fully_delivered * 100.0 / qt.total_orders AS NUMERIC), 1) AS share_of_quarter_orders_pct
FROM group_agg ga
JOIN quarter_totals qt ON qt.year_num = ga.year_num AND qt.quarter_num = ga.quarter_num
ORDER BY
  ga.quarter_num ASC,
  CASE ga.carrier_group
    WHEN 'Albion Parcel' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Landfall Freight' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Lowlands Express' THEN 3
    ELSE 4
  END ASC

question: What is each carrier's order-level delivery reliability (orders placed to orders delivered, within 5 days), in one single consistent query I can use as the ground truth for a reliability ceiling calculation?
reasons: does not compile: Binder Error: Could not ORDER BY column "CASE  WHEN ((per_carrier.carrier = 'ALL CARRIERS')) THEN (1) ELSE 0 END": add the expression/function to every SELECT, or move the UNION into a FROM clause.
sql:
SELECT
  carrier,
  orders_fully_delivered,
  avg_delivery_days,
  pct_within_5_days,
  share_of_orders_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    d.carrier AS carrier,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    ROUND(CAST(AVG(d.delivery_days) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN d.delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (
      SELECT COUNT(*)
      FROM (
        SELECT o2.id AS order_id
        FROM orders o2
        JOIN fulfillments f2a ON f2a.order_id = o2.id
        JOIN shipments s2a ON s2a.fulfillment_id = f2a.id
        WHERE o2.status = 'fulfilled'
          AND o2.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
          AND o2.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
          AND s2a.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
          AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments ff WHERE ff.order_id = o2.id) = 1
          AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments ss WHERE ss.fulfillment_id = f2a.id) = 1
      ) all_d
    ), 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
  FROM (
    SELECT
      o.id AS order_id,
      s.carrier AS carrier,
      (CAST(s.delivered_at AS DATE) - CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)) AS delivery_days
    FROM orders o
    JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
    JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
    WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
      AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
  ) d
  GROUP BY d.carrier
) per_carrier

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'ALL CARRIERS' AS carrier,
  orders_fully_delivered,
  avg_delivery_days,
  pct_within_5_days,
  100.0 AS share_of_orders_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    ROUND(CAST(AVG(delivery_days) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM (
    SELECT
      (CAST(s.delivered_at AS DATE) - CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)) AS delivery_days
    FROM orders o
    JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
    JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
    WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
      AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
      AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
      AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
  ) all_orders
) totals

ORDER BY
  (CASE WHEN carrier = 'ALL CARRIERS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
  orders_fully_delivered DESC,
  carrier ASC

question: Are Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij understaffed relative to their ticket volume compared to the rest of the book?
sql:
with t2025 as (
  select
    tenant_id,
    count(*) as tickets_created,
    count(distinct assignee_agent_id) as distinct_agents_handled,
    count(*) filter (where assignee_agent_id is null) as unassigned_count
  from tickets
  where created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' and created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  group by tenant_id
),
agents as (
  select tenant_id, count(*) as registered_agents
  from support_agents
  group by tenant_id
)
select
  ten.name as merchant_name,
  t.tickets_created,
  coalesce(a.registered_agents, 0) as registered_support_agents,
  t.distinct_agents_handled,
  case when t.distinct_agents_handled > 0
       then round(t.tickets_created::decimal / t.distinct_agents_handled, 1)
       else null
  end as tickets_per_active_agent,
  round(100.0 * t.unassigned_count / t.tickets_created, 1) as pct_unassigned
from t2025 t
join tenants ten on ten.id = t.tenant_id
left join agents a on a.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
where t.tickets_created >= 20
order by tickets_per_active_agent desc nulls last, merchant_name asc
limit 50

question: Is the urgent-ticket resolution failure (missing resolution about half the time, company-wide) concentrated in Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij, or is it a broad pattern across the book?
sql:
SELECT 
  tn.name AS merchant_name,
  u.urgent_created,
  u.urgent_missing,
  ROUND(100.0 * u.urgent_missing / NULLIF(u.urgent_evaluable,0), 1) AS urgent_miss_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.all_missing / NULLIF(a.all_evaluable,0), 1) AS all_priority_miss_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT t.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS urgent_created,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS urgent_evaluable,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL AND (t.resolved_at IS NULL OR extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.created_at))/60 > sp.resolution_target_minutes) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS urgent_missing
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN sla_policies sp ON sp.id = t.sla_policy_id
  WHERE t.priority = 'urgent'
    AND t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
) u
JOIN (
  SELECT t.tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS all_evaluable,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL AND (t.resolved_at IS NULL OR extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.created_at))/60 > sp.resolution_target_minutes) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS all_missing
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN sla_policies sp ON sp.id = t.sla_policy_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
) a ON a.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = u.tenant_id
WHERE u.urgent_evaluable >= 5
ORDER BY urgent_miss_rate_pct DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50

Window: tickets.created_at 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31. Define a ticket as 'missing resolution target' if: resolved_at is null as of 2025-12-31 (i.e. still unresolved), OR extract(epoch from resolved_at - created_at)/60 > sla_policies.resolution_target_minutes. Exclude tickets with a null sla_policy_id from both numerator and denominator (can't be evaluated) and note how many were excluded. 'Urgent resolution miss rate' = urgent tickets missing target ÷ evaluable urgent tickets, percentage rounded to 1 decimal. 'All-priority resolution miss rate' = same calculation across all priorities for that tenant, for comparison within the same merchant. Only include tenants with >=5 evaluable urgent tickets in 2025. Order by urgent resolution miss rate descending, tie-break merchant name ascending. Cap at 50 rows; note total qualifying tenant count.
