question: Do Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij get harder/more complex tickets than the rest of the book, or just more of them?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  tk.ticket_count AS tickets_2025,
  round(coalesce(msg.total_messages, 0)::numeric / tk.ticket_count, 2) AS avg_messages_per_ticket,
  round(coalesce(msg.total_public, 0)::numeric / tk.ticket_count, 2) AS avg_public_messages_per_ticket,
  round(coalesce(tags.total_tags, 0)::numeric / tk.ticket_count, 2) AS avg_distinct_tags_per_ticket,
  count(*) OVER () AS qualifying_tenant_count
FROM tenants t
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) tk ON tk.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ti.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS total_messages,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE tm.is_public) AS total_public
  FROM ticket_messages tm
  JOIN tickets ti ON ti.id = tm.ticket_id AND ti.tenant_id = tm.tenant_id
  WHERE ti.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND ti.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti.tenant_id
) msg ON msg.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ti.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS total_tags
  FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
  JOIN tickets ti ON ti.id = ttm.ticket_id AND ti.tenant_id = ttm.tenant_id
  WHERE ti.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND ti.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti.tenant_id
) tags ON tags.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE tk.ticket_count >= 20
ORDER BY avg_messages_per_ticket DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50

question: Is the broad urgent-ticket resolution failure driven by unrealistically tight SLA targets, or are merchants genuinely resolving urgent tickets slower than a reasonable target?
sql:
WITH evaluable_tickets AS (
  SELECT
    t0.id AS ticket_id,
    t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t0.created_at AS created_at,
    t0.resolved_at AS resolved_at,
    t1.resolution_target_minutes AS resolution_target_minutes,
    CASE WHEN t0.resolved_at IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.resolved_at - t0.created_at)) / 3600.0
    END AS actual_hours,
    CASE
      WHEN t0.resolved_at IS NULL THEN 1
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.resolved_at - t0.created_at)) / 60.0 > t1.resolution_target_minutes THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS is_miss
  FROM tickets t0
  JOIN sla_policies t1 ON t1.id = t0.sla_policy_id
  WHERE t0.priority = 'urgent'
    AND t0.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
    AND t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tenant_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS evaluated_count
  FROM evaluable_tickets
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
),
tenant_target AS (
  SELECT e.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(e.resolution_target_minutes) / COUNT(*) / 60.0 AS weighted_target_hours,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.resolution_target_minutes) AS distinct_target_count
  FROM evaluable_tickets e
  JOIN tenant_counts c ON c.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
  GROUP BY e.tenant_id
),
tenant_actual AS (
  SELECT e.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    AVG(e.actual_hours) AS avg_actual_hours,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY e.actual_hours) AS median_actual_hours
  FROM evaluable_tickets e
  JOIN tenant_counts c ON c.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
  WHERE e.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY e.tenant_id
),
tenant_miss AS (
  SELECT e.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(e.is_miss) AS miss_count
  FROM evaluable_tickets e
  JOIN tenant_counts c ON c.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
  GROUP BY e.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t9.name AS merchant_name,
  ROUND(t1.weighted_target_hours, 1) AS urgent_resolution_target_hours,
  t0.evaluated_count AS urgent_tickets_evaluated_2025,
  ROUND(t2.median_actual_hours, 1) AS median_actual_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(t2.avg_actual_hours, 1) AS avg_actual_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(100.0 * t3.miss_count / t0.evaluated_count, 1) AS urgent_miss_rate_pct,
  CASE WHEN t1.distinct_target_count > 1 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS multiple_urgent_sla_policies
FROM tenant_counts t0
JOIN tenant_target t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN tenant_actual t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
JOIN tenant_miss t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
JOIN tenants t9 ON t9.id = t0.tenant_id
ORDER BY urgent_miss_rate_pct DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50

question: Is the big three's inflated average urgent resolution time caused by a handful of extreme-delay tickets, or by generally slow handling across the board?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  COUNT(*) AS urgent_tickets_evaluated,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_8h,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_8h_24h,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_1d_3d,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_3d_7d,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_over_7d_or_unresolved
FROM (
  SELECT
    tk.id,
    tk.tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN tk.resolved_at IS NULL THEN 5
      WHEN extract(epoch FROM tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 <= 8 THEN 1
      WHEN extract(epoch FROM tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 <= 24 THEN 2
      WHEN extract(epoch FROM tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 <= 72 THEN 3
      WHEN extract(epoch FROM tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 <= 168 THEN 4
      ELSE 5
    END AS bucket
  FROM tickets tk
  JOIN sla_policies sp ON sp.id = tk.sla_policy_id
  WHERE tk.priority = 'urgent'
    AND tk.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
    AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
    AND tk.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    AND tk.tenant_id IN (
      SELECT id FROM tenants
      WHERE name IN ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij', 'Grind Collective', 'Wiesgrund Wohnen')
    )
) b
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = b.tenant_id
GROUP BY t.name
ORDER BY t.name ASC

question: Does urgent-ticket resolution specifically get worse in the same quarters where each merchant's ticket-per-agent load spiked?
sql:
WITH q AS (
  SELECT 1 AS q_num, date '2025-01-01' AS q_start, date '2025-04-01' AS q_end
  UNION ALL SELECT 2, date '2025-04-01', date '2025-07-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT 3, date '2025-07-01', date '2025-10-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT 4, date '2025-10-01', date '2026-01-01'
),
m AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Cragsley Outfitters','Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Grind Collective')
)
SELECT
  m.name AS merchant_name,
  '2025-Q' || q.q_num AS quarter,
  count(tk.id) AS urgent_tickets_evaluated,
  round(
    100.0 * sum(
      case when tk.id is not null
             and (tk.resolved_at is null or tk.resolved_at > tk.created_at + (sp.resolution_target_minutes || ' minutes')::interval)
           then 1 else 0 end
    )::numeric / nullif(count(tk.id), 0)
  , 1) AS urgent_miss_rate_pct,
  round(
    avg(case when tk.resolved_at is not null then extract(epoch from tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 end)::numeric
  , 1) AS avg_actual_resolution_hours,
  round(
    percentile_cont(0.5) within group (
      order by case when tk.resolved_at is not null then extract(epoch from tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 end
    )::numeric
  , 1) AS median_actual_resolution_hours
FROM m
CROSS JOIN q
LEFT JOIN tickets tk
  ON tk.tenant_id = m.id
  AND tk.priority = 'urgent'
  AND tk.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
  AND tk.created_at >= q.q_start AND tk.created_at < q.q_end
LEFT JOIN sla_policies sp ON sp.id = tk.sla_policy_id
GROUP BY m.name, q.q_num
ORDER BY m.name ASC, q.q_num ASC

question: Within Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij, is slow/stuck-ticket handling spread evenly across the support team, or concentrated in one or two agents?
sql:
WITH base_tickets AS (

    t0.id AS ticket_id,
    t0.created_at AS created_at,

  FROM tickets t0
  JOIN tenants t1 ON t1.id = t0.tenant_id

  ROUND(COALESCE(t5.avg_resolution_hours, 0), 1) AS avg_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t5.median_resolution_hours, 0), 1) AS median_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t6.breach_rate_pct, 0), 1) AS sla_breach_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, assignee_agent_id FROM base_tickets
) t0
JOIN (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, name AS merchant_name FROM tenants
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
JOIN (
  SELECT id AS agent_id, display_name AS agent_display_name FROM support_agents
) t3 ON t3.agent_id = t0.assignee_agent_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, assignee_agent_id, COUNT(*) AS tickets_handled

LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    assignee_agent_id,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_resolution_hours,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 3600.0) AS median_resolution_hours
  FROM base_tickets
  WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id, assignee_agent_id
) t5 ON t5.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id AND t5.assignee_agent_id = t0.assignee_agent_id

    t7.tenant_id AS tenant_id,

    CASE WHEN COALESCE(oa.gmv_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (COALESCE(oa.discount_eur, 0) + COALESCE(ra.refund_eur, 0)) / oa.gmv_eur * 100
    END, 1) AS net_leakage_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.month = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN refund_agg ra ON ra.month = m.month_label
ORDER BY m.month_label

title: Is discount-related revenue leakage getting worse over 2025?

question: Is the euro cost of discounting (discounts given plus refunds on those orders) trending up or down over the course of 2025, in step with the refund-rate creep other teams have flagged?
sql:
WITH order_agg AS (
  SELECT
    strftime(o.placed_at, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
    SUM(o.discount_total * CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE 1.0 / er.rate END) AS discount_eur,
    SUM(o.subtotal * CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE 1.0 / er.rate END) AS gmv_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
),
refund_agg AS (
  SELECT
    strftime(o.placed_at, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    SUM(ret.refund_total * CASE WHEN ret.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE 1.0 / er.rate END) AS refund_eur
  FROM order_returns ret
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = ret.order_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = ret.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label FROM calendar_days WHERE year_num = 2025
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.discount_eur, 0), 0) AS discount_given_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ra.refund_eur, 0), 0) AS refund_amount_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.gmv_eur, 0), 0) AS gmv_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(oa.gmv_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (COALESCE(oa.discount_eur, 0) + COALESCE(ra.refund_eur, 0)) / oa.gmv_eur * 100
    END, 1) AS net_leakage_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.month = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN refund_agg ra ON ra.month = m.month_label
ORDER BY m.month_label

question: Beyond return rates, how much revenue does discounting actually cost each vertical once you add up both the discounts given and the refunds paid out on those orders?
sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    t.industry AS industry,
    CASE WHEN o.discount_total > 0 THEN 'discounted' ELSE 'full price' END AS order_group,
    o.subtotal / er.rate AS subtotal_eur,
    o.discount_total / er.rate AS discount_eur
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT
    orr.order_id AS order_id,
    SUM(orr.refund_total / er2.rate) AS refund_eur
  FROM order_returns orr
  JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = orr.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(orr.refunded_at, orr.requested_at) AS date)
  GROUP BY orr.order_id
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT industry, order_group FROM t0
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT industry, order_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
    SUM(discount_eur) AS discount_given_eur_raw,
    SUM(subtotal_eur) AS gmv_eur_raw
  FROM t0
  GROUP BY industry, order_group
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT t0.industry AS industry, t0.order_group AS order_group,
    SUM(COALESCE(t1.refund_eur,0)) AS refund_amount_eur_raw
  FROM t0
  LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.order_id = t0.order_id
  GROUP BY t0.industry, t0.order_group
),
t5 AS (
  SELECT t0.industry AS industry, t0.order_group AS order_group,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN t0.order_id END) AS orders_with_return
  FROM t0
  LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.order_id = t0.order_id
  GROUP BY t0.industry, t0.order_group
)
SELECT
  t2.industry AS industry,
  t2.order_group AS order_group,
  COALESCE(t3.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t3.discount_given_eur_raw,0), 0) AS discount_given_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t4.refund_amount_eur_raw,0), 0) AS refund_amount_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t3.gmv_eur_raw,0), 0) AS gmv_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(t3.gmv_eur_raw,0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (COALESCE(t3.discount_given_eur_raw,0) + COALESCE(t4.refund_amount_eur_raw,0)) / t3.gmv_eur_raw * 100 END
  , 1) AS net_leakage_pct,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(t3.orders_count,0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE COALESCE(t5.orders_with_return,0)::numeric / t3.orders_count * 100 END
  , 1) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM t2
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.industry = t2.industry AND t3.order_group = t2.order_group
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.industry = t2.industry AND t4.order_group = t2.order_group
LEFT JOIN t5 ON t5.industry = t2.industry AND t5.order_group = t2.order_group
ORDER BY t2.industry ASC, t2.order_group ASC

builds_on: Are discounted orders healthier across verticals, or just in B2B?
columns_requested: orders_count - count of orders placed_at in 2025 in that industry/group
discount_given_eur - sum of orders.discount_total converted to EUR, rounded to 0 decimals
refund_amount_eur - sum of order_returns.refund_total (joined on order_id) for orders in that group, converted to EUR, rounded to 0 decimals
gmv_eur - sum of orders.subtotal (pre-discount product value) converted to EUR, rounded to 0 decimals
net_leakage_pct - (discount_given_eur + refund_amount_eur) / gmv_eur * 100, rounded to 1 decimal
refund_rate_pct - share of orders in that cell with at least one linked order_returns row, *100, rounded to 1 decimal

Convert orders.discount_total and orders.subtotal to EUR using exchange_rates as of placed_at date (base_code='EUR', quote_code=order currency, EUR=rate 1); convert order_returns.refund_total to EUR using exchange_rates as of order_returns.refunded_at date (same method). Order by industry ascending, then order_group ascending ('discounted' before 'full price'). Expect ~18-22 rows (industries x 2).

title: The real euro cost of discounting, by vertical

question: Ranking individual coupon codes by discount-plus-refund cost, which specific codes are the worst offenders (like Welcome10), and which are clean?
sql:
WITH redemptions AS (
  SELECT cr.id AS redemption_id, cr.order_id, cr.discount_amount, cr.currency_code, cr.redeemed_at, c.code
  FROM coupon_redemptions cr
  JOIN coupons c ON c.id = cr.coupon_id
  WHERE cr.redeemed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND cr.redeemed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
discount_eur AS (
  SELECT r.code, r.order_id, r.discount_amount / er.rate AS discount_amount_eur
  FROM redemptions r
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = r.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(r.redeemed_at AS date)
),
code_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT code, order_id FROM redemptions
),
orders_eur AS (
  SELECT co.code, co.order_id, o.grand_total / er.rate AS grand_total_eur
  FROM code_orders co
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = co.order_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
),
returns_eur AS (
  SELECT co.code, co.order_id, SUM(orr.refund_total / er.rate) AS order_refund_eur
  FROM code_orders co
  JOIN order_returns orr ON orr.order_id = co.order_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = orr.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(orr.refunded_at AS date)
  GROUP BY co.code, co.order_id
),
discount_agg AS (
  SELECT code, COUNT(*) AS times_redeemed, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_count, SUM(discount_amount_eur) AS discount_given_eur
  FROM discount_eur
  GROUP BY code
),
refund_agg AS (
  SELECT code, SUM(order_refund_eur) AS refund_amount_eur, COUNT(*) AS orders_with_return
  FROM returns_eur
  GROUP BY code
),
order_value_agg AS (
  SELECT code, AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM orders_eur
  GROUP BY code
)
SELECT
  d.code,
  d.times_redeemed,
  d.orders_count,
  ROUND(d.discount_given_eur, 0) AS discount_given_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.refund_amount_eur, 0), 0) AS refund_amount_eur,
  ROUND(d.discount_given_eur + COALESCE(r.refund_amount_eur, 0), 0) AS net_cost_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(r.orders_with_return, 0) / NULLIF(d.orders_count, 0), 1) AS refund_rate_pct,
  ROUND(ov.avg_order_value_eur, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur
FROM discount_agg d
LEFT JOIN refund_agg r ON r.code = d.code
LEFT JOIN order_value_agg ov ON ov.code = d.code
ORDER BY net_cost_eur DESC, d.code ASC
LIMIT 20

columns_requested: times_redeemed - count of coupon_redemptions rows for that code with redeemed_at in 2025
orders_count - count of distinct order_id among those redemptions
discount_given_eur - sum of coupon_redemptions.discount_amount converted to EUR, rounded to 0 decimals
refund_amount_eur - sum of order_returns.refund_total for those same orders, converted to EUR, rounded to 0 decimals
net_cost_eur - discount_given_eur + refund_amount_eur, rounded to 0 decimals
refund_rate_pct - share of those orders with at least one linked order_returns row, *100, rounded to 1 decimal
avg_order_value_eur - average grand_total (EUR) of those orders, rounded to 0 decimals
tags.details: Source: coupon_redemptions (redeemed_at in 2025, all tenants) joined to coupons for the code, and to order_returns on order_id for refund amounts. Convert coupon_redemptions.discount_amount to EUR using exchange_rates as of redeemed_at date; convert order_returns.refund_total to EUR using exchange_rates as of order_returns.refunded_at date; convert orders.grand_total to EUR as of orders.placed_at date (all base_code='EUR', EUR=rate 1). Order by net_cost_eur descending, tie-break code ascending, limit to the top 20 codes by net_cost_eur.

title: Which coupon codes cost more than they're worth

question: Which verticals already have the most referral-driven customers relative to their size, and does the referrer revenue advantage seen platform-wide hold within each vertical too?
sql:
WITH order_amounts AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.grand_total / er.rate AS grand_total_eur
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT
    oa.order_id,
    oa.tenant_id,
    oa.user_id,
    oa.grand_total_eur,
    t.industry,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM referrals r
      WHERE r.tenant_id = oa.tenant_id AND r.referrer_user_id = oa.user_id
    ) THEN 'referrer' ELSE 'non-referrer' END AS segment
  FROM order_amounts oa
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = oa.tenant_id
  WHERE t.industry IS NOT NULL
),
user_level AS (
  SELECT industry, segment, tenant_id, user_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_count
  FROM flagged
  GROUP BY industry, segment, tenant_id, user_id
),
industry_user_totals AS (
  SELECT industry, COUNT(*) AS total_users
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT industry, tenant_id, user_id FROM flagged) x
  GROUP BY industry
),
segment_agg AS (
  SELECT industry, segment,
    COUNT(*) AS users_count,
    AVG(orders_count) AS avg_orders_per_user
  FROM user_level
  GROUP BY industry, segment
),
order_level_agg AS (
  SELECT industry, segment, AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM flagged
  GROUP BY industry, segment
)
SELECT
  s.industry,
  s.segment,
  s.users_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * s.users_count / t.total_users, 2) AS share_of_industry_users_pct,
  ROUND(s.avg_orders_per_user, 2) AS avg_orders_per_user,
  ROUND(o.avg_order_value_eur, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur
FROM segment_agg s
JOIN industry_user_totals t ON t.industry = s.industry
JOIN order_level_agg o ON o.industry = s.industry AND o.segment = s.segment
ORDER BY s.industry ASC, CASE WHEN s.segment = 'referrer' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

builds_on: Do referred or referring shoppers spend differently than everyone else?

avg_orders_per_user - average count of 2025 orders per user in that segment, rounded to 2 decimals

title: Referral reach and value by vertical

question: Controlling for category, do loyalty members actually come back and buy again more than non-members, or does that pattern not hold either once you look within a vertical?
sql:
WITH loyalty_industries AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t.industry
  FROM loyalty_programs lp
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = lp.tenant_id
  WHERE lp.is_active = true AND t.industry IS NOT NULL
),
orders_2025 AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    t.industry,
    o.placed_at,
    o.grand_total,
    o.currency_code,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la
      WHERE la.user_id = o.user_id AND la.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    ) THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.industry IN (SELECT industry FROM loyalty_industries)
),
orders_eur AS (
  SELECT oe.*,
    CASE WHEN oe.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN oe.grand_total
         ELSE oe.grand_total / er.rate
    END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM orders_2025 oe
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = oe.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(oe.placed_at AS DATE)
),
user_stats AS (
  SELECT industry, segment, user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(placed_at AS DATE)) AS distinct_order_days
  FROM orders_eur
  GROUP BY industry, segment, user_id
),
agg_users AS (
  SELECT industry, segment,
    COUNT(*) AS users_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE distinct_order_days >= 2) AS repeat_users,
    AVG(order_count) AS avg_orders_per_user
  FROM user_stats
  GROUP BY industry, segment
),
agg_orders AS (
  SELECT industry, segment, AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM orders_eur
  GROUP BY industry, segment
)
SELECT
  au.industry,
  au.segment,
  au.users_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * au.repeat_users / NULLIF(au.users_count,0), 1) AS repeat_rate_pct,
  ROUND(au.avg_orders_per_user::numeric, 2) AS avg_orders_per_user,
  ROUND(ao.avg_order_value_eur::numeric, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur
FROM agg_users au
JOIN agg_orders ao ON ao.industry = au.industry AND ao.segment = au.segment
ORDER BY au.industry ASC, au.segment ASC

builds_on: Is loyalty members' lower spend a within-industry effect or a merchant-mix effect?

title: Loyalty worth by vertical: repeat-purchase rate

question: Within each vertical that runs a loyalty program, how much of members' revenue is given back as redeemed points, and how large is the unredeemed points liability sitting on the books?
sql:
WITH active_industries AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t.industry
  FROM tenants t
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.tenant_id = t.id
  WHERE lp.is_active = true AND t.industry IS NOT NULL
),
member_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.user_id, t.industry, o.grand_total, o.currency_code, CAST(o.placed_at AS date) AS placed_date
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la ON la.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND la.user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.industry IN (SELECT industry FROM active_industries)
),
member_orders_fx AS (
  SELECT mo.*, er.rate AS eur_rate
  FROM member_orders mo
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = mo.currency_code AND er.as_of = mo.placed_date
),
member_revenue AS (
  SELECT industry, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS members_count,
    SUM(grand_total / eur_rate) AS member_revenue_eur
  FROM member_orders_fx
  GROUP BY industry
),
redemption_tx AS (
  SELECT t.industry, lt.points / lp.points_per_currency AS value_local, lp.currency_code, CAST(lt.occurred_at AS date) AS occ_date
  FROM loyalty_transactions lt
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la ON la.id = lt.loyalty_account_id
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la.loyalty_program_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = la.tenant_id
  WHERE lt.direction = 'burn'
    AND lt.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND lt.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.industry IN (SELECT industry FROM active_industries)
),
redemption_tx_fx AS (
  SELECT rt.industry, rt.value_local / er.rate AS value_eur
  FROM redemption_tx rt
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = rt.currency_code AND er.as_of = rt.occ_date
),
redemption_agg AS (
  SELECT industry, SUM(value_eur) AS points_redeemed_value_eur
  FROM redemption_tx_fx
  GROUP BY industry
),
outstanding AS (
  SELECT t.industry, la.points_balance / lp.points_per_currency AS value_local, lp.currency_code
  FROM loyalty_accounts la
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la.loyalty_program_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = la.tenant_id
  WHERE t.industry IN (SELECT industry FROM active_industries)
),
outstanding_fx AS (
  SELECT o.industry, o.value_local / er.rate AS value_eur
  FROM outstanding o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
),
outstanding_agg AS (
  SELECT industry, SUM(value_eur) AS outstanding_points_value_eur
  FROM outstanding_fx
  GROUP BY industry
)
SELECT ai.industry,
  COALESCE(mr.members_count, 0) AS members_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mr.member_revenue_eur, 0), 0) AS member_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ra.points_redeemed_value_eur, 0), 0) AS points_redeemed_value_eur,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN COALESCE(mr.member_revenue_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE ra.points_redeemed_value_eur / mr.member_revenue_eur * 100 END, 1) AS redemption_cost_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.outstanding_points_value_eur, 0), 0) AS outstanding_points_value_eur
FROM active_industries ai
LEFT JOIN member_revenue mr ON mr.industry = ai.industry
LEFT JOIN redemption_agg ra ON ra.industry = ai.industry
LEFT JOIN outstanding_agg oa ON oa.industry = ai.industry
ORDER BY ai.industry

builds_on: Is loyalty members' lower spend a within-industry effect or a merchant-mix effect?

question: Is there a typical order-count threshold after which a customer becomes a referrer, which would tell us when to prompt the referral ask?
sql:
WITH first_referral AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, referrer_user_id, MIN(created_at) AS first_referral_at
  FROM referrals
  GROUP BY tenant_id, referrer_user_id
),
referrer_orders AS (
  SELECT
    fr.tenant_id,
    fr.referrer_user_id,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN o.placed_at < fr.first_referral_at THEN 1 END) AS orders_before,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 1 END) AS orders_2025
  FROM first_referral fr
  LEFT JOIN orders o
    ON o.tenant_id = fr.tenant_id AND o.user_id = fr.referrer_user_id
  GROUP BY fr.tenant_id, fr.referrer_user_id, fr.first_referral_at
)
SELECT
  bucket_label AS orders_before_first_referral_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS referrer_count,
  ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS share_of_referrers_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(orders_2025), 2) AS avg_total_2025_orders
FROM (
  SELECT
    ro.orders_before,
    ro.orders_2025,
    CASE
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 0 THEN 0
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 1 THEN 1
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 2 THEN 2
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 3 THEN 3
      WHEN ro.orders_before BETWEEN 4 AND 5 THEN 4
      ELSE 6
    END AS sort_key,
    CASE
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 0 THEN '0 (referred before ordering)'
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 1 THEN '1'
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 2 THEN '2'
      WHEN ro.orders_before = 3 THEN '3'
      WHEN ro.orders_before BETWEEN 4 AND 5 THEN '4-5'
      ELSE '6+'
    END AS bucket_label
  FROM referrer_orders ro
) b
GROUP BY bucket_label, sort_key
ORDER BY sort_key

builds_on: Do referred or referring shoppers spend differently than everyone else?
Referral reach and value by vertical
columns_requested: referrer_count - count of distinct (tenant_id, referrer_user_id) pairs falling in that bucket
share_of_referrers_pct - referrer_count / total referrers across all buckets * 100, rounded to 1 decimal
avg_total_2025_orders - average of each referrer's full count of 2025 orders (not just pre-referral), rounded to 2 decimals

For each, count that user's orders (any status) with placed_at strictly before first_referral_at, bucket per the labels above. avg_total_2025_orders = average count of that user's orders with placed_at in 2025 (full year, for context on eventual frequency). Order rows in the fixed sequence 0, 1, 2, 3, 4-5, 6+ (use a CASE-based sort key, not alphabetical). Expect exactly 6 rows.

question: Among orders with no linked marketing attribution, is there a pattern by vertical or by whether the buyer is a new or repeat customer that would tell us if this blind spot is worth chasing?
sql:
SELECT
  industry,
  attribution_status,
  orders_count,
  share_of_industry_orders_pct,
  new_customer_order_pct,
  avg_order_value_eur
FROM (
  SELECT
    industry,
    attribution_status,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
    ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY industry), 1) AS share_of_industry_orders_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(is_new) / COUNT(*), 1) AS new_customer_order_pct,
    ROUND(AVG(amount_eur), 0) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM (
    SELECT
      t.industry AS industry,
      CASE WHEN EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM attributions a WHERE a.order_id = o.id
      ) THEN 'attributed' ELSE 'unattributed' END AS attribution_status,
      CASE WHEN o.placed_at = (
        SELECT MIN(o3.placed_at)
        FROM orders o3
        WHERE o3.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
          AND o3.user_id = o.user_id
          AND o3.placed_at IS NOT NULL
      ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new,
      CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
           ELSE o.grand_total / (
             SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er
             WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
               AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
           )
      END AS amount_eur
    FROM orders o
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
    WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
      AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  ) base
  GROUP BY industry, attribution_status
) agg
ORDER BY industry ASC, attribution_status ASC

share_of_industry_orders_pct - orders_count / total 2025 orders for that industry * 100, rounded to 1 decimal

avg_order_value_eur - average grand_total (EUR) of orders in that cell, rounded to 0 decimals

question: For the attribution rows with no linked campaign, what do their touch_point values look like — is this organic/referral/direct traffic we can legitimately call 'known source', or something else?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(a.touch_point, '(none)') AS touch_point,
    a.order_id,
    a.attributed_revenue,
    a.currency_code,
    a.weight,
    a.occurred_at
  FROM attributions a
  WHERE a.campaign_id IS NULL
    AND a.order_id IS NOT NULL
    AND a.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND a.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
converted AS (
  SELECT
    b.touch_point,
    b.order_id,
    b.weight,
    CASE WHEN b.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN b.attributed_revenue
         ELSE b.attributed_revenue / er.rate END AS revenue_eur
  FROM base b
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = b.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(b.occurred_at AS date)
),
totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders FROM base
)
SELECT
  c.touch_point,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.order_id) AS distinct_orders_count,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT c.order_id) * 100.0 / t.total_orders, 1) AS share_of_no_campaign_orders_pct,
  ROUND(SUM(c.revenue_eur), 0) AS attributed_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(c.weight), 2) AS avg_weight
FROM converted c
CROSS JOIN totals t
GROUP BY c.touch_point, t.total_orders
ORDER BY distinct_orders_count DESC, touch_point ASC

question: Books & Stationery, Food & Coffee, and Pet Supplies show real loyalty members and orders in one report but €0 member revenue in another — is this a currency-conversion gap, and does it change the loyalty cost conclusion?
sql:
SELECT
  t.id AS tenant_id,
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.industry,
  t.default_currency_code,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.user_id) AS members_count,
  COUNT(o.id) AS member_orders_count_2025,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.currency_code = t.default_currency_code THEN o.grand_total ELSE 0 END) AS member_revenue_local_sum,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN er.rate IS NOT NULL THEN o.grand_total / er.rate ELSE 0 END), 0) AS member_revenue_eur_converted,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN er.rate IS NULL THEN 1 END) AS orders_missing_exchange_rate_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT o.currency_code) > 1 THEN true ELSE false END AS has_mixed_currency_orders
FROM tenants t
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT la.tenant_id, la.user_id
  FROM loyalty_accounts la
  JOIN orders o2 ON o2.user_id = la.user_id AND o2.tenant_id = la.tenant_id
  WHERE o2.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o2.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
) m ON m.tenant_id = t.id
JOIN orders o ON o.tenant_id = m.tenant_id AND o.user_id = m.user_id
  AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
WHERE t.industry IN ('Books & Stationery','Food & Coffee','Pet Supplies')
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.industry, t.default_currency_code
ORDER BY t.name ASC, t.id ASC

question: Is Castell Fasteners Q4 web traffic decline normal seasonal behavior shared by other B2B wholesale merchants, or a Castell-specific anomaly?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2023-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2024-01-01') AS sessions_q4_2023,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2024-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2025-01-01') AS sessions_q4_2024,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2026-01-01') AS sessions_q4_2025,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2024-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2025-01-01') = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2026-01-01') - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2024-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2025-01-01')) / COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2024-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2025-01-01'), 1)
  END AS yoy_growth_pct_2024_to_2025,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2023-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2024-01-01') = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2024-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2025-01-01') - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2023-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2024-01-01')) / COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ws.started_at >= DATE '2023-10-01' AND ws.started_at < DATE '2024-01-01'), 1)
  END AS yoy_growth_pct_2023_to_2024
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN web_sessions ws ON ws.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.name IN (
  'Castell Fasteners', 'OfficeHub Nordic', 'Deskline Supplies',
  'Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'Midland Safety Wear', 'Polder Packaging',
  'Kontor24 Burobedarf'
)
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.industry
ORDER BY sessions_q4_2025 DESC, t.id ASC
LIMIT 50

question: In the months before a churned merchant's last order, did sales, shopper repeat-buying, refund rates, or support ticket volume already show warning signs?
sql:
WITH churned_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, name, industry
  FROM tenants
  WHERE status = 'churned'
),
anchor_dates AS (
  SELECT ct.tenant_id, MAX(o.placed_at) AS anchor_at
  FROM churned_tenants ct
  JOIN orders o ON o.tenant_id = ct.tenant_id AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY ct.tenant_id
),
windows AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    anchor_at - interval '90 days' AS final_start,
    anchor_at AS final_end,
    anchor_at - interval '180 days' AS prior_start,
    anchor_at - interval '91 days' AS prior_end
  FROM anchor_dates
),
orders_with_fx AS (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id, o.id AS order_id, o.user_id, o.placed_at, o.currency_code, o.grand_total,
    er.rate
  FROM orders o
  JOIN churned_tenants ct ON ct.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
orders_classified AS (
  SELECT
    ow.tenant_id,
    ow.order_id,
    ow.user_id,
    CASE WHEN ow.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ow.grand_total ELSE ow.grand_total / ow.rate END AS revenue_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN ow.placed_at BETWEEN w.final_start AND w.final_end THEN 'final'
      WHEN ow.placed_at BETWEEN w.prior_start AND w.prior_end THEN 'prior'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS period
  FROM orders_with_fx ow
  JOIN windows w ON w.tenant_id = ow.tenant_id
),
order_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'final') AS orders_final,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'prior') AS orders_prior,
    SUM(revenue_eur) FILTER (WHERE period = 'final') AS revenue_final,
    SUM(revenue_eur) FILTER (WHERE period = 'prior') AS revenue_prior
  FROM orders_classified
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
user_period_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, period, COUNT(*) AS order_cnt
  FROM orders_classified
  WHERE period IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id, period
),
repeat_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id, period,
    COUNT(*) AS customers_total,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_cnt >= 2) AS customers_repeat
  FROM user_period_counts
  GROUP BY tenant_id, period
),
repeat_pivot AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN period = 'final' THEN customers_repeat::numeric / NULLIF(customers_total, 0) END) AS repeat_rate_final,
    MAX(CASE WHEN period = 'prior' THEN customers_repeat::numeric / NULLIF(customers_total, 0) END) AS repeat_rate_prior
  FROM repeat_metrics
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
payments_with_fx AS (
  SELECT
    p.tenant_id, p.captured_at, p.currency_code, p.amount, er.rate
  FROM payments p
  JOIN churned_tenants ct ON ct.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code AND er.as_of = p.captured_at::date
  WHERE p.captured_at IS NOT NULL
),
payments_classified AS (
  SELECT
    pw.tenant_id,
    CASE WHEN pw.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pw.amount ELSE pw.amount / pw.rate END AS amount_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN pw.captured_at BETWEEN w.final_start AND w.final_end THEN 'final'
      WHEN pw.captured_at BETWEEN w.prior_start AND w.prior_end THEN 'prior'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS period
  FROM payments_with_fx pw
  JOIN windows w ON w.tenant_id = pw.tenant_id
),
payment_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    SUM(amount_eur) FILTER (WHERE period = 'final') AS payments_final,
    SUM(amount_eur) FILTER (WHERE period = 'prior') AS payments_prior
  FROM payments_classified
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
refunds_with_fx AS (
  SELECT
    r.tenant_id, r.processed_at, r.currency_code, r.amount, er.rate
  FROM payment_refunds r
  JOIN churned_tenants ct ON ct.tenant_id = r.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = r.currency_code AND er.as_of = r.processed_at::date
  WHERE r.status = 'succeeded' AND r.processed_at IS NOT NULL
),
refunds_classified AS (
  SELECT
    rw.tenant_id,
    CASE WHEN rw.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN rw.amount ELSE rw.amount / rw.rate END AS amount_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN rw.processed_at BETWEEN w.final_start AND w.final_end THEN 'final'
      WHEN rw.processed_at BETWEEN w.prior_start AND w.prior_end THEN 'prior'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS period
  FROM refunds_with_fx rw
  JOIN windows w ON w.tenant_id = rw.tenant_id
),
refund_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    SUM(amount_eur) FILTER (WHERE period = 'final') AS refunds_final,
    SUM(amount_eur) FILTER (WHERE period = 'prior') AS refunds_prior
  FROM refunds_classified
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
tickets_classified AS (
  SELECT
    t.tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN t.created_at BETWEEN w.final_start AND w.final_end THEN 'final'
      WHEN t.created_at BETWEEN w.prior_start AND w.prior_end THEN 'prior'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS period
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN windows w ON w.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
),
ticket_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'final') AS tickets_final,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE period = 'prior') AS tickets_prior
  FROM tickets_classified
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
report AS (
  SELECT
    ct.tenant_id,
    ct.name AS merchant_name,
    ct.industry,
    COALESCE(om.orders_final, 0) AS orders_final_90d,
    COALESCE(om.orders_prior, 0) AS orders_prior_90d,
    CASE
      WHEN om.revenue_prior IS NULL OR om.revenue_prior = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE ROUND(((om.revenue_final - om.revenue_prior) / om.revenue_prior) * 100, 1)
    END AS revenue_growth_pct,
    ROUND(rp.repeat_rate_final * 100, 1) AS repeat_rate_final_pct,
    ROUND(rp.repeat_rate_prior * 100, 1) AS repeat_rate_prior_pct,
    CASE
      WHEN pm.payments_final IS NULL OR pm.payments_final = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE ROUND(COALESCE(rfm.refunds_final, 0) / pm.payments_final * 100, 1)
    END AS refund_rate_final_pct,
    CASE
      WHEN pm.payments_prior IS NULL OR pm.payments_prior = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE ROUND(COALESCE(rfm.refunds_prior, 0) / pm.payments_prior * 100, 1)
    END AS refund_rate_prior_pct,
    COALESCE(tm.tickets_final, 0) AS tickets_final_90d,
    COALESCE(tm.tickets_prior, 0) AS tickets_prior_90d,
    COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_churned_merchants
  FROM churned_tenants ct
  LEFT JOIN order_metrics om ON om.tenant_id = ct.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN repeat_pivot rp ON rp.tenant_id = ct.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN payment_metrics pm ON pm.tenant_id = ct.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN refund_metrics rfm ON rfm.tenant_id = ct.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN ticket_metrics tm ON tm.tenant_id = ct.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  merchant_name,
  industry,
  orders_final_90d,
  orders_prior_90d,
  revenue_growth_pct,
  repeat_rate_final_pct,
  repeat_rate_prior_pct,
  refund_rate_final_pct,
  refund_rate_prior_pct,
  tickets_final_90d,
  tickets_prior_90d,
  total_churned_merchants
FROM report
ORDER BY orders_final_90d ASC, tenant_id ASC
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Churned merchants: identification, size, and timeline
tags.details: For each churned tenant, anchor date is that tenant's own max orders.placed_at excluding cancelled orders. Final window is anchor minus 90 days through anchor. Prior window is anchor minus 180 days through anchor minus 91 days. Orders and revenue from orders table, converted to EUR via exchange_rates, excluding cancelled orders; revenue growth pct is final revenue minus prior revenue, divided by prior revenue, blank if prior is zero. Repeat rate is distinct customers with at least two orders divided by distinct customers with at least one order, per window. Refund rate is sum of payment_refunds.amount EUR divided by sum of payments.amount EUR captured in that window. Tickets is count of tickets rows with created_at in that window for that tenant. Order by orders final 90 days ascending, tie-break tenant_id. Cap 50 rows, note total count.
tags.grain: one row per merchant (tenant) with status equal to churned

title: Pre-churn warning signs across sales, repeat buying, refunds, and support tickets

question: Beyond the 9 formally churned merchants, which substantial merchants have gone quiet without yet being flagged as churned?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  t.status,
  MAX(o.placed_at)::date AS last_order_date,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - MAX(o.placed_at)::date) AS days_since_last_order,
  COUNT(*) AS lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate), 2) AS lifetime_revenue_eur
FROM tenants t
JOIN orders o
  ON o.tenant_id = t.id
 AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
 AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
 AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
 AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
WHERE t.status <> 'churned'
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.industry, t.status
HAVING MAX(o.placed_at) < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-09'
   AND COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY lifetime_revenue_eur DESC, t.id
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Pre-churn warning signs across sales, repeat buying, refunds, and support tickets
tags.details: Tenants with status not equal to churned. From orders (excluding cancelled): last order date is max placed_at; include only tenants whose last order date is before 2025-07-09 (180+ days before 2026-01-05) and whose lifetime order count is at least 20. lifetime revenue EUR is sum of grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates matched to placed_at. days since last order is 2026-01-05 minus last order date. Order by lifetime revenue EUR descending, tie-break tenant_id. Cap 50 rows, note total count.
tags.grain: one row per merchant (tenant), status not churned, no orders in 180+ days, lifetime orders at least 20

title: Silent-churn merchants: substantial accounts gone quiet without a churned flag

question: Do shoppers who stop engaging with campaigns go quiet sooner, and does disengagement show up before they lapse?
sql:
WITH user_orders AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    user_id,
    MAX(placed_at) AS last_order_at,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN order_count >= 3
        AND last_order_at::date <= DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '180 days'
        AND last_order_at::date >= DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '365 days'
        THEN 'lapsed'
      WHEN order_count >= 3
        AND last_order_at::date > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '90 days'
        AND last_order_at::date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
        THEN 'active'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS shopper_group,
    CASE
      WHEN order_count >= 3
        AND last_order_at::date <= DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '180 days'
        AND last_order_at::date >= DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '365 days'
        THEN last_order_at::date
      WHEN order_count >= 3
        AND last_order_at::date > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '90 days'
        AND last_order_at::date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
        THEN DATE '2025-12-31'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS reference_date
  FROM user_orders
),
eligible AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, shopper_group, reference_date
  FROM classified
  WHERE shopper_group IS NOT NULL
),
messages AS (
  SELECT
    e.shopper_group,
    e.tenant_id,
    e.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN (e.reference_date - cm.sent_at::date) BETWEEN 0 AND 90 THEN '0-90 days before reference'
      WHEN (e.reference_date - cm.sent_at::date) BETWEEN 91 AND 180 THEN '91-180 days before reference'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS window_label,
    cm.opened_at,
    cm.clicked_at
  FROM eligible e
  JOIN campaign_messages cm
    ON cm.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
   AND cm.user_id = e.user_id
   AND cm.sent_at IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  shopper_group,
  window_label AS window_before_reference,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id || '-' || user_id) AS shopper_count,
  COUNT(*) AS messages_sent,
  COUNT(opened_at) AS messages_opened,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(opened_at) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1) AS open_rate_pct,
  COUNT(clicked_at) AS messages_clicked,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(clicked_at) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1) AS click_rate_pct
FROM messages
WHERE window_label IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY shopper_group, window_label
ORDER BY shopper_group, window_label

tags.details: Two groups, each needing at least 3 lifetime orders excluding cancelled: 'lapsed' = last order placed_at 180 to 365 days before 2025-12-31; 'active' = last order within 90 days of 2025-12-31. Reference date is the user's own last order date for lapsed, and 2025-12-31 for active. Two windows per group: '0-90 days before reference' and '91-180 days before reference'. From campaign_messages (sent_at, opened_at, clicked_at) count sent, opened, clicked per group/window; open rate pct is opened divided by sent; click rate pct is clicked divided by sent; shopper count is distinct users in that window. Order by shopper group, then window ascending. Expect 4 rows.
tags.grain: one row per shopper group and time window before reference date

title: Marketing engagement before shoppers go quiet: lapsed vs active shoppers

question: Do shoppers who get slower or worse support go quiet sooner, and does that show up before they lapse?
sql:
WITH t0_shopper_last_order AS (
  SELECT
    o0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    o0.user_id AS user_id,
    MAX(DATE(o0.placed_at)) AS last_order_date
  FROM orders o0
  WHERE o0.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o0.tenant_id, o0.user_id
),
t1_shopper_group AS (
  SELECT
    t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t0.user_id AS user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN t0.last_order_date BETWEEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - 365) AND (DATE '2025-12-31' - 180) THEN 'lapsed'
      WHEN t0.last_order_date BETWEEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - 90) AND DATE '2025-12-31' THEN 'active'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS shopper_group,
    CASE
      WHEN t0.last_order_date BETWEEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - 365) AND (DATE '2025-12-31' - 180) THEN t0.last_order_date
      ELSE DATE '2025-12-31'
    END AS reference_date
  FROM t0_shopper_last_order t0
),
t2_shoppers AS (
  SELECT t1.tenant_id, t1.user_id, t1.shopper_group, t1.reference_date
  FROM t1_shopper_group t1
  WHERE t1.shopper_group IS NOT NULL
),
t3_windows AS (
  SELECT
    t2.tenant_id,
    t2.user_id,
    t2.shopper_group,
    '0-90 days before reference' AS window_label,
    1 AS window_sort,
    t2.reference_date - 90 AS window_start,
    t2.reference_date AS window_end
  FROM t2_shoppers t2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    t2.tenant_id,
    t2.user_id,
    t2.shopper_group,
    '91-180 days before reference' AS window_label,
    2 AS window_sort,
    t2.reference_date - 180 AS window_start,
    t2.reference_date - 91 AS window_end
  FROM t2_shoppers t2
),
t4_grain AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t3.shopper_group, t3.window_label, t3.window_sort
  FROM t3_windows t3
),
t5_shopper_counts AS (
  SELECT t2.shopper_group AS shopper_group, COUNT(*) AS shopper_count
  FROM t2_shoppers t2
  GROUP BY t2.shopper_group
),
t6_tickets AS (
  SELECT
    t3.shopper_group AS shopper_group,
    t3.window_label AS window_label,
    COUNT(tk.id) AS ticket_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.first_response_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_first_response_hours
  FROM t3_windows t3
  JOIN tickets tk
    ON tk.tenant_id = t3.tenant_id
   AND tk.requester_user_id = t3.user_id
   AND DATE(tk.created_at) BETWEEN t3.window_start AND t3.window_end
  GROUP BY t3.shopper_group, t3.window_label
),
t7_csat AS (
  SELECT
    t3.shopper_group AS shopper_group,
    t3.window_label AS window_label,
    AVG(cs.score) AS avg_csat_score
  FROM t3_windows t3
  JOIN csat_responses cs
    ON cs.tenant_id = t3.tenant_id
   AND cs.respondent_user_id = t3.user_id
   AND DATE(cs.submitted_at) BETWEEN t3.window_start AND t3.window_end
  GROUP BY t3.shopper_group, t3.window_label
)
SELECT
  t4.shopper_group AS shopper_group,
  t4.window_label AS window_before_reference,
  COALESCE(t5.shopper_count, 0) AS shopper_count,
  COALESCE(t6.ticket_count, 0) AS tickets,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t6.avg_first_response_hours, 0), 2) AS avg_first_response_hours,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t7.avg_csat_score, 0), 2) AS avg_csat_score
FROM t4_grain t4
LEFT JOIN t5_shopper_counts t5 ON t5.shopper_group = t4.shopper_group
LEFT JOIN t6_tickets t6 ON t6.shopper_group = t4.shopper_group AND t6.window_label = t4.window_label
LEFT JOIN t7_csat t7 ON t7.shopper_group = t4.shopper_group AND t7.window_label = t4.window_label
ORDER BY t4.shopper_group ASC, t4.window_sort ASC

tags.details: Same two groups and windows as the marketing-engagement report: 'lapsed' (last order 180-365 days before 2025-12-31) vs 'active' (last order within 90 days), reference date is last order date for lapsed and 2025-12-31 for active, windows '0-90 days before reference' and '91-180 days before reference'. From tickets (created_at, first_response_at, requester_user_id) count tickets and avg first response hours per group/window; from csat_responses (submitted_at, score, respondent_user_id) avg score per group/window. Order by shopper group, then window ascending. Expect 4 rows.
tags.grain: one row per shopper group and time window before reference date

question: Among established merchants (not formally churned), how long since their last order, and were they already slowing down before going quiet?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  t.status,
  CAST(o.last_order_ts AS DATE) AS last_order_date,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(o.last_order_ts AS DATE)) AS days_since_last_order,
  o.lifetime_orders,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
     FROM orders o2
    WHERE o2.tenant_id = t.id
      AND o2.status <> 'cancelled'
      AND o2.placed_at > o.last_order_ts - INTERVAL '90 days'
      AND o2.placed_at <= o.last_order_ts
  ) AS orders_90d_before_last,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
     FROM orders o3
    WHERE o3.tenant_id = t.id
      AND o3.status <> 'cancelled'
      AND o3.placed_at > o.last_order_ts - INTERVAL '180 days'
      AND o3.placed_at <= o.last_order_ts - INTERVAL '90 days'
  ) AS orders_90d_before_prior
FROM tenants t
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, MAX(placed_at) AS last_order_ts, COUNT(*) AS lifetime_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
) o ON o.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.status <> 'churned'
ORDER BY days_since_last_order DESC, t.id ASC
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Silent-churn merchants: substantial accounts gone quiet without a churned flag
columns_requested: orders in 90 days before last order
tags.details: From orders (excluding cancelled): last order date is max placed_at per tenant; lifetime orders is total count. Restrict to tenants with lifetime orders at least 20 and status not equal to churned. days since last order is 2026-01-05 minus last order date. Also compute orders in the 90 days ending at the last order date, and orders in the 90 days before that, to show the trend into their most recent activity. Order by days since last order descending, tie-break tenant_id ascending. Cap 50 rows, note total count.
tags.grain: one row per merchant (tenant) with lifetime orders at least 20 and status not churned

title: Merchants slowing down: order-gap distribution among established merchants

question: How much support volume do our top merchants generate, how fast is our response, and does that show up in their CSAT?
sql:
WITH orders_window AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, o.id AS order_id, o.currency_code, o.grand_total, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-03'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
fx_rates AS (
  SELECT quote_code, as_of, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
orders_eur AS (
  SELECT ow.tenant_id, ow.order_id, ow.grand_total / fx.rate AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders_window ow
  JOIN fx_rates fx
    ON fx.quote_code = ow.currency_code
   AND fx.as_of = CAST(ow.placed_at AS date)
),
tenant_revenue AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, SUM(revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur_total, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders_eur
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
top15 AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, revenue_eur_total, order_count
  FROM tenant_revenue
  ORDER BY revenue_eur_total DESC
  LIMIT 15
),
tickets_window AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, t.id AS ticket_id,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.first_response_at - t.created_at))/3600.0 AS first_response_hours,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at))/3600.0 AS resolution_hours
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN top15 ON top15.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-03'
    AND t.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
tickets_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
    AVG(first_response_hours) AS avg_first_response_hours,
    AVG(resolution_hours) AS avg_resolution_hours
  FROM tickets_window
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
csat_window AS (
  SELECT c.tenant_id, c.score
  FROM csat_responses c
  JOIN top15 ON top15.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE c.submitted_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-03'
    AND c.submitted_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
csat_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, AVG(score) AS csat_avg_score, COUNT(*) AS csat_response_count
  FROM csat_window
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tn.name AS merchant_name,
  tn.industry,
  COALESCE(ta.ticket_count, 0) AS tickets_last_90_days,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ta.ticket_count,0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(top15.order_count,0), 2) AS tickets_per_100_orders,
  ROUND(ta.avg_first_response_hours, 2) AS avg_first_response_hours,
  ROUND(ta.avg_resolution_hours, 2) AS avg_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(ca.csat_avg_score, 2) AS csat_avg_score,
  COALESCE(ca.csat_response_count, 0) AS csat_response_count
FROM top15
JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = top15.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN tickets_agg ta ON ta.tenant_id = top15.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN csat_agg ca ON ca.tenant_id = top15.tenant_id
ORDER BY tickets_last_90_days DESC, top15.tenant_id ASC
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Merchant size and recent growth trend
tags.details: Top 15 ranked by last-90-day gross revenue EUR from orders (placed_at Oct 3 through Dec 31 2025, excluding cancelled, converted to EUR via exchange_rates), matching the earlier size and trend report's definition. For those tenants, from tickets (created_at in the same window): ticket count, avg first response hours (first_response_at minus created_at), avg resolution hours (resolved_at minus created_at); tickets per 100 orders is ticket count divided by the tenant's order count in the window, times 100; from csat_responses (submitted_at in the same window): avg score and response count. Order by tickets last 90 days descending, tie-break tenant_id ascending. Cap 50 rows (expect 15).
tags.grain: one row per merchant (tenant), limited to the top 15 by last-90-day revenue

title: Support experience for our top 15 merchants, and whether it tracks with CSAT

question: Where refunds take longer to process, do shoppers rate us worse and come back less often afterward?
sql:
WITH refund_base AS (
  SELECT
    t_pr.id AS refund_id,
    t_pr.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t_o.id AS order_id,
    t_o.user_id AS user_id,
    t_pr.created_at AS created_at,
    t_pr.processed_at AS processed_at,
    CASE
      WHEN (t_pr.processed_at - t_pr.created_at) <= INTERVAL '7 days' THEN 'fast'
      ELSE 'slow'
    END AS refund_group
  FROM payment_refunds t_pr
  JOIN payments t_pm ON t_pm.id = t_pr.payment_id
  JOIN orders t_o ON t_o.id = t_pm.order_id
  WHERE t_pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND t_pr.processed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND t_pr.created_at IS NOT NULL
),
grain AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t0.refund_group AS refund_group
  FROM refund_base t0
),
m_count_days AS (
  SELECT
    t1.refund_group AS refund_group,
    COUNT(*) AS refund_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t1.processed_at - t1.created_at)) / 86400.0) AS avg_processing_days
  FROM refund_base t1
  GROUP BY t1.refund_group
),
repeat_flags AS (
  SELECT
    t2.refund_id AS refund_id,
    t2.refund_group AS refund_group,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM orders t2o
      WHERE t2o.tenant_id = t2.tenant_id
        AND t2o.user_id = t2.user_id
        AND t2o.id <> t2.order_id
        AND t2o.status <> 'cancelled'
        AND t2o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
        AND t2o.placed_at BETWEEN t2.processed_at AND (t2.processed_at + INTERVAL '90 days')
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_repeat_order
  FROM refund_base t2
),
m_repeat AS (
  SELECT
    t3.refund_group AS refund_group,
    AVG(t3.has_repeat_order) * 100.0 AS pct_with_repeat_order
  FROM repeat_flags t3
  GROUP BY t3.refund_group
),
csat_per_refund AS (
  SELECT
    t4.refund_id AS refund_id,
    t4.refund_group AS refund_group,
    (
      SELECT AVG(t4c.score)
      FROM csat_responses t4c
      WHERE t4c.tenant_id = t4.tenant_id
        AND t4c.respondent_user_id = t4.user_id
        AND t4c.submitted_at BETWEEN t4.processed_at AND (t4.processed_at + INTERVAL '30 days')
    ) AS csat_avg_for_refund
  FROM refund_base t4
),
m_csat AS (
  SELECT
    t5.refund_group AS refund_group,
    AVG(t5.csat_avg_for_refund) AS avg_csat_score
  FROM csat_per_refund t5
  GROUP BY t5.refund_group
)
SELECT
  t_g.refund_group AS refund_speed_group,
  COALESCE(t_cd.refund_count, 0) AS refund_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t_cd.avg_processing_days, 0), 2) AS avg_processing_days,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t_rp.pct_with_repeat_order, 0), 2) AS pct_with_order_within_90d,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t_cs.avg_csat_score, 0), 2) AS avg_csat_within_30d
FROM grain t_g
LEFT JOIN m_count_days t_cd ON t_cd.refund_group = t_g.refund_group
LEFT JOIN m_repeat t_rp ON t_rp.refund_group = t_g.refund_group
LEFT JOIN m_csat t_cs ON t_cs.refund_group = t_g.refund_group
ORDER BY t_g.refund_group

columns_requested: pct with another order within 90 days after
avg csat score within 30 days after
tags.details: From payment_refunds (status equal to succeeded, created_at, processed_at), joined via payments to orders to get user_id. processing days is processed_at minus created_at; group is fast if 7 or fewer days, slow if more. pct with another order within 90 days after is the share of refund events where that user placed another order (excluding cancelled) with placed_at between processed_at and processed_at plus 90 days. avg csat score within 30 days after is the average csat_responses.score where submitted_at is between processed_at and processed_at plus 30 days for that user. Order by group. Expect 2 rows.
tags.grain: one row per refund-speed group (fast: processed within 7 days; slow: more than 7 days)

title: Refund friction and what follows: fast vs slow refunds

question: Using a simpler, reliable timestamp (the request record's own updated_at, not JSON history), roughly when were the 3 rejected-without-completed_at DSARs last touched relative to their received and due dates?
sql:
SELECT

  received_at,
  due_at,
  updated_at,
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - received_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_received_to_updated_at,
  (updated_at <= due_at) AS within_due_at
FROM data_subject_requests
WHERE status = 'rejected'
  AND completed_at IS NULL
ORDER BY received_at ASC

question: Did the February 2025 failed-login spike concentrate in a handful of merchants (and within them, a handful of emails or IPs), or was it spread evenly across the platform?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts_feb,
  SUM(CASE WHEN la.succeeded = false THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_attempts_feb,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN la.succeeded = false THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1) AS pct_failed_feb,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN la.succeeded = false THEN la.email END) AS distinct_emails_with_any_failed_attempt,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN la.succeeded = false THEN la.ip_address END) AS distinct_ips_with_any_failed_attempt,
  (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
      SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
      FROM login_attempts la2
      WHERE la2.tenant_id = t.id
        AND la2.succeeded = false
        AND la2.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-02-01'
        AND la2.occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
      GROUP BY la2.ip_address
  ) ip_counts) AS max_failed_attempts_single_ip,
  (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
      SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
      FROM login_attempts la3
      WHERE la3.tenant_id = t.id
        AND la3.succeeded = false
        AND la3.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-02-01'
        AND la3.occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
      GROUP BY la3.email
  ) email_counts) AS max_failed_attempts_single_email
FROM login_attempts la
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = la.tenant_id
WHERE la.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-02-01'
  AND la.occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
GROUP BY t.id, t.name
ORDER BY failed_attempts_feb DESC, tenant_name ASC

builds_on: Failed login attempts and suspicious access patterns by month
tags.details: Source: login_attempts joined to tenants for the name. Filter strictly to February 2025. Order by failed_attempts_feb descending so the most-affected merchants sort to the top; note the total number of tenants with any February login activity even if only the top 50 are printed. Purpose: see whether the spike is a handful of merchants/accounts/sources (a likely credential-stuffing or targeted-account event) versus a platform-wide even rise (more consistent with a client bug or outage).
tags.grain: one row per tenant (merchant), restricted to login_attempts with occurred_at between 2025-02-01 and 2025-02-28 inclusive (UTC)

question: Among the accounts with 5+ failed logins in February 2025, how many went on to log in successfully afterward, and how soon — i.e. was this a near-miss or just noise?
sql:
WITH failed_feb AS (
  SELECT email, occurred_at
  FROM login_attempts
  WHERE succeeded = false
    AND email IS NOT NULL
    AND occurred_at >= DATE '2025-02-01' AND occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
),
cohort AS (
  SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS failed_cnt, MAX(occurred_at) AS last_failed_at
  FROM failed_feb
  GROUP BY email
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
),
success_feb AS (
  SELECT email, occurred_at
  FROM login_attempts
  WHERE succeeded = true
    AND email IS NOT NULL
    AND occurred_at >= DATE '2025-02-01' AND occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
),
cohort_outcome AS (
  SELECT c.email, c.failed_cnt, c.last_failed_at,
         MIN(s.occurred_at) AS first_success_at
  FROM cohort c
  LEFT JOIN success_feb s
    ON s.email = c.email AND s.occurred_at > c.last_failed_at
  GROUP BY c.email, c.failed_cnt, c.last_failed_at
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    email, failed_cnt,
    CASE
      WHEN first_success_at IS NULL THEN 'never_succeeded_in_month'
      WHEN first_success_at <= last_failed_at + INTERVAL '1 hour' THEN 'succeeded_within_1h'
      WHEN first_success_at <= last_failed_at + INTERVAL '24 hour' THEN 'succeeded_within_24h'
      ELSE 'succeeded_later_in_month'
    END AS outcome_bucket
  FROM cohort_outcome
)
SELECT
  b.outcome_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS email_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cohort), 1) AS pct_of_cohort,
  ROUND(AVG(b.failed_cnt) FILTER (WHERE b.outcome_bucket <> 'never_succeeded_in_month'), 2) AS avg_failed_attempts_before_success,
  COUNT(DISTINCT la.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants_affected
FROM bucketed b
JOIN login_attempts la
  ON la.email = b.email
  AND la.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-02-01' AND la.occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
GROUP BY b.outcome_bucket
ORDER BY CASE b.outcome_bucket
  WHEN 'succeeded_within_1h' THEN 1
  WHEN 'succeeded_within_24h' THEN 2
  WHEN 'succeeded_later_in_month' THEN 3
  WHEN 'never_succeeded_in_month' THEN 4
END

builds_on: Failed login attempts and suspicious access patterns by month
columns_requested: avg_failed_attempts_before_success (for buckets with a success; blank for never_succeeded)
tags.details: Source: login_attempts. Define the cohort as distinct email values with >=5 failed (succeeded=false) rows in Feb 2025. For each such email, find its last failed attempt in Feb 2025, then look for the first subsequent succeeded=true attempt by that same email within February 2025; bucket by the time gap (within 1h, within 24h, later in the month) or 'never_succeeded_in_month' if none found. Report only the aggregated bucket counts — do not print individual email addresses. Order buckets: succeeded_within_1h, succeeded_within_24h, succeeded_later_in_month, never_succeeded_in_month.
tags.grain: one row per outcome bucket, computed over the cohort of distinct emails with >=5 failed login_attempts rows in February 2025 (previously counted at 102)

question: How many compliance/security incidents have been flagged, how severe are they, how long do they typically take to resolve, and is anything still sitting open a long time?
sql:
SELECT
  severity,
  count(*) AS total_events,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE resolved) AS resolved_count,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT resolved) AS unresolved_count,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE resolved) / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 1) AS pct_resolved,
  round(avg(extract(epoch FROM (resolved_at - occurred_at)) / 86400.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved), 1) AS avg_days_to_resolve,
  round(
    (percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (resolved_at - occurred_at)) / 86400.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved))::numeric,
    1
  ) AS median_days_to_resolve,
  round(
    max(CASE WHEN NOT resolved THEN extract(epoch FROM (timestamp '2025-12-31' - occurred_at)) / 86400.0 END)::numeric,
    0
  ) AS oldest_unresolved_age_days,
  count(DISTINCT event_type) AS distinct_event_types
FROM compliance_events
WHERE occurred_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01'
  AND occurred_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY severity
ORDER BY total_events DESC, severity

columns_requested: oldest_unresolved_age_days (2025-12-31 minus occurred_at, for the oldest unresolved event in this severity)
tags.details: Source: compliance_events. Use 2025-12-31 as the fixed reference date for age calculations (not CURRENT_DATE). This is the deferred 'incidents' question from last week — want a clear read on total volume, how severity breaks down, typical time-to-close, and whether any severity tier has old unresolved events that would look bad to a security reviewer. Order by total_events descending.
tags.grain: one row per compliance_events.severity value, across all tenants, all occurred_at dates from 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31

question: For the five tables that currently have no configured retention policy, how far back does the oldest data actually go, and how much of it is already older than our one known retention benchmark (audit_log's 730-day policy)?
sql:
SELECT table_name, earliest_record_date, days_since_earliest_record, total_row_count,
       row_count_older_than_730_days,
       ROUND(100.0 * row_count_older_than_730_days / NULLIF(total_row_count, 0), 2) AS pct_older_than_730_days
FROM (
  SELECT 'access_log' AS table_name,
         MIN(occurred_at)::date AS earliest_record_date,
         (DATE '2025-12-31' - MIN(occurred_at)::date) AS days_since_earliest_record,
         COUNT(*) AS total_row_count,
         SUM(CASE WHEN occurred_at < (DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '730 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS row_count_older_than_730_days
  FROM access_log

  UNION ALL

  SELECT 'change_history' AS table_name,
         MIN(occurred_at)::date,
         (DATE '2025-12-31' - MIN(occurred_at)::date),
         COUNT(*),
         SUM(CASE WHEN occurred_at < (DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '730 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  FROM change_history

  UNION ALL

  SELECT 'compliance_events' AS table_name,
         MIN(occurred_at)::date,
         (DATE '2025-12-31' - MIN(occurred_at)::date),
         COUNT(*),
         SUM(CASE WHEN occurred_at < (DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '730 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  FROM compliance_events

  UNION ALL

  SELECT 'login_attempts' AS table_name,
         MIN(occurred_at)::date,
         (DATE '2025-12-31' - MIN(occurred_at)::date),
         COUNT(*),
         SUM(CASE WHEN occurred_at < (DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '730 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  FROM login_attempts

  UNION ALL

  SELECT 'data_subject_requests' AS table_name,
         MIN(received_at)::date,
         (DATE '2025-12-31' - MIN(received_at)::date),
         COUNT(*),
         SUM(CASE WHEN received_at < (DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '730 days') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  FROM data_subject_requests
) t
ORDER BY table_name

builds_on: Retention policy coverage for audit and compliance-relevant tables
columns_requested: earliest_record_date (min of the relevant timestamp column: occurred_at for access_log/change_history/compliance_events/login_attempts, received_at for data_subject_requests)
tags.details: Sources: access_log, change_history, data_subject_requests, compliance_events, login_attempts (one SELECT per table, unioned into a single result keyed by table_name). Use 2025-12-31 as the fixed reference date. Purpose: size how exposed we are before escalating the 'no retention policy' finding to Rosa — if these tables only go back a few months this is minor, if they go back close to our full 3-year history (like audit_log's archive) it's a bigger conversation. Order by table_name.
tags.grain: one row per table, for access_log, change_history, data_subject_requests, compliance_events, and login_attempts, across all tenants

question: Among the accounts with 5+ failed logins in February 2025, how many went on to log in successfully afterward, and how soon — i.e. was this a near-miss or just noise?
sql:
WITH failed_feb AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, email, occurred_at
  FROM login_attempts
  WHERE succeeded = false
    AND occurred_at >= DATE '2025-02-01'
    AND occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
),
cohort AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, email, COUNT(*) AS failed_count, MAX(occurred_at) AS last_failed_at
  FROM failed_feb
  GROUP BY tenant_id, email
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
),
success_after AS (
  SELECT
    c.tenant_id,
    c.email,
    c.failed_count,
    c.last_failed_at,
    MIN(la.occurred_at) AS success_at
  FROM cohort c
  LEFT JOIN login_attempts la
    ON la.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
    AND la.email = c.email
    AND la.succeeded = true
    AND la.occurred_at > c.last_failed_at
    AND la.occurred_at < DATE '2025-03-01'
  GROUP BY c.tenant_id, c.email, c.failed_count, c.last_failed_at
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    email,
    failed_count,
    CASE
      WHEN success_at IS NULL THEN 'never_succeeded_in_month'
      WHEN success_at <= last_failed_at + INTERVAL '1 hour' THEN 'succeeded_within_1h'
      WHEN success_at <= last_failed_at + INTERVAL '24 hour' THEN 'succeeded_within_24h'
      ELSE 'succeeded_later_in_month'
    END AS outcome_bucket
  FROM success_after
),
cohort_size AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM cohort
),
bucket_list AS (
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    ('succeeded_within_1h', 1),
    ('succeeded_within_24h', 2),
    ('succeeded_later_in_month', 3),
    ('never_succeeded_in_month', 4)
  ) AS b(outcome_bucket, sort_order)
)
SELECT
  b.outcome_bucket,
  COUNT(c.tenant_id) AS pair_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(c.tenant_id) / cs.n, 1) AS pct_of_cohort,
  CASE
    WHEN b.outcome_bucket = 'never_succeeded_in_month' THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(AVG(c.failed_count), 2)
  END AS avg_failed_attempts_before_success,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants_affected
FROM bucket_list b
LEFT JOIN classified c ON c.outcome_bucket = b.outcome_bucket
CROSS JOIN cohort_size cs
GROUP BY b.outcome_bucket, b.sort_order, cs.n
ORDER BY b.sort_order

builds_on: February 2025 repeat-failure accounts: did they succeed afterward?
tags.details: Fix for last night's broken version: scope the cohort to (tenant_id, email) pairs, not email alone, since login_attempts.email is only unique per tenant and matching on email alone silently conflated unrelated users across merchants. For each pair in the cohort, find the first succeeded=true login_attempts row for that same (tenant_id, email) occurring after that pair's last Feb-2025 failed attempt, within February 2025 only. Classify each pair into exactly one bucket using this precedence: succeeded_within_1h, else succeeded_within_24h, else succeeded_later_in_month, else never_succeeded_in_month. Buckets must be mutually exclusive and exhaustive: pair_count across all 4 rows must sum exactly to the cohort size, and pct_of_cohort must sum to 100%. Do not print individual emails. Order buckets in the sequence listed above.
tags.grain: one row per outcome bucket, computed over the cohort of distinct (tenant_id, email) pairs with >=5 failed login_attempts rows in February 2025

question: At the 3 merchants that drove the February 2025 spike, do the failed logins look automated/bot-like (concentrated in a narrow time window, few user agents) or more like a broad client-side bug (spread across the month, many different user agents)?
sql:
with failed_logins as (
  select
    t.id as tenant_id,
    t.name as tenant_name,
    la.user_agent,
    cast(la.occurred_at as date) as failure_day
  from login_attempts la
  join tenants t on t.id = la.tenant_id
  where t.name in ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij')
    and la.succeeded = false
    and la.occurred_at >= timestamp '2025-02-01'
    and la.occurred_at < timestamp '2025-03-01'
),
tenant_totals as (
  select tenant_id, tenant_name, count(*) as total_failed
  from failed_logins
  group by tenant_id, tenant_name
),
user_agent_counts as (
  select tenant_id, user_agent, count(*) as ua_count
  from failed_logins
  group by tenant_id, user_agent
),
distinct_ua as (
  select tenant_id, count(distinct user_agent) as distinct_user_agents
  from failed_logins
  group by tenant_id
),
top_ua as (
  select tenant_id, max(ua_count) as top_ua_count
  from user_agent_counts
  group by tenant_id
),
day_counts as (
  select tenant_id, failure_day, count(*) as day_count
  from failed_logins
  group by tenant_id, failure_day
),
distinct_days as (
  select tenant_id, count(distinct failure_day) as distinct_calendar_days_with_failures
  from failed_logins
  group by tenant_id
),
max_day as (
  select tenant_id, max(day_count) as max_failed_attempts_single_day
  from day_counts
  group by tenant_id
),
ranked_days as (
  select tenant_id, day_count,
    row_number() over (partition by tenant_id order by day_count desc) as rn
  from day_counts
),
top3_days as (
  select tenant_id, sum(day_count) as top3_sum
  from ranked_days
  where rn <= 3
  group by tenant_id
)
select
  tt.tenant_name,
  du.distinct_user_agents,
  round(100.0 * tu.top_ua_count / tt.total_failed, 1) as top_user_agent_share_pct,
  dd.distinct_calendar_days_with_failures,
  md.max_failed_attempts_single_day,
  round(100.0 * t3.top3_sum / tt.total_failed, 1) as pct_failed_attempts_in_top_3_days
from tenant_totals tt
join distinct_ua du on du.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join top_ua tu on tu.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join distinct_days dd on dd.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join max_day md on md.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join top3_days t3 on t3.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
order by tt.tenant_name

builds_on: February 2025 failed login concentration by merchant
columns_requested: top_user_agent_share_pct (share of this tenant's Feb failed attempts from the single most common user_agent string)
tags.details: Source: login_attempts, filtered to these 3 tenants and succeeded=false, occurred_at in February 2025. Purpose: distinguish a likely automated/attack pattern (few user agents, failures clustered in a short burst of days) from a likely broad technical/client bug (many distinct user agents similar to normal traffic, failures spread fairly evenly across most of the month) — directly feeds Aylin's read on whether this was a near-miss security event or an internal issue. Order by tenant_name.
tags.grain: one row per tenant, for the 3 merchants identified last week (Cragsley Outfitters, Marrowby & Vane, Studio Vrij), restricted to their failed login_attempts in February 2025
