question: For the 3 merchants behind the February 2025 spike, was that an isolated one-quarter event, or do they show a recurring pattern of elevated login failures over the full history?
sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT t.id AS tenant_id, t.name AS tenant_name, c.year_num, c.quarter_num
  FROM tenants t
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT year_num, quarter_num
    FROM calendar_days
    WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  ) c
  WHERE t.name IN ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij')
)
SELECT
  b.tenant_name AS tenant_name,
  b.year_num || '-Q' || b.quarter_num AS quarter,
  COALESCE(ta.total_attempts, 0) AS total_attempts,
  COALESCE(fa.failed_attempts, 0) AS failed_attempts,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ta.total_attempts, 0) = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(fa.failed_attempts, 0) / ta.total_attempts, 2)
  END AS pct_failed
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT la.tenant_id, cd.year_num, cd.quarter_num, COUNT(*) AS total_attempts
  FROM login_attempts la
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(la.occurred_at AS DATE)
  GROUP BY la.tenant_id, cd.year_num, cd.quarter_num
) ta ON ta.tenant_id = b.tenant_id AND ta.year_num = b.year_num AND ta.quarter_num = b.quarter_num
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT la.tenant_id, cd.year_num, cd.quarter_num, COUNT(*) AS failed_attempts
  FROM login_attempts la

question: Did the February 2025 failure spike hit the same calendar days across all three affected merchants (pointing to one shared platform cause), and was access-denied logging silent specifically on those spike days?

WITH target_tenants AS (

days AS (

),
failed_logins AS (

  WHERE la.succeeded = false
    AND la.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01'
    AND la.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01'
  GROUP BY la.tenant_id, DATE(la.occurred_at)
),
access_denied_all AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log
  WHERE action = 'access_denied'
    AND occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01'
    AND occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT tenant_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log_archive
  WHERE action = 'access_denied'
    AND occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01'
    AND occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01'
),
access_denied_daily AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(ad.occurred_at) AS event_date,
    COUNT(*) AS access_denied_count
  FROM access_denied_all ad
  JOIN target_tenants tt ON tt.id = ad.tenant_id
  GROUP BY DATE(ad.occurred_at)
)
SELECT
  d.calendar_date AS date,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN tt.name ILIKE '%cragsley%' THEN fl.failed_count END), 0) AS cragsley_failed_logins,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN tt.name ILIKE '%marrowby%' THEN fl.failed_count END), 0) AS marrowby_vane_failed_logins,

  COALESCE(MAX(adn.access_denied_count), 0) AS access_denied_events_3_merchants
FROM days d
LEFT JOIN failed_logins fl ON fl.login_date = d.calendar_date
LEFT JOIN target_tenants tt ON tt.id = fl.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN access_denied_daily adn ON adn.event_date = d.calendar_date
GROUP BY d.calendar_date
ORDER BY d.calendar_date ASC

question: Is the near-zero web-session count for subscription merchants a tracking blind spot, or does it reflect real behavior — customers browsing once to sign up and then never browsing again?
sql:
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
  COUNT(*) AS customers,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cust.before_cnt > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_with_session_before,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cust.after_cnt > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_with_session_after,
  ROUND(AVG(cust.after_cnt), 2) AS avg_sessions_after_first_order_per_customer
FROM (
  SELECT fo.tenant_id, fo.user_id, fo.first_order_at,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM web_sessions ws WHERE ws.tenant_id = fo.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = fo.user_id AND ws.started_at <= fo.first_order_at) AS before_cnt,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM web_sessions ws WHERE ws.tenant_id = fo.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = fo.user_id AND ws.started_at > fo.first_order_at) AS after_cnt
  FROM (
    SELECT tenant_id, user_id, MIN(placed_at) AS first_order_at
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Brennquell Kaffee','Spice Route Box','Grind Collective','Honeycomb Larder'))
    GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
  ) fo
) cust
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = cust.tenant_id
GROUP BY t.name
ORDER BY t.name

question: Does basket size, price point, or discount usage differ between carts that convert quickly and carts that stall for hours or days?
sql:
WITH tenant_filter AS (
  SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
cart_base AS (
  SELECT c.id, c.tenant_id, c.status, c.item_count, c.subtotal, c.currency_code, c.created_at,
         coalesce(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) AS resolved_at,
         er.rate AS eur_rate
  FROM carts c
  JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = c.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code = c.currency_code AND er.as_of = c.created_at::date
  WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
cart_calc AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE WHEN currency_code='EUR' THEN subtotal ELSE subtotal / NULLIF(eur_rate,0) END AS subtotal_eur,
    CASE WHEN resolved_at IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at))/3600.0 END AS resolution_hours
  FROM cart_base
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN resolution_hours IS NULL THEN 'unresolved/still active'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 1 THEN '<1 hour'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 24 THEN '1-24 hours'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 168 THEN '1-7 days'
      ELSE '>7 days'
    END AS duration_bucket
  FROM cart_calc
),
order_discount_flag AS (
  SELECT o.cart_id, CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od WHERE od.order_id = o.id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_discount
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.cart_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  b.duration_bucket AS duration_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
  ROUND(AVG(b.item_count)::numeric, 2) AS avg_item_count,
  ROUND(AVG(b.subtotal_eur)::numeric, 2) AS avg_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY b.subtotal_eur)::numeric, 2) AS median_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.status='converted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_converted,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.status='converted' AND odf.has_discount=1) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.status='converted'),0), 1) AS pct_converted_with_discount
FROM bucketed b
LEFT JOIN order_discount_flag odf ON odf.cart_id = b.id
GROUP BY b.duration_bucket
ORDER BY CASE b.duration_bucket
  WHEN '<1 hour' THEN 1
  WHEN '1-24 hours' THEN 2
  WHEN '1-7 days' THEN 3
  WHEN '>7 days' THEN 4
  WHEN 'unresolved/still active' THEN 5
END

question: Did cart conversion dip during the week cart-reminder emails broke (week of Nov 24, 2025), suggesting those reminders meaningfully nudge stalled carts toward purchase?

with tenant as (

  where name = 'Cragsley Outfitters'

cart_weeks as (

    c.id,
    c.status,
    c.created_at,

    cd.week_start
  from carts c
  join tenant t on c.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  join calendar_days cd on cd.calendar_date = c.created_at::date
  where cd.week_start >= date '2025-10-06'
    and cd.week_start <= date '2025-12-22'
)

  count(*) as carts_created,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when status = 'converted' then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as overall_conversion_pct,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when status = 'converted' and converted_at is not null
            and extract(epoch from (converted_at - created_at)) / 3600.0 <= 1
            then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_converted_within_1_hour,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when status = 'converted' and converted_at is not null
            and extract(epoch from (converted_at - created_at)) / 3600.0 >= 24
            and extract(epoch from (converted_at - created_at)) / 3600.0 <= 168
            then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_converted_1_to_7_days
from cart_weeks
group by week_start
order by week_start asc

question: Is checkout hesitation concentrated in higher-priced carts specifically (not just low-item-count carts), i.e. does price point on its own predict stalling?
sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
cart_population AS (
  SELECT c.id, c.tenant_id, c.currency_code, c.subtotal, c.item_count, c.status, c.created_at, c.converted_at
  FROM carts c
  JOIN target_tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
cart_with_eur AS (
  SELECT cp.*,
    CASE WHEN cp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN cp.subtotal
         ELSE cp.subtotal / er.rate END AS subtotal_eur
  FROM cart_population cp
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = cp.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(cp.created_at AS DATE)
),
tiered_carts AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN subtotal_eur < 50 THEN '<€50'
      WHEN subtotal_eur < 100 THEN '€50-100'
      WHEN subtotal_eur < 200 THEN '€100-200'
      ELSE '€200+'
    END AS price_tier,
    CASE WHEN status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_converted,
    CASE WHEN status = 'converted' AND converted_at <= created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS resolved_1h,
    CASE WHEN status = 'converted' AND converted_at > created_at + INTERVAL '1 day' AND converted_at <= created_at + INTERVAL '7 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS resolved_1_7d
  FROM cart_with_eur
),
tier_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_carts FROM tiered_carts
),
tier_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    price_tier,
    COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
    AVG(item_count) AS avg_item_count,
    SUM(is_converted) AS converted_count,
    SUM(resolved_1h) AS resolved_1h_count,
    SUM(resolved_1_7d) AS resolved_1_7d_count
  FROM tiered_carts
  GROUP BY price_tier
)
SELECT
  ta.price_tier AS price_tier,
  ta.cart_count AS cart_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.cart_count / tt.total_carts, 2) AS pct_of_total_carts,
  ROUND(ta.avg_item_count, 2) AS avg_item_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.converted_count / ta.cart_count, 2) AS overall_conversion_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.resolved_1h_count / ta.cart_count, 2) AS pct_resolved_within_1_hour,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.resolved_1_7d_count / ta.cart_count, 2) AS pct_resolved_in_1_7_days
FROM tier_aggregates ta
CROSS JOIN tier_totals tt
ORDER BY
  CASE ta.price_tier
    WHEN '<€50' THEN 1
    WHEN '€50-100' THEN 2
    WHEN '€100-200' THEN 3
    WHEN '€200+' THEN 4
  END

  SELECT c.id, c.tenant_id, c.user_id, c.status, c.converted_at, c.created_at
  FROM carts c
  JOIN six_tenants st ON st.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c.created_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND NOT (c.status = 'converted' AND c.converted_at IS NOT NULL AND c.converted_at <= c.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour')
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT p.*,
    CASE WHEN p.user_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM email_log e
      WHERE e.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
        AND e.user_id = p.user_id
        AND e.sent_at > p.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
        AND e.sent_at <= p.created_at + INTERVAL '48 hour'
    ) THEN 'received_email' ELSE 'no_email' END AS grp
  FROM population p
),
agg AS (
  SELECT grp,
    COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE user_id IS NULL) AS guest_cart_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'converted') AS converted_count
  FROM grouped
  GROUP BY grp
),
medians AS (
  SELECT grp,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (converted_at - created_at))/86400.0) AS median_days_to_convert
  FROM grouped
  WHERE status = 'converted'
  GROUP BY grp
)
SELECT
  a.grp AS group_name,
  a.cart_count,
  a.guest_cart_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.converted_count / a.cart_count, 1) AS pct_eventually_converted,
  ROUND(m.median_days_to_convert::numeric, 1) AS median_days_to_convert
FROM agg a
LEFT JOIN medians m ON m.grp = a.grp
ORDER BY CASE WHEN a.grp = 'received_email' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, a.grp

question: Once we separate carts that could never receive an email (guests) from logged-in customers who simply weren't emailed, does receiving an email still look like it drives recovery?
sql:
WITH base_carts AS (
  SELECT c.tenant_id, c.user_id, c.status, c.created_at, c.converted_at,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM email_log e
      WHERE e.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
        AND e.user_id = c.user_id
        AND e.sent_at >= c.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
        AND e.sent_at <= c.created_at + INTERVAL '48 hour'
    ) AS has_email
  FROM carts c
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
    AND c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c.created_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND NOT (c.status = 'converted' AND c.converted_at IS NOT NULL AND c.converted_at <= c.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour')
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN user_id IS NULL THEN 'guest'
      WHEN has_email THEN 'received_email'
      ELSE 'logged_in_no_email'
    END AS group_name,
    status,
    converted_at,
    created_at
  FROM base_carts
)
SELECT
  group_name AS "group",
  COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'converted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_eventually_converted,
  ROUND(
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (
      ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (converted_at - created_at)) / 86400.0
    ) FILTER (WHERE status = 'converted')
  , 1) AS median_days_to_convert
FROM grouped
GROUP BY group_name
ORDER BY CASE group_name WHEN 'received_email' THEN 1 WHEN 'logged_in_no_email' THEN 2 WHEN 'guest' THEN 3 END

question: Does the 'single-item carts convert worse' pattern hold once we separate out guest (never logged in) carts, or is it mostly just another expression of the guest-vs-logged-in gap?
sql:
with target_tenants as (
    select id, name
    from tenants
    where name in ('Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
scoped_carts as (
    select
        c.id,
        c.status,
        case when c.user_id is null then 'guest' else 'logged_in' end as user_status,
        case when c.item_count = 1 then 'single-item' else 'multi-item' end as item_count_group
    from carts c
    join target_tenants t on t.id = c.tenant_id
    where c.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
      and c.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      and c.item_count >= 1
),
grouped as (
    select
        user_status,
        item_count_group,
        count(*) as cart_count,
        sum(case when status = 'converted' then 1 else 0 end) as converted_count
    from scoped_carts
    group by user_status, item_count_group
)
select
    user_status,
    item_count_group,
    cart_count,
    round(100.0 * converted_count / cart_count, 1) as conversion_pct
from grouped
order by
    case
        when user_status = 'logged_in' and item_count_group = 'multi-item' then 1
        when user_status = 'logged_in' and item_count_group = 'single-item' then 2
        when user_status = 'guest' and item_count_group = 'multi-item' then 3
        when user_status = 'guest' and item_count_group = 'single-item' then 4
    end

question: Is the email that correlates with cart recovery a deliberate cart-reminder/recovery mechanism, or just general marketing/engagement email that happens to land in that window?
sql:
WITH t0 AS ( -- stalled carts: created in window, not converted within first hour
  SELECT
    c0.id AS cart_id,
    c0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    c0.user_id AS user_id,
    c0.created_at AS created_at
  FROM carts c0
  JOIN tenants t0t ON t0t.id = c0.tenant_id
  WHERE t0t.name IN (
      'Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty',
      'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik'
    )
    AND c0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c0.created_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND NOT (
      c0.status = 'converted'
      AND c0.converted_at IS NOT NULL
      AND c0.converted_at <= c0.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
    )
),
t1 AS ( -- distinct matched email_log rows per stalled cart owner, in the recovery window
  SELECT DISTINCT
    e1.id AS email_log_id,
    e1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    e1.template_id AS template_id
  FROM email_log e1
  JOIN t0 ON t0.tenant_id = e1.tenant_id
         AND t0.user_id = e1.user_id
         AND e1.sent_at >= t0.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
         AND e1.sent_at <= t0.created_at + INTERVAL '48 hour'
),
t2 AS ( -- email counts per (tenant, template)
  SELECT
    t1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t1.template_id AS template_id,
    COUNT(*) AS email_count
  FROM t1
  GROUP BY t1.tenant_id, t1.template_id
),
t3 AS ( -- grand total of matched emails, for pct calc
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_matched
  FROM t1
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(tn.name, 'multiple merchants') AS merchant,
  COALESCE(nt.code, 'no template / ad hoc') AS template_code,
  COALESCE(nt.name, 'no template / ad hoc') AS template_name,
  COALESCE(nt.channel, 'n/a') AS channel,
  t2.email_count AS email_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * t2.email_count / NULLIF(t3.total_matched, 0), 2) AS pct_of_matched_emails
FROM t2
CROSS JOIN t3
LEFT JOIN notification_templates nt ON nt.id = t2.template_id
LEFT JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = t2.tenant_id AND nt.id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY t2.email_count DESC, template_code, merchant

question: How big a slice of our 2025 collected revenue comes from B2B wholesale merchants (industrial supplies, office equipment) versus every other vertical, so we know whether omitting their receivables line from the board pack is material?
sql:
SELECT
  coalesce(t.industry, '(none)') as industry,
  count(distinct p.tenant_id) as tenant_count,
  sum(p.amount / er.rate) as total_2025_money_collected_eur,
  round(
    sum(p.amount / er.rate) * 100.0 / sum(sum(p.amount / er.rate)) over (),
    1
  ) as pct_of_total_revenue
FROM payments p
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
  AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
  AND er.as_of = date(p.captured_at)
WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
  AND p.captured_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
  AND p.captured_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY coalesce(t.industry, '(none)')
ORDER BY total_2025_money_collected_eur DESC, industry

question: Is the refund-after-payout-settled problem concentrated in a handful of merchants, and did it get bigger or smaller in the second half of 2025 versus the first?
sql:
WITH late_refunds AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id, pr.processed_at, pr.amount, pr.currency_code
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payment_id = pr.payment_id
  JOIN payouts po ON po.id = pi.payout_id
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at > po.paid_at
),
converted AS (
  SELECT
    lr.tenant_id,
    lr.processed_at,
    CASE WHEN lr.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN lr.amount
         ELSE lr.amount / er.rate END AS eur_amount
  FROM late_refunds lr
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = lr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(lr.processed_at AS date)
),
tenant_totals AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    SUM(eur_amount) FILTER (WHERE processed_at < DATE '2025-07-01') AS h1_2025_late_refund_eur,
    SUM(eur_amount) FILTER (WHERE processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-01') AS h2_2025_late_refund_eur
  FROM converted
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
totals AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    COALESCE(h1_2025_late_refund_eur,0) + COALESCE(h2_2025_late_refund_eur,0) AS total_2025_late_refund_eur,
    h1_2025_late_refund_eur, h2_2025_late_refund_eur
  FROM tenant_totals
),
grand_total AS (
  SELECT SUM(total_2025_late_refund_eur) AS grand_total_eur FROM totals
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  ROUND(tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur, 2) AS h1_2025_late_refund_eur,
  ROUND(tot.h2_2025_late_refund_eur, 2) AS h2_2025_late_refund_eur,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND((tot.h2_2025_late_refund_eur - tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur) / tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur * 100, 1)
  END AS change_pct,
  ROUND(tot.total_2025_late_refund_eur, 2) AS total_2025_late_refund_eur,
  ROUND(tot.total_2025_late_refund_eur / gt.grand_total_eur * 100, 1) AS pct_of_all_late_refunds_2025
FROM totals tot
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tot.tenant_id
CROSS JOIN grand_total gt
ORDER BY tot.total_2025_late_refund_eur DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 20

Group by tenant (join tenants on payment_refunds.tenant_id). h1_2025_late_refund_eur = sum for processed_at in Jan-Jun 2025, converted to EUR via exchange_rates using payment_refunds.currency_code and processed_at date. h2_2025_late_refund_eur = same for Jul-Dec 2025. change_pct = (h2 - h1) / h1 * 100, rounded to 1 decimal (NULL if h1 is 0). total_2025_late_refund_eur = h1 + h2. pct_of_all_late_refunds_2025 = total_2025_late_refund_eur / (sum of total_2025_late_refund_eur across ALL tenants with any late refunds in 2025, not just those shown) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: payment_refunds, payout_items, payouts, tenants, exchange_rates. Show only the top 20 tenants by total_2025_late_refund_eur. Order by total_2025_late_refund_eur descending.

question: At the portfolio level, how much of the gap between order value and money collected is just timing (recent orders not yet settled) versus a permanent shortfall that age doesn't fix?
sql:
WITH order_base AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.grand_total,
    o.currency_code,
    o.placed_at,
    (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) AS age_days,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 3 THEN '0-3 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 7 THEN '4-7 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 14 THEN '8-14 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 30 THEN '15-30 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 60 THEN '31-60 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 90 THEN '61-90 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 180 THEN '91-180 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 365 THEN '181-365 days'
      ELSE '366+ days'
    END AS age_bucket
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
order_count_agg AS (
  SELECT t0.age_bucket, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM order_base t0
  GROUP BY t0.age_bucket
),
grand_total_agg AS (
  SELECT t1.age_bucket, SUM(t1.grand_total / t2.rate) AS orders_grand_total_eur
  FROM order_base t1
  JOIN exchange_rates t2
    ON t2.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND t2.quote_code = t1.currency_code
    AND t2.as_of = CAST(t1.placed_at AS date)
  GROUP BY t1.age_bucket
),
payment_agg AS (
  SELECT t3.age_bucket, SUM(t4.amount / t5.rate) AS matched_money_collected_eur
  FROM order_base t3
  JOIN payments t4
    ON t4.order_id = t3.order_id
    AND t4.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
  JOIN exchange_rates t5
    ON t5.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND t5.quote_code = t4.currency_code
    AND t5.as_of = CAST(t4.captured_at AS date)
  GROUP BY t3.age_bucket
)
SELECT
  t6.age_bucket,
  t6.order_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t7.orders_grand_total_eur, 0), 2) AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t8.matched_money_collected_eur, 0), 2) AS matched_money_collected_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t8.matched_money_collected_eur, 0) / NULLIF(t7.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS match_rate_pct
FROM order_count_agg t6
LEFT JOIN grand_total_agg t7 ON t7.age_bucket = t6.age_bucket
LEFT JOIN payment_agg t8 ON t8.age_bucket = t6.age_bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE t6.age_bucket
    WHEN '0-3 days' THEN 1
    WHEN '4-7 days' THEN 2
    WHEN '8-14 days' THEN 3
    WHEN '15-30 days' THEN 4
    WHEN '31-60 days' THEN 5
    WHEN '61-90 days' THEN 6
    WHEN '91-180 days' THEN 7
    WHEN '181-365 days' THEN 8
    ELSE 9
  END

builds_on: Order-to-payment gap re-measured with refund-inclusive payment status
tags.details: Population: all orders with status not 'cancelled' and placed_at between 2023-01-01 and 2025-12-31. Bucket each order by its age in days as of 2025-12-31: '0-3 days', '4-7 days', '8-14 days', '15-30 days', '31-60 days', '61-90 days', '91-180 days', '181-365 days', '366+ days'. order_count = count of orders in the bucket. orders_grand_total_eur = sum of orders.grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=orders.currency_code, as_of=placed_at date). matched_money_collected_eur = sum of linked payments.amount (payments.order_id = orders.id) where payments.status in ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded'), converted to EUR via payments.currency_code and captured_at date (an order's full matched total if it has multiple such payments). match_rate_pct = matched_money_collected_eur / orders_grand_total_eur * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: orders, payments, exchange_rates. Order by age_bucket from youngest to oldest.

question: Do any marketing segments or analytics cohorts already encode a definition like 'customers who purchased recently' or 'all customers', so we can certify a customer count the business already uses rather than inventing a new one?
sql:
SELECT
    'segment' AS source,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    s.name AS name,
    s.is_dynamic AS is_dynamic,
    s.member_count AS member_count,
    substring(cast(s.rules AS varchar), 1, 500) AS rules_definition,
    s.last_refreshed_at AS last_updated
FROM segments s
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = s.tenant_id
UNION ALL
SELECT
    'cohort' AS source,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    c.name AS name,
    c.is_dynamic AS is_dynamic,
    c.member_count AS member_count,
    substring(cast(c.definition AS varchar), 1, 500) AS rules_definition,
    c.computed_at AS last_updated
FROM cohorts c
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
ORDER BY member_count DESC, tenant_name ASC, name ASC
LIMIT 50

question: Does the 8-14 day dip in order-to-payment match rate trace to a specific payment method with inherently slower capture (e.g. bank transfer or wire), supporting the 'it's timing, not a hole' explanation?
sql:
SELECT
  t0.kind AS kind,
  COALESCE(t1.payment_count, 0) AS payment_count,
  t2.avg_days_order_to_capture AS avg_days_order_to_capture,
  t3.pct_captured_within_7_days AS pct_captured_within_7_days,
  t4.pct_captured_within_14_days AS pct_captured_within_14_days
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT pm0.kind AS kind FROM payment_methods pm0) t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm1.kind AS kind, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payments p1
  JOIN payment_methods pm1 ON p1.payment_method_id = pm1.id
  JOIN orders o1 ON p1.order_id = o1.id
  WHERE p1.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p1.order_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm1.kind
) t1 ON t1.kind = t0.kind
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm2.kind AS kind,
         ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p2.captured_at - o2.placed_at)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_order_to_capture
  FROM payments p2
  JOIN payment_methods pm2 ON p2.payment_method_id = pm2.id
  JOIN orders o2 ON p2.order_id = o2.id
  WHERE p2.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p2.order_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p2.captured_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o2.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm2.kind
) t2 ON t2.kind = t0.kind
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm3.kind AS kind,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN (p3.captured_at - o3.placed_at) <= INTERVAL '7 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_captured_within_7_days
  FROM payments p3
  JOIN payment_methods pm3 ON p3.payment_method_id = pm3.id
  JOIN orders o3 ON p3.order_id = o3.id
  WHERE p3.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p3.order_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p3.captured_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o3.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm3.kind
) t3 ON t3.kind = t0.kind
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm4.kind AS kind,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN (p4.captured_at - o4.placed_at) <= INTERVAL '14 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_captured_within_14_days
  FROM payments p4
  JOIN payment_methods pm4 ON p4.payment_method_id = pm4.id
  JOIN orders o4 ON p4.order_id = o4.id
  WHERE p4.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p4.order_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p4.captured_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o4.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm4.kind
) t4 ON t4.kind = t0.kind
WHERE COALESCE(t1.payment_count, 0) > 0
ORDER BY t2.avg_days_order_to_capture DESC NULLS LAST, t0.kind ASC

builds_on: Order-to-payment match rate by order age
tags.details: Population: payments with status in ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded'), joined to payment_methods on payments.payment_method_id = payment_methods.id to get kind (card, bank_transfer, paypal, wallet, wire, credit), and joined to orders on payments.order_id = orders.id to get placed_at (only include payments linked to an order; skip payments with a null order_id). Group by payment_methods.kind. payment_count = count of such payments. avg_days_order_to_capture = average of (payments.captured_at minus orders.placed_at) in days, rounded to 1 decimal. pct_captured_within_7_days = percentage of these payments where (captured_at - placed_at) <= 7 days, rounded to 1 decimal. pct_captured_within_14_days = percentage where (captured_at - placed_at) <= 14 days, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: payments, payment_methods, orders. Order by avg_days_order_to_capture descending.
tags.grain: payment method kind (payment_methods.kind)

question: Which tenants are actually operating as B2B wholesalers (by using the deals/CRM module, not just by industry label), how much 2025 revenue do they represent, and what does their receivables picture look like on the corrected tenant list?
sql:
SELECT
  tenant_agg.tenant_name,
  tenant_agg.industry,
  tenant_agg.deal_count,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.total_contract_value_eur, 2) AS total_contract_value_eur,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.total_2025_revenue_eur, 2) AS total_2025_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.total_2025_revenue_eur / NULLIF(company_total.total, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_2025_revenue,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.open_amount_due_eur, 2) AS open_amount_due_eur,
  tenant_agg.pct_amount_due_overdue
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.id,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    t.industry,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deals d WHERE d.tenant_id = t.id) AS deal_count,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(d.contract_value / er.rate), 0)
       FROM deals d
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = d.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = COALESCE(d.signed_at, CAST(d.created_at AS date))
      WHERE d.tenant_id = t.id
    ) AS total_contract_value_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(p.amount / er.rate), 0)
       FROM payments p
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
      WHERE p.tenant_id = t.id
        AND p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
        AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) AS total_2025_revenue_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(i.amount_due / er.rate), 0)
       FROM invoices i
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
      WHERE i.tenant_id = t.id
        AND i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
        AND i.amount_due > 0
    ) AS open_amount_due_eur,
    (SELECT CASE
              WHEN SUM(i.amount_due / er.rate) = 0 THEN NULL
              ELSE ROUND(
                     SUM(CASE WHEN i.due_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' THEN i.amount_due / er.rate ELSE 0 END)
                     / SUM(i.amount_due / er.rate) * 100, 1)
            END
       FROM invoices i
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
      WHERE i.tenant_id = t.id
        AND i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
        AND i.amount_due > 0
    ) AS pct_amount_due_overdue
  FROM tenants t
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deals d WHERE d.tenant_id = t.id)
) AS tenant_agg
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(p2.amount / er2.rate), 0) AS total
  FROM payments p2
  JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = p2.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = CAST(p2.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p2.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p2.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p2.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
) AS company_total
ORDER BY tenant_agg.total_2025_revenue_eur DESC, tenant_agg.tenant_name

builds_on: 2025 revenue share by industry vertical
B2B wholesaler receivables aging
tags.details: Population: every tenant that has at least one row in the deals table (closed-won B2B contracts), which per the company briefing is the module used by B2B wholesale merchants. For each such tenant: industry = tenants.industry (as stored, for cross-reference against last night's industry report). deal_count = count of deals rows. total_contract_value_eur = sum of deals.contract_value converted to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=deals.currency_code, as_of=signed_at date, or created_at date if signed_at is null). total_2025_revenue_eur = sum of this tenant's payments.amount where status in ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded') and captured_at in 2025, converted to EUR via payments.currency_code and captured_at date. pct_of_total_2025_revenue = total_2025_revenue_eur / (sum of total_2025_revenue_eur across ALL tenants company-wide, not just this list) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. open_amount_due_eur = sum of invoices.amount_due for this tenant where invoices.status in ('open','past_due') and amount_due > 0, as of snapshot 2025-12-31, converted to EUR via invoices.currency_code and as_of=2025-12-31. pct_amount_due_overdue = (sum of amount_due where due_at < 2025-12-31) / open_amount_due_eur * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: deals, tenants, payments, invoices, exchange_rates. Order by total_2025_revenue_eur descending.

question: What are Castell Fasteners' actual open invoices, so we can reconcile my €14,481 open-receivables figure against Merchant Success's reported €5,080 and present one consistent number to the board?
sql:
SELECT
  t0.invoice_number AS invoice_number,
  t0.status AS status,
  t0.currency_code AS currency_code,
  t0.total AS total,
  t0.amount_due AS amount_due,
  t0.issued_at AS issued_at,
  t0.due_at AS due_at,
  CASE
    WHEN t0.due_at IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE GREATEST(CAST(DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(t0.due_at AS date) AS integer), 0)
  END AS days_overdue
FROM invoices t0
JOIN tenants t1 ON t1.id = t0.tenant_id
WHERE t1.name = 'Castell Fasteners'
  AND t0.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
  AND t0.amount_due > 0
ORDER BY t0.amount_due DESC, t0.invoice_number ASC

question: Are the 6 B2B-CRM tenants showing exactly 0.0 revenue/contract value/receivables genuinely inactive, or is this a currency-conversion or join artifact hiding real activity?
sql:
WITH deal_tenants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id FROM deals
),
deal_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    string_agg(DISTINCT currency_code, ',') AS deal_currency_codes,
    count(*) AS deal_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE contract_value > 0) AS deals_with_positive_value_count,
    sum(contract_value) AS raw_contract_value_total
  FROM deals
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
line_items_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    sum(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct)) AS raw_deal_line_items_total
  FROM deal_line_items
  WHERE tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM deal_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
orders_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS orders_count_2025
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM deal_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
payments_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS payments_captured_count_2025
  FROM payments
  WHERE status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM deal_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.default_currency_code AS tenant_default_currency_code,
  ds.deal_currency_codes,
  ds.deal_count,
  ds.deals_with_positive_value_count,
  ds.raw_contract_value_total,
  li.raw_deal_line_items_total,
  COALESCE(os.orders_count_2025, 0) AS orders_count_2025,
  COALESCE(ps.payments_captured_count_2025, 0) AS payments_captured_count_2025
FROM deal_summary ds
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ds.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN line_items_summary li ON li.tenant_id = ds.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN orders_summary os ON os.tenant_id = ds.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN payments_summary ps ON ps.tenant_id = ds.tenant_id
ORDER BY ds.deal_count DESC, t.name

question: Is Cragsley Outfitters' outsized share of company-wide late refunds just proportional to how big it is, or does it refund late at a higher rate than other large merchants?
sql:
WITH refund_eur AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         pr.amount / er.rate AS eur_amount,
         CASE WHEN po.paid_at IS NOT NULL AND pr.processed_at > po.paid_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_late
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  LEFT JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payment_id = pr.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN payouts po ON po.id = pi.payout_id
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tenant_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
         SUM(eur_amount) AS total_refunds_2025_eur,
         SUM(CASE WHEN is_late = 1 THEN eur_amount ELSE 0 END) AS late_refunds_2025_eur
  FROM refund_eur
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
company_agg AS (
  SELECT SUM(eur_amount) AS total_eur,
         SUM(CASE WHEN is_late = 1 THEN eur_amount ELSE 0 END) AS late_eur
  FROM refund_eur
)
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
       ta.total_refunds_2025_eur,
       ta.late_refunds_2025_eur,
       ROUND(ta.late_refunds_2025_eur / NULLIF(ta.total_refunds_2025_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_own_refunds_late,
       ROUND(ca.late_eur / NULLIF(ca.total_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS company_avg_pct_late_2025
FROM tenant_agg ta
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ta.tenant_id
CROSS JOIN company_agg ca
ORDER BY ta.total_refunds_2025_eur DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 15

question: With the full, verified 9-tenant B2B wholesale list and EUR handled correctly, what does the receivables aging actually look like for the board pack?
sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name
  FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN (
    'Ballycorran Industrial Supply',
    'Kontor24 Burobedarf',
    'OfficeHub Nordic',
    'Midland Safety Wear',
    'Castell Fasteners',
    'Hanse Industriebedarf',
    'Polder Packaging',
    'Deskline Supplies',
    'Papeterie Grossiste'
  )
),
rates AS (
  SELECT quote_code, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR' AND as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
),
inv AS (
  SELECT
    i.id,
    i.amount_due,
    i.currency_code,
    i.due_at,
    CASE
      WHEN i.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN i.amount_due
      ELSE i.amount_due / r.rate
    END AS amount_due_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= DATE '2025-12-31' THEN 'Not yet due'
      WHEN DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date) BETWEEN 1 AND 30 THEN '1-30 days overdue'
      WHEN DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date) BETWEEN 31 AND 60 THEN '31-60 days overdue'
      WHEN DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date) BETWEEN 61 AND 90 THEN '61-90 days overdue'
      ELSE '90+ days overdue'
    END AS aging_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= DATE '2025-12-31' THEN 0
      ELSE DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date)
    END AS days_past_due
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN target_tenants t ON t.id = i.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN rates r ON r.quote_code = i.currency_code
  WHERE i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
    AND i.amount_due > 0
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    aging_bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS invoice_count,
    SUM(amount_due_eur) AS amount_due_eur,
    AVG(days_past_due) AS avg_days_past_due
  FROM inv
  GROUP BY aging_bucket
)
SELECT
  aging_bucket,
  invoice_count,
  ROUND(amount_due_eur, 2) AS amount_due_eur,
  ROUND(amount_due_eur / SUM(amount_due_eur) OVER () * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_amount_due,
  ROUND(avg_days_past_due, 1) AS avg_days_past_due
FROM agg
ORDER BY amount_due_eur DESC, aging_bucket ASC

question: If a query naively joins exchange_rates for EUR the same way it does for every other currency, how much revenue silently vanishes, and is EUR the only currency affected?
sql:
WITH pop AS (
  SELECT currency_code, amount, captured_at
  FROM payments
  WHERE status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
naive AS (
  SELECT p.currency_code, SUM(p.amount / er.rate) AS naive_eur
  FROM pop p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
  GROUP BY p.currency_code
),
correct AS (
  SELECT p.currency_code,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p.amount ELSE p.amount / er.rate END) AS correct_eur
  FROM pop p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
  GROUP BY p.currency_code
)
SELECT
  c.currency_code,
  COALESCE(n.naive_eur, 0) AS total_2025_revenue_naive_eur,
  c.correct_eur AS total_2025_revenue_correct_eur,
  c.correct_eur - COALESCE(n.naive_eur, 0) AS shortfall_eur,
  ROUND((c.correct_eur - COALESCE(n.naive_eur, 0)) / c.correct_eur * 100, 1) AS shortfall_pct
FROM correct c
LEFT JOIN naive n ON n.currency_code = c.currency_code
ORDER BY c.correct_eur DESC, c.currency_code

Tables: payments, exchange_rates. Order by total_2025_revenue_correct_eur descending.

question: What is the real 2025 revenue and open receivables for all 9 verified B2B wholesale tenants, now that the EUR-conversion bug that zeroed out 6 of them is fixed?
sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT t0.id AS tenant_id, t0.name AS tenant_name, t0.default_currency_code AS currency_code
  FROM tenants t0
  WHERE t0.name IN (
    'Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'Kontor24 Burobedarf', 'OfficeHub Nordic',
    'Midland Safety Wear', 'Castell Fasteners', 'Hanse Industriebedarf',
    'Polder Packaging', 'Deskline Supplies', 'Papeterie Grossiste'
  )
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deals d0 WHERE d0.tenant_id = t0.id)
),
revenue_tenant AS (
  SELECT p0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p0.amount
             ELSE p0.amount / er0.rate END) AS total_2025_revenue_eur
  FROM payments p0
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er0.quote_code = p0.currency_code
   AND er0.as_of = CAST(p0.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p0.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p0.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p0.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p0.tenant_id
),
revenue_all AS (
  SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p1.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p1.amount
                  ELSE p1.amount / er1.rate END) AS total_revenue_eur_all
  FROM payments p1
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = p1.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = CAST(p1.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p1.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p1.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p1.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
open_invoices_tenant AS (
  SELECT i0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN i0.amount_due
             ELSE i0.amount_due / er2.rate END) AS open_amount_due_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i0.due_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00'
             THEN (CASE WHEN i0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN i0.amount_due
                        ELSE i0.amount_due / er2.rate END)
             ELSE 0 END) AS overdue_amount_due_eur
  FROM invoices i0
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = i0.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
  WHERE i0.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
    AND i0.amount_due > 0
  GROUP BY i0.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tt0.tenant_name AS tenant_name,
  tt0.currency_code AS currency_code,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rt0.total_2025_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS total_2025_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rt0.total_2025_revenue_eur, 0) / NULLIF(ra0.total_revenue_eur_all, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_2025_revenue,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oi0.open_amount_due_eur, 0), 2) AS open_amount_due_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(oi0.open_amount_due_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE oi0.overdue_amount_due_eur / oi0.open_amount_due_eur * 100 END
  , 1) AS pct_amount_due_overdue
FROM target_tenants tt0
LEFT JOIN revenue_tenant rt0 ON rt0.tenant_id = tt0.tenant_id
CROSS JOIN revenue_all ra0
LEFT JOIN open_invoices_tenant oi0 ON oi0.tenant_id = tt0.tenant_id
ORDER BY total_2025_revenue_eur DESC, tt0.tenant_name

question: Beyond Owner/Administrator accounts, how much other access (ordinary staff logins, open sessions, active API keys, active webhooks) is still live on tenants that have already churned?
sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users u WHERE u.tenant_id = t.id AND u.deleted_at IS NULL) AS total_users,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users u WHERE u.tenant_id = t.id AND u.deleted_at IS NULL AND u.status = 'active') AS active_users,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions s WHERE s.tenant_id = t.id AND s.revoked_at IS NULL) AS open_sessions,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM api_keys ak WHERE ak.tenant_id = t.id AND ak.status = 'active') AS active_api_keys,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM webhooks w WHERE w.tenant_id = t.id AND w.is_active = true) AS active_webhooks,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_accounts sa WHERE sa.tenant_id = t.id) AS service_accounts
FROM tenants t
WHERE t.status = 'churned'
ORDER BY active_users DESC, tenant_name ASC

Order by 'users with status = active' descending, tenant name as tie-break. Expect a small number of rows (well under 50) — note total churned tenant count.

question: For the two 'deletion-like' events on our financial documents that don't use soft-delete — a cancelled order, a voided invoice — is there any audit_log record at all tying back to that specific row?
sql:
SELECT
  'order cancellations' AS entity_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
      WHERE al.entity_table = 'orders'
        AND al.entity_id = o.id
        AND al.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    )
  ) AS events_with_match,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
        WHERE al.entity_table = 'orders'
          AND al.entity_id = o.id
          AND al.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
      )
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1
  ) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM orders o
WHERE o.status = 'cancelled'
  AND o.cancelled_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND o.cancelled_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'invoice voids' AS entity_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
      WHERE al.entity_table = 'invoices'
        AND al.entity_id = i.id
        AND al.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
    )
  ) AS events_with_match,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
        WHERE al.entity_table = 'invoices'
          AND al.entity_id = i.id
          AND al.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
      )
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1
  ) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM invoices i
WHERE i.status = 'void'
  AND i.voided_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND i.voided_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

ORDER BY entity_type

builds_on: Audit-trail coverage of actual soft-deletions, by entity table
columns_requested: events with at least one matching audit_log row (any action, entity_table + entity_id match)
tags.details: Row 1: orders where status = 'cancelled'. For each such order, check whether any audit_log row exists with entity_table = 'orders' and entity_id = orders.id (any action, not just 'delete', since the logged action type for a cancellation isn't known in advance). Row 2: invoices where status = 'void'. Same existence check against audit_log with entity_table = 'invoices' and entity_id = invoices.id. coverage_rate = events with a match / total events, rounded to 1 decimal percent. This is a looser test than the soft-delete report (any audit row at all for that record, not specifically a 'delete' action) — flag in the report notes that even a 100% match here wouldn't confirm the cancellation/void itself was logged, only that the record has some audit trail presence.

question: Is the missing deletion audit trail we found for products a narrow, one-table problem, or does it extend across most of the tables that support soft-deletion?

  UNION ALL SELECT 'categories', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM categories WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'products', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'product_variants', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM product_variants WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'collections', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM collections WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'users', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'billing_profiles', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM billing_profiles WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL SELECT 'coupons', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM coupons WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'promotions', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM promotions WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'campaigns', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM campaigns WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL SELECT 'landing_pages', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM landing_pages WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'referrals', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM referrals WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'loyalty_programs', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM loyalty_programs WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ab_tests', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM ab_tests WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'experiments', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM experiments WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'cohorts', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM cohorts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'funnels', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM funnels WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'contacts', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM contacts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'accounts', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM accounts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'knowledge_articles', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM knowledge_articles WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'macros', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM macros WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'files', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM files WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'utm_links', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM utm_links WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'suppliers', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM suppliers WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'warehouses', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM warehouses WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
),
audit_counts AS (
  SELECT entity_table, COUNT(*) AS deleted_audit_rows
  FROM audit_log
  WHERE action = 'delete'
  GROUP BY entity_table
)
SELECT
  sd.entity_table,
  sd.total_soft_deleted,
  COALESCE(ac.deleted_audit_rows, 0) AS matching_audit_rows,
  CASE WHEN sd.total_soft_deleted = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(ac.deleted_audit_rows, 0) / sd.total_soft_deleted, 1)
  END AS coverage_rate_pct,

question: Has any invoice actually been voided or marked uncollectible on the platform, and if so, is the event dated and traceable in audit_log — or was last night's zero result just because voided_at is missing?
sql:
SELECT
  i.status AS invoice_status,
  COUNT(*) AS total_invoices,
  COUNT(i.voided_at) AS voided_at_populated,
  SUM(CASE WHEN i.voided_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS voided_at_null,
  SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log a
      WHERE a.entity_table = 'invoices'
        AND a.entity_id = i.id
        AND a.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matching_audit_log_rows,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log a
      WHERE a.entity_table = 'invoices'
        AND a.entity_id = i.id
        AND a.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)
  , 1) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM invoices i
WHERE i.status IN ('void', 'uncollectible')
GROUP BY i.status
ORDER BY total_invoices DESC, invoice_status

builds_on: Audit traceability of order cancellations and invoice voids
columns_requested: total invoices in this status (all-time, regardless of voided_at)
of those, rows with a populated voided_at timestamp
of those, rows with voided_at null (undated, can't tell when it happened)
matching audit_log rows (any action, entity_table = 'invoices', entity_id = invoices.id)
coverage rate among all invoices in this status (%)
tags.details: Source: invoices where status in ('void','uncollectible'), grouped by status. Do NOT filter out rows with null voided_at from the total count this time — count all of them, then separately report how many have voided_at populated vs null, so we can tell whether last night's zero was 'no voids ever happened' or 'voids happened but aren't timestamped.' Coverage test is an EXISTS against audit_log by (entity_table='invoices', entity_id=invoices.id, same tenant_id), any action. Order by total invoices descending, status as tie-break (only 2 rows expected).
tags.grain: one row per terminal invoice status: 'void' and 'uncollectible'

question: Generic audit_log barely covers order cancellations (0.2%) — but does the purpose-built order_status_history table actually capture who cancelled each order and when?
sql:
WITH cancelled_orders AS (
    SELECT
        id AS order_id,
        tenant_id
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = 'cancelled'
),
joined AS (
    SELECT
        co.tenant_id,
        co.order_id,
        h.id AS history_id,
        h.changed_by_user_id
    FROM cancelled_orders co
    LEFT JOIN order_status_history h
        ON h.order_id = co.order_id
        AND h.to_status = 'cancelled'
        AND h.tenant_id = co.tenant_id
),
per_tenant AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS cancelled_orders,
        COUNT(history_id) AS matching_history_rows,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN history_id IS NOT NULL THEN order_id END) AS orders_with_match,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN changed_by_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS matching_rows_with_actor
    FROM joined
    GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    pt.cancelled_orders,
    pt.matching_history_rows,
    ROUND(100.0 * pt.orders_with_match / pt.cancelled_orders, 1) AS coverage_rate_pct,
    pt.matching_rows_with_actor
FROM per_tenant pt
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = pt.tenant_id
ORDER BY
    coverage_rate_pct ASC,
    pt.cancelled_orders DESC,
    tenant_name ASC
LIMIT 50

builds_on: Audit traceability of order cancellations and invoice voids
columns_requested: of matches, rows with a non-null changed_by_user_id (a named actor, not just a timestamp)
tags.details: Source: orders where status = 'cancelled', left-joined to order_status_history on order_status_history.order_id = orders.id and order_status_history.to_status = 'cancelled' (same tenant_id). coverage_rate = orders with at least one such matching history row / total cancelled orders for that tenant, rounded to 1 decimal percent. Also report how many of the matched rows have changed_by_user_id is not null, since a transition logged with no actor still doesn't answer 'who'. Order by coverage rate ascending (worst first), cancelled orders count descending as tie-break, tenant name as final tie-break. Cap at 50 rows; note total tenant count if more (expect ~90 per last night's report 2).
tags.grain: one row per tenant that has at least one cancelled order

title: Order status history coverage for cancelled orders

question: Since shopper accounts have 0% MFA, what actually stands in for a second factor today — are most shoppers authenticating through an OAuth provider (Google/Apple/etc., which carries its own security), or are they overwhelmingly raw password-only accounts with no backup at all?
sql:
with shoppers as (
    select id, tenant_id, email
    from users
    where is_staff = false
      and deleted_at is null
),
oauth_linked_users as (
    select distinct user_id
    from oauth_accounts
),
confirmed_mfa_users as (
    select distinct user_id
    from mfa_devices
    where confirmed_at is not null
),
recent_login_users as (
    select distinct s.id as user_id
    from shoppers s
    join login_attempts la
      on la.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
     and (la.user_id = s.id or la.email = s.email)
    where la.occurred_at >= timestamp '2025-10-05'
      and la.occurred_at <  timestamp '2026-01-01'
),
classified_shoppers as (
    select
        s.id,
        case when o.user_id is not null then 'OAuth-linked' else 'password-only' end as method_category
    from shoppers s
    left join oauth_linked_users o on o.user_id = s.id
),
total_shoppers as (
    select count(*) as total_count from shoppers
)
select
    cs.method_category,
    count(*) as shopper_user_count,
    round(100.0 * count(*) / t.total_count, 1) as share_of_shoppers_pct,
    count(mfa.user_id) as confirmed_mfa_count,
    count(rl.user_id) as recently_active_count
from classified_shoppers cs
cross join total_shoppers t
left join confirmed_mfa_users mfa on mfa.user_id = cs.id
left join recent_login_users rl on rl.user_id = cs.id
group by cs.method_category, t.total_count
order by shopper_user_count desc, cs.method_category

builds_on: Platform-wide MFA adoption trend by month, staff vs. shoppers
columns_requested: method category ('OAuth-linked' = has ≥1 oauth_accounts row, 'password-only' = no oauth_accounts row)
of those, confirmed MFA count (expected near-zero, included to double-check for any overlap)
of those, users with at least one login_attempt in the last 90 days (2025-10-05 to 2025-12-31), i.e. recently active
tags.details: Source: users where is_staff = false and deleted_at is null, left-joined to oauth_accounts (user_id) to classify into the two categories, and to mfa_devices (confirmed_at is not null) and login_attempts (occurred_at in the window, matched by email or user_id) for the other two measures. Share of all shoppers = category count / total shoppers, rounded to 1 decimal percent. Only 2 rows expected (OAuth-linked, password-only); order by shopper user count descending.
tags.grain: one row per authentication method category among shopper (is_staff = false) users

title: Shopper authentication method mix: OAuth-linked vs password-only

sql:
SELECT

    (DATE '2026-01-05' - ak.created_at::date) AS age_days,

question: Are broadly-scoped (admin_api) keys specifically a feature of our oldest, longest-unrotated keys, or is that scope just how every integration key is set up regardless of age — i.e. is 'old + broad' a rotation failure or simply the norm?
sql:
SELECT
  bucket AS age_bucket,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ak_id) AS total_active_keys,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN has_admin_api THEN ak_id END) AS admin_api_scoped_keys,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN has_admin_api THEN ak_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ak_id), 0), 1) AS admin_api_share_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN no_scope_recorded THEN ak_id END) AS no_scope_recorded_keys,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM (
  SELECT
    ak.id AS ak_id,
    ak.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 90 THEN 'Under 90 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 365 THEN '90 days-1 year'
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 730 THEN '1-2 years'
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 1460 THEN '2-4 years'
      ELSE '4+ years'
    END AS bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 90 THEN 1
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 365 THEN 2
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 730 THEN 3
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 1460 THEN 4
      ELSE 5
    END AS bucket_order,
    CASE WHEN rl.has_admin_api = 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_admin_api,
    CASE WHEN rl.api_key_id IS NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS no_scope_recorded
  FROM api_keys ak
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT api_key_id, MAX(CASE WHEN limit_scope = 'admin_api' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_admin_api
    FROM rate_limits
    WHERE api_key_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY api_key_id
  ) rl ON rl.api_key_id = ak.id
  WHERE ak.status = 'active'
) sub
GROUP BY bucket, bucket_order
ORDER BY bucket_order

builds_on: Active API key age distribution (rotation hygiene)
Scope tally across all 76 long-lived (4+ year) active API keys
columns_requested: of those, keys with no matching rate_limits row ('no scope recorded')

Order rows by bucket from youngest to oldest in the fixed sequence (not alphabetical), so the trend is readable top to bottom.

question: Is 'zero portability requests in 3 years' a real zero, or are shopper data exports being fulfilled outside the formal DSAR process (a logging blind spot)?
sql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN dsr.id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS linked_to_dsar,
  COUNT(*) AS export_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT de.subject_user_id) AS distinct_subject_users,
  MIN(de.requested_at) AS earliest_requested_at,
  MAX(de.requested_at) AS latest_requested_at,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE de.status = 'completed') AS completed_export_count,
  AVG(de.row_count) FILTER (WHERE de.row_count IS NOT NULL) AS avg_row_count
FROM data_exports de
LEFT JOIN data_subject_requests dsr ON dsr.data_export_id = de.id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY linked_to_dsar ASC

builds_on: Data subject requests: monthly volume, closure time, and overdue backlog
columns_requested: distinct subject users (count of distinct subject_user_id)
completed export count (status indicating the export finished)
average row_count (for exports where row_count is not null)
tags.details: Source: data_exports LEFT JOIN data_subject_requests ON data_subject_requests.data_export_id = data_exports.id. 'Linked' = a matching data_subject_requests row exists (regardless of that row's request_type); 'not linked' = no such row. Platform-wide, full history, no date filter. If the 'not linked' row has a meaningful count, that indicates shopper data exports happen outside the DSAR table entirely, which would mean request_type='portability' showing 0 in data_subject_requests is a process/logging gap rather than genuine zero demand. Order by linked_to_dsar (Y first, then N).
tags.grain: one row per linked-to-DSAR status (2 rows: linked, not linked)

question: What is the defensible, auditable count of privacy (DSAR) requests by type and status, so we can reconcile against the ~48 figure quoted elsewhere and the 60 we found last week before briefing the regulator?
sql:
SELECT
  request_type,
  status,
  count(*) AS request_count,
  min(received_at)::date AS earliest_received_at,
  max(received_at)::date AS latest_received_at,
  round(
    percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (
      ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (completed_at - received_at)) / 86400.0
    ) FILTER (WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL),
    1
  ) AS median_days_to_close
FROM data_subject_requests
GROUP BY request_type, status
ORDER BY request_type, status

builds_on: Data subject request status audit: does completed_at reflect true closure?
columns_requested: median days to close (completed_at minus received_at, in days, for rows where completed_at is not null; blank if none)
tags.details: Source: data_subject_requests, no date or tenant filter (full history, platform-wide, matching what last week's reports covered). Group by request_type and status exactly as stored (do not normalize casing) so we can see if any unexpected type/status strings exist. This is meant to be the single ground-truth table that explains how other reported totals (e.g. Risk & Payments' ~48) might be a subset of ours (e.g. excluding a status or request_type) — order by request_type, then status, so all rows for a type are grouped together.

question: Beyond the confirmed email_log failure, how much data in the other four policy-covered tables is currently sitting past its stated retention window?
sql:
WITH policy AS (
  SELECT entity_table, MIN(retention_days) AS retention_days, MIN(action_on_expiry) AS action_on_expiry
  FROM retention_policies
  WHERE entity_table IN ('events','job_runs','page_views','system_health_checks')
  GROUP BY entity_table
),
events_stats AS (
  SELECT 'events' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.occurred_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.occurred_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'events'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM events t0
),
job_runs_stats AS (
  SELECT 'job_runs' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.queued_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.queued_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'job_runs'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM job_runs t0
),
page_views_stats AS (
  SELECT 'page_views' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.viewed_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.viewed_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'page_views'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM page_views t0
),
system_health_checks_stats AS (
  SELECT 'system_health_checks' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.checked_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.checked_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'system_health_checks'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM system_health_checks t0
),
all_stats AS (
  SELECT * FROM events_stats
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM job_runs_stats
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM page_views_stats
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM system_health_checks_stats
)
SELECT
  a.entity_table AS entity_table,
  COALESCE(p.retention_days, 0) AS stated_retention_days,
  COALESCE(p.action_on_expiry, 'unknown') AS action_on_expiry,
  a.total_rows AS total_rows,
  a.oldest_age_days AS oldest_row_age_days,
  a.exceeding_rows AS rows_exceeding_retention,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.exceeding_rows / NULLIF(a.total_rows, 0), 2) AS pct_exceeding_retention
FROM all_stats a
LEFT JOIN policy p ON p.entity_table = a.entity_table
ORDER BY pct_exceeding_retention DESC, a.entity_table ASC

builds_on: Retention policy landscape: distinct rules by entity table
email_log actual retention vs. the stated 730-day delete policy
audit_log actual archiving vs. the stated 730-day archive policy
columns_requested: stated retention_days (from retention_policies, confirmed uniform across tenants last week)
total rows currently in the live table (platform-wide)
oldest row age in days (as of 2026-01-05)
pct of rows exceeding stated retention
tags.details: Source: retention_policies for the stated retention_days/action_on_expiry per table (one value each, already confirmed uniform across all 120 tenants last week), joined against each live table using its natural timestamp: events.occurred_at, job_runs.queued_at, page_views.viewed_at, system_health_checks.checked_at. Use the literal date 2026-01-05 for all age math (never CURRENT_DATE/now()). This mirrors last week's email_log/audit_log checks but at a compact one-row-per-table summary so all four fit on one page, giving a complete current picture of retention-window violations across every policy-covered table, not just the one confirmed so far. Order by pct of rows exceeding retention, descending (worst first).
tags.grain: one row per entity_table: events, job_runs, page_views, system_health_checks

question: Are the data subject requests received before 2023-01-01 legitimate historical/backfilled compliance records, or a data quality artifact?
sql:
SELECT
  t0.public_id AS public_id,
  t1.name AS tenant_name,
  t0.request_type AS request_type,
  t0.status AS status,
  t0.received_at AS received_at,
  t0.completed_at AS completed_at,
  t0.created_at AS created_at,
  ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.created_at - t0.received_at)) / 86400.0, 1) AS days_received_to_created,
  LEFT(COALESCE(t0.notes, ''), 200) AS notes
FROM data_subject_requests t0
JOIN tenants t1 ON t1.id = t0.tenant_id
WHERE t0.received_at < DATE '2023-01-01'
ORDER BY t0.received_at ASC, t0.public_id ASC

columns_requested: created_at (when this row was written into our system)
tags.details: Source: data_subject_requests filtered to received_at < '2023-01-01', platform-wide, full history. The key diagnostic is the gap between received_at and created_at: a large gap (row created well after 2023, e.g. during a migration) supports 'legitimate backfill with original historical date preserved'; a near-zero gap would be suspicious since the new platform/warehouse history is stated to start 2023-01-01. Order by received_at ascending.

question: For the 3 accounts under a payment-dispute legal hold, what internal evidence (payment status, support ticket activity) suggests whether the underlying dispute is still active or has gone stale?
sql:
WITH holds AS (
  SELECT lh.id AS legal_hold_id, lh.tenant_id, lh.subject_user_id, lh.placed_at, t.name AS tenant_name
  FROM legal_holds lh
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = lh.tenant_id
  WHERE lh.is_active = true
    AND t.name IN ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Rue Lafayette Studio', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
),
latest_payment AS (
  SELECT h.legal_hold_id, p.status, p.updated_at, p.amount, p.currency_code,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY h.legal_hold_id ORDER BY p.updated_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM holds h
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = h.subject_user_id AND o.tenant_id = h.tenant_id
  JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id
),
latest_payment_top AS (
  SELECT * FROM latest_payment WHERE rn = 1
),
open_tickets AS (
  SELECT h.legal_hold_id, COUNT(*) AS open_ticket_count
  FROM holds h
  JOIN tickets tk ON tk.requester_user_id = h.subject_user_id AND tk.tenant_id = h.tenant_id
  WHERE tk.status NOT IN ('solved','closed')
  GROUP BY h.legal_hold_id
),
latest_ticket AS (
  SELECT h.legal_hold_id, tk.last_message_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY h.legal_hold_id ORDER BY tk.last_message_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM holds h
  JOIN tickets tk ON tk.requester_user_id = h.subject_user_id AND tk.tenant_id = h.tenant_id
),
latest_ticket_top AS (
  SELECT * FROM latest_ticket WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
  h.tenant_name,
  h.subject_user_id,
  CAST(h.placed_at AS date) AS hold_placed_date,
  DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(h.placed_at AS date) AS days_since_placed,
  lp.status AS latest_payment_status,
  CAST(lp.updated_at AS date) AS latest_payment_updated_date,
  lp.amount AS latest_payment_amount,
  lp.currency_code AS latest_payment_currency,
  COALESCE(ot.open_ticket_count, 0) AS open_ticket_count,
  CAST(lt.last_message_at AS date) AS latest_ticket_activity_date,
  DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lt.last_message_at AS date) AS days_since_ticket_activity
FROM holds h
LEFT JOIN latest_payment_top lp ON lp.legal_hold_id = h.legal_hold_id
LEFT JOIN open_tickets ot ON ot.legal_hold_id = h.legal_hold_id
LEFT JOIN latest_ticket_top lt ON lt.legal_hold_id = h.legal_hold_id
ORDER BY days_since_placed DESC, h.tenant_name

builds_on: Legal holds: active scope, coverage, and staleness
Linking rejected erasure requests to active legal holds
columns_requested: latest payment status for this user (most recent by updated_at, via orders.user_id = subject_user_id joined to payments)
open ticket count for this user (tickets.requester_user_id, status not in solved/closed)
most recent ticket last_message_at for this user (date)
days since that last ticket activity
tags.details: Source: legal_holds (the 3 active rows identified last week) joined by subject_user_id to orders -> payments (most recent payment by updated_at for that user) and to tickets (requester_user_id = subject_user_id). legal_holds has no populated entity_schema/entity_table/entity_id for these rows, so there's no direct link to a specific disputed payment — this report approximates by looking at the user's most recent payment activity and most recent support ticket activity as indirect evidence of whether the case is still live or has gone quiet. Use literal date 2026-01-05 for age math. Order by days since placed, descending.
tags.grain: one row per legal hold (3 rows: Marrowby & Vane, Rue Lafayette Studio, Cragsley Outfitters)

title: Evidence check on the 3 legal-hold-linked chargeback disputes

question: Across the full history, how many consent purposes do we actually track, and is the analytics_cookies 'always 100% opted in, zero withdrawals' pattern unique or does it appear elsewhere?
sql:
SELECT
  cr.purpose,
  COUNT(*) AS total_records,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cr.user_id) AS distinct_users,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.status = 'granted') AS granted_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.status = 'withdrawn') AS withdrawn_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.status = 'expired') AS expired_count,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * (
      SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sub.user_id)
      FROM consent_records sub
      WHERE sub.purpose = cr.purpose
        AND sub.status IN ('withdrawn', 'expired')
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT cr.user_id), 0)
  , 2) AS pct_users_ever_withdrawn_or_expired,
  MIN(cr.occurred_at) AS earliest_occurred_at,
  MAX(cr.occurred_at) AS latest_occurred_at
FROM consent_records cr
GROUP BY cr.purpose
ORDER BY total_records DESC, cr.purpose

builds_on: Consent trend by purpose and month: grants, withdrawals, and net opt-in rate
columns_requested: pct of distinct users with at least one withdrawn or expired record ever
tags.details: Source: consent_records, platform-wide, full history (not restricted to 2023-2025, in case any purpose has pre-2023 rows similar to what we just found in data_subject_requests). Group by purpose. This confirms whether there are really only 2 purposes in the system (as the row counts implied last week) and gives a definitive, auditable answer on whether 'never withdrawn' is isolated to analytics_cookies or a broader pattern that would undermine describing our consent capture as reliable to a regulator. Order by total records descending.
tags.grain: one row per distinct consent_records.purpose value, full history, no date filter
