question: Is the growing points liability just a 'young programme, redemptions lag issuance' phase that will level out, or do even our oldest member cohorts still show a structurally low redemption rate?
sql:
with cohort_accounts as (
    select
        la.id as loyalty_account_id,
        la.loyalty_program_id,
        cd.year_num,
        cd.quarter_num,
        cd.quarter_start
    from loyalty_accounts la
    join calendar_days cd on cd.calendar_date = cast(la.enrolled_at as date)
    where cd.quarter_start >= date '2023-01-01'
      and cd.quarter_start <= date '2025-10-01'
),

account_currency as (
    select
        ca.loyalty_account_id,
        ca.year_num,
        ca.quarter_num,
        ca.quarter_start,
        lp.points_per_currency,
        lp.currency_code
    from cohort_accounts ca
    join loyalty_programs lp on lp.id = ca.loyalty_program_id
),

transaction_amounts as (
    select
        ac.loyalty_account_id,
        ac.year_num,
        ac.quarter_num,
        ac.quarter_start,
        lt.direction,
        case
            when ac.currency_code = 'EUR' then (lt.points / ac.points_per_currency)
            else (lt.points / ac.points_per_currency) / er.rate
        end as amount_eur
    from account_currency ac
    join loyalty_transactions lt on lt.loyalty_account_id = ac.loyalty_account_id
    left join exchange_rates er
        on er.base_code = 'EUR'
       and er.quote_code = ac.currency_code
       and er.as_of = cast(lt.occurred_at as date)
),

cohort_members as (
    select
        year_num,
        quarter_num,
        quarter_start,
        count(distinct loyalty_account_id) as member_count
    from cohort_accounts
    group by year_num, quarter_num, quarter_start
),

cohort_transactions as (
    select
        year_num,
        quarter_num,
        quarter_start,
        sum(case when direction = 'earn' then amount_eur else 0 end) as total_points_earned_value_eur,
        sum(case when direction <> 'earn' then amount_eur else 0 end) as total_points_redeemed_value_eur
    from transaction_amounts
    group by year_num, quarter_num, quarter_start
)

select
    cast(cm.year_num as varchar) || '-Q' || cast(cm.quarter_num as varchar) as enrollment_quarter,
    cm.member_count,
    (extract(year from date '2025-12-31') - extract(year from cm.quarter_start)) * 12
        + (extract(month from date '2025-12-31') - extract(month from cm.quarter_start))
        as months_since_cohort_quarter_start,
    round(coalesce(ct.total_points_earned_value_eur, 0), 2) as total_points_earned_value_eur,
    round(coalesce(ct.total_points_redeemed_value_eur, 0), 2) as total_points_redeemed_value_eur,
    round(
        case when coalesce(ct.total_points_earned_value_eur, 0) = 0 then null
             else ct.total_points_redeemed_value_eur / ct.total_points_earned_value_eur * 100
        end, 2
    ) as lifetime_redemption_rate_pct
from cohort_members cm
left join cohort_transactions ct
    on ct.year_num = cm.year_num
   and ct.quarter_num = cm.quarter_num
   and ct.quarter_start = cm.quarter_start
order by cm.quarter_start asc

tags.details: Group loyalty_accounts by the calendar quarter of enrolled_at (2023-Q1 through 2025-Q4). member_count = distinct accounts in that cohort. months_since_cohort_quarter_start = number of months between that quarter's start date and 2025-12-31 (fixed reference, so older cohorts show a higher number, e.g. 2023-Q1 to 2025-12-31 is about 36 months). For each cohort's members, total_points_earned_value_eur = lifetime sum of 'earn'-direction loyalty_transactions converted to currency via the account's program points_per_currency and currency_code, then to EUR via exchange_rates as_of occurred_at (same method as the earlier cost-by-month and unit-economics reports). total_points_redeemed_value_eur = same conversion for non-'earn'-direction transactions. lifetime_redemption_rate_pct = total_points_redeemed_value_eur divided by total_points_earned_value_eur as a percentage. Order by enrollment_quarter ascending (oldest cohort first) so the trend across cohort age is easy to read.

question: Within Apparel and Footwear alone, where 72% of loyalty members sit, do members still look worse off than non-members on orders, revenue and refunds once we also control for how long they have been a customer?
sql:
WITH apparel_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
),
qualifying_users AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id, u.created_at
  FROM users u
  JOIN apparel_tenants t ON t.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM orders o
      WHERE o.user_id = u.id
        AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
        AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    )
),
order_agg AS (
  SELECT
    o.user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_order_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled') AS non_cancelled_order_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN o.grand_total / er.rate ELSE 0 END) AS total_revenue_eur,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
         OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)
    ) AS refunded_order_count
  FROM orders o
  JOIN qualifying_users qu ON qu.user_id = o.user_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at)::date
  GROUP BY o.user_id
),
segmented AS (
  SELECT
    qu.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la WHERE la.user_id = qu.user_id)
      THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member'
    END AS segment,
    CASE
      WHEN qu.created_at > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '6 months' THEN 'under 6 months'
      WHEN qu.created_at > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '12 months' THEN '6 to 12 months'
      WHEN qu.created_at > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '24 months' THEN '12 to 24 months'
      ELSE 'over 24 months'
    END AS tenure_band
  FROM qualifying_users qu
)
SELECT
  s.tenure_band,
  s.segment,
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  ROUND(AVG(oa.total_order_count), 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(oa.total_revenue_eur), 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(oa.total_revenue_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(oa.non_cancelled_order_count), 0), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(oa.refunded_order_count) / NULLIF(SUM(oa.total_order_count), 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM segmented s
JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.user_id = s.user_id
GROUP BY s.tenure_band, s.segment
ORDER BY
  CASE s.tenure_band
    WHEN 'under 6 months' THEN 1
    WHEN '6 to 12 months' THEN 2
    WHEN '12 to 24 months' THEN 3
    WHEN 'over 24 months' THEN 4
  END,
  CASE s.segment WHEN 'loyalty member' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END

question: Is the large average-order-value gap seen among Apparel members (28-40% lower than non-members across every tenure band) explained by heavier discounting at checkout, or do members simply buy cheaper products before any discount is applied?
sql:
WITH apparel_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.currency_code, o.subtotal, o.discount_total, o.grand_total, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id
  WHERE t.industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
    AND u.is_staff = false
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
user_segment AS (
  SELECT ao.*,
    CASE WHEN la.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM apparel_orders ao
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) la ON la.user_id = ao.user_id
),
fx_converted AS (
  SELECT us.segment,
    us.subtotal / CASE WHEN us.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS subtotal_eur,
    us.discount_total / CASE WHEN us.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS discount_total_eur,
    us.grand_total / CASE WHEN us.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM user_segment us
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = us.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(us.placed_at AS DATE)
),
segment_agg AS (
  SELECT segment,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    AVG(subtotal_eur) AS avg_subtotal_eur,
    AVG(discount_total_eur) AS avg_discount_total_eur,
    AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_grand_total_eur,
    SUM(discount_total_eur) AS sum_discount_eur,
    SUM(subtotal_eur) AS sum_subtotal_eur
  FROM fx_converted
  GROUP BY segment
)
SELECT
  segment,
  order_count,
  ROUND(avg_subtotal_eur, 2) AS avg_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(avg_discount_total_eur, 2) AS avg_discount_total_eur,
  ROUND(avg_grand_total_eur, 2) AS avg_grand_total_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * sum_discount_eur / NULLIF(sum_subtotal_eur,0), 2) AS discount_rate_pct
FROM segment_agg
ORDER BY CASE WHEN segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, segment

builds_on: Apparel and Footwear: loyalty member vs non-member behavior by tenure
tags.details: Population: non-cancelled orders placed 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31 by users (is_staff = false) belonging to tenants with tenants.industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'. Segment = 'loyalty member' if the user has a loyalty_accounts row, else 'non-member'. avg_subtotal_eur, avg_discount_total_eur and avg_grand_total_eur are averages of orders.subtotal, orders.discount_total and orders.grand_total respectively, each converted to EUR via exchange_rates (order currency_code to EUR, rate as_of placed_at). discount_rate_pct = (sum of discount_total in EUR) divided by (sum of subtotal in EUR) for the segment, as a percentage (an aggregate rate, not an average of per-order ratios). Order rows: 'loyalty member' first, then 'non-member'.

question: Using date-proximity matching instead of the unusable order_id link, do loyalty members' orders that coincide with a points redemption on the same calendar day show a different refund rate than their other orders?
sql:
WITH loyalty_user_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
eligible_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.placed_at, o.grand_total, o.currency_code, o.status
  FROM orders o
  JOIN loyalty_user_ids lu ON lu.user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
burn_by_user_day AS (
  SELECT user_id, CAST(occurred_at AS DATE) AS burn_date, SUM(ABS(points)) AS day_points
  FROM loyalty_transactions
  WHERE direction = 'burn'
  GROUP BY user_id, CAST(occurred_at AS DATE)
),
classified_orders AS (
  SELECT
    eo.order_id,
    eo.user_id,
    eo.placed_at,
    eo.grand_total,
    eo.currency_code,
    eo.status,
    bd.day_points,
    CASE WHEN bd.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'same-day points redemption' ELSE 'no same-day points redemption' END AS order_type
  FROM eligible_orders eo
  LEFT JOIN burn_by_user_day bd
    ON bd.user_id = eo.user_id AND bd.burn_date = CAST(eo.placed_at AS DATE)
),
refund_flags AS (
  SELECT
    co.order_id,
    co.order_type,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = co.order_id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
      OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = co.order_id)
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM classified_orders co
),
order_value_eur AS (
  SELECT
    co.order_id,
    co.order_type,
    CASE WHEN co.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN co.grand_total
         ELSE co.grand_total / er.rate END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM classified_orders co
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = co.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(co.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE co.status <> 'cancelled'
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT order_type, COUNT(*) AS order_count, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS distinct_customers, AVG(COALESCE(day_points,0)) AS avg_points_redeemed_that_day
  FROM classified_orders
  GROUP BY order_type
),
refund_rates AS (
  SELECT order_type, AVG(is_refunded) * 100 AS refund_rate_pct
  FROM refund_flags
  GROUP BY order_type
),
avg_values AS (
  SELECT order_type, AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM order_value_eur
  GROUP BY order_type
)
SELECT
  oc.order_type,
  oc.order_count,
  oc.distinct_customers,
  ROUND(rr.refund_rate_pct, 2) AS refund_rate_pct,
  ROUND(av.avg_order_value_eur, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(oc.avg_points_redeemed_that_day, 1) AS avg_points_redeemed_that_day
FROM order_counts oc
JOIN refund_rates rr ON rr.order_type = oc.order_type
JOIN avg_values av ON av.order_type = oc.order_type
ORDER BY CASE WHEN oc.order_type = 'same-day points redemption' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, oc.order_type

question: Among enrolled loyalty members, do the ones who generate the most revenue use the programme differently - redeeming more or less, staying longer, returning less - giving a hint at what a healthier version of the programme would look like?
sql:
WITH loyalty_members AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
population AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.tenant_id, o.user_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN loyalty_members lm ON lm.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND lm.user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
orders_base AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.id AS order_id, o.status, o.placed_at, o.grand_total, o.currency_code
  FROM orders o
  JOIN population p ON p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND p.user_id = o.user_id
),
payment_refund AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, order_id, MAX(CASE WHEN amount_refunded > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_refund
  FROM payments
  WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id, order_id
),
return_flag AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, order_id
  FROM order_returns
),
orders_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    ob.tenant_id, ob.user_id, ob.order_id, ob.status, ob.placed_at,
    CASE WHEN ob.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ob.grand_total
         ELSE ob.grand_total / er.rate END AS grand_total_eur,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(pr.has_refund,0) = 1 OR rf.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM orders_base ob
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = ob.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(ob.placed_at AS DATE)
  LEFT JOIN payment_refund pr ON pr.tenant_id = ob.tenant_id AND pr.order_id = ob.order_id
  LEFT JOIN return_flag rf ON rf.tenant_id = ob.tenant_id AND rf.order_id = ob.order_id
),
member_orders AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id, user_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN status <> 'cancelled' THEN COALESCE(grand_total_eur,0) ELSE 0 END) AS lifetime_revenue_eur,
    COUNT(*) AS lifetime_orders,
    MAX(placed_at) AS last_order_at,
    SUM(is_refunded) AS refunded_orders
  FROM orders_enriched
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
),
tx_value AS (
  SELECT lt.tenant_id, lt.user_id, lt.direction, lt.occurred_at,
    lt.points / lp.points_per_currency AS points_currency_amount,
    lp.currency_code
  FROM loyalty_transactions lt
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la ON la.id = lt.loyalty_account_id
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la.loyalty_program_id
  JOIN population p ON p.tenant_id = lt.tenant_id AND p.user_id = lt.user_id
),
tx_value_eur AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, direction,
    CASE WHEN currency_code = 'EUR' THEN points_currency_amount
         ELSE points_currency_amount / er.rate END AS value_eur
  FROM tx_value tv
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = tv.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(tv.occurred_at AS DATE)
),
member_loyalty AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN direction = 'burn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ever_redeemed,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'earn' THEN value_eur ELSE 0 END) AS earned_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'burn' THEN value_eur ELSE 0 END) AS redeemed_eur
  FROM tx_value_eur
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
),
member_full AS (
  SELECT
    mo.tenant_id, mo.user_id,
    mo.lifetime_revenue_eur, mo.lifetime_orders, mo.refunded_orders,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (mo.last_order_at - u.created_at)) / 86400.0 AS tenure_days,
    COALESCE(ml.ever_redeemed,0) AS ever_redeemed,
    COALESCE(ml.earned_eur,0) AS earned_eur,
    COALESCE(ml.redeemed_eur,0) AS redeemed_eur
  FROM member_orders mo
  JOIN users u ON u.tenant_id = mo.tenant_id AND u.id = mo.user_id
  LEFT JOIN member_loyalty ml ON ml.tenant_id = mo.tenant_id AND ml.user_id = mo.user_id
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    mf.*,
    NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue_eur DESC) AS quartile
  FROM member_full mf
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN quartile = 1 THEN 'Top 25% by lifetime revenue' ELSE 'Remaining 75%' END AS performance_group,
  COUNT(*) AS member_count,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_revenue_eur), 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_orders), 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(tenure_days), 1) AS avg_tenure_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(ever_redeemed), 1) AS pct_who_ever_redeemed_points,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(redeemed_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(earned_eur), 0), 1) AS own_redemption_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(refunded_orders) / NULLIF(SUM(lifetime_orders), 0), 1) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM ranked
GROUP BY CASE WHEN quartile = 1 THEN 'Top 25% by lifetime revenue' ELSE 'Remaining 75%' END
ORDER BY MIN(quartile)

builds_on: Loyalty programme unit economics: points cost vs revenue per customer
Loyalty points redemption rate by enrollment cohort age
tags.details: Population: all users with a loyalty_accounts row who placed at least one order between 2023-01-01 and 2025-12-31. Rank these members by lifetime revenue (sum of grand_total on non-cancelled orders, converted to EUR via exchange_rates as_of placed_at) and split into the top 25% and the remaining 75% by that ranking. avg_lifetime_orders = average count of orders (any status) per member in the group. avg_tenure_days = average of (last order placed_at minus users.created_at) in days per member in the group. pct_who_ever_redeemed_points = share of members in the group with at least one 'burn'-direction loyalty_transactions row. own_redemption_rate_pct = for the group, (sum of redeemed points value in EUR) divided by (sum of earned points value in EUR), using the same points-to-EUR conversion method as the unit-economics report. refund_rate_pct = share of orders (any status) in the group with payments.amount_refunded greater than 0 OR an order_returns row. Order rows: 'top 25% by lifetime revenue' first.

title: What distinguishes higher-revenue loyalty members from the rest

question: Is the programme's realized cost concentrated entirely in the minority of members who actually redeem, while the disengaged majority sits as pure unclaimed liability rather than real cost?
sql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN m.is_ever_redeemed THEN 'ever-redeemed member' ELSE 'never-redeemed member' END AS "group",
  COUNT(*) AS member_count,
  SUM(m.revenue_eur) AS total_revenue_eur,
  SUM(m.revenue_eur) / COUNT(*) AS revenue_per_customer_eur,
  SUM(m.redeemed_cost_eur) AS total_points_redeemed_cost_eur,
  SUM(m.earned_liability_eur) AS total_points_earned_liability_eur,
  CASE WHEN SUM(m.revenue_eur) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(m.redeemed_cost_eur) / SUM(m.revenue_eur) * 100 END AS redeemed_cost_pct_of_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT
    u.id AS user_id,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_transactions lt WHERE lt.user_id = u.id AND lt.direction = 'burn') AS is_ever_redeemed,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
             ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END
      ), 0)
     FROM orders o
     LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
     WHERE o.user_id = u.id
       AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
       AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) AS revenue_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN lp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ABS(lt2.points) / lp.points_per_currency
             ELSE (ABS(lt2.points) / lp.points_per_currency) / er2.rate END
      ), 0)
     FROM loyalty_transactions lt2
     JOIN loyalty_accounts la2 ON la2.id = lt2.loyalty_account_id
     JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la2.loyalty_program_id
     LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2 ON er2.base_code = 'EUR' AND er2.quote_code = lp.currency_code AND er2.as_of = CAST(lt2.occurred_at AS DATE)
     WHERE lt2.user_id = u.id AND lt2.direction = 'burn'
    ) AS redeemed_cost_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN lp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ABS(lt3.points) / lp.points_per_currency
             ELSE (ABS(lt3.points) / lp.points_per_currency) / er3.rate END
      ), 0)
     FROM loyalty_transactions lt3
     JOIN loyalty_accounts la3 ON la3.id = lt3.loyalty_account_id
     JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la3.loyalty_program_id
     LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er3 ON er3.base_code = 'EUR' AND er3.quote_code = lp.currency_code AND er3.as_of = CAST(lt3.occurred_at AS DATE)
     WHERE lt3.user_id = u.id AND lt3.direction = 'earn'
    ) AS earned_liability_eur
  FROM users u
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la WHERE la.user_id = u.id)
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o2 WHERE o2.user_id = u.id AND o2.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o2.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01')
) m
GROUP BY m.is_ever_redeemed
ORDER BY m.is_ever_redeemed DESC

title: Loyalty unit economics: ever-redeemed vs never-redeemed members

question: Once we separate loyalty members into those who have actually redeemed a point at least once versus those who never have, do the engaged ones match or beat non-members of similar tenure, while the disengaged majority lags behind?
sql:
WITH apparel_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
),
eligible_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS user_id, u.tenant_id, u.created_at
  FROM users u
  JOIN apparel_tenants t ON t.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM orders o
      WHERE o.user_id = u.id
        AND o.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
        AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01'
        AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    )
),
loyalty_group AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN la.user_id IS NULL THEN 'non-member'
      WHEN lb.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'ever-redeemed member'
      ELSE 'never-redeemed member'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM eligible_users eu
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) la
    ON la.user_id = eu.user_id
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_transactions WHERE direction = 'burn') lb
    ON lb.user_id = eu.user_id
),
tenure AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - eu.created_at::date) < 182 THEN 'under 6 months'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - eu.created_at::date) < 365 THEN '6 to 12 months'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - eu.created_at::date) < 730 THEN '12 to 24 months'
      ELSE 'over 24 months'
    END AS tenure_band
  FROM eligible_users eu
),
orders_scoped AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.status,
    CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN
      CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
           ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END
    ELSE NULL END AS revenue_eur,
    CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_noncancelled,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
         OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM orders o
  JOIN eligible_users eu ON eu.user_id = o.user_id AND eu.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
),
user_agg AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS lifetime_orders,
    SUM(is_noncancelled) AS noncancelled_orders,
    SUM(COALESCE(revenue_eur, 0)) AS lifetime_revenue_eur,
    SUM(is_refunded) AS refunded_orders
  FROM orders_scoped
  GROUP BY user_id
),
user_level AS (
  SELECT
    t.tenure_band,
    lg.customer_group,
    ua.lifetime_orders,
    ua.noncancelled_orders,
    ua.lifetime_revenue_eur,
    ua.refunded_orders
  FROM eligible_users eu
  JOIN tenure t ON t.user_id = eu.user_id
  JOIN loyalty_group lg ON lg.user_id = eu.user_id
  JOIN user_agg ua ON ua.user_id = eu.user_id
)
SELECT
  tenure_band,
  customer_group AS "group",
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_orders)::numeric, 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_revenue_eur)::numeric, 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND((SUM(lifetime_revenue_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(noncancelled_orders), 0))::numeric, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND((100.0 * SUM(refunded_orders) / NULLIF(SUM(lifetime_orders), 0))::numeric, 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM user_level
GROUP BY tenure_band, customer_group
ORDER BY
  CASE tenure_band
    WHEN 'under 6 months' THEN 1
    WHEN '6 to 12 months' THEN 2
    WHEN '12 to 24 months' THEN 3
    WHEN 'over 24 months' THEN 4
  END,
  CASE customer_group
    WHEN 'non-member' THEN 1
    WHEN 'never-redeemed member' THEN 2
    WHEN 'ever-redeemed member' THEN 3
  END

title: Apparel: never-redeemed vs ever-redeemed members vs non-members, by tenure

question: Among members who have redeemed at least once, does their order frequency and spend actually pick up after that first redemption, or were they already heavy buyers beforehand - i.e. does redeeming look like a cause of engagement or just a marker of customers who were already engaged?
sql:
WITH population AS (
  SELECT 
    t0.id AS user_id,
    t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t0.created_at AS user_created_at,
    t1.status AS tenant_status,
    t2.first_redeem_at AS first_redeem_at
  FROM users t0
  JOIN tenants t1 ON t1.id = t0.tenant_id
  JOIN (
    SELECT t3.user_id AS user_id, t3.tenant_id AS tenant_id, MIN(t3.occurred_at) AS first_redeem_at
    FROM loyalty_transactions t3
    WHERE t3.direction = 'burn'
    GROUP BY t3.user_id, t3.tenant_id
  ) t2 ON t2.user_id = t0.id AND t2.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts t4
    WHERE t4.user_id = t0.id AND t4.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
  )
),
base_orders AS (
  SELECT
    t5.id AS order_id,
    t5.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t5.user_id AS user_id,
    t5.placed_at AS placed_at,
    t5.status AS status,
    t5.currency_code AS currency_code,
    t5.grand_total AS grand_total,
    CASE WHEN t5.placed_at < t6.first_redeem_at THEN 'before first redemption' ELSE 'after first redemption' END AS period
  FROM orders t5
  JOIN population t6 ON t6.user_id = t5.user_id AND t6.tenant_id = t5.tenant_id
  WHERE t5.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND t5.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND t5.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
),
periods AS (
  SELECT 'before first redemption' AS period
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'after first redemption' AS period
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT
    t7.period AS period,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t7.user_id) AS distinct_customers
  FROM base_orders t7
  GROUP BY t7.period
),
aov AS (
  SELECT
    t8.period AS period,
    AVG(
      CASE WHEN t8.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN t8.grand_total
           ELSE t8.grand_total / t9.rate
      END
    ) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM base_orders t8
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates t9
    ON t9.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t9.quote_code = t8.currency_code
   AND t9.as_of = CAST(t8.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE t8.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY t8.period
),
order_refund_flags AS (
  SELECT
    t10.order_id AS order_id,
    t10.period AS period,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(t11.has_refund, false) OR COALESCE(t12.has_return, false) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM base_orders t10
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT t13.order_id AS order_id, bool_or(t13.amount_refunded > 0) AS has_refund
    FROM payments t13
    WHERE t13.order_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY t13.order_id
  ) t11 ON t11.order_id = t10.order_id
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT t14.order_id AS order_id, true AS has_return
    FROM order_returns t14
  ) t12 ON t12.order_id = t10.order_id
),
refund_rate AS (
  SELECT
    t15.period AS period,
    100.0 * SUM(t15.is_refunded) / COUNT(*) AS refund_rate_pct
  FROM order_refund_flags t15
  GROUP BY t15.period
),
exposure_before AS (
  SELECT
    'before first redemption' AS period,
    t16.user_id AS user_id,
    GREATEST(
      1,
      CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t16.first_redeem_at - COALESCE(t17.first_order_before, t16.user_created_at))) / 86400 AS BIGINT)
    ) AS exposed_days
  FROM population t16
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT t18.user_id AS user_id, MIN(t18.placed_at) AS first_order_before
    FROM base_orders t18
    WHERE t18.period = 'before first redemption'
    GROUP BY t18.user_id
  ) t17 ON t17.user_id = t16.user_id
),
exposure_after AS (
  SELECT
    'after first redemption' AS period,
    t19.user_id AS user_id,
    GREATEST(
      1,
      CAST(
        EXTRACT(
          EPOCH FROM (
            COALESCE(
              CASE WHEN t19.tenant_status = 'churned' THEN t20.last_order_after ELSE TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' END,
              t19.first_redeem_at
            ) - t19.first_redeem_at
          )
        ) / 86400 AS BIGINT
      )
    ) AS exposed_days
  FROM population t19
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT t21.user_id AS user_id, MAX(t21.placed_at) AS last_order_after
    FROM base_orders t21
    WHERE t21.period = 'after first redemption'
    GROUP BY t21.user_id
  ) t20 ON t20.user_id = t19.user_id
),
exposure_union AS (
  SELECT * FROM exposure_before
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM exposure_after
),
exposure_years AS (
  SELECT
    t22.period AS period,
    SUM(t22.exposed_days) / 365.0 AS exposed_customer_years
  FROM exposure_union t22
  GROUP BY t22.period
)
SELECT
  t23.period AS period,
  COALESCE(t24.distinct_customers, 0) AS distinct_customers,
  COALESCE(t24.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t25.avg_order_value_eur, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t24.total_orders, 0) / NULLIF(t27.exposed_customer_years, 0), 2) AS orders_per_customer_per_year,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t26.refund_rate_pct, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM periods t23
LEFT JOIN order_counts t24 ON t24.period = t23.period
LEFT JOIN aov t25 ON t25.period = t23.period
LEFT JOIN refund_rate t26 ON t26.period = t23.period
LEFT JOIN exposure_years t27 ON t27.period = t23.period
ORDER BY CASE WHEN t23.period = 'before first redemption' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, t23.period

tags.details: Population: users with a loyalty_accounts row who have at least one 'burn'-direction loyalty_transactions row. For each such user, find their first redemption's occurred_at timestamp. Split their orders (any status, placed_at not null, 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31) into 'before first redemption' (placed_at before that timestamp) and 'after first redemption' (placed_at on or after that timestamp). total_orders and distinct_customers are counts within each period. avg_order_value_eur uses non-cancelled orders, grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates (as_of placed_at). refund_rate_pct = share of orders in the period with payments.amount_refunded greater than 0 OR an order_returns row. orders_per_customer_per_year = total_orders in the period divided by (sum across customers of exposed days in that period divided by 365); exposed days before = first-redemption timestamp minus the customer's first order placed_at (or users.created_at if no earlier order); exposed days after = (customer's last order placed_at, or 2025-12-31 if still active) minus the first-redemption timestamp; floor exposed days at 1. Order rows: 'before first redemption' first, then 'after first redemption'.

title: Member order behavior before vs after their first points redemption

question: Are members who redeem points very soon after enrolling - likely signup-bonus hunters - disproportionately the ones who never place another order, which would be the clearest sign of rewards given without real repeat purchase behind them?
sql:
WITH member_enroll AS (
  SELECT la.user_id AS user_id, MIN(la.enrolled_at) AS enrolled_at
  FROM loyalty_accounts la
  GROUP BY la.user_id
),
member_first_burn AS (
  SELECT lt.user_id AS user_id, MIN(lt.occurred_at) AS first_burn_at
  FROM loyalty_transactions lt
  WHERE lt.direction = 'burn'
  GROUP BY lt.user_id
),
member_base AS (
  SELECT
    t0.user_id AS user_id,
    t0.enrolled_at AS enrolled_at,
    t1.first_burn_at AS first_burn_at,
    CASE
      WHEN (t1.first_burn_at::date - t0.enrolled_at::date) <= 30 THEN 'within 30 days of enrollment'
      WHEN (t1.first_burn_at::date - t0.enrolled_at::date) <= 180 THEN '31 to 180 days'
      ELSE 'over 180 days'
    END AS bucket
  FROM member_enroll t0
  JOIN member_first_burn t1 ON t1.user_id = t0.user_id
),
orders_after_count AS (
  SELECT
    mb.user_id AS user_id,
    COUNT(o.id) AS orders_after_count
  FROM member_base mb
  LEFT JOIN orders o
    ON o.user_id = mb.user_id
   AND o.placed_at >= mb.first_burn_at
  GROUP BY mb.user_id
),
orders_after_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    mb.user_id AS user_id,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN o.id IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
        ELSE o.grand_total / NULLIF(er.rate, 0)
      END
    ) AS revenue_after_eur
  FROM member_base mb
  LEFT JOIN orders o
    ON o.user_id = mb.user_id
   AND o.placed_at >= mb.first_burn_at
   AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  GROUP BY mb.user_id
)
SELECT
  mb.bucket AS time_to_first_redemption_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS member_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(oac.orders_after_count, 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_with_no_orders_after_redemption,
  ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(oac.orders_after_count, 0)), 2) AS avg_orders_after_per_customer,
  ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(oar.revenue_after_eur, 0)), 2) AS avg_revenue_after_eur
FROM member_base mb
LEFT JOIN orders_after_count oac ON oac.user_id = mb.user_id
LEFT JOIN orders_after_revenue oar ON oar.user_id = mb.user_id
GROUP BY mb.bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE mb.bucket
    WHEN 'within 30 days of enrollment' THEN 1
    WHEN '31 to 180 days' THEN 2
    WHEN 'over 180 days' THEN 3
  END

builds_on: Member order behavior before vs after their first points redemption
tags.details: Population: users with a loyalty_accounts row who have at least one 'burn'-direction loyalty_transactions row. For each such user, compute days between loyalty_accounts.enrolled_at and the occurred_at of their first 'burn' transaction; bucket into 'within 30 days of enrollment', '31 to 180 days', 'over 180 days'. pct_with_no_orders_after_redemption = share of members in the bucket with zero orders placed on or after their first redemption's occurred_at. avg_orders_after_per_customer = average count of orders (any status) placed on or after the first redemption, per member in the bucket (including zeros). avg_revenue_after_eur = average EUR revenue (non-cancelled orders, grand_total converted via exchange_rates as_of placed_at) from orders placed on or after the first redemption, per member in the bucket (including zeros). Order rows by time_to_first_redemption_bucket in the order listed above.
tags.grain: one row per time-to-first-redemption bucket, among members who have redeemed at least once

title: Post-redemption drop-off by how quickly members first redeemed

question: Does order frequency drop off after a member's first redemption because redeeming specifically reduces engagement, or do non-members and never-redeemed members show the same kind of natural slowdown over their lifetime?
sql:
WITH user_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.user_id, o.tenant_id, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id AND u.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
user_stats AS (
  SELECT user_id, tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, MIN(placed_at) AS first_order, MAX(placed_at) AS last_order
  FROM user_orders
  GROUP BY user_id, tenant_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
),
loyalty_acct AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
loyalty_burn AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_transactions WHERE direction = 'burn'
),
user_group AS (
  SELECT us.user_id, us.tenant_id, us.first_order, us.last_order,
    us.first_order + (us.last_order - us.first_order)/2 AS midpoint,
    CASE
      WHEN la.user_id IS NULL THEN 'non-member'
      WHEN lb.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'ever-redeemed member'
      ELSE 'never-redeemed member'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM user_stats us
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_acct la ON la.tenant_id = us.tenant_id AND la.user_id = us.user_id
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_burn lb ON lb.tenant_id = us.tenant_id AND lb.user_id = us.user_id
),
order_period AS (
  SELECT uo.order_id, uo.user_id, uo.tenant_id, uo.placed_at,
    ug.customer_group,
    CASE WHEN uo.placed_at < ug.midpoint THEN 'first half' ELSE 'second half' END AS period
  FROM user_orders uo
  JOIN user_group ug ON ug.user_id = uo.user_id AND ug.tenant_id = uo.tenant_id
),
payment_refund AS (
  SELECT order_id, tenant_id, MAX(CASE WHEN amount_refunded > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_refund
  FROM payments
  WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY order_id, tenant_id
),
return_flag AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id, tenant_id, 1 AS has_return
  FROM order_returns
),
order_refund AS (
  SELECT op.order_id, op.user_id, op.tenant_id, op.customer_group, op.period,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(pr.has_refund,0) = 1 OR rf.has_return = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM order_period op
  LEFT JOIN payment_refund pr ON pr.order_id = op.order_id AND pr.tenant_id = op.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN return_flag rf ON rf.order_id = op.order_id AND rf.tenant_id = op.tenant_id
),
customer_period AS (
  SELECT customer_group, period, user_id, tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(is_refunded) AS refund_count
  FROM order_refund
  GROUP BY customer_group, period, user_id, tenant_id
),
customer_period_exposed AS (
  SELECT cp.customer_group, cp.period, cp.user_id, cp.tenant_id, cp.order_count, cp.refund_count,
    CASE WHEN cp.period = 'first half'
      THEN GREATEST(1, CAST(ug.midpoint AS date) - CAST(ug.first_order AS date))
      ELSE GREATEST(1, CAST(ug.last_order AS date) - CAST(ug.midpoint AS date))
    END AS exposed_days
  FROM customer_period cp
  JOIN user_group ug ON ug.user_id = cp.user_id AND ug.tenant_id = cp.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  customer_group AS "group",
  period,
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  SUM(order_count) AS total_orders,
  ROUND(CAST(SUM(order_count) / (SUM(exposed_days) / 365.0) AS numeric), 2) AS orders_per_customer_per_year,
  ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(refund_count) / SUM(order_count) AS numeric), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM customer_period_exposed
GROUP BY customer_group, period
ORDER BY
  CASE customer_group WHEN 'non-member' THEN 1 WHEN 'never-redeemed member' THEN 2 WHEN 'ever-redeemed member' THEN 3 END,
  CASE period WHEN 'first half' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END

question: Does the Apparel finding - that engaged (ever-redeemed) members beat tenure-matched non-members while never-redeemed members lag behind - hold up across the whole platform, or was it specific to Apparel?
sql:
WITH eligible_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS user_id, u.tenant_id, u.created_at
  FROM users u
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
),
tenure AS (
  SELECT
    user_id, tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN created_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' - INTERVAL '6 months' THEN 'under 6 months'
      WHEN created_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' - INTERVAL '12 months' THEN '6 to 12 months'
      WHEN created_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' - INTERVAL '24 months' THEN '12 to 24 months'
      ELSE 'over 24 months'
    END AS tenure_band
  FROM eligible_users
),
loyalty_member AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id, tenant_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
loyalty_redeemed AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id, tenant_id FROM loyalty_transactions WHERE direction = 'burn'
),
membership AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id, eu.tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN lm.user_id IS NULL THEN 'non-member'
      WHEN lr.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'ever-redeemed member'
      ELSE 'never-redeemed member'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM eligible_users eu
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_member lm ON lm.user_id = eu.user_id AND lm.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_redeemed lr ON lr.user_id = eu.user_id AND lr.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id
),
order_refund_flag AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
        OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)
      THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS is_refunded
  FROM orders o
),
order_eur AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.status,
    CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN o.grand_total / er.rate ELSE NULL END AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) AS date)
),
customer_orders AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id,
    eu.tenant_id,
    COUNT(o.id) AS lifetime_orders,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN oe.revenue_eur ELSE 0 END) AS lifetime_revenue_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_cancelled_order_count,
    SUM(orf.is_refunded) AS refunded_order_count
  FROM eligible_users eu
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = eu.user_id AND o.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id
  JOIN order_eur oe ON oe.order_id = o.id
  JOIN order_refund_flag orf ON orf.order_id = o.id
  GROUP BY eu.user_id, eu.tenant_id
),
final AS (
  SELECT
    t.tenure_band,
    m.customer_group,
    COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
    AVG(co.lifetime_orders) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
    AVG(co.lifetime_revenue_eur) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
    SUM(co.lifetime_revenue_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(co.non_cancelled_order_count), 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
    100.0 * SUM(co.refunded_order_count) / NULLIF(SUM(co.lifetime_orders), 0) AS refund_rate_pct
  FROM tenure t
  JOIN membership m ON m.user_id = t.user_id AND m.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  JOIN customer_orders co ON co.user_id = t.user_id AND co.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  GROUP BY t.tenure_band, m.customer_group
)
SELECT
  tenure_band,
  customer_group AS "group",
  customer_count,
  ROUND(avg_lifetime_orders, 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(avg_lifetime_revenue_eur, 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(avg_order_value_eur, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(refund_rate_pct, 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM final
ORDER BY
  CASE tenure_band
    WHEN 'under 6 months' THEN 1
    WHEN '6 to 12 months' THEN 2
    WHEN '12 to 24 months' THEN 3
    WHEN 'over 24 months' THEN 4
  END,
  CASE customer_group
    WHEN 'non-member' THEN 1
    WHEN 'never-redeemed member' THEN 2
    WHEN 'ever-redeemed member' THEN 3
  END

question: Looking at Youssef Meijer's own deals one by one — which accounts, what sizes, how long open — does his low win rate look like a few bad accounts/territory, or a pattern across all his work?
sql:
WITH polder_tenant AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE name = 'Polder Packaging'
),
owner AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id
  FROM users u
  JOIN polder_tenant pt ON u.tenant_id = pt.tenant_id
  WHERE u.full_name = 'Youssef Meijer'
),
pipeline AS (
  SELECT p.id AS pipeline_id
  FROM pipelines p
  JOIN polder_tenant pt ON p.tenant_id = pt.tenant_id
  WHERE p.name = 'New business'
),
target_opportunities AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.account_id,
    o.amount,
    o.currency_code,
    o.is_won,
    o.created_at,
    o.closed_at
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN owner ON o.owner_user_id = owner.user_id
  JOIN pipeline ON o.pipeline_id = pipeline.pipeline_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
),
with_account AS (
  SELECT
    t.*,
    a.name AS account_name
  FROM target_opportunities t
  JOIN accounts a ON t.account_id = a.id
),
with_rate AS (
  SELECT
    wa.*,
    CASE
      WHEN wa.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0
      ELSE (
        SELECT er.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er
        WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = wa.currency_code
          AND er.as_of <= wa.closed_at::date
        ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )
    END AS eur_rate
  FROM with_account wa
)
SELECT
  account_name,
  CASE WHEN is_won THEN 'won' ELSE 'lost' END AS outcome,
  ROUND(amount / eur_rate, 2) AS amount_eur,
  currency_code,
  (closed_at::date - created_at::date) AS days_open,
  created_at,
  closed_at
FROM with_rate
ORDER BY closed_at ASC, account_name ASC

question: Is the current complete absence of open new-business pipeline a constant feature of the last three years, or did merchants used to carry live open deals and that's changed recently?
sql:
with month_ends as (
    select
        year_num,
        month_num,
        max(calendar_date) as month_end_date
    from calendar_days
    where year_num between 2023 and 2025
    group by year_num, month_num
),
scoped_tenants as (
    select id as tenant_id, name
    from tenants
    where name in (
        'Ballycorran Industrial Supply',
        'Castell Fasteners',
        'Hanse Industriebedarf',
        'Midland Safety Wear',
        'Polder Packaging'
    )
),
new_business_pipelines as (
    select p.id as pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
    from pipelines p
    join scoped_tenants st on st.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
    where p.name = 'New business'
),
scoped_opportunities as (
    select o.id, o.tenant_id, o.created_at, o.closed_at
    from opportunities o
    join new_business_pipelines nbp
        on nbp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id
        and nbp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
),
monthly_open_opportunities as (
    select
        me.month_end_date,
        o.id as opportunity_id,
        (me.month_end_date - o.created_at::date) as age_days
    from month_ends me
    cross join scoped_opportunities o
    where o.created_at::date <= me.month_end_date
        and (o.closed_at is null or o.closed_at::date > me.month_end_date)
)
select
    me.month_end_date,
    count(moo.opportunity_id) as opportunities_open_at_month_end,
    round(avg(moo.age_days)::numeric, 1) as avg_age_days_of_open_opportunities_at_month_end,
    max(moo.age_days) as oldest_age_days_of_open_opportunity_at_month_end
from month_ends me
left join monthly_open_opportunities moo
    on moo.month_end_date = me.month_end_date
group by me.month_end_date
order by me.month_end_date asc

question: For deals that eventually get lost, does sales activity cluster early, stay steady throughout, or come in a late flurry right before the deal is given up on — or does it go quiet before the end (stalled and forgotten)?
sql:
WITH scoped_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
),
new_business_pipelines AS (
  SELECT p.id AS pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
  FROM pipelines p
  JOIN scoped_tenants st ON st.id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE p.name = 'New business'
),
lost_opps AS (
  SELECT o.id AS opportunity_id, o.tenant_id, o.created_at, o.closed_at
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN new_business_pipelines nbp ON nbp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND nbp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.is_won = false
),
total_lost AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_lost_opps FROM lost_opps
),
activity_positions AS (
  SELECT
    a.id AS activity_id,
    lo.opportunity_id,
    CASE
      WHEN lo.closed_at IS NULL OR lo.created_at IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN lo.closed_at = lo.created_at THEN NULL
      ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (a.occurred_at - lo.created_at)) / EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (lo.closed_at - lo.created_at))
    END AS relative_position
  FROM activities a
  JOIN lost_opps lo ON lo.opportunity_id = a.opportunity_id AND a.tenant_id = lo.tenant_id
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    activity_id,
    opportunity_id,
    CASE
      WHEN relative_position IS NULL OR relative_position < 0 OR relative_position > 1 THEN 'outside window'
      WHEN relative_position < 0.25 THEN 'Q1 (0-25%)'
      WHEN relative_position < 0.5 THEN 'Q2 (25-50%)'
      WHEN relative_position < 0.75 THEN 'Q3 (50-75%)'
      ELSE 'Q4 (75-100%)'
    END AS lifecycle_quartile
  FROM activity_positions
),
totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_activities_all FROM bucketed
)
SELECT
  b.lifecycle_quartile,
  COUNT(*) AS total_activities_in_bucket,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / t.total_activities_all, 2) AS pct_of_total_activities,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.opportunity_id) AS opportunities_with_at_least_one_activity_in_bucket,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT b.opportunity_id) / tl.total_lost_opps, 2) AS pct_of_lost_opportunities_with_activity_in_bucket
FROM bucketed b
CROSS JOIN totals t
CROSS JOIN total_lost tl
GROUP BY b.lifecycle_quartile, t.total_activities_all, tl.total_lost_opps
ORDER BY CASE b.lifecycle_quartile
  WHEN 'Q1 (0-25%)' THEN 1
  WHEN 'Q2 (25-50%)' THEN 2
  WHEN 'Q3 (50-75%)' THEN 3
  WHEN 'Q4 (75-100%)' THEN 4
  ELSE 5
END

For each such opportunity, join activities where activities.opportunity_id = opportunity.id. For each activity compute relative_position = (activity.occurred_at - opportunity.created_at) / NULLIF(opportunity.closed_at - opportunity.created_at, 0), expressed as a fraction of the deal's own lifespan. Bucket into quartiles: Q1 [0, 0.25), Q2 [0.25, 0.5), Q3 [0.5, 0.75), Q4 [0.75, 1.0] inclusive of activities right at closed_at. question: Do lost deals linger longest at particular times of year (e.g., end-of-quarter or holiday periods), or is the ~35-day drag before a deal is given up on roughly constant regardless of when it started?
sql:
with tenant_scope as (
    select id as tenant_id, name
    from tenants
    where name in ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
),
pipeline_scope as (
    select p.id as pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
    from pipelines p
    join tenant_scope t on p.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
    where p.name = 'New business'
),
lost_opportunities as (
    select
        o.id as opportunity_id,
        o.created_at,
        o.closed_at,
        (extract(epoch from (o.closed_at - o.created_at)) / 86400.0) as days_open
    from opportunities o
    join pipeline_scope ps
        on o.pipeline_id = ps.pipeline_id
        and o.tenant_id = ps.tenant_id
    where o.is_closed = true
      and o.is_won = false
      and o.closed_at is not null
),
dated as (
    select
        lo.opportunity_id,
        lo.days_open,
        cd.year_num,
        cd.quarter_num
    from lost_opportunities lo
    join calendar_days cd on cd.calendar_date = lo.closed_at::date
)
select
    (year_num || 'Q' || quarter_num) as quarter,
    count(*) as lost_opportunities_count,
    round(avg(days_open)::numeric, 1) as avg_days_open,
    round(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by days_open)::numeric, 1) as median_days_open
from dated
group by year_num, quarter_num
order by year_num, quarter_num

question: Is Youssef Meijer's pattern of winning small deals but losing his biggest one a one-off, or do several reps actually perform worse on a dollar basis than their deal-count win rate suggests?
sql:
SELECT
  u.full_name AS rep_name,
  t.name AS merchant,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS count_win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END), 2) AS total_amount_won_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN NOT sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END), 2) AS total_amount_lost_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(sub.amount_eur), 0), 1) AS dollar_weighted_win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(
    (100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*))
    - (100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(sub.amount_eur), 0))
  , 1) AS gap_pct_points
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    o.owner_user_id,
    o.is_won,
    CASE
      WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
      ELSE o.amount / (
        SELECT er.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er
        WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
          AND er.as_of <= CAST(o.closed_at AS DATE)
        ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN tenants t2 ON t2.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id
  WHERE t2.name IN (
      'Ballycorran Industrial Supply',
      'Castell Fasteners',
      'Hanse Industriebedarf',
      'Midland Safety Wear',
      'Polder Packaging'
    )
    AND p.name = 'New business'
    AND o.is_closed = true
) sub
JOIN users u ON u.id = sub.owner_user_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = sub.tenant_id
GROUP BY sub.owner_user_id, u.full_name, t.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY gap_pct_points DESC, rep_name ASC

WITH target_pipelines AS (

created AS (

  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN target_pipelines tp ON tp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND tp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.created_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

),
closed AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.closed_at)::date AS month_start, count(*) AS cnt
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN target_pipelines tp ON tp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND tp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id

WITH opp AS (

),
rated AS (
  SELECT
    opp.merchant,
    opp.is_won,

    CASE
      WHEN opp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN opp.amount

        SELECT er.rate

        WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = opp.currency_code

  FROM rated

question: Does the 'Missing - suspected theft' reason concentrate in a handful of specific warehouses/sites, or is it spread evenly across all sites that log stock adjustments?

WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    w.id AS warehouse_id,
    w.name AS warehouse_name,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    sa.reason,
    sa.adjusted_by_user_id
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sa.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    warehouse_id,
    warehouse_name,
    tenant_name,
    COUNT(*) AS total_adjustments_at_site,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE reason = 'Missing - suspected theft') AS theft_tagged_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT adjusted_by_user_id) FILTER (WHERE reason = 'Missing - suspected theft') AS distinct_staff_logging_theft_here
  FROM base
  GROUP BY warehouse_id, warehouse_name, tenant_name
)

  warehouse_name,
  tenant_name,
  total_adjustments_at_site,
  theft_tagged_count,
  ROUND(theft_tagged_count * 100.0 / NULLIF(total_adjustments_at_site, 0), 1) AS pct_theft_of_site_adjustments,
  distinct_staff_logging_theft_here,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_warehouses_with_adjustments_2025
FROM agg
ORDER BY theft_tagged_count DESC, pct_theft_of_site_adjustments DESC, warehouse_name ASC
LIMIT 50

WITH periods AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    date_trunc('month', calendar_date)::date AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN day_of_month <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS half
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND calendar_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
adj AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', sa.created_at)::date AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN EXTRACT(day FROM sa.created_at)::int <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS half,
    sa.stock_location_id,
    sa.quantity_delta
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sa.stock_location_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
adj_agg AS (
  SELECT
    month_start, half,
    COUNT(*) AS events,
    SUM(ABS(quantity_delta)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(quantity_delta) AS net_units_variance,
    COUNT(DISTINCT stock_location_id) AS distinct_locations_active
  FROM adj
  GROUP BY month_start, half
),
wh AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', w.created_at)::date AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN EXTRACT(day FROM w.created_at)::int <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS half,
    COUNT(*) AS new_warehouses
  FROM warehouses w
  WHERE w.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND w.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY month_start, half
)
SELECT
  to_char(p.month_start, 'YYYY-MM') || ' (' ||
    CASE WHEN p.half = 1 THEN '1-15'
         ELSE '16-' || EXTRACT(DAY FROM (p.month_start + INTERVAL '1 month' - INTERVAL '1 day'))::int
    END || ')' AS period_label,
  COALESCE(a.events, 0) AS events,
  COALESCE(a.abs_units_variance, 0) AS abs_units_variance,
  COALESCE(a.net_units_variance, 0) AS net_units_variance,
  COALESCE(a.distinct_locations_active, 0) AS distinct_locations_active,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(a.distinct_locations_active, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE a.events::numeric / a.distinct_locations_active
    END, 2
  ) AS events_per_active_location,
  COALESCE(w.new_warehouses, 0) AS new_warehouses_opened_this_period
FROM periods p
LEFT JOIN adj_agg a ON a.month_start = p.month_start AND a.half = p.half
LEFT JOIN wh w ON w.month_start = p.month_start AND w.half = p.half
ORDER BY p.month_start, p.half

question: Do the B2B wholesale/office-supply merchants behind the December 31 correction run any routine, day-to-day stock-count activity during the year, or does their stock sit untouched in bulk storage until a single year-end true-up?
sql:
WITH loc AS (
  SELECT sl.id AS stock_location_id, w.tenant_id, sl.kind
  FROM stock_locations sl
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Deskline Supplies', 'OfficeHub Nordic', 'Kontor24 Bürobedarf', 'Hanse Industriebedarf', 'Castell Fasteners', 'Midland Safety Wear', 'Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'Polder Packaging')
),
loc_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    count(*) AS total_stock_locations,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'bulk') AS bulk_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'pick') AS pick_count
  FROM loc
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
adj AS (
  SELECT l.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS routine_stock_adjustments_2025,
    count(DISTINCT sa.variant_id) AS distinct_variants_with_routine_adjustment
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN loc l ON l.stock_location_id = sa.stock_location_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY l.tenant_id
),
dec31 AS (
  SELECT l.tenant_id,
    sum(abs(sm.quantity)) AS dec31_correction_abs_units,
    count(DISTINCT sm.variant_id) AS dec31_correction_distinct_variants
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN loc l ON l.stock_location_id = sm.stock_location_id
  WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment' AND sm.occurred_at::date = DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY l.tenant_id
)
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
  la.total_stock_locations,
  round(100.0 * la.bulk_count / la.total_stock_locations, 1) AS pct_locations_kind_bulk,
  round(100.0 * la.pick_count / la.total_stock_locations, 1) AS pct_locations_kind_pick,
  coalesce(adj.routine_stock_adjustments_2025, 0) AS routine_stock_adjustments_2025,
  coalesce(adj.distinct_variants_with_routine_adjustment, 0) AS distinct_variants_with_routine_adjustment,
  coalesce(dec31.dec31_correction_abs_units, 0) AS dec31_correction_abs_units,
  coalesce(dec31.dec31_correction_distinct_variants, 0) AS dec31_correction_distinct_variants
FROM tenants t
JOIN loc_agg la ON la.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN adj ON adj.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN dec31 ON dec31.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.name IN ('Deskline Supplies', 'OfficeHub Nordic', 'Kontor24 Bürobedarf', 'Hanse Industriebedarf', 'Castell Fasteners', 'Midland Safety Wear', 'Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'Polder Packaging')

question: Is the apparel/footwear concentration in stock-count discrepancies explained by those warehouses simply being bigger (more pick locations), or do specific apparel sites show a genuinely higher discrepancy rate per location?
sql:
SELECT warehouse_name, tenant_name, distinct_pick_locations, total_routine_adjustments_2025,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN distinct_pick_locations = 0 THEN NULL ELSE total_routine_adjustments_2025::numeric / distinct_pick_locations END, 2) AS events_per_pick_location,
  distinct_variants_affected,
  avg_hour_of_day_of_entries
FROM (
  SELECT w.id as warehouse_id, w.name as warehouse_name, t.name as tenant_name,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stock_locations sl2 WHERE sl2.warehouse_id = w.id AND sl2.kind = 'pick') as distinct_pick_locations,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stock_adjustments sa2
       WHERE sa2.stock_location_id IN (SELECT sl3.id FROM stock_locations sl3 WHERE sl3.warehouse_id = w.id)
       AND sa2.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa2.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') as total_routine_adjustments_2025,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sa3.variant_id) FROM stock_adjustments sa3
       WHERE sa3.stock_location_id IN (SELECT sl4.id FROM stock_locations sl4 WHERE sl4.warehouse_id = w.id)
       AND sa3.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa3.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') as distinct_variants_affected,
    (SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(HOUR FROM sa4.created_at)), 1) FROM stock_adjustments sa4
       WHERE sa4.stock_location_id IN (SELECT sl5.id FROM stock_locations sl5 WHERE sl5.warehouse_id = w.id)
       AND sa4.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa4.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') as avg_hour_of_day_of_entries
  FROM warehouses w
  JOIN tenants t ON w.tenant_id = t.id
  WHERE t.industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
) sub
ORDER BY events_per_pick_location DESC NULLS LAST, total_routine_adjustments_2025 DESC, warehouse_name ASC, warehouse_id ASC
LIMIT 50

question: At Atlanta (Cragsley Outfitters), Reading (Marrowby & Vane) and Den Haag (Studio Vrij) — the three sites with by far the most stock-count discrepancies — is the problem spread across the catalog, or concentrated in a handful of specific products/size-color variants?
sql:
WITH three_warehouses AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM warehouses
  WHERE name IN ('Atlanta Fulfilment Centre','Reading Fulfilment Centre','Den Haag Fulfilment Centre')
),
adjustments AS (
  SELECT sa.variant_id, sa.reason, sa.created_at, w.name AS warehouse_name
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sa.stock_location_id
  JOIN three_warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
variant_info AS (
  SELECT pv.id AS variant_id, pv.sku, pv.name AS variant_name, p.name AS product_name
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT
    a.warehouse_name,
    vi.product_name,
    vi.sku,
    vi.variant_name,
    COUNT(*) AS adjustment_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.reason = 'Missing - suspected theft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_theft_reason,
    COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(a.created_at)) AS distinct_days_affected
  FROM adjustments a
  JOIN variant_info vi ON vi.variant_id = a.variant_id
  GROUP BY a.warehouse_name, vi.product_name, vi.sku, vi.variant_name
)
SELECT
  warehouse_name,
  product_name,
  sku,
  variant_name,
  adjustment_count,
  pct_theft_reason,
  distinct_days_affected,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_distinct_variants
FROM aggregated
ORDER BY adjustment_count DESC, warehouse_name ASC, sku ASC
LIMIT 50

question: Did the 407 stock_movements kind='adjustment' events in 2025 all fire at the exact same timestamp (suggesting one system/data event), or do different merchants' corrections have distinct timestamps (consistent with independent, organic annual stocktakes)?
sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT sm0.occurred_at AS occurred_at
  FROM stock_movements sm0
  WHERE sm0.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm0.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm0.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT sm1.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         COUNT(*) AS event_count
  FROM stock_movements sm1
  WHERE sm1.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm1.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm1.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm1.occurred_at
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT sm2.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         COUNT(DISTINCT sl2.warehouse_id) AS distinct_warehouses
  FROM stock_movements sm2
  JOIN stock_locations sl2 ON sl2.id = sm2.stock_location_id
  WHERE sm2.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm2.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm2.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm2.occurred_at
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT sm3.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         COUNT(DISTINCT w3.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
  FROM stock_movements sm3
  JOIN stock_locations sl3 ON sl3.id = sm3.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w3 ON w3.id = sl3.warehouse_id
  WHERE sm3.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm3.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm3.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm3.occurred_at
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT sm4.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         SUM(ABS(sm4.quantity)) AS total_abs_quantity
  FROM stock_movements sm4
  WHERE sm4.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm4.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm4.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm4.occurred_at
)
SELECT
  t0.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
  COALESCE(t1.event_count, 0) AS event_count,
  COALESCE(t3.distinct_tenants, 0) AS distinct_tenants,
  COALESCE(t2.distinct_warehouses, 0) AS distinct_warehouses,
  COALESCE(t4.total_abs_quantity, 0) AS total_abs_quantity
FROM t0
LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
ORDER BY event_count DESC, occurred_at ASC

question: The apparel merchants' secondary sites named '...Warehouse' (as opposed to '...Fulfilment Centre') showed zero stock-count activity all year — are these empty/inactive shells, or do they hold meaningful live inventory that is simply never being counted (a blind spot)?
sql:
SELECT
  w.name AS warehouse_name,
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(si.quantity), 0)
     FROM stock_items si
     JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = si.stock_location_id
    WHERE sl.warehouse_id = w.id) AS total_stock_on_hand,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT si.variant_id)
     FROM stock_items si
     JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = si.stock_location_id
    WHERE sl.warehouse_id = w.id
      AND si.quantity > 0) AS distinct_variants_stocked,
  ROUND(
    (
      (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(si.quantity), 0)
         FROM stock_items si
         JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = si.stock_location_id
        WHERE sl.warehouse_id = w.id)::numeric
      /
      NULLIF(
        (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(si2.quantity), 0)
           FROM stock_items si2
           JOIN stock_locations sl2 ON sl2.id = si2.stock_location_id
           JOIN warehouses w2 ON w2.id = sl2.warehouse_id
          WHERE w2.tenant_id = w.tenant_id), 0
      ) * 100
    ), 1
  ) AS pct_of_tenant_total_stock_units
FROM warehouses w
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
WHERE (t.name, w.name) IN (
  VALUES
    ('Oakhurst Tailoring', 'Aarhus Warehouse'),
    ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Boston Warehouse'),
    ('Studio Vrij', 'Brussels Warehouse'),
    ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Calgary Warehouse'),
    ('Thistlecombe', 'Glasgow Warehouse'),
    ('Studio Vrij', 'Groningen Warehouse'),
    ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Limerick Warehouse'),
    ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Preston Warehouse'),
    ('Rue Lafayette Studio', 'Toulouse Warehouse'),
    ('Velvet Ash', 'Uppsala Warehouse')
)
ORDER BY total_stock_on_hand DESC, warehouse_name

question: Can we independently verify what macros.usage_count is actually counting, using the audit trail, before we repeat that number anywhere?
sql:
SELECT
  tm.title AS macro_title,
  tm.usage_count AS current_usage_count,
  COALESCE(ch.event_count, 0) AS logged_update_event_count,
  ch.sum_increment AS sum_of_logged_increments,
  ch.first_update_at AS first_logged_update_at,
  ch.last_update_at AS last_logged_update_at,
  tm.created_at AS macro_created_at
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, usage_count, created_at
  FROM macros
  ORDER BY usage_count DESC, id
  LIMIT 5
) tm
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    entity_id,
    COUNT(*) AS event_count,
    SUM((after_data->>'usage_count')::numeric - (before_data->>'usage_count')::numeric) AS sum_increment,
    MIN(occurred_at) AS first_update_at,
    MAX(occurred_at) AS last_update_at
  FROM change_history
  WHERE entity_table = 'macros'
    AND 'usage_count' = ANY(changed_columns)
  GROUP BY entity_id
) ch ON ch.entity_id = tm.id
ORDER BY tm.usage_count DESC, tm.id

question: What share of 2025 tickets carry no topic tag at all, and do untagged tickets differ from tagged ones enough to change the topic/breach story from last week?
sql:
WITH ticket_base AS (
    SELECT
        t0.id AS ticket_id,
        t0.created_at AS created_at,
        t0.resolved_at AS resolved_at,
        CASE
            WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ticket_tags_map t1 WHERE t1.ticket_id = t0.id)
            THEN 'Tagged'
            ELSE 'Untagged'
        END AS coverage_status
    FROM tickets t0
    WHERE t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
counts AS (
    SELECT
        t2.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
    FROM ticket_base t2
    GROUP BY t2.coverage_status
),
grand_total AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_tickets
    FROM ticket_base t3
),
resolution_time AS (
    SELECT
        t4.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t4.resolved_at - t4.created_at)) / 60.0) AS avg_resolution_minutes
    FROM ticket_base t4
    WHERE t4.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY t4.coverage_status
),
resolution_breaches AS (
    SELECT
        t5.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        COUNT(DISTINCT t6.ticket_id) AS resolution_breach_count
    FROM ticket_base t5
    JOIN sla_breaches t6
        ON t6.ticket_id = t5.ticket_id
        AND t6.breach_kind = 'resolution'
    GROUP BY t5.coverage_status
),
first_response_breaches AS (
    SELECT
        t7.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        COUNT(DISTINCT t8.ticket_id) AS first_response_breach_count
    FROM ticket_base t7
    JOIN sla_breaches t8
        ON t8.ticket_id = t7.ticket_id
        AND t8.breach_kind = 'first_response'
    GROUP BY t7.coverage_status
)
SELECT
    t9.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
    t9.ticket_count AS ticket_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * t9.ticket_count / NULLIF(t10.total_tickets, 0), 1) AS pct_of_total_tickets,
    ROUND(COALESCE(t11.avg_resolution_minutes, 0), 0) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
    ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t12.resolution_breach_count, 0) / NULLIF(t9.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
    ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t13.first_response_breach_count, 0) / NULLIF(t9.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS first_response_breach_rate
FROM counts t9
CROSS JOIN grand_total t10
LEFT JOIN resolution_time t11 ON t11.coverage_status = t9.coverage_status
LEFT JOIN resolution_breaches t12 ON t12.coverage_status = t9.coverage_status
LEFT JOIN first_response_breaches t13 ON t13.coverage_status = t9.coverage_status
ORDER BY
    CASE WHEN t9.coverage_status = 'Tagged' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
    t9.coverage_status

builds_on: Ticket volume and speed by topic tag

A ticket counts as 'Tagged' if it has at least one row in ticket_tags_map, regardless of how many tags; 'Untagged' otherwise. 2 rows total. Order 'Tagged' first then 'Untagged'. Round pct and rates to 1 decimal percent, minutes to whole numbers.

question: For Marrowby & Vane and Studio Vrij, does their high breach rate look like a staffing shortfall (high tickets-per-agent) or inherently harder tickets (more back-and-forth, higher-priority mix), compared to other top merchants like Cragsley Outfitters?
sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, name AS tenant_name
  FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Cragsley Outfitters','Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Brennquell Kaffee','Grind Collective','Petalcourt Beauty')
),
tickets_2025 AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.tenant_id, t.priority, t.created_at, t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN target_tenants tt ON tt.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ticket_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets_2025
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
message_counts AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(tm.id) AS message_count
  FROM tickets_2025 t
  JOIN ticket_messages tm ON tm.ticket_id = t.id
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
),
agent_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS agent_count
  FROM support_agents
  WHERE tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM target_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
priority_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN priority IN ('high','urgent') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_urgent_count
  FROM tickets_2025
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
resolution_stats AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 60.0) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM tickets_2025
  WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
breach_counts AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT sb.ticket_id) AS breach_count
  FROM tickets_2025 t
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = t.id AND sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tt.tenant_name,
  tc.ticket_count,
  COALESCE(ac.agent_count, 0) AS agent_count,
  ROUND(tc.ticket_count::numeric / NULLIF(ac.agent_count, 0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mc.message_count, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(tc.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS avg_messages_per_ticket,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(pc.high_urgent_count, 0) / NULLIF(tc.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS pct_high_or_urgent_priority,
  ROUND(rs.avg_resolution_minutes, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(bc.breach_count, 0) / NULLIF(tc.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM target_tenants tt
JOIN ticket_counts tc ON tc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN agent_counts ac ON ac.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN message_counts mc ON mc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN priority_counts pc ON pc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN resolution_stats rs ON rs.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN breach_counts bc ON bc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
ORDER BY resolution_breach_rate DESC, tt.tenant_name

question: Is Marrowby & Vane's and Studio Vrij's slowness concentrated in specific topics (especially delivery-related ones), or uniformly slow across all topics, compared to Cragsley Outfitters?
sql:
WITH tenant_filter AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Cragsley Outfitters')
),
ticket_tags AS (
  SELECT t.id AS ticket_id, t.tenant_id, t.created_at, t.resolved_at, st.name AS tag_name
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN ticket_tags_map ttm ON ttm.ticket_id = t.id
  JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id
  JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tenant_totals AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_tickets
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
),
breaches AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ticket_id FROM sla_breaches WHERE breach_kind = 'resolution'
)
SELECT
  tf.name AS tenant_name,
  tt.tag_name,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / tot.total_tickets, 1) AS pct_of_tenant_tickets,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN tt.resolved_at IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tt.resolved_at - tt.created_at)) / 60.0 END)) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.ticket_id IS NOT NULL THEN tt.ticket_id END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM ticket_tags tt
JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = tt.tenant_id
JOIN tenant_totals tot ON tot.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN breaches b ON b.ticket_id = tt.ticket_id
GROUP BY tf.name, tt.tag_name, tot.total_tickets
ORDER BY tf.name, ticket_count DESC, tt.tag_name

question: Is there any visible relationship between how much customers engage with the knowledge base and how many tickets we get — even a rough, non-causal signal?
sql:
SELECT m.month_label,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets t WHERE t.created_at >= m.month_start AND t.created_at < m.month_end) AS ticket_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM page_views pv WHERE pv.viewed_at >= m.month_start AND pv.viewed_at < m.month_end AND (pv.path ILIKE '%/help%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/kb%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%knowledge%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/faq%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/support%')) AS kb_engagement_count,
       'page_views.path ILIKE any of %/help%, %/kb%, %knowledge%, %/faq%, %/support% (best-guess pattern)' AS kb_engagement_signal_used
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start, (month_start + INTERVAL '1 month') AS month_end
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
) m
ORDER BY m.month_label ASC

question: Once we strip out the known carrier-incident months, do Marrowby & Vane and Studio Vrij still look worse than Cragsley Outfitters, or does that fully explain the gap?
sql:
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  excluded_period,
  ticket_count_after_exclusion,
  avg_resolution_minutes_after_exclusion,
  resolution_breach_rate_after_exclusion
FROM (
  SELECT
    ft.tenant_name,
    ft.excluded_period,
    count(*) AS ticket_count_after_exclusion,
    round(avg(extract(epoch from (ft.resolved_at - ft.created_at)) / 60.0)) AS avg_resolution_minutes_after_exclusion,
    round(
      100.0 * sum(
        case when exists (
          select 1 from sla_breaches sb
          where sb.ticket_id = ft.ticket_id and sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
        ) then 1 else 0 end
      ) / count(*),
      1
    ) AS resolution_breach_rate_after_exclusion
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tk.id as ticket_id,
      t.name as tenant_name,
      case
        when t.name = 'Marrowby & Vane' then 'Excludes Nov-Dec 2025'
        when t.name = 'Studio Vrij' then 'Excludes May-Jul 2025'
        else 'None'
      end as excluded_period,
      tk.created_at,
      tk.resolved_at
    FROM tickets tk
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tk.tenant_id
    WHERE t.name IN ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
      AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
      AND tk.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      AND NOT (
        (t.name = 'Marrowby & Vane' AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-11-01' AND tk.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01')
        OR
        (t.name = 'Studio Vrij' AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-05-01' AND tk.created_at < timestamp '2025-08-01')
      )
  ) ft
  GROUP BY ft.tenant_name, ft.excluded_period
) x
ORDER BY resolution_breach_rate_after_exclusion DESC, tenant_name

Round avg_delivery_days to 1 decimal, pct to 1 decimal percent.
tags.grain: one row per month in 2025, for Marrowby & Vane shipments carried by Albion Parcel only

title: Albion Parcel monthly on-time performance at Marrowby & Vane
